As a main application we derive an in-radius lower bound depending on the curvature which then also implies Heinz-type estimates for minimal graphs and uniform area bounds for graphical hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
papers.abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the coefficients in these expansions, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$.

papers.title: Self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
papers.authors: Yunjoo Kim, Bongsuk Kwon, Wanyong Shim
papers.abstract: We prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $C^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ H\"older regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. This class includes the Camassa--Holm and Degasperis--Procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. In the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized Hunter--Saxton (gHS) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. Consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. To handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the gHS family. The key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. We identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. This leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp H\"older regularity. The theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.

papers.title: Robust High-Order BUG Integrators without Basis Augmentation
papers.abstract: We develop robust high-order basis-update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation without basis augmentation or rank truncation. The basis and core updates use the same approximate increment. We establish a two-sided relaxed-exactness estimate that controls the error in the low-rank approximation by the increment error. Under the stated assumptions on the vector field and its normal component, sufficiently accurate increments yield local and global error bounds whose constants and step-size restrictions are independent of small singular values. Using explicit Runge--Kutta increments, we obtain robust orders two, three, and four for the explicit midpoint method, Heun's third-order method, and Merson's fourth-order method, respectively. Every internal stage and final approximation has rank at most the prescribed rank $r$. We also prove that these orders are retained under arbitrary basis augmentation followed by best rank-$r$ SVD truncation at the internal stages and the endpoint, without a separate assumption on the truncation error. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence orders and show comparable performance with and without augmentation.

papers.title: Isomorphic embeddings of $L_q(0,1)$ into Lorentz--Schatten ideals
Moving Cut Loci and Gaussian Fluctuations of Intrinsic Huber Means on Compact Riemannian Manifolds
papers.authors: Rui Qiu, Yiwei Yao, Zhou Yu
papers.abstract: Moving cut loci can change the limiting covariance of sample Huber means even when the cut locus of the population mean has probability zero. On a closed connected Riemannian manifold, we prove that the averaged logarithm field is $C^1$ near a point $m$ whenever the sampling law has a continuous density near its cut locus. The result holds for every continuous weight depending only on the observation, and the covariant derivative includes an explicit integral over the regular cut locus. When $m$ is a Huber mean for a fixed positive threshold, assume that the distance to $m$ has no atom at that threshold. The Hessian of the population risk then equals the expected pointwise Hessian minus a positive semidefinite cut locus correction. If $m$ is unique and this Hessian is positive definite, every measurable selection of global minimizers for i.i.d. samples satisfies a tangent-space central limit theorem. The cut loci of points in a ball of radius $\delta$ sweep out a region of volume $O(\delta)$, uniformly in the centre. These results establish the volume and integrability conditions previously assumed in a central limit theorem for intrinsic Fr\'echet means. At each fixed centre, the volume measure on this region, divided by $\delta$, converges weakly to an explicit measure on the regular cut locus. The Huber correction vanishes exactly when the region swept out about $m$ has probability $o(\delta)$.

papers.title: Volume asymptotics for a family of hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
papers.abstract: For the family $\{\mathcal{M}_{g,k}\}_{g\geqslant k\geqslant 0}$ of orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary and cusps introduced by R.~Frigerio, B.~Martelli, and C.~Petronio, the volume of the manifolds depends only on the non-negative integer parameters $g$ and $k$; thus the volume function $Vol(g,k)$ is well defined. The main result of the paper is an asymptotic description of this function: it is approximated by a linear function of $g$ and $k$ whose coefficients are explicitly expressed in terms of the volumes of the regular ideal tetrahedron and the regular ideal octahedron; moreover, the volume does not exceed the linear approximation by a difference of order $O(1/g)$. As consequences, three theorems comparing volumes are obtained: monotonicity under coordinatewise increase of the parameters, estimates for the passage from parameter $g$ to $g+1$, and monotonicity along lines of constant complexity $g+k$. For small values of the parameters, approximate values of the volumes are computed and collected in a table used in verifying the cases $g<8$.

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

papers.title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
papers.abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/\Gamma$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].

papers.title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
papers.abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+\Delta)\) is nef and big, then \((X,\Delta)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata. We construct such a curve from a free Campana curve by attaching to it free rational curves which intersect positively with divisors that span the cone of effective divisors, and smooth the resulting comb.

papers.title: The Calder\'on Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $\rho\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-\Delta+P^2\rho-\omega^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-\Delta+P^2\rho$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.

papers.title: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems
papers.authors: Seraphin F. Kimaryo, Jung-Mo Moon, Kyungchun Lee
papers.abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.

papers.title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
papers.authors: Oliver Gaul, Tim Donkiewicz, Marco L\"ubbecke
papers.abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

papers.title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
papers.abstract: We prove that the collection of all cluster boundaries of near-critical site percolation (with a fixed parameter) on the triangular lattice has a unique scaling limit in the loop-ensemble space, as the mesh size tends to 0. This answers a problem proposed by Camia, Fontes and Newman (2006). Using this, we also prove that near-critical percolation exploration path in a disk converges in distribution to a continuous path as the mesh size goes to 0. The main idea of our proof is to construct the cut-off loop ensembles under the near-critical coupling, based on the enhanced networks and the quad-crossing scaling limits of near-critical percolation constructed by Garban, Pete and Schramm (2018); the proof also relies on the study of the geometry of cluster chains. Some properties of the limiting loop ensemble, including rotation invariance, scale covariance and finite chaining, are established. Moreover, a few applications of our scaling-limit result and proof strategy are discussed.

papers.title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constants
papers.abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge2$ that is not a power of two there are constants $c_n>0$ and $B_n>2$ such that $s(C_n^r)\ge c_nB_n^r$ for all $r\ge1$. For powers of two, Harborth's formula gives growth rate exactly $2$. For the remaining even exponents, the previous lower bounds were of order $r2^r$. When $n=2m$ with $m\ge3$ odd, we prove the transfer inequality \[ A_n(H\oplus C_n^5)\ \ge\ 12\,A_n(H\oplus C_n)+8\,A_n(H\oplus C_m), \] where $A_n(G)$ is the maximal length of a sequence over $G$ without an $n$-term zero-sum subsequence and $H$ is any finite abelian group whose exponent divides $n$. The transfer extends a configuration of Elsholtz to twenty full cyclic fibers. Combined with a nine-point binary construction for $2m$-term zero-sums over $C_m^r$, it gives bases at least $2.0341$ that tend to $2.0394\ldots$; combined with a finite-field construction, it gives $s(C_6^r)\ge c\cdot 2.0491^r$. For exponents divisible by $4$ that are not powers of two, we obtain a base above two from a weighted random construction on the eighteen-point configuration of Wang and Zeng.

papers.title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
papers.authors: Tien Dat Dinh, Nguyen Thac Dung, Glen Wheeler
papers.abstract:
We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided
  \[
  \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,d\mu=0
  \]
  for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis.
  We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if
  \[
  \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,d\mu = O(r^d)
  \]
  for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.

papers.title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
papers.authors: Shuliang Bai, Haoxuan Cheng, Bobo Hua
papers.abstract: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.

papers.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
papers.authors: Manuela Aguiar, Ana Dias, Fahimeh Mokhtari
papers.abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

papers.title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
papers.authors: Ana Djurdjevac, M\'at\'e Gerencs\'er, Helena Kremp
papers.abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

papers.title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
papers.abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincar\'e map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

papers.title: The P\'{o}lya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
papers.authors: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun, Yong Zhang
papers.abstract: We prove the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $\Lambda_1\left(\Omega\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 \lambda_1^{\mathrm D}\left(\Omega\right)$, where $\lambda_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{\nu,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.

papers.title: Small cells in great-circle arrangements
papers.abstract:
We study the areas of the cells determined by an arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ of $n$ distinct great circles on the unit sphere, with no three concurrent. Let $m(\mathcal{A})$ and $M(\mathcal{A})$ denote the smallest and largest cell areas, respectively. Our first result is the bound \[
  m(\mathcal{A})\le \frac{C_*+O(n^{-3/4})}{n^2},
  \qquad C_*=7.0666071493\ldots , \] where the implied constant is absolute. This improves the coefficient $\pi^2$ obtained from classical polygonal perimeter estimates. We also prove that $M(\mathcal{A})/m(\mathcal{A})>13$ for all sufficiently large $n$, improving the bound $7.43$ of L.~Fejes T\'oth. The main tool is a perimeter inequality for planar polygons which takes account of their exterior angles. We combine this with a positive semidefinite kernel on the sphere and use gnomonic projection to obtain bounds for spherical cells.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous First-order Differential Operator Representations of $E_6$ and Graded Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We realize the restricted dual Verma modules of arbitrary highest weight for the complex simple Lie algebra of type $E_6$ by inhomogeneous first-order differential operators in $36$ variables. The construction is obtained by applying Xu's functor (2016) to the full conformal oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{o}(10)$. We construct polynomial bases for all six fundamental $E_6$-modules and obtain a finite spanning set for every finite-dimensional irreducible $E_6$-module $V(\lambda)$. The degree in $16$ selected variables gives $V(\lambda)$ a grading over the symmetric algebra of the opposite abelian nilradical. We compute its Hilbert series and graded Betti numbers, and verify the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks conjecture for this family. The minimal graded free resolution of $V(\lambda)$ is pure precisely when $\lambda$ is a nonnegative multiple of the Weyl vector of $E_6$. Among nonzero dominant integral $\lambda$'s, the minimum total Betti number is $435204$, attained exactly at two minuscule weights $\omega_1$ and $\omega_6$.

papers.title: Growth function of the cactus groups
papers.abstract: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.

papers.title: Higher order schemes for the numerical solution of integro-differential equation-based age-of-infection models with time-dependent contact rates
papers.authors: Anna Wendler, Jan Hasenauer, Martin J. K\"uhn
papers.abstract:
Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging.
  Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. The resulting numerical schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulations of IDE-based epidemic models with general sojourn time distributions and changing contact patterns.

papers.title: Nearly Computable Numbers with Additional Properties
papers.abstract:
A real number is called \emph{nearly computable} if it is the limit of a computable sequence of rational (or dyadic) numbers that has the additional property that for any computable subsequence the sequence of differences of consecutive elements converges to $0$ computably. The main result of this article provides methods for constructing nearly computable numbers with additional properties. The main result is proved by an infinite injury priority argument. Using these methods, we construct nearly computable numbers with several different additional properties:
  - a nearly computable number that is not divergence bounded computable,
  - for any left-computable number $\alpha$ that is neither in the least nor in the highest Solovay degree, a left-computable, nearly computable number that is Solovay incomparable with $\alpha$,
  - a nearly computable number $\gamma$ that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers but has the property that for any two left-computable numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$ wih $\gamma=\alpha-\beta$ both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are Martin-L\"of random.
  We also look at two classes of nearly computable numbers: the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ of differences of real numbers that are nearly computable and left-computable, and the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$ of nearly computable numbers that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers. Both classes form real closed fields, in fact, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is closed under computable functions with open domain that are Lipschitz continuous or differentiable. Finally, we show that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is a proper subset of $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$.

papers.title: Exact Decisions and Certified Values in $L_\infty$-Norm Computation from State-Space Representations
papers.authors: Alban Quadrat, Fabrice Rouillier, Grace Younes
papers.abstract: Computing the $L_\infty$-norm of a time-invariant linear ordinary differential control system is a routine task in robust control, usually delegated to floating-point routines that perform well on most practical systems. Behind the numerical value, however, lies a discrete decision: whether a pole lies on the imaginary axis, and whether a mode of a realization is actually a pole of the transfer matrix. Floating-point arithmetic can only replace this decision with a tolerance. This paper explains, for a control audience, what reliable symbolic-numeric computation offers for this problem: exact arithmetic where a decision has to be made, and certified enclosures where a value has to be computed. We show how the problem is turned into a small polynomial system directly from state-space data, how this system is solved in practice, and what it costs. A benchmark on the {\tt COMPleib} library and on families of systems with known norms shows that two standard numerical routines err in opposite directions on the imaginary-axis decision, and never on the same system, while the certified method decides it correctly on every instance tested and computes the norm at a cost comparable to that of the numerical routines on most systems. We conclude with practical guidelines for users of numerical tools.

papers.title: Lempert and pluricomplex Green functions near non-semipositive boundary points
papers.abstract: We study the two-step Lempert function and the pluricomplex Green function near a non-semipositive boundary point of a bounded domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove a sharp upper estimate for the two-step Lempert function in terms of the local boundary scale $H_D$, and obtain matching estimates for the pluricomplex Green function. As a consequence, these quantities have the same boundary behaviour as the Kobayashi distance. For the usual Lempert function, we prove an upper estimate of order $\sqrt{H_D}$, which implies the optimal local $1/4$-H\"older estimate, and determine its precise boundary behaviour along the real normal.

papers.title: Quasihyperbolic geodesics in the twice-puntured plane
papers.authors: Yali Du, Yike Ma, Shengyou Wen
papers.abstract: We study quasihyperbolic distance and geodesic uniqueness in the plane punctured at 0 and 2. For endpoints on the perpendicular bisector of the punctures and on opposite sides of the real axis, the distance is the smaller of the length of the vertical segment and the least length of a feasible detour. For symmetric endpoints 1 \pm it with t > 0, the geodesic is unique precisely when arsinh t + arctan t < \pi. At equality there are exactly three geodesic images, and above the threshold there are exactly two. For arbitrary endpoints, we derive variational formulas for the distance in terms of admissible logarithmic spirals and their contacts with the bisector. The minimizing candidates in these formulas give all geodesic images and yield a length-comparison criterion for uniqueness.

papers.title: Multicontinuum Poroelasticity Model. Analysis and Computation
papers.authors: Jing Zhang, Mohammed Al Kobaisi, Dmitry Ammosov, Jian Huang, Yunqing Huang
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a macroscopic multicontinuum model for Biot poroelasticity. The full macroscopic multicontinuum system is derived by projecting the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces enriched with first-order multiscale corrections. This construction retains generalized pressure storage and coupling terms, with effective coefficients inherited from the microscopic bilinear forms. Under suitable coefficient assumptions, we establish well-posedness and energy stability of the macroscopic multicontinuum model. A fully discrete scheme combining the Galerkin finite element method in space with the backward Euler method in time is then developed. Its well-posedness and stability are proved, and a priori error estimates are derived using appropriate projection operators and energy arguments. Finally, numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate the accuracy of the multicontinuum model with respect to the averaged fine-scale solution.

papers.title: Sharp Liouville theorems for the Hardy-H\'enon p-Laplace equation and classification of positive solutions for the critical Hardy p-Laplace equation
papers.abstract: We prove subcritical nonexistence for $-\Delta_pu=|x|^au^q$ in $R^N$, with $1<p<N$ and $a>-p$, in the positive locally bounded weak class. Continuous Steiner symmetrization of a nonlinear auxiliary potential yields a directional pressure inequality; a localized Pohozaev identity and scaling give the Liouville theorem. At criticality, for $N\ge3$ and $-p<a<0$, we classify all positive entire weak solutions in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(R^N)$, without assuming local boundedness, symmetry, stability, finite energy, or decay at infinity.

papers.title: On shared responsibility, fish, and the strong law of large numbers
papers.abstract: We give a new, short, and intuitive proof of the strong law of large numbers for i.i.d. random variables.

papers.title: Small classes have linear neighbourhood complexity
papers.authors: John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev, Maksim Zhukovskii
papers.abstract: A hereditary graph class is small if it contains at most $n!c^n$ labelled graphs on $n$ vertices for some constant $c$. Small classes include proper minor-closed classes and classes of bounded twin-width. We prove that every small class has linear neighbourhood complexity, that is, in every graph in the class, vertex neighbourhoods intersect any $k$-vertex set in only $O(k)$ distinct ways. This resolves a conjecture of Bonnet, Duron, and the first two authors (ITCS 2025) and makes the algorithmic, structural, and representation consequences of linear neighbourhood complexity available for every small class. In particular, every small class admits an adjacency labelling scheme with $O(\log^2 n)$-bit labels, improving the previous $O(\log^3 n)$ bound.

papers.title: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations
papers.abstract:
The paper presents a brief overview of recent advances in the mathematical theory of evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems.
  The structure of expansions representing non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for hierarchies of fundamental evolution equations for many quantum particles is outlined. It has been shown that the concept of cumulants of operator semigroups forms the basis for non-perturbative representation of solutions to hierarchies of evolution equations that describe the state and observables.
  It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.

papers.title: Path complexes with concatenation and their relation to digraphs
papers.abstract: The path homology theory is based on the notion of path complex and is a part of GLMY-theory created and developed by Grigor'yan, Lin, Muranov, and Yau in a cycle of papers in 2012-2014. In this paper we define a path complex with concatenation ($PC$-complex) which is a particular case of a path complex. We define a natural topology on a set of vertices of any $PC$-complex, and describe properties of this topology and its relation to the discrete topology of Alexandroff. We prove the existence of functorial relations between some categories of $PC$-complexes and digraphs. These relations allow to transfer covering, homotopy and various versions of homology theory from digraph theory to $PC$-complexes.

papers.title: Nonabelian Hodge theory in positive characteristic for rank-2 vector bundles over curves
papers.abstract: We describe the Nonabelian Hodge Theory correspondence in positive characteristic between nilpotent Higgs bundles and flat bundles with nilpotent p-curvature, as constructed in the seminal paper by Ogus-Vologodsky, in the special case of rank-2 vector bundles over a smooth projective curve. In this set-up we can rephrase this correspondence as a shift of the extension class of a rank-2 vector bundle by a cohomology class encoding a W_2-lift of the curve. As an application, we obtain that a general rank-2 vector bundle of degree 0 admits a connection with non-zero nilpotent p-curvature.

papers.title: Polynomial approximations to Calabi--Yau metrics on quartic K3 surfaces and quintic threefolds
papers.abstract: On the Fermat quartic K3 surface and the Fermat quintic threefold, we construct K\"ahler metrics from explicit rational polynomial potentials and bound their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics in integral tensor norms. For specified compact families of smooth quartic and quintic hypersurfaces near the Fermat hypersurfaces, we give a terminating algorithm that constructs polynomial K\"ahler metrics with prescribed pointwise bounds on their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics and on their Ricci forms. The resulting metrics converge to the Ricci-flat metrics in every $C^r$ norm, uniformly in the parameter.

papers.title: Surface evolution under conformal map and linearized energy-stable parametric finite element methods
papers.abstract: In this paper, we aim to develop a linearized, energy-stable, second-order-in-time parametric finite element method without Lagrange multipliers for surface evolution equations on surfaces with or without boundaries, including (volume-preserving) mean curvature flow and surface diffusion. We first reformulate the original equations into a new unified form in which the tangential motion is determined by requiring the flow map to be conformal. Based on this new formulation, we present a family of parametric finite element schemes that employ a linearized Euler or Crank-Nicolson discretization in time. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the resulting linear system, as well as the energy stability of the schemes. Our discrete methods can be applied to general surfaces although the second-order scheme may degenerate to first-order accuracy in certain cases. Numerical results verify the robustness of our method and demonstrate its ability to preserve mesh quality.

papers.title: Hyperexponential Stabilization of Nonholonomic Systems by Oscillating Controls
papers.authors: Victoria Grushkovskaya, Mark\'eta Hrani\v{c}kov\'a, Alexander Zuyev
papers.abstract: We address the problem of designing time-varying feedback controls that stabilize a given equilibrium of a nonholonomic system at a faster than the exponential rate. We consider systems with an arbitrary degree of nonholonomy and prove a theorem on practical hyperexponential stabilization under a suitable assumption on the parameterized dither signals. The convergence proof is based on a comparison equation with a prescribed power of logarithmic terms. We apply this result to stabilize a model of a car with two off-hooked trailers.

papers.title: The maximum product of nontrivial cross $t$-intersecting families
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be nonempty families of $k$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $|A\cap B|\ge t$ for all $A\in\mathcal A$ and $B\in\mathcal B$, and suppose that each family has fewer than $t$ common elements. For $k\ge t+2\ge4$ and $n\ge(t+1)(k-t+1)$, we prove \[
  |\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\le\max\{h_t(n,k)^2,b_t(n,k)^2\}, \] where \[
  h_t(n,k)=\binom{n-t}{k-t}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-t}+t,\quad
  b_t(n,k)=(t+2)\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-1}+\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-2}. \] The bound is sharp, and we characterize all extremal pairs, whose families have equal sizes but need not coincide. The proof combines clique lifts, exchanges of generating families and a density inequality for cross-intersecting uniform layers. This gives a product version of the Hilton--Milner--Frankl theorem throughout the Erd\H{o}s--Ko--Rado range. In particular, it answers a question of Wen and Lv on whether a threshold of order $kt$ suffices for the sharp product bound.

papers.title: K-stable Fano varieties can have obstructed deformations
papers.abstract: We exhibit examples of K-stable Fano varieties with obstructed qG-deformations; more precisely, their miniversal qG-deformation spaces can be non-reduced. As a consequence, we show that both the K-moduli stack and the K-moduli space can be non-reduced, and hence non-smooth, at points corresponding to K-stable Fano varieties.

papers.title: $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$
papers.abstract: We classify all controlled $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$ up to Morita equivalence. This provides a proof of Donovan's Conjecture for resistant $2$-generated $2$-groups.

papers.title: Duality and hidden symmetries for time-inhomogeneous Markov processes
papers.abstract: We study the notion of duality in the setting of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. We define duality with time-dependent duality functions. We establish the connection between duality and time-dependent symmetries and intertwinings. We illustrate the abstract results with examples from interacting particle systems and diffusion processes.

papers.title: Classification of G-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces G/H with G simple
papers.authors: Huibin Chen, Zhiqi Chen, Zaili Yan, Fuhai Zhu
papers.abstract: We classify the $G$-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces $G/H$, where $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group and $H$ is an arbitrary closed subgroup. We give the complete list of nonnormal metrics, including their parameter conditions and the possible mixing between equivalent isotropy summands. The proof uses rigidity criteria for arbitrary cometric operators, reductions through centralizers, and the stabilizers of the relevant representations. For every fixed pair $(G,H)$, the space spanned by the $G$-g.o. cometrics has dimension at most three, and we determine the equality cases. We also compare the classification with the compact weakly symmetric pairs and explain why the choice of the transitive group is essential.

papers.title: Numerical solution of the Cauchy problem for second-order evolutionary equations with damped sinusoidal memory
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for a second-order evolutionary equation with an integral term containing the convolution of a memory kernel with the second derivative of the solution. The kernel is specified by a finite sum of damped sinusoidal functions with positive damping coefficients, amplitudes, and frequencies. A transformation of the original nonlocal problem into an equivalent local system of coupled second-order differential equations with additional variables is proposed. For the local system, an energy identity with a dissipative term is constructed and a priori estimates of the solution are obtained. On the basis of the local formulation, a three-level difference scheme with a weight parameter is considered. The decrease of the discrete energy under standard constraints on the weight parameter is proved, which ensures unconditional stability of the scheme in the corresponding energy norm. The theoretical consideration is supplemented by the results of numerical solution of a problem with memory for a one-dimensional wave equation.

papers.title: Non-concordant knots with the same trace
papers.abstract: Miller and Piccirillo demonstrated the existence of non-concordant knots that share the same 0-trace. In this short note, we generalize their result by showing that every smooth concordance class contains a knot K such that, for every nonzero integer n, there exists a knot $K_n$ whose n-trace is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to that of K, but for which $p[K_n] \ne p[K]$ in the topological concordance group for every positive integer p. Furthermore, $p[K_n]$ is distinct from $p[K']$ for any knot K' obtained from K by mirroring and/or reversing its orientation.

papers.title: Universal Realization of Milnor Attractors in Low Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the realization problem for Milnor attractors on compact metric spaces and establish a general sufficient criterion for universal realization. In particular, we prove that every smooth compact one-dimensional manifold, with or without boundary, and every smooth closed two-dimensional manifold has the property that each nonempty closed subset is the Milnor global attractor of a continuous self-map. If the manifold is connected, the realizing map may be chosen to be a homeomorphism. We also investigate the realization problem on selected one-dimensional continua and exhibit spaces for which universal realization fails.

papers.title: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition
papers.abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.

papers.title: The minimum size of the 3-dimensional torus
papers.authors: Seunghun Lee, Geunho Lim, Eran Nevo
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of K\"uhnel, Lassmann, and Lutz, first asked in 1984, that the minimal number of vertices in a triangulation of the $3$-dimensional torus is $15$.

papers.title: MetaCom: Meta Codebook Learning for Robust V2X Semantic Communications
papers.authors: Muge Yu, Danlan Huang, Xinyi Zhou, Shuqi Chai, Zhiyong Feng
papers.abstract: Collaborative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks faces dual challenges: strictly limited bandwidth and channel impairments. Existing static quantization schemes often suffer from feature manifold drift caused by highly non-stationary traffic environments. To address this, we propose MetaCom, a robust digital semantic communication framework featuring a Meta-Codebook Learning paradigm. First, we introduce a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications (DQSemCom) module trained with perturbations induced by the simulated digital modulation and channel via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. Building on this, we design a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism (Bi-MEM) that treats manifold drift as a sequence of rapid adaptation tasks, aligning the codebook via data-level smoothing and parameter-level meta-updates. Furthermore, we validate MetaCom under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Experimental results demonstrate that MetaCom achieves superior trade-offs between perception precision and communication overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin under low-SNR conditions.

papers.title: On the structure of the sets of connections between libration points and some applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the global description of the sets of heteroclinic and homoclinic connections between the center manifolds of the collinear libration points of the spatial circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. The approach builds on high-order parameterizations of the center-stable and center-unstable invariant manifolds and uses them to extract global information on how connections are organized across broad energy ranges. It involves: (a) constructing connectivity maps at the level of invariant tori, which encode which tori in the neighborhoods of $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected through heteroclinic and homoclinic trajectories; (b) refining this description to the level of individual connections by computing traces of torus--center manifold connections and using them to determine the number and distribution of distinct connecting trajectories between selected pairs of tori. Results are given for the Earth--Moon and Sun--Earth problems, together with examples illustrating how the resulting connectivity information can be used to design heteroclinic and homoclinic pseudo-trajectories with different purposes.

papers.title: Combinatorial results for semigroups of order-preserving mappings
papers.abstract: We investigate combinatorial properties of the semigroup of all order- preserving mappings on {1, 2, . . . , n} and of its subsemigroup of all decreasing order-preserving mappings. We show that the cardinal of the latter is the nth Catalan number and obtain a new proof of the standard Catalan identity. Using ballot arguments and the Reflection principle we find the probability that a random order-preserving mapping is indecomposable, and via the Wallis product we show that the mean number of orbits is of order root n. By contrast, the mean number of orbits of a random decreasing mapping of this type never exceeds 3; we find the distribution of the orbit number explicitly in both cases and obtain the limiting distribution for the Catalan monoid.

papers.title: Set-coloring Ramsey numbers with multiple intersections
papers.authors: Guantao Chen, Laihao Ding, Qiong Fan, Xiaolan Hu, Suyun Jiang, Chunxiang Wang
papers.abstract:
For integers $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$, we introduce the Ramsey number $R(G;r,s,t)$, defined as the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]$ to each edge of $K_N$ yields a copy of $G$ whose edges have at least $t$ colors in common. This generalizes the classical set-coloring Ramsey number $R(G;r,s)=R(G;r,s,1)$, studied since the work of Erdos, Hajnal, and Rado. We show that $t$ cannot in general be eliminated by reparametrization: infinitely many quadruples $(G;r,s,t)$ satisfy $R(G;r,s,t)\ne R(G;a,b)$ for every $a\ge b\ge1$.
  Writing $\alpha=\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$, the shadow inequality $R(G;r,s,t)\le R(G;\binom{r}{t},\binom{s}{t},1)$ and the recent proof of the Erdos--Sos conjecture imply $R(T_n;r,s,t)\le\lfloor\alpha(n-2)\rfloor+2$ for every $n$-vertex tree $T_n$. For stars, we obtain packing bounds and exact values under suitable divisibility conditions. For paths and even cycles $G$ of order $n$, we improve the upper bound to $R(G;r,s,t)\le(\alpha-\gamma+o(1))n$ as $n\to\infty$, for fixed $r>s\ge t\ge1$ and some $\gamma=\gamma(r,s,t)>0$. We also prove that, for fixed $s,t$, the tree bound is asymptotically sharp for paths as $r,n\to\infty$, and for even cycles when $n\to\infty$ first and then $r\to\infty$.
  For cliques $K_n$, we transfer known bounds of Conlon et al. for ordinary set-coloring Ramsey numbers to the general parameter $t$, obtaining two-sided exponential bounds. For each fixed $n\ge3$, we identify an explicit piecewise-linear function $\Phi_n$ that determines a growth threshold. If $s/r\to\sigma$ and $t/r\to\tau$ as $r\to\infty$, with $0<\tau\le\sigma<1$, then $R(K_n;r,s,t)=O(1)$ when $\tau<\Phi_n(\sigma)$, whereas $R(K_n;r,s,t)\ge\exp(cr)$ for some $c>0$ when $\tau>\Phi_n(\sigma)$.

papers.title: Sharp L^p and variation inequalities for maximal operators on finite connected graphs
papers.authors: Feng Liu, Yongzhi Lian, Yanzhen Wang
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V_G,E_G)$ be a finite connected graph (here $V_G$ and $E_G$ denote the set of vertices and edges of $G$ respectively). The primary aim of this paper is to study the sharp variation and $L^p$ inequalities of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator $M_G$ defined on $G$ and its fractional variant $M_{\alpha,G}\,(0<\alpha<1)$). Set $${\bf C}_{\alpha,G}^{p,q}=\sup\limits_{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)>0}\frac{{\rm Var}_{q,G}(M_{\alpha,G}f)}{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)},$$ where ${\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)$ denotes the $p$-variation of $f$ on $G$. We denote by $K_n$ (resp., $S^n$) the complete (resp., star) graph with $n\geq4$ vertices. When $\alpha=0$, we prove ${\bf C}_{\alpha,S_n}^{p,p} =1-\frac{1}{n}$ for $0<p<1$. This solve a question originally posed by Liu and Xue in 2021. In the fractional case $0<\alpha<1$, we prove ${\bf C}_{\alpha,S_n}^{1,q}=1-n^{-\alpha}$ and ${\bf C}_{\alpha,K_n}^{1,q} =(1-n^{\alpha-1})(n-1)^{-\alpha}$ for $q=\frac{1}{1-\alpha}$, which provide some examples focusing on sharp variation inequalities of fractional maximal operators. The sharp variation inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operators are also established. In addition, the sharp $L^p$ inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operator $\widetilde{M}_{\alpha,G}$ are also studied. More precisely, we obtain lower bounds and upper bounds for $C_{q,G}$ such that the inequality $\|\widetilde{M}_{\alpha,G}f\|_q\leq C_{q,G}\|f\|_p$ holds and the complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$ are two extreme graphs that reach the lower bound and upper bound respectively.

papers.title: On least periods of a class of arithmetic functions
papers.abstract: Let $k, a, c$ be positive integers, let $b$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a nonvanishing complex-valued multiplicative function. Qian, Tan and Hong proved that $$G_f(n)=\frac{\prod\limits_{i=0}^k f(b+a(n+i c))}{f\left(\operatorname*{lcm}\limits_{0 \leq i \leq k}\{b+a(n+i c)\}\right)}$$ is periodic and asked for its least positive period. In this paper, we answer this problem by giving an explicit formula for this period in terms of finitely many values of $f$ at prime powers. In particular, we determine the least periods for $f(n)=\sigma_\alpha(n)=\sum\limits_{d \mid n} d^\alpha$ for every real $\alpha$, and for $f(n)=n^{\varepsilon}$ for every real $\varepsilon$.

papers.title: On the Equivalence of Linear and $C^*$ Extremality for Unital Completely Positive Maps on Commutative Real $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital commutative real $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal H$ be a finite dimensional real Hilbert space. In this article, an easily verifiable necessary and sufficient condition for a linear extreme unital completely positive (UCP) map $\Phi:\mathcal A \rightarrow B(\mathcal H)$ to be C*-extreme, is obtained. As an application, the $C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A$ on which linear extreme UCP maps coincide with the $C^*$-extreme ones, are classified.

papers.title: Harmonic functions and the topology of 3-manifolds under nonnegative scalar curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish and recover some results about noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and some topological assumptions. Firstly, we apply the work in Oronzio \cite{Oro1,Oro2} to obtain a nonexistence result of the harmonic function. Secondly, we use the argument in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} to establish a rigidity result, which states that such manifold is isometric to the warped product of a flat tours and a half line. Finally, we recover a topological result in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} via a different argument.

papers.title: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination for Multi-Cell XL-MIMO under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity
papers.authors: Muhammad Shoaib Ayub, Rana Muhammad Subhan, Insoo Koo, Felipe Augusto Pereira de Figueiredo
papers.abstract: Spatial non-stationarity in multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) confines each user to a visibility region (VR) of each array. VR-Net exploits these regions for subarray-level coordinated beamforming. A base-station (BS)-indexed conflict graph identifies overlapping VRs; gain-based association and a masked multi-cell weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) iteration restrict beam design and channel state information (CSI) uploads to the relevant subarray blocks. We establish conditions for exact per-cell decoupling, derive the expected CSI loads, bound the loss of designing on the VR-gated channel and the loss of the support constraint, and characterize single-edge visibility contrast through a closed-form Fresnel transition width. Simulations use a 3GPP TR 38.901 Release-19-based near-field UMi channel with modular facade arrays and pre-registered criteria. At a 30 dB threshold, VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of the full-aperture WMMSE sum rate in every tested setting while uploading 10-39% fewer complex CSI entries. It gains up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz over an all-user adaptation of the multi-cell scheme of P\'erez-Ad\'an et al. at moderate power and dense load, and inter-cell coordination adds up to 33% over per-cell design.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity Notions on Complete Non-Compact Complex Manifolds
papers.abstract: Gromov's K\"ahler hyperbolicity, extended by McMullen to complete manifolds of finite volume and bounded geometry, has non-K\"ahler analogues (balanced, SKT, Gauduchon and divisorial hyperbolicity) that have so far been studied only on compact manifolds. We define these notions for complete Hermitian manifolds and prove the following. A manifold carrying a balanced metric and a Hermitian metric with bounded $(\partial+\bar\partial)$-potentials satisfies a Cheeger inequality, so its fundamental group is non-amenable in the compact case. K\"ahler and SKT hyperbolic manifolds are Brody hyperbolic, and balanced and Gauduchon hyperbolic manifolds are divisorially hyperbolic, without any compactness assumption. Products give complete non-compact non-K\"ahler examples. A non-compact surface may be divisorially hyperbolic without being Brody hyperbolic. Finally, no functorial pseudo-distance characterises divisorial hyperbolicity.}

papers.title: Nonlinear selection in vanishing discount problems for Hamilton--Jacobi equations
papers.abstract: We study the vanishing discount problem $G(x,Du_\lambda,\lambda u_\lambda)=c_0$, where $G$ is convex and superlinear in the momentum and strictly increasing in its last variable. Assuming a leading-order expansion of the Lagrangian of order $q>0$, we prove uniform convergence and characterize the selected solution by nonlinear inequalities against Mather measures. In particular, our results cover discount terms whose first derivative at the origin vanishes, such as the cubic discount, beyond existing convergence results based on first-order nondegeneracy. Our proof uses truncated calibrated curves and time averages, without the exponentially weighted measures used by Davini--Fathi--Iturriaga--Zavidovique. In the linear case, it gives a short alternative proof of their convergence and selection theorem. An example shows that linear and cubic discounts may select critical solutions that do not differ by an additive constant.

papers.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
papers.authors: Zixuan Qiu, Pengshuai Shi, Ruijun Wu
papers.abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.

papers.title: Packing sets by rigid motions and similarities
papers.authors: Daewoong Cheong, Thang Pham, Chun-Yen Shen
papers.abstract: For nonempty Borel sets $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $\Theta\subset O(d)\times\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge2$, let $\Theta(E)$ be the union of the rigid copies $gE+z$, where $(g,z)\in\Theta$. We prove that $\Theta(E)$ has positive Lebesgue measure whenever $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E+\dim_H\Theta>\frac{d(d+1)}2$, where $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E$ is the spherical Fourier dimension of $E$. This resolves a conjecture on packing by arbitrary Borel families of rigid motions. Our proof develops a discrete-to-continuous framework by adapting a finite-field averaging argument to $\mathbb R^d$ using Sobolev estimates on the group of rigid motions. We also obtain analogous packing results for similarities. The same framework can be used to show that if $\tau$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the similarity group with finite $\bigl(\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1\bigr)$-energy, then every compactly supported $\tau$-stationary probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ has a smooth density. We deduce that a nonempty compact set has nonempty interior if its family of similarity self-embeddings has Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1$.

papers.title: Bergman Kernel Zeros on Generalized Hartogs Triangles
papers.abstract: We study zeros of the Bergman kernel on the generalized Hartogs triangles $H_\gamma=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^\gamma<|z_2|<1\}$. For every real $1<\gamma<2$, suitable sections near the singular vertex contain exactly $\lceil(\gamma-1)^{-1}\rceil-1$ zeros in a prescribed disk, all of them simple. This answers a question of Edholm and Mathew [\emph{Math. Z.} \textbf{313} (2026)] and, together with the known cases, shows that $H_\gamma$ has a zero-free Bergman kernel precisely when $\gamma$ is the reciprocal of a positive integer. We also fix the second kernel argument and a complex line in the first argument, and prove that the total number of zeros on the admissible section is comparable to $(\gamma-1)^{-1}$ as $\gamma\to1^+$; a comparable number are simple and nonreal. For the sections near the vertex, all but at most one of the counted zeros concentrate near the unit circle, and the angular counting error is uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Cleanness and real rank zero in $C^*$-algebras
papers.authors: Lu Cui, Minghui Ma, Wei Yuan
papers.abstract: A unital $C^*$-algebra is called clean if every element is the sum of an idempotent and an invertible element. We prove that cleanness is equivalent to real rank zero. More precisely, the invertible summand can be chosen with inverse norm at most $2+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and the constant $2$ is optimal. In particular, every von Neumann algebra is clean, answering a question of Lam. Clean decompositions with uniformly bounded idempotent summands characterize real rank zero and stable rank one. Moreover, $*$-cleanness, defined by requiring the idempotent summands to be projections, is equivalent to real rank zero, stable rank one, and triviality of the $K_1$-group. Finally, sharp cleanness, defined by requiring clean decompositions with inverse norm at most $2$, is equivalent to real rank zero and the $SAW^*$ property.

papers.title: On the orders of irreducible subgroups of finite classical groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite almost simple classical group over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with socle $G_0$ and natural module $V$ of dimension $n$. Let $H$ be a core-free maximal subgroup of $G$. By a well-known theorem of Aschbacher, either $H$ is contained in one of eight subgroup collections that are defined in terms of the geometry of $V$, or $H$ is almost simple and the embedding of $H$ in $G$ arises from an absolutely irreducible representation of a covering group of the socle of $H$. We write $\mathcal{S}$ for the latter collection of irreducibly embedded almost simple subgroups. Determining the subgroups in $\mathcal{S}$ is an intractable problem, in general, which has only been fully resolved in low dimensions. However, many applications require some control on the subgroups in $\mathcal{S}$, expressed in terms of their order, or properties of their elements, for example. Extending a theorem of Liebeck from the 1980s, and building on later work by Burness, Guralnick and Saxl, in this paper we determine all the subgroups $H \in \mathcal{S}$ satisfying the lower bound $|H| \geqslant q^n$. We also highlight a recent application of our main result to a problem in finite geometry.

papers.title: Coset Geometries and Tameness of Certain Classes of Shephard Groups
papers.authors: Claudio Alexandre Piedade, Travis Scrimshaw, Philippe Tranchida
papers.abstract: For the class of Shepard groups (which contain Coxeter groups, Artin-Tits groups, and many finite complex reflection groups), we investigate the structure of the coset incidence systems defined using the standard parabolic subgroups. For the class of tame Shephard groups, which is when all the standard parabolic subgroups are equal to the corresponding Shephard groups, then the intersection of standard parabolic subgroups is also a standard parabolic subgroup. We show that when the Shephard group is either finite, right-angled, or rank two, then it is tame; this is further evidence that all Shephard groups are tame. Finally, we mix the Burau and the geometric representations to produce a representation for all Shephard groups, but we show it is not faithful in rank two unless the Shephard group is finite or an Artin-Tits group.

papers.title: Wiener-path-based exact and splitting simulation of linear and semi-linear SDEs with additive noise
papers.abstract:
Strong, or pathwise, simulation of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) requires linking a generated SDE path to the corresponding realization of its driving Wiener process. In this work, we develop Wiener-path-based simulation procedures for multidimensional linear and semi-linear SDEs with additive noise that preserve this connection.
  Building upon a known Wiener-path-based exact simulation approach for linear SDEs, we extend this construction to generate coherent paths simultaneously on different time grids. We further propose an alternative exact simulation procedure that requires fewer random numbers and therefore provides a more efficient construction, while retaining a controlled approximation of the coupling between the SDE path and its associated Wiener path. The proposed methods are illustrated on a stochastic harmonic oscillator, a well-known model from classical mechanics, with the simulation results confirming the theoretical findings.
  We then extend the Wiener-path-based construction to semi-linear SDEs, which arise in many real-world applications. In contrast to linear SDEs, their solutions are generally not available in closed form, making numerical approximation methods necessary. For Euler--Maruyama-type methods, the relation between a given Wiener path and the corresponding approximate SDE path is explicit, whereas constructing Wiener-path-based simulations using structure-preserving splitting methods is less immediate. We address this challenge by incorporating the aforementioned Wiener-path-based constructions into splitting methods. Illustrations on the stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo model and the stochastic Jansen--Rit neural mass model, two important models from neuroscience, demonstrate the applicability of the proposed procedures to non-linear stochastic systems.

papers.title: Optimal approximation results for non-standard growth functionals in the super-dimensional case
papers.abstract: In the super-dimensional case $p>n$ we show that $W^{1,p}$-functions can be uniformly approximated by H\"older continuous functions with improved exponent $\frac {p-n}{p-1}$. We use this to show density of smooth functions and absence of Lavrentiev's phenomenon for $(p, q)$-growth with optimal conditions. The special cases of double phase and Musielak--Orlicz growth are also included. Finally, we improve the conditions for maximal regularity of the double phase minimizers. In each case the optimality of our range of exponents is shown by known examples.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian approximation for Polyak--Ruppert averaged linear stochastic approximation
papers.authors: Bogdan Butyrin, Eric Moulines, Alexey Naumov, Sergey Samsonov
papers.abstract: We study how quickly the normalized Polyak--Ruppert average approaches its Gaussian limit in linear stochastic approximation with bounded i.i.d.\ coefficients. For step sizes decaying as $k^{-\gamma}$, with $1/2\le\gamma<1$, we prove an upper bound of order $n^{\gamma-1}$ on the approximation error over convex sets in fixed dimension. A matching lower bound holds for every fixed model. The fastest rate in this range is $n^{-1/2}$, attained at $\gamma=1/2$. We also obtain an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound on the error of the recursive multiplier bootstrap procedure.

papers.title: Escaping the Curse of Dimensionality in One-Step Flow-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: Flow and diffusion-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art quality, but require multiple forward passes at inference time, making them computationally costly. Consistency models overcome this by learning a flow map directly, enabling few-step generation and dramatically reducing the computation needed at test time. However, formal statistical guarantees for such one-step generators are scarce. Existing results either suffer from the curse of dimensionality or rely on impractical loss functions. We investigate whether one-step flow-based models can escape the curse of dimensionality under the assumption that the data distribution is generated by a low-dimensional surface perturbed with Gaussian noise. In this setup, we derive approximation and generalization error bounds for the flow map estimate that circumvent the curse of dimensionality. Our findings provide the first principled explanation for practical success of one-step flow-based generative models.

papers.title: On JT boundary algebras
papers.abstract: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.

papers.title: Semigroups with periodic complex-time boundedness and holomorphy regions
papers.abstract: We study the periodicity of complex-time boundedness and holomorphy domains of operator semigroups. We show that an imaginary-time covariance identity involving an isometry yields periodicity of these domains. The method is applied to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator and the hypoelliptic Laplacian on the circle, providing a spectral explanation of periodicity independent of the explicit geometry of their boundedness regions. We also discuss the distinction between boundedness and contractivity, using the classical heat semigroup as an example.

papers.title: Finite Element Approximation of Three-Dimensional Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Curve-Supported Controls
papers.abstract: We consider a linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problem in three dimensions with a box-constrained control supported on a compact embedded $C^{1,1}$ curve strictly contained in a bounded convex polyhedral domain. The right-hand side of the state equation is a measure supported on the curve, and the state is singular along it. We establish well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions and derive curve-adapted weighted inequalities and finite element error estimates for the singular state. For continuous piecewise linear finite elements on quasi-uniform tetrahedral meshes and variational discretization of the control, assuming exact integration over the curve, we prove the almost quadratic estimate $\|\bar q-\bar q_h\|_{L^2(\gamma)}\le Ch^2(1+\abs{\ln h})^3$. The proof of this estimate requires new results, which are of independent interest. The convergence rate observed in a numerical experiment is consistent with the predicted algebraic order.

papers.title: Extremal disc packings in compact hyperbolic surfaces of minimal genus
papers.abstract: A compact hyperbolic surface is $k$-extremal if it contains $k$ disjoint embedded discs of the largest possible radius; such surfaces are uniformized by surface subgroups of the triangle groups $\Delta^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We determine all extremal $k$-packings in every $k$-extremal surface of minimal genus, orientable of genus $2$ and non-orientable of genus $3$: $373$ surface groups in total, all treated in a unified way; $264$ of them had never been studied before. The computation is automatic and verified in exact arithmetic, each packing being certified by an element $\alpha\in\mathrm{PGL}_2$ over an explicit number field with $\alpha^{-1}K\alpha<\Delta^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We also obtain the full isometry groups of these surfaces. In every surface but one, all the extremal packings are related by isometries. The exception is the genus two surface $X_6$ of Girondo and Gonz\'alez-Diez, which has exactly five extremal $4$-packings, one invariant under all isometries and four forming an orbit; it is also the only one of these surfaces uniformized by two non-conjugate subgroups of the same triangle group, and we show that the two facts are equivalent. We find its equation, $y^2=x^6+2\sqrt{3}\,i\,x^3+1$. The results form a catalogue with detailed data and pictures of every surface (packings, isometries, Weierstrass points, Dirichlet domains), distributed with programs that allow the reader to consult it and to reproduce it completely.

papers.title: Markov Population Potential Game: An Alternative Framework for Markovian Traffic Assignment
papers.authors: Xuhang Liu, Kenan Zhang, Rui Yao
papers.abstract: Understanding the equilibrium behavior of large populations of interacting agents in transportation systems is challenging due to the high-dimensional state space and the coupled decision-making among agents. This study proposes the Markov population potential game (MPPG) that integrates Markov games, potential games, and population games as a unified framework for analyzing such interactions. The framework extends the classical Markov potential game to the population level and establishes theoretical conditions on stage rewards and state transitions under which the Markov population game admits a Beckmann-type potential function. Accordingly, every KKT point of the associated optimization problem yields an MPPG equilibrium. We further demonstrate that if only the reward condition holds, each KKT point of the optimization problem corresponds to a support-restricted $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, meaning the Q-values of any two active actions differ by at most $\varepsilon$, thereby significantly extending the applicability of MPPG. We further establish both priori and posteriori upper bounds of $\varepsilon$ to efficiently evaluate the approximation error. Inspired by the equivalent optimization problem, a projected-gradient (PG) policy iteration algorithm is developed. The theoretical bounds and PG algorithm are demonstrated through numerical experiments on a parametric Markov population game.

papers.title: Newforms as test vectors for representations of Saito-Kurokawa type
papers.abstract: We study irreducible (admissible) representations $\pi$ of the split group $G_n=SO(2n+1)$, both over finite and $p$-adic fields, which are distinguished for the (unramified) nonsplit form of $K_n=SO(2n)$ and for one more subgroup $H_n$. Over finite fields, $H_n$ is the split $SO(2n)$ while over $p$-adic fields it is the Gross-Tsai paramodular subgroup (of minimal level for $\pi$). These are all multiplicity one situations. With $0 \neq \ell_{n,K} \in {\rm Hom}_{K_n}(\pi_n,1)$ and $0 \neq v_{n,H} \in \pi_n^{H_n}$, both being one dimensional spaces, we are interested in the vanishing/nonvanishing of $|\ell_{n,K}(v_{n,H})|^2$. Appropriately normalized, this defines the notion of the correlation coefficient $c(\pi;H_n,K_n)$ of $H_n$ and $K_n$ in $G_n$ with respect to $\pi$. Via the theta correspondence between ${\rm SL}(2)$ (or ${\rm Mp}(2)$), we establish a bijection $\pi_n \leftrightarrow \pi_1$ between representations of $G_n$ and $G_1$ under consideration. Our main results then prove that $d_n c(\pi_n;H_n,K_n)$ is independent of the rank $n$, where $d_n =\dim \pi_n$ for finite fields and is defined in terms of the index of $H_n$ in the standard maximal compact subgroup of $G_n$ in the $p$-adic case. We also highlight a conjecture from [Ana25] on Legendre polynomials modulo $p$. Its truth will have the arithmetic consequence that over $\mathbb F_p$, given $\pi_1$, we can choose $u \in \mathbb F_p$ such that, in every rank $n$, all the correlation coefficients $c(\pi_n;H_n,u_nK_n u_n^{-1})$ are simultaneously nonzero and moreover they belong to $\mathbb Z_p^\times$ under any identification $\mathbb C \simeq \overline{\mathbb Q}_p$, where $u_n$ is a specific unipotent element in $G_n$ corresponding to $u$.

papers.title: Independent sets in regular uniform hypergraphs
papers.authors: An Chang, Lusheng Fang, Guorong Gao, Caihong Yang
papers.abstract: We prove that, for all integers $r\ge 2$ and $d\ge 1$, every finite simple $d$-regular $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $n$ vertices satisfies \[ \operatorname{ind}(H)\le \operatorname{ind}(H_d^r)^{n/(rd)}, \] with equality if and only if $H$ is a disjoint union of copies of $H_d^r$. Here $\operatorname{ind}(G)$ denotes the number of independent sets in $G$, and $ H_d^r$ is the $d$-regular $r$-partite $r$-graph on $rd$ vertices obtained by taking all $r$-sets consisting of one vertex from a fixed $d$-vertex set and one of $d$ pairwise disjoint $(r-1)$-sets partitioning the remaining vertices. This settles the conjecture of Balogh, Bollob\'as and Narayanan, who proved the bound for quasi-bipartite hypergraphs.

papers.title: Probabilistically Exact Convexification of Mixed-Integer Quadratic Optimization with Indicators
papers.abstract: We study the convexification of mixed-integer quadratic optimization with indicator variables. The problem remains NP-hard even when the quadratic matrix has bandwidth two, posing a fundamental obstacle to tractable exact convexification.
