To overcome this challenge in realistic settings, we introduce probabilistically exact (inner) convexification, a framework that relaxes the requirement of exactness for every objective while preserving exact optimality for statistically relevant ones. Our approach is motivated by inference applications, where the objective is determined by a data vector drawn from a distribution and a regularization vector chosen from a prescribed family. Our convexification preserves the exactness of the optimal value with high probability over the data distribution, simultaneously for every regularization vector in this family. We apply this notion to quadratic matrices of any fixed bandwidth. Despite their worst-case NP-hardness, we construct probabilistically exact convexifications that admit exact extended second-order cone formulations of size polynomial in the dimension $n$ and the inverse failure probability $1/\delta$. The required assumptions for their high-probability exactness are surprisingly mild: they accommodate both light-tailed and heavy-tailed data, including distributions without finite mean, as well as arbitrary nonnegative regularization coefficients.

papers.title: A Rigorous Fredholm Framework and Stabilized Equal-Order Finite Element Methods for the Time-Harmonic Biot Model
papers.authors: Mingchao Cai, Yiming Fu, Jingzhi Li
papers.abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and finite element approximation of a three-field formulation of the time-harmonic Biot model, motivated by frequency-domain magnetic resonance elastography. The underlying complex-valued mixed variational problem is noncoercive because of the inertial elasticity term and the coupled three-field structure. Continuous well-posedness is established under a non-resonance condition by decomposing the variational operator into an invertible principal part and a compact perturbation and applying the Fredholm alternative. We then develop stabilized equal-order finite element methods based on momentum-residual stabilization and local projection stabilization of the pore pressure. For the discrete problem, we establish mesh-uniform stability and well-posedness on sufficiently fine meshes via an a priori stability estimate and a Schatz-type compactness argument, without invoking discrete $T$-coercivity. Optimal-order a priori error estimates are derived in the natural energy norm. We also develop systematic selection principles for the stabilization parameters. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate stable approximations for heterogeneous low-permeability media and anatomically realistic brain geometries relevant to magnetic resonance elastography.

papers.title: Lax Centers and Monoidal Functors for Comodule Categories Associated with Acyclic Quivers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the monoidal category of finite-dimensional right comodules over the path algebra $\Bbbk Q$ of a finite acyclic quiver $Q$, equipped with the weak bialgebra structure in which every path is grouplike. We prove that the lax center of this category is monoidally equivalent to $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\Bbbk}(Q)$, the category of finite-dimensional representations of $Q$. We also classify all $\Bbbk$-linear strong monoidal functors between any two such comodule categories, and all monoidal natural transformations between them. For the right adjoint of such a functor, we determine when the left or right projection formula holds. When both projection formulas hold, this adjoint will induce a functor between the lax centers, and we describe the induced functor explicitly on quiver representations.

papers.title: Rateless Coding for Efficient Model Broadcast in Federated Learning
papers.authors: Zijun Qin, Zuolin Jin, Jingxuan Huang, Ming Xiao, Xianhao Chen
papers.abstract: Model broadcast in federated learning (FL) with wireless channels faces significant challenges due to large model sizes and heterogeneous, unreliable channel conditions. While rateless coding has been widely adopted in modern broadcast communications to handle channel heterogeneity, its potential for model broadcast in FL remains largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we propose a joint source-channel coding scheme based on rateless coding to improve the robustness and efficiency of downlink model broadcast in FL. Specifically, we establish a rigorous convergence analysis of FL to inform the rateless code and quantization design under noisy downlink channel conditions. Moreover, by observing that the iterative process of FL naturally provides prior information about client updates, we leverage client-side local models as conditional prior information to aid the decoding process, thereby reducing transmission costs. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our rateless coding scheme significantly enhances downlink model broadcast efficiency in FL, while retaining comparable training accuracies for both homogeneous and heterogeneous data distributions.

papers.title: Latroids on Young's Lattice
papers.abstract: Latroids are a generalization of matroids and polymatroids, given by a submodular rank function on a modular lattice. We study integer-valued latroids whose length function is the height of a finite modular lattice, without assuming that the lattice is complemented. We show that their cyclic flats form a lattice and, together with their ranks, determine the rank function. We also characterize which families of lattice elements, together with prescribed rank values, occur as the cyclic flats of such latroids. We then focus on principal intervals of Young's lattice, where we classify the latroids with modular rank functions and characterize the sparse paving ones. Finally, we attach a latroid to every Ferrers diagram rank-metric code and show that its cyclic flats, together with their ranks, determine the dimensions of all shortenings to Young subdiagrams.

papers.title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
papers.abstract: For a real polynomial of degree $n$ with $n$ distinct real roots, assume that no two different nonconstant derivatives, including the polynomial itself, share a root. Recording the derivative orders of all roots from left to right gives a Rolle word. We present an exact, computer-assisted classification in degree six: $2706$ words are realizable, with a word and its reversal counted separately. Starting from $33592$ formal interlacing words, published necessary restrictions leave $13404$ candidates. Integer realization certificates and $53$ exact exclusion stages classify every candidate. The surviving set agrees exactly with the set of certified realizations. All verification uses integer and rational arithmetic. The accompanying code, certificates, proof notes, and per-word exclusion ledger make the computation reproducible. The result concerns degree six; it does not resolve the classification problem in arbitrary degree or count connected components of coefficient space. Most of the mathematical development, code, certificates, and initial manuscript were generated using ChatGPT under the author's direction. No independent human audit of the complete proof chain has yet been completed.

papers.title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.

papers.title: The periodic Short-Pulse equation by the Riemann-Hilbert problem approach
papers.authors: Iryna Karpenko, Dmitry Shepelsky, Gerald Teschl
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate a Riemann--Hilbert problem framework -- based on the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) -- for the Short Pulse equation posed on a periodic domain. Under the stated spectral and reconstruction regularity assumptions, we show that a local solution of the periodic initial-value problem can be reconstructed from the solution of a suitably defined Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose jump data are explicitly characterized by spectral functions associated with the initial condition.

papers.title: Every rank-three matroid is Z-Rayleigh
papers.abstract: We prove that every matroid of rank or corank at most three is $Z$-Rayleigh: its multivariate Tutte polynomial satisfies the Rayleigh inequalities for every positive weighting and every parameter $0<q\le1$. This settles a conjecture of Mani and answers the rank-$3$ spanning-correlation question of Cocks and the correlated-matroid question of Semple and Welsh. For simple rank-$3$ matroids, we obtain an explicit decomposition of each spanning-set Rayleigh difference into the corresponding basis Rayleigh difference, positively weighted squares, and a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. A second identity compares the normalized multivariate Tutte Rayleigh difference with $(1-q)^2$ times the spanning-set difference, with a remainder of the form $q(1-q)R(q,x)$, where $R$ has nonnegative coefficients. The proof uses the bipartite incidence graph of the lines through two fixed elements and Wagner's theorem that rank-$3$ matroids are basis-Rayleigh. The rank bound is sharp, since a rank-four matroid can fail even the basis Rayleigh inequalities.

papers.title: Directional maximal functions along algebraic curves
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal operator over line segments in $N$ arbitrary directions on a real algebraic curve of degree $D$ in $\mathbb R^n$ has $L^2$ operator norm at most $C_{n,\varepsilon}D^{C_n}N^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, with $C_n$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Combined with polynomial partitioning, this gives the sharp bound $N^{\frac14}$, up to a polylogarithmic factor, for $N$ arbitrary directions in $\mathbb R^3$. The first main ingredient is a new quantitative strengthening of the property that the curve crosses each affine hyperplane at most $D$ times. This condition controls the overlap of variable-width neighborhoods of hyperplanes. The width attached to each direction is a small multiple of its distance to the osculating hyperplane at an endpoint of its arc. The problem is projectively invariant, and a projective almost orthogonality principle turns the overlap control into the $L^2$ bound. The second main ingredient, building on the complex cellular preparation of Binyamini and Novikov, is a new effective decomposition of algebraic curves. Up to $D^{C_n}$ points, the curve is covered by $D^{C_n}$ arcs whose coordinates, in a suitable parametrization and projective frame, are monomials with distinct exponents times nearly constant units. In these charts we verify the quantitative crossing condition with polynomial dependence on $D$. The framework also applies to nonalgebraic curves with doubling Frenet curvature measures. Consequences include local Sobolev maximal estimates along measurable vector fields with values in an algebraic curve, and the same bounds, up to a logarithmic factor, for directional Calder\'on--Zygmund operators.

papers.title: Integers with many divisors in a dyadic interval
papers.authors: Kevin Ford, Mikhail R. Gabdullin, Kyle Pratt
papers.abstract: We find the correct order of magnitude for the number of $n\leq x$ having at least $r$ divisors in the interval $(y,2y]$, uniformly in a wide range of the parameters $x,y,r$.

papers.title: Strictly Deza Graphs among the Prime Graphs of Solvable Groups
papers.abstract: We study strictly Deza graphs that occur as prime graphs of finite solvable groups and admit a partition into two cliques. Using Gruber's characterization of the prime graphs of finite solvable groups, we relate this problem to bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs. We first show that a non-complete regular graph with a partition into two cliques has equal parts. For a graph of diameter two, writing $F$ for its $c$-regular complement on $2m$ vertices, the Deza condition is equivalent to every component of $F$ being a bipartite $(0,2)$-graph. Within this class, strongly regular graphs occur exactly when $c=1$; we give elementary descriptions for $c=2$ and $c=3$, and translate the existing classification of bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs of valency at most eight. A counting argument yields $m\ge1+c(c-1)/2$, with equality corresponding to biplanes. These observations recover the ten feasible parameter pairs for $m\le7$ without enumeration and give infinite families of strictly Deza prime graphs. We also exhibit a known eight-vertex strictly Deza graph whose complement is triangle-free and three-colourable but not bipartite, showing that clique cover number three occurs.

papers.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
papers.abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.

papers.title: Slicing a Doughnut at Random
papers.abstract: Choose a random plane that hits a solid torus. How likely is the slice to be a single disk, and how fat should the doughnut be to make this as likely as possible? Answering requires saying precisely what a "random plane" is. We explain this from scratch, first for random lines in the plane and then for random planes in space, and then solve the problem with nothing more than calculus. Along the way we meet a two-dimensional cousin of the problem (the doughnut's shadow) and two tempting wrong turns. One wrong turn appeared in print; it turns out to be a correct solution of the two-dimensional cousin. The other was the author's own first attempt, which luckily stayed in a drawer.

papers.title: Controlling avalanche sizes in the Abelian sandpile model
papers.authors: Maike C. de Jongh, Antal A. J\'arai, Richard J. Boucherie, M. N. M. van Lieshout
papers.abstract: The Abelian sandpile model is a classical framework for studying large cascading events, such as those arising in models of forest fires and earthquakes. This work studies the control of such avalanches through the targeted removal of sand grains. We formulate this sequential control problem as an average-cost Markov decision process in which, before each grain addition, a controller may remove a sand grain from a selected vertex. The objective is to balance the long-run expected avalanche size against the cost of intervention. We analyze local intervention policies, which remove grains from a prescribed set of vertices whenever possible, and establish structural results for the recurrent classes and stationary distributions of the induced Markov chains. When the intervention set satisfies a property called topple-freeness, we sharpen these results, derive expressions for the gain and bias functions, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality on general finite graphs. Finally, we apply the general theory to several specific graph classes and obtain a complete characterization of optimal policies on the one-dimensional lattice, the complete graph and the star graph for every value of the intervention cost.

papers.title: Gluing Geometric Chains Of Manifolds And Orbifolds With Corners
papers.abstract: Geometric chains are formal combinations of smooth maps from compact oriented manifolds or orbifolds with corners. In earlier work the author showed that, modulo a relation D that kills degenerate chains, they compute rational singular homology. We show that D can be replaced by a gluing relation, which identifies a chain with the sum of its restrictions to finitely many pieces whenever its source is glued from these pieces along whole codimension-one faces. With this relation the comparison map from singular homology is an isomorphism in all degrees for compact polyhedra and smooth manifolds without boundary, with rational and with integer coefficients. Unlike D, the gluing relation is defined through the sources alone, and chain-level identities such as the equivalence of a degree d covering with d times its base, which fails modulo D, and the correction terms of the chain map from a Morse complex, which are degenerate modulo D, become gluing relations. The proof is axiomatic; injectivity comes from integration or dual cells, surjectivity from cutting along regular levels, where the cut of a gluing relation is again one, and at the point we use Whitehead triangulations of manifolds with corners subordinate to their corner strata. The gluing relation, read on underlying spaces, also suffices for orbifold sources, with integer coefficients modulo classes with an orientation reversing automorphism, and for effective orbifold targets.

papers.title: Constructing option portfolio
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of constructing a portfolio composed of a set of financial options. We present a mixed-integer linear program. We apply our approach to index options for the S&P 500.

papers.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
papers.abstract:
We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture.
  Our proof studies escape of mass using dynamics on the boundary of the Chabauty compactification of the space of lattices, together with averaging operators defined by leafwise measures along horospherical subgroups.

papers.title: Hypercyclic Algebras for Weighted Double Shifts
papers.authors: Xiang Chen, Wei Wang, Ze-hua Zhou
papers.abstract: Building on the approach of Bayart, Costa J\'unior and Papathanasiou, we establish a Baire criterion for possibly noncommuting operator pairs to support hypercyclic algebras, with hypercyclicity defined through all finite compositions.We then study weighted double backward shifts under different multiplications and topologies.We characterize the existence of hypercyclic algebras for coordinatewise multiplication on sequence algebras admitting a continuous norm and, separately, on $\omega^2=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N_0^2}$ with the product topology.For the noncommutative triangular product induced by upper triangular matrix multiplication, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of dense hypercyclic algebras on $\omega^2$.In this setting, their existence is equivalent to that of one freely generated by countably infinitely many elements.Finally, we exhibit a pair on a fixed Fr\'echet space that supports a dense hypercyclic algebra for coordinatewise multiplication and a nonzero hypercyclic algebra, but no dense one, for the triangular product.

papers.title: A note on equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion
papers.abstract: In this note, we introduce an equivariant version of twisted holomorphic analytic torsion for the twisted Dolbeault complex on a complex manifold equipped with an action of a compact Lie group. Our construction is motivated by Ray and Singer's holomorphic analytic torsion, by the equivariant analytic torsion developed for elliptic complexes with group actions, notably in the work of Donnelly and later in the holomorphic setting by Bismut, and by Mathai and Wu's twisted analytic torsion for the twisted de Rham complex. Using pseudodifferential operators and the equivariant noncommutative residue, we define the equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion. We also state its variation formulas under changes of the metric and of the twisting element, and present its functorial properties.

papers.title: Sampled resolvents of $C_0$-semigroups: aliasing and sharp rates on the Crandall-Pazy scale
papers.abstract: For a $C_0$-semigroup $(S_t)$ with generator $B$, sampling the Laplace integral $(\lambda-B)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}S_t\,dt$ on the grid $T\mathbb{N}$ gives $Q_T=T(I-e^{-\lambda T}S_T)^{-1}$, the impulse-invariant discretization of the resolvent. The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $\lambda-2\pi in/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. Our main result is a sharp scale of rates for the trapezoid correction $Q_T-\frac T2I$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $\alpha\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/\alpha})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^\alpha)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{\alpha+\theta})$ on the interpolation space of order $\theta$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+\alpha})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $\alpha$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda$. This interpolates between unitary groups with unbounded generator ($\alpha=0$, no convergence in norm) and analytic semigroups ($\alpha=1$), and every exponent is attained. For smooth data an Euler--Maclaurin expansion justifies Romberg extrapolation. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations. Experiments, including a structurally damped string whose semigroup is of Gevrey class, confirm the rates.

papers.title: A high-order recombination algorithm with adaptive scale selection for weak approximation of stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract:
High-order recombination keeps weak approximation trees of diffusions small
  by a moment-preserving reduction of the measure on each patch of nodes.
  The weighted Litterer--Lyons (WLL) test of Ninomiya and Shinozaki
  sets the patch scale using a scalar \(\lambda>0\) chosen
  beforehand, whose appropriate value depends on coordinate units.
  First, the anisotropically weighted Litterer--Lyons (AWLL) rule
  selects the scale during recombination within a bounded factor of
  the measured increment amplitude. On a fixed set of nodes, expanding
  coordinate units leaves the AWLL patch-count bound unchanged but raises
  the WLL lower bound as a power until saturation. In Heston and shifted Stochastic-Alpha-Beta-Rho (sSABR)
  systems with initial price or forward rate 100, AWLL reduces
  the terminal supports of WLL with \(\lambda=1\) by factors of 137 and
  1488 at comparable errors, but enlarges them at smaller Heston initial
  prices. Second, \(\lambda\) is extended to a positive definite matrix
  with a joint error bound for prices and sensitivities, a bound on
  the gain of its shape, and patch-count bounds. Third, the elimination stage of batched basis
  exchange requires \(O(J)\)
  arithmetic operations for \(J\) nodes at fixed moment rank and panel width, against
  \(\Theta(J^{3})\) for the direct kernel update of Ninomiya and Shinozaki.

papers.title: Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
papers.authors: Katianny Rosa Freitas, Ant\'onio Mart\'inez, Jo\~ao Paulo dos Santos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as {\phi}-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions {\phi}, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions {\phi} we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.

papers.title: Strongly reducible operators in factors
papers.authors: Minghui Ma, Rui Shi, Jianming Yang, Shanshan Yang
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a factor acting on a separable complex Hilbert space. For every operator $T$ in $\mathcal M$ with dense generalized kernel and $T^2\ne 0$, we characterize the strong reducibility of $T$ relative to $\mathcal M$ based on a $3\times 3$ asymmetric matrix representation of $T$. As applications, we obtain criteria for the strong reducibility of algebraic operators in finite factors and type $\mathrm{III}$ factors. We also prove that every Hilbert space operator with an infinite-dimensional multicyclic direct summand is similar to an irreducible operator.

papers.title: Determination of a Bi-periodic Refractive Index for the Helmholtz Equation
papers.abstract: We investigate an inverse problem for the Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional half-space with a biperiodic medium above a sound-soft plane. We establish the uniqueness of a real-valued, bounded, biperiodic refractive index that depends only on the horizontal variables using spectral techniques. %The frequency and quasiperiodicity parameter are fixed. An orthogonality identity is first derived from near-field measurements. By constructing suitable separated solutions, this identity is reduced to relations involving eigenfunctions of two-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. To recover Fourier information from these relations, we project horizontal plane waves onto suitable high-energy spectral subspaces, obtaining finite combinations of eigenfunctions that approximate the plane waves with a quantified error. Combining these approximations with the orthogonality identity, we show that all Fourier coefficients of the difference of two refractive indices vanish, thereby establishing the desired uniqueness.

papers.title: Covering numbers of metric spaces
papers.abstract: We propose and provide evidence for the following conjecture: the covering number of a product of metric spaces with the sum metric is greater than or equal to the product of their covering numbers. This generalizes Vizing's conjecture in graph theory. We prove an infinitesimal version of the conjecture for Finsler manifolds of dimension at least six.

papers.title: Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
papers.abstract: In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Representation Theory and the Algebraic K-Theory of Geometric Fields
papers.abstract: We apply a derived completion construction for commutative ring spectra to give a description of the K-theory spectrum of a geometric field F (i.e. containing an algebraically closed subfield $k$) of characteristic zero purely in terms of the representation theory of its absolute Galois group $G_F$. A result that follows is that the l-adically completed Milnor K-theory of F is isomorphic to the derived completion of the representation ring of $G_F$. The main result, from which this follows, is that $K(F)$ completed at l is equivalent to the derived completion of the K-theory of the category of finite dimensional representations of $G_F$ in $k$.

papers.title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
papers.abstract: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Pl\"ucker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.

papers.title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
papers.abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $\kappa$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(\mu) := \min \{ \lambda \in \mathrm{card} \colon \mu \leq 2^{\lambda} \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $\mu$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(\kappa)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists \kappa \in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

papers.title: Categorical orbifold theory
papers.authors: Chongying Dong, Siu-Hung Ng, Li Ren, Feng Xu
papers.abstract: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.

papers.title: Metriplectic Lotka--Volterra systems with noise:interactions invisible at stationarity, visible in time
papers.authors: J. A. Capit\'an, A. Meg\'ias, C. Sard\'on
papers.abstract: We show that a Lotka--Volterra system with an interior equilibrium admits a metriplectic structure, with a Volterra function $V_C$ as energy and an entropy variable for the environment, if and only if Volterra's dissipativity condition $CA+A^{\top}C\le0$ holds, and we construct it explicitly with a log-canonical Poisson bivector. Adding noise through the fluctuation--dissipation relation of stochastic GENERIC yields multiplicative environmental noise, with covariance fixed by the symmetric part of $AC^{-1}$, whose stationary law is an explicit Gibbs measure: a product of independent Gamma distributions. Unlike known Gibbs measures for stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems, this holds for nonsymmetric interactions, predator--prey included. The stationary law determines only the equilibrium and $C/k$: every interaction matrix in an open cone of dimension $n^2$, in particular any Poisson part, produces with its compatible noise the same law as uncoupled stochastic logistic equations. Gamma-distributed, uncorrelated abundance fluctuations, as observed in microbial communities, are therefore no evidence of absence of interactions. The interactions are, however, visible in time: the zero-lag derivative of the log-abundance covariance equals $A(C/k)^{-1}$, and its antisymmetric part is the Poisson part, which carries all the stationary entropy production, computed in closed form. Finally, for general noise we prove an exact Lyapunov-type identity $AK+K^\top A^\top+Q=0$ for $K=\mathrm{Cov}(x,\log x)$ at any stationary solution. It implies that the populations are independent if and only if the noise is metriplectically compatible, and gives an explicit lower bound on interspecies cross-covariances in terms of the distance of $Q$ to the compatible family. Simulations of a predator--prey model show that the bound is nearly sharp.

papers.title: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $\Delta(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r \Delta(r)=\Theta(\sqrt{N})=\Theta(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum. The normalized peaks $d_k=\max_{r\in R_k}\Delta(r)/2^{k/2}$ oscillate between values near 1/2 and values that approach, but do not exceed, 1. The data suggest $\liminf d_k=1/2$ and $\limsup d_k\le 1$. We conjecture the same square-root law for the exhaustive maximum, with those normalized envelopes. A Brownian-bridge heuristic accounts for the square-root scale. The same profiles do not place the recorded maximizer at mid-path: after folding by the complement identity $\Delta(M-r)=\Delta(r)$, the median of $\min(\rho^*_k,1-\rho^*_k)$ is 0.35, and several $k$ (notably 16 and 28) peak on a short window. Mid-horizon $\Delta$ remains a large fraction of the peak, so the square-root scale can still come from a Brownian-bridge envelope. The same range has two readings of the starting offset: a pairing fragment in serial-knockout scheduling, and a change to the plaintext on an LFSR orbit. The location of the maximizer is not part of the conjecture. Open questions that separate the conjecture from a theorem are listed.

papers.title: Calder\'on-Zygmund estimates and their failure for PDE with linear growth
papers.abstract: We investigate when Calder\'on-Zygmund estimates hold for PDEs of the type \[ \operatorname{div}(A(\nabla u)) = \operatorname{div}(F) \] where $A: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is a continuous map with linear growth. We show that, under natural assumptions, $L^p$-Calder\'on-Zygmund estimates hold for all $p \in (1,\infty)$ if and only if $v \mapsto \lim_{t \to \infty} A(tv)/t$ is linear and non-degenerate.

papers.title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

papers.title: Base Change Of Local Fundamental Group Schemes
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $\pi^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $\pi^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow \pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.

papers.title: Asymptotic behaviors of solutions to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equations with Hardy potential
papers.authors: Jungang Li, Yansheng Shen, Zeming Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider positive weak solutions $u\in\mathcal{D}^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equation with Hardy potential $(-\Delta_p)^s u-\mu\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{ps}}=u^{p_s^{*}-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $N\geqslant 2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying $ps<N$, $p_s^{*}=\frac{Np}{N-ps}$ and $\mu\in(0,\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p})$, $\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p}$ denotes the sharp constant of the fractional Hardy inequality. By means of a suitable comparison principle for weak subsolutions and supersolutions of the equations $(-\Delta_p)^sf=\big(\frac{\mu}{|x|^{ps}}+a(x)\big)f^{p-1}$ on general open set $\Omega$, with nonzero exterior data and $a\in L^{\frac{N}{ps}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$, combined with careful constructions of the weak subsolutions and supersolutions, we prove that every positive weak solution $u$ of the above problem satisfies $C^{-1}\leqslant|x|^{\mu_1}(1+|x|)^{\mu_2-\mu_1}u(x)\leqslant C$ for a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $\mu_1<\mu_2$ are the two roots of the indicial equation associated with the Hardy operator and $C\in[1,\infty)$ depends on $u$. Also, we show that the constant $C$ cannot be chosen to depend only on $N$, $s$, $p$ and $\mu$.

papers.title: Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator
papers.abstract:
We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator.
  Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update. We establish existence using Brouwer degree, without requiring global convexity, and reduce uniqueness to uniqueness of the corresponding zero.
  Under suitable differentiability and spectral-gap assumptions, we derive a finite-dimensional criterion for local exponential convergence of both the physical distribution and controller parameters at sufficiently small positive learning rates. The criterion involves the Jacobian of the reduced equation, computed using linear response to include the effect of controller-induced changes in the invariant distribution. The asymptotic slow relaxation time scales inversely with the learning rate.
  We rigorously verify the assumptions and apply the theory to a noisy Duffing-type system with a neural residual compensator, providing a nontrivial example of adaptive control with provable existence, uniqueness, and local stability of an adaptive equilibrium. Numerical experiments illustrate statistical feedback and the role of time-scale separation.

papers.title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
papers.abstract: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

papers.title: Meridional ranks of iterated Whitehead doubles
papers.authors: Honghao Gao, Shijie Gu, Zhenkun Li, Jian Wang
papers.abstract: We prove that every iterated untwisted Whitehead double of a nontrivial two-bridge knot satisfies the meridional rank conjecture. More precisely, for such a knot $K$ and every $N\geq0$, the augmentation rank, meridional rank, and bridge number of $\operatorname{Wh}^N(K)$ are all $2^{N+1}$. We use microlocal sheaf theory and a doubling construction to produce a lower bound for the meridional rank of the Whitehead double, assuming the peripheral data satisfy suitable conditions. For two-bridge knots, the required curves arise from ideal points detecting nonzero boundary slopes. In contrast, the ordinary group rank of an $N$-fold Whitehead double is at most the rank of the companion group plus $N$. We also give a non-example when the doubling construction does not work -- the first Whitehead double of the square knot has augmentation rank at most 5, whereas its meridional rank and bridge number are 6.

papers.title: Newton's Method and Policy Iterations for Viscous Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
papers.authors: Diogo A. Gomes, Xiaoqin Guo, Yeoneung Kim, Hung V. Tran, Yuming P. Zhang
papers.abstract: We study Newton's method for the Cauchy problem for viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations with Hamiltonians that need not be convex. Each Newton step solves a linear parabolic equation obtained by linearizing the equation at the current iterate. We prove that the iterates converge geometrically in \(L^\infty\) from any initial guess satisfying the initial condition, and quadratically in the parabolic H\"older space \(C^{2+\alpha,1+\alpha/2}\) from initial guesses close to the solution. When the Hamiltonian admits a control representation, the Newton iterates coincide with those of classical policy iteration, which therefore inherits both convergence rates. We extend the local quadratic convergence to uniformly parabolic fully nonlinear equations. For small viscosity, we introduce a Nash--Moser variant that smooths the iterate and the residual in space, and we give a convergence criterion with constants independent of the viscosity. Finally, we show how computable residuals certify the error of inexact Newton corrections computed with physics-informed neural networks.

papers.title: Artin-style characterizations of the multiple gamma and sine functions
papers.abstract: We extend Artin's characterizations of the gamma function to the multiple setting by means of the Kubert identity. We obtain uniqueness theorems for positive continuous solutions of a difference equation $G(z + 1) = \alpha(z)G(z)$ that also satisfy an Artin-type multiplication formula, remaining within the class of continuous functions under a modest initial condition. The results apply in particular to the Barnes multiple gamma functions and the Kurokawa multiple sine functions.

papers.title: Density of periodic measures on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with prescribed arithmetic information
papers.authors: Lifan Guan, Chengyang Wu, Weisheng Wu
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be the diagonal flow on the modular space $X_2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_f$ be the set of positive square-free numbers, which is identified with the set of all real quadratic fields via the natural map $d\mapsto \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any finite subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f$, there exists a density-zero set $B\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f\setminus A$ such that the set of all $F$-periodic measures with associated quadratic fields from $B$ is dense in the set of all $F$-invariant measures on $X_2$.

papers.title: Algebraic coarsening of hierarchical splines with guaranteed error control
papers.authors: Marcelo Actis, Silvano Figueroa, Eduardo M. Garau
papers.abstract: We present a purely algebraic coarsening operator for hierarchical spline spaces, obtained by inverting locally the refinement matrix that relates the coarsened basis to the current one. Only the B-splines that interact with the coarsened region are involved, so that a coarsening step reduces to one small least-squares problem followed by explicit corrections of the surviving coefficients, without mass matrices or numerical quadrature. The operator is a left inverse of the refinement matrix, hence exact whenever the fine spline belongs to the coarse space, and leaves the spline unchanged away from the coarsened region. The residual of the least-squares problem bounds the $L^\infty$-error with no unknown constants and is available before the mesh is modified, which yields an adaptive multi-level algorithm that guarantees a prescribed tolerance. The construction carries over to truncated hierarchical B-splines, where the corrections disappear. In numerical experiments, the bound is sharp within an order of magnitude, the local transfer is nearly as accurate as a global $L^2$-projection, and much of the refinement left behind a moving front is removed without degrading the solution.

papers.title: A posteriori space error estimates for the finite element approximation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations based on the variational multiscale framework
papers.authors: Javad Sekhavati, Ignacio Mart\'inez-Su\'arez, Sheraz Ahmed Khan, Joan Baiges, Guillermo Hauke, Ramon Codina
papers.abstract: This study introduces a novel a posteriori space error estimator derived within the variational multiscale (VMS) framework for the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this framework, the continuous problem is decomposed into coarse and fine scales. The fine scale, often referred to as the sub-grid scale (SGS), is modeled as proportional to the component of the residual orthogonal to the finite element (FE) space. This modeled SGS then serves as a reliable error estimator. Specifically, the approach employs a scaled norm of the SGSs as an a posteriori error estimate, evaluated within the stabilized norm associated with the problem. This methodology was previously applied to the stationary convection-diffusion-reaction equation (Codina et al., 2025) and is now extended to the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. The accuracy and robustness of the proposed space error estimator are assessed through a series of numerical experiments on both manufactured and benchmark incompressible flow problems. Additionally, its performance is compared in selected cases with the space error estimator proposed by Irisarri and Hauke (2021).

papers.title: Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes
papers.authors: Alexander von Bank, Oliver Griebel, Eike-Manuel Edelmann, Norbert Wehn, Laurent Schmalen
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.

papers.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.

papers.title: HKT-Einstein metrics on circle bundles
papers.abstract: We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.

papers.title: A posteriori error estimates for the bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with dynamic boundary conditions
papers.abstract: This paper develops reliable residual-based a posteriori error estimators for the full discretization of a bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with a two-parameter family of dynamic boundary conditions on a curved domain. The main novelty are theoretically justified computable temporal, coarsening and geometric error estimators. The numerical method combines a linear bulk--surface finite element method in space and a linearly implicit backward Euler method in time. Based on the derived error indicators, a space--time adaptive algorithm is proposed and numerical experiments illustrate and complement the theoretical result.

papers.title: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
papers.authors: Christian B\"ohning, Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer, Alena Pirutka, Zhijia Zhang
papers.abstract: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.

papers.title: Energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness for the anisotropic Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with only horizontal dissipation in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{R}^2_+$. The combination of the missing directional regularity and the influence of the boundary presents an essential difficulty for the pressure estimates. We circumvent this difficulty by establishing an extension theorem for the weak formulation, based on the divergence-free condition and the homogeneous impermeability boundary condition. A key feature of this extension principle is that no boundary condition is required for the tangential velocity component. Consequently, every weak solution in the natural energy class on $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ admits a reflection extension that is a weak solution of the corresponding whole-space problem on $\mathbb{R}^2$. This extension allows us to transfer the energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness properties established by Demmel and Wiedemann \cite{E-W} to the half-plane setting. In particular, we prove the energy equality for weak solutions in the natural energy class and establish weak--strong uniqueness under the corresponding additional regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Ideal polyhedral surfaces with prescribed cusped hyperbolic metric and their degeneration
papers.authors: Wai Yeung Lam, Carl O. R. Lutz
papers.abstract: Rivin showed that every cusped hyperbolic metric on a punctured sphere is uniquely realized by a convex ideal polyhedron in hyperbolic space with possible degeneration. We consider the analogous problem for cusped hyperbolic metrics on a punctured surface of positive genus: locally convex ideal polyhedral surfaces in hyperbolic space. Each such surface determines a complex projective structure on the underlying closed surface. With a cusped hyperbolic metric $h$ prescribed, we investigate the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ of such ideal polyhedral realizations and their possible degeneration. Particularly in the case of tori, we show that the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and that the induced map to Teichm\"uller space of the closed torus is a $C^1$-embedding. This map extends to a bijection from the closure of $\mathcal{P}(h)$ onto the whole Teichm\"uller space, where the added points are degenerate surfaces. This is dual to the Kojima-Mizushima-Tan conjecture about circle patterns on closed surfaces with complex projective structures.

papers.title: Trust-region high-index saddle dynamics for ill-conditioned saddle-point computation
papers.authors: Guanghua Ji, Longjing Li, Zhen Xu, Jianyuan Yin
papers.abstract: We propose a trust-region high-index saddle dynamics (TRHiSD) framework for computing high-index saddle points in ill-conditioned problems. To address the deterioration of high-index saddle dynamics caused by inappropriate step sizes and search directions, we exploit its intrinsic local min--max structure and construct separate trust-region subproblems on the maximization and minimization subspaces to adapt the two trust-region radii to different local curvature scales. Under suitable assumptions and with exact spectral subspaces, we prove local linear convergence of the Cauchy-point variant and local quadratic convergence of the Newton-step variant. Numerical experiments on modified Rosenbrock functions are consistent with the predicted convergence rates. For the Landau--de Gennes model, a TRHiSD variant using a truncated conjugate-gradient step for the minimization subproblem substantially reduces the outer-iteration count and the wall-clock time in the tested cases.

papers.title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
papers.abstract: We study a three-dimensional dynamic thermoplastic system with a temperature-dependent convex yield set whose deviatoric section may collapse completely at a finite temperature. The underlying constitutive model is rate-independent Prandtl-Reuss perfect plasticity, without Kelvin-Voigt viscosity, hardening, or a safe-load condition. We construct global approximation-generated relaxed entropy-energy states by a one-parameter Temam-Norton-Hoff-Galerkin scheme with an undiscretized heat equation and untruncated plastic heat production. The logarithmic temperature is strongly compact in $L^2(0,T;L^q(\Omega))$ for every $q<6$ and in $L^p((0,T)\times\Omega)$ for every $p<8/3$. An entropy-weighted work estimate yields convergence of the overstress at rate $O(\sqrt{\log n/n})$ in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and identifies stress admissibility. The constitutive limit comprises a distributional plastic balance, finite support-weighted measures, and compact-fibre lifts carrying exact normality and maximum plastic work. A locally finite lift on the positive-radius fibres unifies the level-restricted limits at every continuity level. At the macroscopic level, however, the available compactness does not identify a canonical stress-plastic-flow pairing. Moreover, an explicit smooth state satisfying the intrinsic relaxed balance conditions shows that these conditions do not imply macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality. In the fully collapsed regime, an energy-entropy rigidity argument determines the evolution and yields approximation-generated examples in which the plastic flow need not be a finite measure or the displacement need not retain its full boundary trace. Thermal concentration and plastic entropy production remain explicit throughout.

papers.title: Shuffles of permutations in cycle form
papers.authors: Ron M. Adin, Sergi Elizalde, Ira M. Gessel, Yuval Roichman
papers.abstract:
We study a variation of the shuffle operation on permutations, which acts on their cycle structure instead of their one-line notation. Given two permutations $\sigma\in S_k$ and $\tau\in S_{n-k}$, the $\textit{shuffle-by-cycle}$ $\sigma \mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c \tau$ is the set of all permutations in $S_n$ whose set of cycles can be separated into two disjoint subsets: one whose standardization is $\sigma$, and one whose standardization is $\tau$. One can think of the sets $\sigma \mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c \tau$ as refinements of conjugacy classes.
  We show that if $\sigma$ and $\tau$ have no order-isomorphic cycles, then the descent set has the same distribution, over the set $\sigma \mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c \tau$ of shuffles-by-cycle, as over the set $\sigma \mathbin{\sqcup\!\sqcup} \tau$ of standard shuffles; our proof is bijective. This result no longer holds when $\sigma$ and $\tau$ have order-isomorphic cycles. For an arbitrary shuffle-by-cycle, we provide a description of the distribution of the descent set in terms of plethysm of quasisymmetric functions. For the set $\sigma \mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c \sigma \subset S_{2n}$, where $\sigma$ is an $n$-cycle, we deduce explicit generating functions for the bivariate distribution of descent number and major index.

papers.title: Intersections, Equations, and Singularities of Lissajous Varieties
papers.abstract: Lissajous varieties are affine algebraic varieties parametrized by sine and cosine functions. They generalize algebraic Lissajous curves in the plane to higher dimensions by applying a component-wise trigonometric map to a rational affine subspace and are motivated by applications in dynamical systems (Kuramoto model) and semidefinite optimization (graph elliptopes). We establish several algebraic and geometric properties of Lissajous varieties. In particular, we show that intersections of Lissajous varieties are finite unions of such varieties and describe them explicitly. We investigate algebraic properties of the defining polynomials of Lissajous hypersurfaces and describe the singular locus of Lissajous varieties.

papers.title: The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle
papers.abstract: Bonnefont, Rajam\"aki and Vargas conjectured that, for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from a single real Gaussian field, the Fourier dimension at $\alpha+i\beta$ equals the dimension of the real chaos at $\alpha$ minus $\beta^2$. We prove the conjecture on the circle throughout their stated parameter range. For the canonical holomorphic family, the identity holds on one event of probability one for all $\gamma=\alpha+i\beta$ in the union of the open unit disk and the region $1/\sqrt2<|\alpha|<\sqrt2$, $|\alpha|+|\beta|<\sqrt2$. For each fixed parameter on the conjecture's sloping boundary, where $1<|\alpha|<\sqrt2$ and $|\alpha|+|\beta|=\sqrt2$, the Fourier coefficients decay at a logarithmic rate almost surely and the Fourier dimension is zero. For nonzero interior parameters with $|\alpha|\ne1/\sqrt2$, the critical Sobolev index is half the Fourier dimension minus $1/2$. The chaos fails to belong to the corresponding space when $|\alpha|<1/\sqrt2$ and belongs to it when $|\alpha|>1/\sqrt2$. For $1/\sqrt2<|\alpha|<\sqrt2$ and $|\beta|\le\sqrt2-|\alpha|$, we bound the Fourier coefficients at the decay power predicted by the dimension formula, up to logarithmic factors. For $0<|\gamma|<1$ and $\alpha^2<1/2$, the measures obtained by multiplying the squared modulus of the smoothed chaos by $\epsilon^{|\gamma|^2}$ converge weakly almost surely along $\epsilon=e^{-m}$, uniformly on compact parameter sets, to explicit multiples of the real chaos at $2\alpha$.

papers.title: Exceptional parameters in the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem
papers.abstract: The Erd\H os similarity conjecture says that for every infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$, there exists a set $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure which does not contain any affine copy of $x + tA$ of $A$ (with $t \neq 0$). Kolountzakis proved that for every infinite $A$, there exists $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure so that the exceptional sets $D_E(A)$ of scales $t$, and $\mathcal E_E(A)$ of affine maps $(x,t)$, for which $x+tA\subseteq E$, are both Lebesgue null. We show that these exceptional parameter sets are small in two finer senses. First, given any countable family of Fourier decay rates, a single $E$ can be constructed so that $D_E(A)$ is null with respect to every measure whose Fourier transform decays at one of these rates. Consequently, there are compact sets $K$ of measure arbitrarily close to $1$ for which $D_K(A)$ and $\mathcal E_K(A)$ have modified Fourier dimension zero. Second, we give a criterion, depending both on the growth of a gauge function $h$ and on the gaps between elements of lacunary sequences in $A$, which guarantees that $\mathcal H^h(D_E(A))=0$ for gauges with $h(u)/u\to\infty$, as well as a similar result for $\mathcal E_K(A)$. For sets such as $A = \{1/n!\}$ and $A = \{e^{-n^q}\}$, this yields explicit gauges of the form $h(u) = u\exp((\log 1/u)^\theta)$ with $0 < \theta < 1$.

papers.title: Skew Zero Forcing Matroids
papers.authors: Dennis Hall, Simon Pfeil, Jesse Taylor
papers.abstract: Matroid theory and skew zero forcing (SZF) in graphs are both topics of mathematical interest, but very little is known about their overlap. When a matroid arises from a graph in the traditional way, the edges of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. However, the SZF color change rule for graphs can be viewed as a closure operator on the vertices of a graph. As such, when a matroid arises from a graph via SZF, the vertices of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. We call such a matroid SZF-realizable. Notably, unlike the traditional method of obtaining a matroid from a graph, skew zero forcing in a graph does not always give rise to a matroid. This paper establishes fundamental results in graph and matroid theory with respect to (1) which matroids are SZF-realizable, and (2) what kinds of graphs do and do not give rise to SZF matroids. The main result of the paper focuses on cycle matroids of outerplanar graphs.

papers.title: Quadratic Convexification with Two Switching Variables via Extreme Rays
papers.authors: Yipeng Zhang, Yuyuan Ouyang, Boshi Yang
papers.abstract: We consider the convex hull of the quadratic lift $(x,xx^\top,y)$ of the set $\{(x,y) \mid 0 \le x \le y,\ y \in \{0,1\}^n \}$. Descriptions of this convex hull provide convex relaxations for quadratic optimization with switching variables, including problems with indefinite quadratic objectives and constraints. For $n=2$, we completely characterize the extreme rays of the corresponding cone of nonnegative quadratic functions, which consists of two switching rays, six boundary-product rays, discounted affine-square rays, and a parameterized family of discounted rank-two rays. These families generate the cone, so their linearizations give a complete valid-inequality description of the convex hull in the lifted space. The discounted rank-two rays also show that rank-one liftings cannot generate all valid inequalities. Using this classification, we prove a conjecture of Anstreicher and Burer on an exact semidefinite representation of this convex hull.

papers.title: Minimizing Monotone Norms in Fractional Load Balancing
papers.authors: Daniel Blankenburg, Antonia Ellerbrock, Thomas Kesselheim, Jens Vygen
papers.abstract:
We devise a fully polynomial time approximation scheme for minimizing a monotone norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert$ over a convex set $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$. We study the multi-customer setting, where $X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the solution set $X_i\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ is given by a linear minimization oracle for each customer $i$. Our algorithm computes, for any given $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution. With high probability, it uses $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \varepsilon^{-2}(n+d) \right)$ single-customer linear minimization oracle calls and the same number of generalized KL projections to the dual space $Y=\{y\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}: \left\lVert y \right\rVert^* \le 1\}$. We assume no prior knowledge on $X$, and our running time depends only on $n$, $d$, and $\varepsilon$. Our result is robust in the sense that it allows for approximate linear minimization oracles and approximate KL projections. We show that the (approximate) KL projection can be performed efficiently for large classes of monotone norms, demonstrating the applicability of our approach.
  While such a result (with exact projection) is well-known for the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm via multiplicative weight updates and was recently obtained for ordered norms via a smooth norm approximation and a novel randomization, existing techniques do not extend to general monotone norms. In particular, a key feature used in previous proofs was dual price stability, which was derived from a global contraction property of the KL projection to the dual space $Y$. We show that this property does not extend to general monotone norms. Therefore, we use a different price mechanism, based on the well-known mirror descent paradigm, for which a local contraction property holds and guarantees stability.

papers.title: Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
papers.authors: Peter Banda, John Caughman, Tobi Lehman
papers.abstract: A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension. We give an explicit closed-form enumeration for all $n$, $d$, and alphabet sizes $\sigma$, in which the two-dimensional coefficients $1$, $p+1$, and $p$ become $r_d(p,v)=p^{\binom{v}{2}}\binom{d}{v}_p$, with $\binom{d}{v}_p$ the Gaussian binomial; it extends to configurations with a prescribed number of active cells and to all finite abelian groups. The case of prime $n$ recovers, in complement form, a result of Castillo-Ramirez and Gadouleau; the multi-prime closed form and the dynamical consequences beyond the stabilizer inclusion are new. We prove a lower bound attained exactly when $n$ is prime, and upper bounds, among them $(2^d-1+2\log_2 n)\,\sigma^{n^d/2}$. As $d$ grows, the symmetry probability decays as $\sigma^{-c\,n^d}$ with $c\to1-1/p_1(n)$, set solely by the smallest prime factor of $n$, and the symmetry advantage of the side $p+1$ over a prime side $p$ inverts within an explicit window around $d_c(p)\approx p\ln 2$. Under the necessary hypothesis of translation-equivariant neighborhoods, shift-symmetry is irreversible, the per-prime symmetry ranks never decrease, and non-symmetric tasks are unsolvable from symmetric inputs. We give a detection algorithm with worst-case cost $O(n^d\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{p^d-1}{p-1})$ and an average-case analysis, exact for each subgroup test. The mathematical content of every numbered statement is formally verified in Lean 4, and the correspondence between each theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary and its formal statement was audited by hand.

papers.title: Asymptotically Optimal Bounds for Counting Near-Minimum Circuits in Regular Matroids
papers.abstract: For a regular matroid on $m$ elements with positive weights and weighted girth $g_w$, we prove that the number of circuits of weight at most $\alpha g_w$ is bounded by $(Km)^{2\alpha}$, for every real $\alpha\ge1$ and an absolute constant $K$. This improves the previous $m^{O(\alpha^2)}$ bound of Gurjar and Vishnoi and matches classic graph cut and cycle counting bounds of Karger and Subramanian. We also show this is asymptotically optimal for all real $\alpha\geq 1$ under the Erd\H{o}s girth conjecture, while unconditional optimality holds for half-integer $\alpha$ by prior results. As consequences, we resolve a recent conjecture by Khanna, Putterman, and Song implying the existence of a parallel basis search algorithm for regular matroids terminating in logarithmically many rounds of independence queries, and obtain improved bounds on the number of near-minimum weight codewords in regular codes and near-shortest vectors in totally unimodular lattices under $\ell_p$-norms.

papers.title: Space-Filling Hypersurfaces
papers.authors: Victoria Bourgeois-Conti, Han-Bom Moon, Erick Perez, Amelia Warren
papers.abstract: We seek space-filling hypersurfaces of a projective space over a finite field. They are hypersurfaces contain all rational points. The main goal is to construct a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree. For each projective space over a finite field, we find a lower bound of the minimum degree of space-filling hypersurface, and construct an example without any singular rational points. Finally, over an odd-dimensional projective space or for fields of characteristic two, we provide a construction of a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree.

papers.title: A negative answer to the final question in "Les petits cailloux"
papers.abstract: We consider polynomial-time computation over arbitrary structures, with unit cost for the primitive operations and relations and with nondeterministic witnesses consisting of arbitrary structure elements. We prove that every finite-signature structure with two distinct available elements and containing a binary operation $*$ and total unary operations $L,R$ such that $L(x*y)=x$ and $R(x*y)=y$ satisfies $P\ne NP$. The proof encodes an exponentially long computation in one element. An incorrect transition has a polynomial-size binary address, and hence the existence of an error is an $NBP$ problem. Existence of a correct accepting trace belongs to the mixed second level $\Sigma_2^{S,B}$, with an arbitrary-element existential block followed by a binary universal block. We obtain $EXP\subseteq\Sigma_2^{S,B}\subseteq PH$. A hypothetical equality $P=NP$ would collapse this hierarchy to $P$ and imply $P=EXP$, contradicting a direct deterministic diagonalization over the same structure. A simulation by function graphs extends the obstruction to every jointly injective binary primitive under the same assumptions on equality and available elements. Consequently no unary predicate on Malcev's free binary-tree algebra yields $P=NP$, with or without the projections. In contrast, starting from the author's unary example, we construct five infinite structures with binary operations and $P=NP$. These include an algebra with one binary operation and one constant, an expansion with an associative rectangular-band operation, and an algebra with one binary operation whose every row and column has infinite image.

papers.title: Counting eigenvalues below the lowest Landau level Robin Dirichlet boundary conditions in an annulus
papers.abstract: We study a charged quantum particle confined to an annulus and subject to a strong uniform magnetic field. A Dirichlet condition is imposed on the inner boundary and a Robin condition on the outer boundary. We are interested in the number of bound states whose energy lies below the lowest Landau level, the threshold set by the magnetic field in the whole plane. In the semiclassical regime, we derive an asymptotic formula for this number. It shows how the count depends on the geometry of the annulus, through the length and curvature of the outer boundary, and on the strength of the Robin parameter. We treat both the repulsive and the attractive cases of the Robin condition and describe how the attractive case changes the boundary behavior that produces these low-lying states. The proof reduces the problem to an effective one-dimensional model near the outer boundary and relies on separation of variables in angular momentum.

papers.title: The One-Skeleton of Multilinear Polytopes and Their Standard Relaxations
papers.abstract: Edge-following methods, such as the simplex method, move along edges of a polytope. Their behavior depends on which vertices are adjacent and on the diameter. We study both for the two polytopes of binary polynomial optimization: the multilinear polytope and its standard linear relaxation. For quadratic polynomials, Padberg showed that two integral vertices are adjacent in both polytopes if and only if the variables where they differ induce a connected subgraph. For higher degree, we replace this subgraph by a contracted hypergraph on the same variables, built from the monomials whose constraints tie these variables together. We show that its connectivity decides adjacency in the relaxation but, unlike in the quadratic case, not always in the multilinear polytope. Adjacency is the same in both polytopes exactly when the relaxation has the Trubin property. We investigate when this property holds and characterize it for cubic polynomials. The contracted hypergraph also yields short paths. The diameter of the multilinear polytope is at most the number of variables, and that of the relaxation is linear in the numbers of variables and monomials. Similar linear bounds hold for the number of pivots between bases of the relaxation.

papers.title: Affine Grassmannian from divisors
papers.abstract: We generalize Mirkovi\'c's construction of Zastava spaces. These spaces form an inductive system, giving a generalization of affine and Beilinson--Drinfeld Grassmannians as indschemes, defined for any integral symmetric matrix $\kappa$ with even diagonal entries. When $\kappa$ is the Cartan matrix from a simply-laced Kac--Moody algebra, we also construct an action of the Tits group on the generalized affine Grassmannian.

papers.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
papers.abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $\Psi_F$, the Boij-S\"oderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leq\Psi_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $\Psi$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

papers.title: Entropic Ricci bounds at conic singularities and boundaries
papers.abstract: We study synthetic Ricci bounds and related rigidity phenomena in conic and boundary neighborhoods through the behavior of entropy along optimal transports.
