For cones over manifolds, we show that two-sided entropic Ricci bounds at the vertex force the fiber to have constant sectional curvature 1, while non-trivial quotient singularities, such as Euclidean cones over spherical space forms, remain admissible. An analogous rigidity holds for Riemannian manifolds with conic singularities. We also give a local characterization of boundary convexity in terms of entropic lower Ricci bounds, based on a direct optimal transport argument.

papers.title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract:
We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, \Theta)$ satisfies that $I_X(2\Theta)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme.
  As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebraic-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

papers.title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.

papers.title: Exponential Multiple Riordan Arrays
papers.abstract: We extend exponential double Riordan arrays to exponential multiple Riordan arrays $[g;f_1,\ldots,f_\ell]$, whose columns are generated, in exponential form, by a function $g$ of $t^\ell$ and $\ell$ multipliers $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell$ used cyclically. We prove an $\ell$-case fundamental theorem, define the exponential multiple Riordan group, and determine its identity, inverses, and its Appell, associated, and $\ell$ Bell-type subgroups; the group is the semidirect product of its Appell and associated subgroups. We compute the production matrix in terms of $2\ell$ sequences, the $c_r$- and $r_r$-sequences ($0\leq r\leq \ell-1$), give its bivariate generating function in terms of generalized hyperbolic functions, and derive recurrence relations for the entries. Finally, we give two sequence characterizations: one by $\ell-1$ one-step $A$-sequences, an $\ell$-step $A$-sequence, and a $Z$-sequence, and one by a single $\ell$-step $A$-sequence and $\ell$ $Z$-sequences. For $\ell=2$ all results reduce to those for exponential double Riordan arrays.

papers.title: Statistical-to-computational gaps in central limit theorems for high-dimensional tensors
papers.abstract: We study high-dimensional central limit theorems (CLTs) as hypothesis testing problems, comparing the number of summands needed for statistical and computational indistinguishability of the normalized sum from the limiting Gaussian distribution as the dimension and number of summands grow together. For the off-diagonal entries of sums of i.i.d. rank-one tensors formed from standard Gaussian vectors (equivalently, the problem of distinguishing Wigner from Wishart tensors), we prove total variation bounds sharpening previous estimates of Mikulincer (2020) and give matching polynomial-time tests. This shows that the statistical and computational thresholds coincide for this CLT, contrary to a proposal by Kunisky, Moore, and Wein (2024). On the other hand, we also show that, for tensors of order at least three, sufficient Gaussian dilution of the summands by adding independent Gaussian noise and rescaling gives a CLT model with a statistical-to-computational gap (in the above setting and ones with more general rank-one summand distributions). To the best of our knowledge, such a phenomenon has not been observed before in any high-dimensional CLT. In particular, in the relevant parameter regimes, we show that a brute-force search achieves strong detection, while polynomials of degree up to $n^{\Omega(1)}$ cannot achieve strong separation. The latter lower bounds control low-degree $\chi^2$-divergences by a novel method based on cumulant generating functions, and we further illustrate the use of these tools by applying them to masked tensor CLT models where only a prescribed subset of tensor entries is revealed.

papers.title: A short route to Diening's averaging criterion in spaces of homogeneous type
papers.abstract: We present a short, self-contained proof of the averaging-operator criterion for the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over unbounded spaces of homogeneous type. Building on techniques of Diening and Lerner, we establish a Jensen-type inequality with uniformly summable error, from which the criterion follows directly via a Calder\'on-Zygmund argument.

papers.title: $q$-$\gamma$-positivity of two $q$-Narayana polynomials
papers.abstract: We address the question of $q$-$\gamma$-positivity of $q$-Narayana polynomials for $q$-super Catalan numbers $A_{n,m}(q)$ and their duals, $B_{n,m}(q)$. We offer three main results. First, both the $q$-$m$-Narayana polynomials, whose coefficients refine the q-super Catalan numbers, and the dual q-Narayana polynomials are $q$-$\gamma$-positive of index one. Second, the dual $q$-Narayana polynomials are also $q$-$\gamma$-positive of index two. Third, both the $q$- Narayana numbers and their duals are coefficient-wise $q$-unimodal.

papers.title: Meta-Nested Recurrences
papers.authors: Beno\^it Cloitre, Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang
papers.abstract: We study recurrences in which a previous sequence value determines the number of iterations of an inner map. Campbell's example has an explicit power-of-three formula and inner orbits of eventual period at most two. Its normalized lower and upper limits are $2/5$ and $3/4$. For a variable-depth Conway recurrence $C$, we prove the golden-ratio lower bound, its exact equality set, a Fibonacci upper cap, and the landing of the inner orbit at every Fibonacci index $F_k$ with $k\ge6$. These proofs are elementary and start from twenty-four initial values. The plateau of $C$ to the left of $F_k$ has width exactly $\lfloor(2k-9)/3\rfloor$, and $C(F_k+t)=F_{k-1}+t$ for $0\le t\le\lfloor(k-8)/6\rfloor$. A maximum principle turns a finite exact computation into the bound $\limsup C(n)/n<0.65446923$. We characterize the convergence of $C(n)/n$ to $\alpha=(\sqrt5-1)/2$ in terms of negative selected orbit jumps and of a limiting convex profile, and we derive entropy and variance budgets for the recursive splits. Along inverse rays of the map $x\mapsto C(x)$, the relative errors are absolutely summable and the growth is asymptotically Fibonacci. For Grytczuk's fixed-depth recurrence, we give a Pascal-word proof of convergence with the sharp error order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ along interval maxima. The full variable-depth limit remains open.

papers.title: Adaptive linear quadratic optimal control for discrete-time stochastic systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the adaptive linear quadratic optimal control problem for a class of discrete-time stochastic systems, where the system matrix pair $(A,B)$ is unknown and the state weighting matrix $Q$ in the cost function is not necessarily positive semidefinite. Our proposed adaptive optimal control only assumes that the corresponding algebraic Riccati equation has a stabilizing solution, which weakens the standard controllable and observable assumptions used in the literature. To address this problem, we modify a weighted least squares algorithm by incorporating a random regularization method, which ensures the uniform stabilizability of the family of estimated models. Additionally, a diminishing excitation is introduced in the design of the proposed adaptive control to guarantee the strong consistency of the desired components of the estimates. Finally, by leveraging this family of estimates and employing a suitable switching method, we demonstrate that a certainty equivalence control with such a diminishing excitation is an optimal adaptive control.

papers.title: Optimal higher order convergence rates for the MUON optimizer
papers.authors: Thomas Beretti, Thang Do, Steffen Dereich, Arnulf Jentzen
papers.abstract: Gradient descent optimization methods are the key tools to train deep neural networks in artificial intelligence systems. In practice, one typically employs suitable accelerated gradient descent optimization methods such as the momentum optimizer, the Adam optimizer, or the MUON optimizer proposed by Jordan et al. in 2024. In 1964 Polyak showed that, in a neighborhood of a local minimizer, the momentum optimizer converges with the rate $(\sqrt{\chi}+1)^{-1}(\sqrt{\chi}-1)$, which is strictly faster than the rate $(\chi+1)^{-1}(\chi-1)$ of the standard gradient descent optimizer, where $\chi\in(1,\infty)$ is the condition number (the ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue) of the Hessian of the objective function at the local minimizer. Recently, the same faster rate has been established for the Adam optimizer. In this work we show that the MUON optimizer achieves the same higher speed of convergence and we establish the optimality of the obtained convergence rates. More specifically, we propose a precise concept for measuring the speed of convergence of gradient descent optimization methods, and we establish optimal convergence rates for the standard gradient descent, the momentum, the RMSprop, the Adam, and the MUON optimizers.

papers.title: Second homology of some quandles
papers.abstract: We derive formulas from Eisemann's formula for the second quandle homology of quandles. We prove that for a finite injective quandle $Q$, the second quandle homology $H_2(Q)$ can be computed in a representation group of $Q$, which is a finite quotient of the enveloping group of $Q$, by giving a formula for that. We use this to compute $H_2(Q)$ for $Q$ the subquandle of $k$-cycles of $S_n$ and $Q$ the quandle corresponding to the conjugacy class of a diagonalizable element of $SL(n,q)$, with some exceptions. For $G$ a finite group with trivial Bogomolov multiplier, as many classical groups, simple groups and (with exceptions) quasi-simple groups, we derive a formula for $H_2(Conj(G))$ that can be computed in $G$ alone. The formula relies on conjugacy classes of $G$, centralizers in $G$ of representative of such classes and the derived group of $G$. If $G$ is moreover perfect this formula can be related to the first Hochschild homology of the group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$. As an application, we compute $H_2(Q)$ for $Q$ the conjugacy quandle of $GL(2,q)$ for $q\neq 2,3$.

papers.title: Dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions
papers.abstract: We prove that the Artin--Schelter Gorenstein and Artin--Schelter regular properties descend from a graded Ore extension to its coefficient algebra, for every twisting automorphism and every skew derivation. We then determine the dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions for all gradings compatible with the Ore structure. They are exactly the semidirect products of a dual reflection group of the coefficient algebra by the cyclic group generated by the degree of the new variable, meeting it trivially, and a nonzero skew derivation never contributes a new degree. For iterated Ore extensions we characterize the dual reflection groups by an order formula analogous to the theorem of Shephard, Todd and Chevalley, and we prove the binomial conjecture of Buzaglo and Rogalski for these algebras. We show that their covariant rings are complete intersections of growth type, whose Ext-algebras grow like a polynomial ring in as many variables as there are generators of nontrivial degree. This answers a question of Kirkman, Kuzmanovich and Zhang for these algebras. Finally, we describe the smash product as a Cayley quiver with relations, factor its matrix Hilbert series, and show that the extension becomes Hopf--Galois once the Jacobian is inverted.

papers.title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
papers.abstract: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schr\"odinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau. Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.

papers.title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
papers.authors: Yevhenii Yu. Chapovskyi, Serhii D. Koval
papers.abstract: We compute the point symmetry pseudogroup of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation using both the direct and the algebraic methods. We also revisit the classical Lie symmetry analysis of this model in detail, concentrating on hidden infinitesimal and hidden point symmetries. Additionally, we re-examine the symmetry properties of each codimension-one reduced model and determine their point symmetry pseudogroups.

papers.title: Normality in generalized Rudin spaces
papers.abstract:
In \cite{Kojman2026}, Kojman generalized Mary Ellen Rudin's construction of a ZFC Dowker space to larger cardinals and gave a pcf-theoretic condition ensuring that the resulting spaces are collectionwise normal. A subsequent manuscript by Eisworth, Kojman, Lambie-Hanson, and Marun \cite{EKLM2026} develops the theory further and leaves open whether these generalized Rudin spaces can fail to be normal. We answer this question by proving that, for cardinals $\mu<\delta$ with $\operatorname{cf}(\delta)=\aleph_0$, the generalized Rudin space $X(\mu,\delta)$ is normal if and only if $\operatorname{pp}(
u)<\delta$ for every cardinal $
u\in(\mu,\delta)$ with $\operatorname{cf}(
u)=\aleph_0$. Given this characterization, known consistency results provide consistent examples of nonnormal generalized Rudin spaces.

papers.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
papers.abstract:
We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Koll\'ar. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume.
  The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Koll\'ar's gluing techniques.

papers.title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
papers.abstract: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

papers.title: Some families of birational cubic and Verra fourfolds
papers.abstract: We study the birational relationship between cubic fourfolds and Verra fourfolds, which are double covers of the product of two projective planes. We show that in?nitely many divisors in the moduli space of cubic fourfolds containing a plane parametrize cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. Our approach relies on the geometry of quadric surface bundles and their associated K3 surfaces, together with the study of Brauer classes. We also investigate two particularly interesting families, providing explicit geometric descriptions and equations for the associated varieties. In one case, the cubic fourfolds have two planes and the two projections from these planes directly show the existence of birational isomorphisms with Verra fourfolds.

papers.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

papers.title: Proximal random reshuffling with inexact gradients for nonconvex composite optimization
papers.abstract: We design and justify a proximal inexact random reshuffling method for minimizing sums of the finite average of functions with Lipschitz continuous gradients and lower semicontinuous regularizers that may be nonconvex. Each epoch visits every component once, using inexact gradients with a prescribed tolerance, and ends with a single proximal step. Our analysis is pathwise: it holds for every sequence of permutations and does not depend on how the reshuffling is performed. We show that when the stepsizes and error tolerances satisfy suitable summability conditions, the objective values converge and every accumulation point is stationary. Furthermore, under the Polyak--{\L}ojasiewicz--Kurdyka condition at a single accumulation point and sufficient decrease of stepsizes, the entire sequence has finite length and converges to that point. For polynomial stepsizes and power-type desingularizing functions, we derive convergence rates for objective values and iterates. Finally, faster objective-value rates are derived when the limit is a local minimizer.

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: We study how stability and the independence property of the norm formula $\varphi(x,y)=\lVert x+y\rVert$ on a real Banach space relate to the same properties in its complete theory. We construct separable Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ and a separable elementary extension $W$ of $X$. The norm formula is stable on $X$ and has the independence property on $W$, and therefore in $\operatorname{Th}(X)$. It is unstable on $Y$ and has no independence property in any model of $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$. Together with $\ell_2$ and $X\oplus_2Y$, these spaces realize all five possible combinations of stability, instability without the independence property, and the independence property on a space with the presence or absence of the independence property in its complete theory. All five spaces are uniformly convex and $\sqrt3$-isomorphic to Hilbert space. Their norms satisfy the common midpoint estimate $\lVert x\rVert,\lVert y\rVert\leq1 \Longrightarrow \lVert(x+y)/2\rVert^2\leq1-(1/12)\lVert x-y\rVert^2$, and $W$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. The proof for $Y$ uses coordinate truncation and a polynomial bound on threshold patterns for vectors of bounded support. These bounds give finite fat-shattering dimension at each positive scale, from which the complete-theory conclusion follows.

papers.title: Wasserstein Stability of the Nerve Map
papers.abstract: Given a locally finite open cover of a paracompact space, a subordinate partition of unity defines a map into the geometric realization of the nerve. When the cover is good, the nerve theorem asserts that this map is a homotopy equivalence. In applied topology, one specializes this construction to covers of metric data by open balls centered at finitely many landmarks. The corresponding nerve map represents the data inside the \v{C}ech complex, enabling one to pull cohomological or spectral invariants back to the data. Since point cloud data often comes equipped with weights encoding domain-specific importance, we introduce a weighted version of the nerve map and study its stability under perturbations of the landmarks and weights using metrics from optimal transport. Our main result is a Lipschitz stability theorem for the weighted nerve map under a uniform nondegeneracy assumption. We state the bound in terms of a scale-dependent optimal transport distance, and give an example where our estimate is attained. Since this distance is dominated by a multiple of the $1$-Wasserstein distance, Wasserstein stability follows as a corollary. We also give geometric conditions ensuring nondegeneracy, obtain explicit estimates of the Lipschitz constant for closed Riemannian manifolds, and sketch applications to Laplacian eigenvector cascading and Eilenberg--MacLane coordinates.

papers.title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
papers.authors: Dominik Burek, Tymoteusz Chmiel, S{\l}awomir Cynk, Marcin Oczko
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.

papers.title: Almost sure behaviour of empirical measures for intermittent maps whose return time distribution is 1-regularly varying
papers.abstract: In this article we study sets of limit points $\mathcal{L}$ for the sequence of empirical measures of intermittent maps with several equally sticky neutral fixed points. Such intermittent maps come with a parameter $\alpha > 0$ which determines the "stickiness" of the neutral fixed points. When $\alpha \neq 1$, it is known that two different behaviours can occur: either $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely the singleton $\{\mu\}$ where $\mu$ is an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure; or $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely given by the entire simplex $\pi\mathcal{S}$ of invariant measures supported at the neutral fixed points. We study the case that $\alpha = 1$ and show that neither of these two behaviours occur and that $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely equal to a star-shaped subset of the simplex $\pi \mathcal{S}$. Moreover, we show that when slowly varying functions are introduced one can obtain a large range of different behaviours, including both the possible outcomes when $\alpha \neq 1$. Our results apply to a large class of intermittent interval maps as well as parabolic rational maps of the Riemann sphere.

papers.title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
papers.abstract: We develop a pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot-Poisson-Nernst-Planck system describing ionic transport in a charged, saturated, and deformable porous medium. The mechanical equations are reformulated in terms of a non-symmetric pseudostress and the solid displacement, while mixed formulations are retained for the Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations. The nonlinear electrostatic and advective couplings are treated in a Banach space setting. The formulation provides direct approximations of the pseudostress, fluxes, and concentration gradients, and permits algebraic reconstruction of the displacement gradient and Cauchy stress. Under block-stability and small-data assumptions, we establish continuous and discrete well-posedness, with poroelastic stability bounds uniform with respect to the first Lame parameter. A conforming Raviart-Thomas discretization, completed by discontinuous polynomials, yields a priori error estimates and convergence rates. For the coupled scheme in two dimensions, we construct a residual-based a posteriori error estimator and establish its reliability under an additional smallness condition on the prescribed data. Local efficiency is proved for polynomial boundary data, with boundary-data oscillation included for general traces. We also describe the estimator modifications for nonhomogeneous displacement and normal-flux data under corresponding stability and solvability hypotheses. Numerical experiments examine convergence of the mixed and reconstructed fields, robustness in the nearly incompressible regime, adaptive refinement, and ionic polarization in a charged porous medium.

papers.title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
papers.authors: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Do Kien Hoang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract:
We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$.
  For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: Pointwise Convergence and Approximation of Matrix-Transform Means of Vilenkin--Fourier Series
papers.authors: Nino Anakidze, M\'at\'e Szilveszter, George Tephnadze, Ferenc Weisz
papers.abstract: We study convergence, divergence, and approximation of matrix-transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series. For bounded groups, we prove convergence along ${M_n}$ at Vilenkin--Lebesgue points without additional diagonal conditions. For arbitrary bounded or unbounded groups, every regular matrix-transform method admits divergence on any prescribed null set along any increasing sequence. We also obtain $L_p(G_m)$ approximation estimates in terms of the modulus of continuity.

papers.title: Finiteness properties of Bestvina-Brady kernels for graph products with torsion
papers.authors: Eduardo Flores Mart\'inez, Luis Jorge S\'anchez Salda\~na
papers.abstract: We study Bestvina-Brady kernels associated to graph products whose vertex groups are either infinite cyclic or finite. Using a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ cubical complex constructed by Ruane and Witzel, on which the graph product with defining graph $\Gamma$ acts, together with an equivariant Morse function, we establish sufficient conditions for homological finiteness properties in terms of the topology of the flag complex $\Gamma^\blacktriangle$, the subcomplex $\Gamma^\blacktriangle_\infty$ spanned by the infinite vertices, and the ascending and descending links of certain vertices. We also prove a partial converse, showing that, under additional vanishing hypotheses on homology in the next degree, non-vanishing homology of these complexes obstructs higher finiteness properties of the Bestvina-Brady kernel. The main new features are the presence of finite stabilizers and the resulting additional link conditions, which are expressed in terms of the flag complex of $\Gamma$. When the finite vertex groups are abelian, we characterize when the kernel has finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, describe the normalizers of its finite subgroups as Bestvina-Brady kernels of smaller graph products, and obtain a criterion for the kernel to be of Bredon type $\underline{\mathrm{FP}}_n$.

papers.title: Analysis of TraceFEM for the Surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard Model
papers.abstract: We analyze a trace finite element method (TraceFEM) for a surface fluid with a stabilization term that filters out Killing vector fields, and use it to discretize the surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard problem in space only. Assuming no geometric error, we show that the discrete inf-sup condition that our method requires is equivalent to the usual condition found in the literature and known to hold for trace Taylor-Hood pairs of arbitrary order in intrinsic dimension two. Inspired by a continuous dependence estimate at the PDE level, we derive error estimates for our scheme in the energy norms, which in turn lead to estimates in $L^2$-norms and, for two-dimensional surfaces, $L^\infty$-norm for the phase variable. To that end, we introduce a $p$-dependent scaling for the normal derivative volume stabilization, and use it to prove new approximation and inverse estimates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-based setting ($p \in [1,\infty]$ for approximation and $p \in [2,\infty]$ for inverse estimates). Finally, we corroborate the analysis with numerical experiments.

papers.title: K3 surfaces and BHK Mirror symmetry: A counterexample
papers.authors: Alexis Barrett, Archer Clayton, Ben DeVries, Nathan Priddis
papers.abstract: For K3 surfaces of BHK type, there are two versions of mirror symmetry that might be applied, namely BHK mirror symmetry and LPK3 mirror symmetry of Dolgachev, which involved choosing a polarizing lattice. It has been conjectured that for a pair of BHK mirror K3 surfaces, one can choose a polarizing lattice as the invariant lattice of some nonsymplectic diagonal symmetry. We provide a counterexample, showing that LPK3 mirror symmetry cannot be realized by polarizing surfaces by the invariant lattice of a diagonal symmetry. However, in our example the polarizing lattice can be realized as the invariant lattice of a permutation symmetry.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract:
Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. Working in dimension $n \ge 2$ throughout the paper, we prove that for symmetric uniformly elliptic operators with bounded measurable coefficients, every bounded open set satisfying the mean value inequality for all integrable subsolutions defined on that set (what we call ``strong mean value sets'') agrees almost everywhere with the canonical set from Caffarelli's construction which has the same center and volume. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison.
  Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ``mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume as this weak mean value ball has a hole of positive measure.

papers.title: Path Components of Almost Doubly Commuting Fredholm Tuples
papers.authors: Chen Li, Guohao Li, Kai Wang
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that the Fredholm index classifies the norm-path components of almost doubly commuting Fredholm n-tuples on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space. Using Kasparov's technical theorem, we join each tuple to an essentially normal one by a straight-line Fredholm path and applying the Douglas-Curto theorem.

papers.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
papers.abstract: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $\mu$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $P\Gamma_N$ generated by a semigroup $\Gamma_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $P\Gamma_N$ and that the chain graphs of $P\Gamma_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $\Gamma_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(\Gamma)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(\Gamma_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.

papers.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
papers.abstract:
We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite.
  In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators.
  We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

papers.title: On the algebraic Mackey deformation
papers.abstract: This paper provides a conceptual understanding of the Mackey bijection from the admissible dual of a real reductive group $G$ into the admissible dual of its Cartan motion group $G_0$, by studying the primitive spectrum of a Hecke algebra over $\mathbb{C}[t]$ arising from the contraction of $G$ to $G_0$. If $K$ denotes a maximal compact subgroup of $G$, our approach leads to the following two results: the admissible Mackey bijection is a piecewise homeomorphism, each piece being defined by the length of the lowest $K$-types; the Hecke algebras of $G$ and $G_0$ have, up to $K$-types not exceeding a certain length, the same periodic cyclic homology.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
papers.abstract: We investigate the blow-up behavior of solutions to the semilinear wave equation $$ \partial_t^2 u - \partial_x^2 u = |u|^{p-1}u \ln^a(u^2+2), \quad (x,t)\in \mathbb{R} \times [0,T), $$ with $p > 1$ and $a<0$. While the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. The main obstruction is that known constructions of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. Focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a Lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. This yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. To our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.

papers.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
papers.abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(\sigma)$ to $L^q(\omega)$ for the operator $H_\sigma g(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,d\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $\omega$ is a $\sigma$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $\kappa_{p,q}$ in $C_*\le\kappa_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $\omega$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Os\k{e}kowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.

papers.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.

papers.title: Zero detection via Cox random measures
papers.abstract: Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's {\xi} function.

papers.title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Brou\'e--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.

papers.title: On the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Fr\'echet structure over AF algebras I: The compact case
papers.abstract: This is the first of two papers devoted to spatial Fr\'echet structures on AF algebras and their derivations. Here, we study the simplest example of such a structure: the Fr\'echet algebra of almost-local compact operators associated with a fixed orthonormal basis. We revisit the characterization of its continuous derivations in terms of infinite matrices and their operator-theoretic implementation on rapidly decreasing vectors. Reformulating this description in the language of 0-chains, borrowed from the theory of quantum many-body systems, we establish a sufficient condition for continuity in terms of spatial growth. Finally, we construct a Fr\'echet-continuous symmetric derivation that does not generate a one-parameter group of automorphisms of this algebra that is strongly continuous with respect to its Fr\'echet topology.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Hypercubes and Beta--Gaussian Mixtures
papers.authors: Ali Darijani, Emadedin Soufian, J\"urgen Beyerer
papers.abstract: We derive closed-form Gaussian information projections of Beta--Gaussian distributions whose tangential components are supported on affine embedded hypercubes and whose normal components are Gaussian. The optimal Gaussian is uniquely characterized by moment matching, and the corresponding minimum Kullback--Leibler divergence admits an explicit expression depending only on the intrinsic Beta parameters, independently of the embedding geometry, ambient dimension, and normal Gaussian parameters. In the uniform case, this divergence reduces to a linear function of the intrinsic dimension. We further extend this construction to finite, pure embedded cubical complexes by considering mixtures of the componentwise Gaussian projections. Using the joint convexity of the Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish an explicit upper bound on the approximation error of the resulting Gaussian Mixture. For uniform tangential distributions and volume-based mixture weights, the bound is linear in the intrinsic dimension and independent of the geometry of the complex, its embedding, and the normal Gaussian parameters.

papers.title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
papers.abstract: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincar\'e duality algebras.

papers.title: Formal completions and decompositions of matrix factorization categories of Fano mirrors
papers.abstract: We study the derived categories of matrix factorizations for certain toric Landau--Ginzburg models that are mirror dual to del Pezzo surfaces and Fano threefolds. Some of these models have non-isolated singularities: their critical loci may contain curves and surfaces, possibly with intersecting irreducible components. We handle these cases by studying the potential in the formal neighborhood of each irreducible component of the critical locus. Away from $\operatorname{Sing}(\operatorname{CritLoc}(W)_{\mathrm{red}})$, we construct global formal coordinates and determine the local normal form of the singularity. Near the singular or intersection strata, we analyze how the pieces of the whole connected formal neighborhood are related by localization. This gives explicit decompositions of the derived categories of matrix factorizations after idempotent completion. For the five rank-one pairs $(B_d,V_{4d+2})$, we also compare projective compactifications. The isolated sectors and central-component counts agree for $d=2,3,4,5$ and differ for $d=1$. Equivalence of the distinguished compactified contributions for the remaining matched pairs requires compatible global gluing data or compactified Homological Mirror Symmetry.

papers.title: Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
papers.authors: David Favero, Mykola Sapronov, Dash Stevanovich
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang. On the other hand, we provide an example of a smooth projective toric DM stack where this intrinsic window is never a grade restriction window despite the many possible choices. As an application, we demonstrate that reordering and/or taking a subset of an HKKN stratification sometimes changes the grade restriction window and sometimes does not.

papers.title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $\Pi_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.

papers.title: MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime
papers.abstract: We study MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to remain positive for a long time when $|\theta|>1$, where $\theta$ denotes the coupling parameter. We show that, for a fixed starting point, the finite-dimensional distributions of the conditioned process converge and identify the limiting process as a Doob $h$-transform with explicit function $h$. We also obtain precise asymptotics for the corresponding persistence probabilities. The limiting process exhibits qualitatively different behaviour depending on $\theta$ and on the support of the innovation distribution. We also determine stationary distributions of the limiting conditioned processes for all $\theta\ne 1$.

papers.title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
papers.abstract:
This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for It\^o diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem.
  More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehat\mu_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\delta_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehat\mu_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$.
  In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehat\mu_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2\lambda_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2\lambda_d}$, where $\lambda_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.

papers.title: Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher
papers.authors: Felipe de Jes\'us F\'elix-Arredondo, Nezih Nieto-Guti\'errez, Carlos Astengo-Noguez, Alejandro Ucan-Puc
papers.abstract: A discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network, a classical state-space fact: a fixed linear memory of the running integral and the last error, read out by three trainable weights that map one-to-one to the PID gains. Networks with bounded hidden states, such as LSTMs of any width, only approximate it. Trained only on a one-step physical cost (the expected cost of one transition from a fixed state distribution), with no demonstrations, teacher controller, or known gains, the network solves a strongly convex least-squares problem, so gradient descent converges from any initialization to the unique one-step optimal PID gains; the limit network is that PID, with the same action on every error sequence. Partitioned regression then shows what extra capacity buys. Orthogonal residual features keep these gains and improve on the PID if and only if they correlate with the part of the optimal action outside the PID span. On a nonlinear second-order example the gap is 5.88% of the optimal PID cost, and 4.00% against PID with a bias; no controller can improve on PID by more on this objective. A residual started at a tuned PID begins exactly at that PID; at the one-step optimal PID, a fixed-feature residual's first gradient step lowers the cost if and only if its features can improve on the PID. Experiments confirm the realization, recovery, and gap results to numerical precision. On held-out plants of three families, under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, a residual warm-started at a heavily tuned PID and trained with it lowers the long-horizon cost by 3.5%, 3.5%, and 1.9%, with family-wise 95% bounds excluding zero, also under distribution shift; a post hoc comparison with the PID tuned alone suggests that most of it comes from the recurrent part in two families. The primary endpoint, a gain of at least 5% from a generic PID start, is not met in any family.

papers.title: Floating Body Asymptotics via Fractal Strings
papers.abstract: Sch\"utt and Werner associated an almost polygonal planar convex body with a decreasing convex sequence and obtained two-sided estimates for the area removed by its floating body. We reinterpret the gaps of the defining sequence as the lengths of a normalized fractal string. Our main result shows that the area deficit, that is, the difference between the area of the set and its floating body, is comparable to an integral transform of the inner tubular volume of this string. As a consequence, if the string has Minkowski dimension $D$, then the principal power exponent of the area deficit is $1-D/3$. We also derive refinements for regularly varying tube functions, establish a realization criterion extending the almost polygonal case of the theorem of Sch\"utt and Werner, and discuss several examples. As an application, we obtain corresponding asymptotic rates for the expectations and variances of the missed area and the number of vertices of random polygons, including new intermediate behaviors between the classical polygonal and smooth cases.

papers.title: Counterexample to Flow-Transfer Conjectures
papers.abstract: An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp. $M$-tension) taking values in $B$. For subsets $B=-B\subseteq M$ with $M$ an abelian group, \v{S}\'amal conjectured that a graph admits an $(M,B)$-flow if and only if it admits an $FT_M$ map to the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)$. DeVos conjectured that, whenever there is a graph homomorphism $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)\to\operatorname{Cay}(M',B')$, every graph admitting an $(M,B)$-flow also admits an $(M',B')$-flow. We prove that these conjectures are equivalent and give a counterexample using the Petersen graph.

papers.title: Triply conservative schemes for degenerate convection-dispersion equations
papers.authors: Kaichang Yu, Juan Cheng, Chi-Wang Shu
papers.abstract: It is well known that for numerically solving hyperbolic conservation laws, even a convergent numerical scheme still may not always converge to a weak solution. The remedy is the famous Lax-Wendroff theorem. In a recent work on degenerate convection-diffusion equations, an analogous phenomenon was identified and doubly conservative schemes were introduced. In this paper, we address the same issue for solving the following nonlinear degenerate dispersive or convection-dispersion equations: \begin{equation*} u_t+f(u)_x+A(u)_{xxx}=0. \end{equation*} The resulting equation is regarded as degenerate if $A'(u)$ is allowed to vanish. An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. In contrast to classical KdV solitons possessing exponentially decaying tails, $K(m,n)$ equations can admit compactly supported solitary waves, known as compactons, whose regularity can deteriorate at the boundary of their support. We first give an example in which both a classical conservative and doubly conservative scheme converges to a limit that fails to satisfy the ultra-weak formulation. To address this issue, we introduce the notion of a triply conservative (TriC) scheme and prove a Lax-Wendroff type theorem for consistent TriC schemes. Under suitable assumptions, a convergent sequence generated by a consistent TriC scheme will converge to an ultra-weak solution. Several existing high-order schemes are shown to have a TriC structure. We further introduce a new high-order TriC finite volume scheme based on a connection between triple cell averages and quadratic B-splines. The theory and the scheme are also suited for two-dimensional anisotropic problems and non-uniform meshes. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions confirm the high-order accuracy on smooth solutions and illustrate the behavior of the schemes for compactons and traveling fronts.

papers.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
papers.abstract:
Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\alpha)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+y\alpha)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture.
  We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.

papers.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
papers.abstract: We study the average one-guess success probability of an adversary who observes the ordinary integer sum of a finite-support secret and an independent integer-valued mask, subject to an absolute-moment budget on the mask. For a uniform secret on an interval the exact optimum and an explicit optimiser are obtained. For a biased bit the masks that achieve no increase over the prior baseline are characterised and their minimal cost is determined. The entire cost-vulnerability frontier is then determined for every bias. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks. It has infinitely many affine pieces, which accumulate at the critical cost, where the frontier meets the prior baseline with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both the vulnerability and the cost are exactly additive. The results give exact design guidance for additive integer noise under the average one-guess metric; they do not constitute a cryptographic masking scheme.

papers.title: Rigid Theories
papers.abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

papers.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
papers.authors: Milena Brockhof, Giovane Galindo, Ludmil Katzarkov, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins
papers.abstract:
Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology.
  Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

papers.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
papers.authors: Jonah Gaster, Didac Martinez-Granado, Christopher-Lloyd Simon
papers.abstract:
We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=\Gamma(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $\lambda$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $\lambda$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT).
  We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

papers.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted \'etale groupoid model
papers.authors: Nikolay A. Ivanov, Ali I. Raad
papers.abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal \'etale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
papers.authors: Rafael Benchimol Klausner, Alexandre Street, Joaquim Dias Garcia, Luiz Barroso
papers.abstract: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

papers.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
papers.authors: A. N. Abyzov, O. V. Lyubimtsev, A. A. Tuganbaev
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

papers.title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
papers.authors: Eduardo Abi Jaber, Dorinel Bastide, Ronan P\'echeul, Cl\'ement Rey
papers.abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,\alpha): x\in U, \alpha \in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),\alpha(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract:
We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$.
  At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques.
  Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

papers.title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_\phi\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $\phi$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

papers.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
papers.abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

papers.title: On classifying knotted surfaces
papers.abstract: These notes, which are based on four lectures delivered at the summer school "Knotted Surfaces in Four-Manifolds" at PCMI in 2026, discuss classifications of locally flat surfaces in simply-connected $4$-manifolds.

papers.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract:
We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails.
  The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. It does not use the $2$-converse or the $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and employed by OpenAI. We define the rational numbers with square denominator using rational points on certain quadratic twists of the congruent number elliptic curve. The criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, in Smith's formulation, implies that these quadratic twists have analytic rank one. A height estimate for rational points on a fixed quotient of a Shimura curve allows us to express multiplication of elliptic-curve indices. We obtain this estimate by bounding the modular levels of the associated quaternionic abelian surfaces. The level bound is based on a compatible system of Galois representations over $\mathbb{Q}$ with controlled ramification and on Khare--Wintenberger's proof of Serre's conjecture. Green--Tao--Ziegler's theorem on linear patterns of primes supplies the rational solutions needed for a Diophantine model of integer arithmetic.

papers.title: Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
papers.authors: Willian Cintra, J\^onatas Peralta, Julio D. Rossi, Antonio Su\'arez
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.
