Thus, the same $\Theta(n)$ finite length improvement is applicable to both general linear structure and symplectic self-orthogonality.

papers.title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
papers.authors: Ming Hu, Bei Liu, Bolin Liu, Jie Shen
papers.abstract: We develop a transform-adapted approximation framework for shallow neural networks based on the short-time special affine Fourier transform (STSAFT). Replacing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the definition of classical modulation spaces, we work with weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces, building on the existing SAFT-associated modulation-space framework, and use their chirp correspondence with classical weighted modulation spaces through the chirp factorization of the SAFT kernel. We construct an associated neural dictionary and establish an $N$-term Sobolev approximation bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ on bounded one-dimensional domains. A global approximation theorem is also obtained when the spatial translation parameter ranges over the whole real line; a compact-support argument explains why an unrestricted global conclusion cannot in general be inferred from a bounded translation range. For a fixed-scale chirp family $f_\kappa(x)=e^{i\pi\kappa x^2}u(x)$, we combine the global estimate with a phase analysis to obtain the stronger phase-dependent upper-bound factor $\langle\lambda\rangle^n\langle\kappa-\lambda\rangle^{n+3/2-1/r}.$ For each fixed nonzero Schwartz envelope, matching the dictionary phase reduces the growth of this specified upper bound from order $|\kappa|^{n+3/2-1/r}$ to order $|\kappa|^n$, while preserving the $N^{-1/2}$ rate. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. We discuss the effective number of fitted output coefficients, including the rank loss of the sine branch at zero phase, and distinguish the numerical diagnostics from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.

papers.title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.

papers.title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
papers.authors: Linfang Hou, Si Li, Yongchang Zhu
papers.abstract: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space. The same conclusion is obtained for arbitrary affine-state insertions. Finally, we compute the cases of at most four currents and the nodal limit $q\to 0$, in which the type-1 and type-2 elliptic cycle coefficients degenerate to rational genus-zero cycle coefficients and the module trace reduces to the ground-state space.

papers.title: Almost sure asymptotics of numerical errors for SDEs with additive noise
papers.authors: Chuchu Chen, Xinyu Chen, Jialin Hong
papers.abstract: In this paper, we characterize the sharp almost sure asymptotics for the numerical error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to stochastic differential equations with additive noise. Specifically, we establish, to our knowledge, the first sharp laws of the iterated logarithm for Euler--Maruyama errors in this setting along geometric mesh refinements $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}=(\alpha^i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}$ for any integer $\alpha\geq 2$. These results identify $(N_i)^{-1}\sqrt{\log\log N_i}$ as the sharp almost sure error scale and provide an explicit expression for the path-dependent constants governing the asymptotic error envelopes. The LIL constants also admit a natural interpretation through the asymptotic error distribution, specifically through the conditional covariance matrix of the stable limit of the rescaled error given the driving Wiener process. A central challenge in establishing these results is to characterize the almost sure fluctuations of Skorohod integrals arising in the error expansion, which are generally anticipating, non-Gaussian, and dependent across refinement levels. The analysis also provides a framework for studying analogous asymptotics for other numerical methods.

papers.title: Chromatic polynomials of signed graphs with a balancing vertex
papers.authors: Akihiro Higashitani, Go Kamata, Masato Konoike
papers.abstract: We study the zero-free chromatic polynomial $Z_\Sigma(q)$ of a signed graph $\Sigma$ and the characteristic polynomial $\chi_\Sigma(q)=Z_\Sigma(q-1)$ of its associated hyperplane arrangement containing all coordinate hyperplanes. For a connected signed graph on $n\ge 2$ vertices with a balancing vertex, we prove the equivalence of the following four conditions: (i) $Z_\Sigma(q)$ is the chromatic polynomial of an ordinary graph; (ii) the numerator of $\sum_{q\ge 1}\chi_\Sigma(q)t^q$, written with denominator $(1-t)^{n+1}$, has nonnegative coefficients; (iii) $\Sigma$ has a balanced block; and (iv) $\chi_\Sigma(2)=0$. We also provide explicit counterexamples showing that neither the balancing-vertex assumption nor connectedness can be omitted.

papers.title: New $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant infinite families and the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image
papers.authors: Mason Adams, Prasit Bhattacharya, Arannya Bhattacherjee, Alex Waugh
papers.abstract: Let $a$ denote the stabilization of the Euler class of the sign representation of $\mathrm{C}_2$. In this paper, we show that the Behrens-Shah periodic $u$-self-equivalence of $C(a^i)$ -- a direct consequence of J.F. Adams' calculation of James periodicity -- determines the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image of the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant sphere spectrum, recovering a recent theorem of Guo-Li-Lu-Wu-Xu-Yang-Zhang via a different method. Furthermore, we use the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant periodic $u$-self-equivalences on the cofiber spectra $C(a^i)$ to construct new infinite families in the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant stable stems whose $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image is trivial.

papers.title: Gaussian processes with random pointwise regularity
papers.authors: C\'eline Esser, St\'ephane Jaffard, B\'eatrice Vedel
papers.abstract: Using wavelet series, we construct Gaussian stochastic processes whose pointwise H\"older exponent is random along a typical sample path, although at every fixed point the exponent is deterministic almost surely. We first give a local non-sparsity condition under which the H\"older exponent almost surely is a deterministic function. In the opposite direction, a lacunary construction shows that the exceptional set on which the exponent is modified can have full Hausdorff dimension. For this model we determine the marginal multifractal spectra and the bivariate spectrum of the deterministic series and its Gaussian randomization.

papers.title: Physics-constrained differentiable causal discovery of constitutive mechanisms through boundary value problems
papers.abstract: Data-driven constitutive model discovery is recast as causal discovery of mechanism parent sets using time-unrolled structural causal models. Hard-coding balance laws and constitutive skeletons, candidate graphs score environment--mechanism and state--state edges via weak-form equilibrium gaps evaluated from full-field displacements, avoiding the need to measure stresses or internal variables. An adaptive lasso and a NOTEARS-type constraint ensure graph acyclicity and an explicit evaluation order, treating climate-chamber protocols as interventions. Automatic differentiation yields the score's Gauss--Newton matrix as a local identifiability certificate, driving greedy D-optimal test design. In a synthetic study on a hygro-thermo-viscoelastic damaging plate (8 true edges among 13 candidates), interventional data recover the exact true graph in 7 of 10 runs (0.01px displacement noise) with zero attribution error. Conversely, observational data with a temperature--moisture correlation of $-0.998$ fail entirely because confounded scores are 250--380 times flatter. Observationally discovered models reproduce training climates (3.6% error) but mispredict hot and humid climates by up to 41.5% (16.9% average), whereas interventionally discovered models stay within 3.2%. A correlation sweep shows the certificate successfully predicts attribution errors, though weak-form score noise bias remains a primary limitation. Computed without knowledge of the truth, the D-optimal design selects test sets ranked second or third out of 126 candidates.

papers.title: On the algebraic bipartite graphs $D(4s,q)$
papers.authors: Chen Zhang, Xiaoyan Cheng, Yuansheng Tang, Ming Xu
papers.abstract: Lazebnik-Ustimenko graphs $D(k,q)$ constitute a notable family of $q$-regular, edge-transitive bipartite graphs characterized by high symmetry and large girth, with wide applications in algebraic graph theory and coding theory. The precise girth of $D(k,q)$ is governed by a celebrated conjecture proposed by F\"{u}redi et al., which remains unresolved in general cases. Although prior works have validated this conjecture for several specific parameter regimes and established fundamental structural properties of graph girth, a systematic characterization of girth cycles for even-indexed subfamilies of \(D(k,q)\) is still absent. This paper focuses on the graph subclass $D(4s,q)$ and conducts structural analysis via its isomorphic bipartite model $\Lambda_{k,q}$. We derive an explicit necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of length-$(4s+4)$ backtrackless circuits in $\Lambda_{4s,q}$. Using this criterion, we completely characterize all girth cycles of $\Lambda_{8,q}$ and verify the F\"{u}redi-Lazebnik-Ustimenko girth conjecture for the parameter family $k=2(p^r+1)p^t-4$ over finite fields of odd characteristic $p\geq 3$ with $q=p^m>3$. The results further enrich the structural theory of symmetric large-girth bipartite graphs and extend the valid parameter range of this classic girth conjecture.

papers.title: Posterior contraction rates for banded approximations of Gaussian processes
papers.authors: Omar Kassi, Bernhard Stankewitz, Botond Szabo
papers.abstract:
Gaussian process regression models are widely used in modern statistics and machine learning due to their flexibility, interpretability, built-in uncertainty quantification, and strong theoretical foundations. However, training Gaussian processes (GPs) has a computational cost of $O(n^3)$, while the memory and prediction costs are also $O(n^2)$.
  For large datasets commonly encountered in practice, this becomes infeasible and necessitates the use of approximate posterior methods.
  In this work, we propose a class of approximations based on sparse covariance matrices, where the kernel matrix is sparsified according to the spatial proximity of the design points.
  We analyze the accuracy of the resulting approximate posterior distribution and show that the proposed approach preserves optimal statistical inference properties, provided that the dependencies among a sufficient number of neighboring points for each feature are retained.
  We derive explicit sufficient and necessary conditions on the number of neighbors required in a general setting and apply these results to standard kernels, including the squared exponential and Mat\'ern kernels. Our theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Discrete Approximation of differential two-stage stochastic linear complementarity problems
papers.authors: Xiaojun Chen, Jian Guo, Seungjun Lee
papers.abstract: This paper studies differential two-stage stochastic linear complementarity problems, in which an ordinary differential equation (ODE) is coupled with a two-stage stochastic linear complementarity problem (SLCP) under a time-dependent probability distribution. The right-hand side of the ODE involves a solution pair (here-and-now and wait-and-see decisions) of the two-stage SLCP, while the two-stage SLCP involves two functions depending on the time $t$ and the state $x(t)$ of the ODE. Under appropriate conditions, we prove that the solution function of the two-stage SLCP is Lipschitz continuous in $x(t)$ and locally $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older continuous in $t$, and establish the existence and uniqueness of a classical solution to the differential two-stage SLCP. Moreover, we develop a discrete approximation scheme for the differential two-stage SLCP. We first use a finite-scenario partition with mesh size $\delta_N$ to approximate the distribution, then apply the Euler method for time discretization with step size $h$, and finally solve the resulting finite-dimensional problems using an inexact progressive hedging method with tolerance $\eta$. We prove that the error between a computed solution by the discrete approximation scheme and the classical solution of the original problem is bounded by $C(\delta_N+h+\eta)$, where $C>0$ is a constant independent of $N$, $h$ and $\eta$. Finally, we apply our method to find an equilibrium point of a differential two-stage stochastic two-player zero-sum game. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates and the efficiency of the discrete approximation scheme.

papers.title: Renormalized volume, Generalized Loewner energy, and Grunsky determinant of multiply connected domains
papers.abstract: We define and study three M\"obius invariant functionals for multiply connected planar domains with finitely many boundary components: the Loewner energy, the renormalized volume, and the Grunsky determinant. Using quasiconformal variations, we prove that when the boundary curves are sufficiently regular, the three functionals differ only by a modulus-dependent constant. We also prove that the Loewner energy is finite if and only if every boundary curve is a Weil--Petersson quasicircle. Moreover, we prove that the three functionals all attain their unique extremal value at the circle domains. In particular, the Loewner energy is zero if and only if it is evaluated at a circle domain. Finally, we use the minimization of Loewner energy to give a new proof of the finitely connected version of Koebe uniformization theorem.

papers.title: Analogs of crystalline measures in tube sets
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a pure point complex measure on a tube set $R^d+i F$, where $F$ is a compact convex subset in $R^d$, such that this tube set is the minimal closed convex tube set containing support of $\mu$. Furthermore, assume that the Fourier transform $\hat\mu$ (in the sense of distributions) is a measure. We determine conditions on the measure $\mu$ under which the variation of the measure $\hat\mu$ grows at least as $\exp\{2\pi H_F(t)\}$, as well as conditions under which this variation grows at most as $\exp\{2\pi H_F(t)\}$; here $H_F(t)$ is the support function of $F$.

papers.title: Counting Triangulated 3-Spheres, Nuclei, and Polyhedra
papers.abstract: We exploit two-dimensional dual polyhedra to study triangulated $3$-spheres and nuclei. First, we show that the long-standing open problem of whether the number of triangulated $3$-spheres is exponentially bounded is equivalent to the corresponding problem for one-vertex generalized triangulations, and hence also for special spines of the $3$-ball. This also establishes an equivalent counting problem for nuclei. Second, we investigate properties of nuclei, including their dual polyhedra. We also prove that every nontrivial nucleus contains a tetrahedron with six interior edges, identify the unique vertex-minimal nontrivial nucleus with $11$ vertices and $35$ tetrahedra, and construct nuclei whose dual graphs have genus growing linearly with the number of tetrahedra.

papers.title: Characterizations of products of projective spaces and quadrics
papers.abstract: We characterize products of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using Schur functors and positivity of vector bundles. First, we obtain characterizations of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using positivity of arbitrary Schur functors of extensions of a unipotent bundle by the tangent bundle, generalizing several existing results. We then prove that almost nef regular foliations whose direct sum is a subbundle of the tangent bundle determine a product decomposition, if the corresponding Schur functors admit suitable positive Schur submodules. For smooth weak Fano varieties similar results are obtained by replacing almost nefness and individual integrability of the foliations by the integrability of their total image. As special cases, we obtain product analogues of well-known characterizations of projective spaces and quadrics.

papers.title: On the Adams spectral sequence of $eo_2(C_4)$
papers.abstract: We calculate the mod $2$-homology of the fixed points of the $C_4$-equivariant Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel theory $BP^{((C_4))}\langle 1\rangle$, as an $\mathcal{A}_*$-comodule algebra. $2$-locally these fixed points are $tmf_0(5)$ by a theorem of Quinn. We deduce that $tmf_0(5)$ is an indecomposable $tmf$-module that is an extension of two $tmf$-modules of the form $tmf\otimes K$ for a finite spectrum $K$. The $K(2)$-localization of $tmf_0(5)$ is $32$-periodic, and we compute the Adams spectral sequence of $tmf_0(5)$ through the $32$-stem.

papers.title: The Evertse-Ferretti interval result for a set of weights, and the exponent $1/2$ in three complexity bounds
papers.abstract: The interval result of Evertse and Ferretti (2013) concerns a tuple $L$ of linear forms and one tuple $c$ of weights. It says that the parameters $Q$ for which the twisted height $H_{L,c,Q}$ has a small value outside an exceptional subspace $T(L,c)$ lie in $O(\delta^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$ intervals $[Q_i,Q_i^{\omega})$. We prove this for a whole set $\mathcal{C}$ of weights with the same forms. At most $J$ subspaces $T(L,c)$ occur, where $J$ depends only on the dimension and on the number of places, and one family of $O(\delta^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$ intervals serves every $c\in\mathcal{C}$ at once. Neither count depends on $\mathcal{C}$. In applications of Bugeaud-Evertse type the solutions are sorted into about $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes with the same forms and different weights, and one application now serves all classes. We deduce three complexity bounds. For a real algebraic irrational number $\xi$, the number $p(n,\xi,b)$ of blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion satisfies $\limsup p(n,\xi,b)/(n(\log n)^\eta)=\infty$ for every $\eta<1/2$; Bugeaud and Evertse proved this for $\eta<1/11$. The same holds for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, and for the steering word of $(3/2)^n$. We explain why $1/2$ is the limit of the method. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: To Race or Not to Race? Exploiting Performance Variability in Mixed-Integer Programming via Root-Gated Resource Allocation
papers.authors: Mourchid Adegbindin, Brenda Dietrich, Jamol Pender
papers.abstract:
Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver runtimes vary substantially across random seeds. Parallel replication exploits this variability but can waste computational resources when applied indiscriminately. We investigate whether information from an ordinary solve can guide this allocation decision.
  We formulate replication under a finite deadline, establish an exact relationship between runtime dispersion and the value of independent searches, and analyze delayed replication and imperfect allocation decisions. Using 101,615 seeded SCIP runs, we examine the association between root-LP dual degeneracy and replication value. We then introduce a non-invasive root-gated policy that preserves the original solver trajectory and launches three additional seeded processes when a root dual-degeneracy indicator reaches a fixed threshold.
  In a prospective two-hour experiment on 130 paired instances, root-gated racing proves optimality on 77 instances (59.23%), versus 73 (56.15%) for both Single and unconditional Race-4, while reducing active worker-process occupancy by 43.00% relative to unconditional racing. These findings demonstrate the promise of selective parallel resource allocation without solver-source modifications.

papers.title: Polynomial eigenfunctions and recurrences of fixed length
papers.abstract: This paper solves the fixed-length recurrence problem posed by Horozov, Shapiro and Tater. For the rational Darboux transformations specified here, it also resolves the order and classification questions raised by their two conjectures. It classifies monic polynomial sequences whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients and for which multiplication by the variable involves a fixed number of consecutive polynomials. Orthogonality is not assumed, and only sufficiently large degrees need be prescribed. If the lowest recurrence index is $n-m+1$, with $m\ge3$, the differential order equals $m$ times the degree of the eigenvalue as a polynomial in $n$. After translating the variable, every such sequence is a finite rational Darboux transform of an explicit family with differential order $m$ and eigenvalue $n$. Necessary and sufficient conditions on the factors determine all polynomial differential eigenoperators of the resulting family. For families that cannot be obtained by these transformations from families of smaller minimum differential order, the minimum differential and recurrence orders coincide. All such families are classified in minimum differential orders at least three, including additional families in composite orders.

papers.title: Central limit theorems for Frobenius, Hecke and Kloosterman angles
papers.authors: Shreyas Pai, Kaneenika Sinha, Naman Thakkar
papers.abstract: The Frobenius angles of non-CM elliptic curves and the Hecke angles of non-CM newforms are equidistributed with respect to the Sato--Tate measure, while for Kloosterman angles, this is known on average over natural families. We study the fluctuations around these laws in large families, for smooth test functions. We prove an unconditional central limit theorem for Frobenius angles of elliptic curves for a much larger class of test functions than previously considered; earlier results assumed the Riemann hypothesis for $L$-functions of Hecke eigenforms of full level. This result follows from a general framework, developed here, which yields Gaussian moments for statistics of sequences in $[0,1]$ varying over families. In this framework, independence is replaced by two quantitative conditions: approximate independence at distinct indices, and convergence of the family averages to the Weyl limits at a suitable rate. As further applications, we extend central limit theorems for Kloosterman angles and for Hecke angles of newforms to larger classes of test functions, the latter with the weight and the level varying simultaneously. We also treat the dilated angles $\alpha\theta$ for integers $\alpha\geq2$, whose limiting distribution is uniform. Finally, we discuss sharp statistics, obtaining a central limit theorem for Hecke angles and explaining the obstruction for the other two families.

papers.title: The asymptotic number of $BCK(p)$-terms
papers.abstract: A $BCK(p)$-term is a closed lambda-term in which each abstraction binds at most $p$ variables; for $p=1$ these terms are related to the axiom system BCK of combinatory logic. We determine the number of $BCK(p)$-terms of size $n$, up to a constant multiplicative factor, for every $p\ge2$. For $p=2$ the result is fully explicit: \[ f\_n\sim A\,n^{2n/5}2^{n/5}e^{-2n/5}n^{-3/5}e^{P(n^{1/5})}, \] where $P$ is an explicit polynomial of degree $4$. In general the asymptotic formula involves $n^{pn/(2p+1)}$ and an exponential of a polynomial in $n^{1/(2p+1)}$. The proof combines a linearization of the defining functional equation, the analysis of the Borel transform of the linearized generating function, which satisfies a linear differential equation with an irregular singularity at infinity, the saddle point method for Hayman-admissible functions, and positivity arguments comparing the original and the linearized sequences. For $p=1$ this comparison fails: the quadratic term then also changes the polynomial factor.

papers.title: On graceful labeling of Jahangir graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph with q edges, a graceful labeling assigns distinct integers from {0,...,q} its vertices so that the absolute differences across the edges are exactly 1,...,q. A Jahangir graph J_{n,m}, with n >= 2 and m >= 3, consists of an outer cycle on nm vertices and a hub joined to m equally spaced vertices of that cycle, with q = (n+1)m edges. This family of graphs is known to be graceful. In this paper we strengthen the gracefulness property of such graphs by assigning labels to their vertices through a parametric formula. These labeled graphs have a mono tonicity property: deleting an edge from the outer cycle leaves a path whose edge differences, in the negative orientation, are strictly increasing for even n and strictly decreasing for odd n. The starting observation is that large differences admit few endpoint pairs and require adjacencies between high and low labels. This suggests a construction based on alternating two separated label sets along the outer cycle. The formula has two parity branches, each with two cases modulo 4. Applications are given for every case.

papers.title: Kobayashi distance to submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold
papers.abstract: We prove that totally geodesic hypersurfaces are at infinite Kobayashi distance in a Kobayashi hyperbolic Riemannian manifold. To do this, we prove a Schwarz lemma on minimal maps with a uniform control on their Laplacians. Finally we give a full characterisation of submanifolds at infinite distance on spaces of constant sectional curvature in dimension at least 4.

papers.title: Critical mass for infinite-time blow-up in a Keller-Segel system with indirect signal production on closed Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study a parabolic-elliptic-ODE chemotaxis system with indirect signal production on closed connected Riemannian surfaces. For all sufficiently regular nonnegative initial data, the system admits a unique global classical solution. We show that the solution remains globally bounded if the total mass $M<8\pi$. For each $M>8\pi$, we find initial data of mass $M$ that yield infinite-time blow-up solutions. We then adapt the argument to the corresponding Neumann problem in a smooth bounded planar domain and obtain infinite-time blow-up solutions for any mass $M>4\pi$. At the critical mass $M=8\pi$, we show that the solutions are globally bounded on spheres equipped with the canonical spherical metric, and we construct a solution blowing up in infinite time on the Riemann sphere equipped with a special metric.

papers.title: Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.

papers.title: A locally complete family of Kummer type hyperk\"ahler fourfolds
papers.authors: Franco Giovenzana, Andr\'es Rojas, Jieao Song
papers.abstract: We construct a 4-dimensional family of projective hyperk\"ahler fourfolds of Kummer type. A general member of this family can be described as an irreducible component of a complete intersection of Heisenberg-invariant cubics in an 8-dimensional projective space. Several properties of the corresponding moduli space are also obtained. Our arguments rely on specializing to the case of generalized Kummer fourfolds of genus-two Jacobians, and make use of classical results dating back to Burkhardt and Coble.

papers.title: Recovering Small Perturbations of a Known Inclusion from One Mixed Steklov Eigenpair with Local Boundary Data
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of small normal displacements of a known inclusion from a single mixed Steklov eigenpair. The data consist of the eigenvalue and the eigenfunction trace on any nonempty open subset of the fixed outer boundary, with the eigenfunction normalized using only that subset. For an inner Dirichlet condition, we prove that the linearized measurement map is injective at every simple eigenvalue. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. For the principal Dirichlet eigenpair, the same local data also determine the inclusion uniquely among sufficiently small normal graphs. In a three-dimensional concentric shell, the eigenvalue determines the mean displacement at first order, while spherical harmonics diagonalize the remaining full-boundary trace map. The singular values decay exponentially with harmonic degree, yielding logarithmic conditional stability under a Sobolev prior. Numerical experiments using the perturbed geometry illustrate the quadratic linearization error and the deterioration of conditioning as the observed patch shrinks. For an inner Neumann condition, we prove linearized injectivity at every positive simple eigenvalue.

papers.title: Minimising Disquotational Truth
papers.abstract: We present a new axiomatic theory of disquotational truth based on the theory of positive disquotation PUTB. Formulated in classical logic, PUTB restricts the T-schema to positive sentences and satisfies key epistemic desiderata (semantic conservativity and trustworthiness). However, it fares poorly in proof-theoretic strength compared to reflective truth frameworks. To address this, we propose a new theory of positive disquotation aimed at axiomatizing its least fixed-point model. Without requiring additional resources, we achieve this by incorporating ill-founded reasoning under suitable soundness restrictions, applying the tools of cyclic proof theory to axiomatic theories of truth. The resulting theory, CPUTB, is sound relative to the minimal fixed-point model and proves the same arithmetical theorems as the impredicative theory ID1.

papers.title: The dynamical Sepp\"al\"ainen-Johansson model and the Brownian web landscape
papers.authors: Julian Ransford, B\'alint Vet\H{o}, B\'alint Vir\'ag
papers.abstract: The dynamical Sepp\"al\"ainen-Johansson first passage percolation defines a random directed metric on $\mathbb Z^2$ where the environment is updated according to a Poisson process. We show that its finite dimensional distributions converge after $0:1:2$ scaling to those of the Brownian web landscape defined on the finite dimensional marginals of the dynamical Brownian web. We prove non-uniqueness of geodesics in the Brownian web landscape and we relate it to exact formulas on one-sided reflected Brownian motions. We prove a locally uniform law of large numbers and uniform deviation bounds, and identify Poisson increment-stationary laws for the associated height evolution.

papers.title: Coarse geometry of stable mixed commutator length II: coarse kernels for nilpotent quotients
papers.authors: Morimichi Kawasaki, Mitsuaki Kimura, Shuhei Maruyama, Takahiro Matsushita, Masato Mimura
papers.abstract: This paper studies the global difference between the stable commutator length ${\rm scl}_G$ and the stable mixed commutator length ${\rm scl}_{G,N}$ from the perspective of coarse geometry, as well as the space ${\rm W}(G,N)$ of non-extendable quasimorphisms modulo invariant homomorphisms. Our main theorem concerns a finitely generated group $G$ and its normal subgroup $N$ such that the quotient group $ \Gamma = G/N$ is nilpotent. In this setting, we prove that the natural inclusion map of coarse groups from $[G,N]$ to $[G,G]$, equipped with the metrics induced by ${\rm scl}_{G,N}$ and ${\rm scl}_G$, respectively, is coarsely surjective. Moreover, this map has a splitting coarse kernel that is coarsely isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}^n, \| \cdot \|_1)$, where $n$ is the dimension of ${\rm W}(G,N)$. As a consequence, $[G,N]$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^n \times [G,G]$ as a coarse group.

papers.title: Quantitative flocking of Cucker-Smale flocks under time-delay and noise
papers.authors: Seung-Yeal Ha, Xinyu Wang, Chen Wu, Fanqin Zeng
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic flocking dynamics of the delayed stochastic Cucker-Smale (in short, DSCS) model driven by agent-wise independent, component-wise multiplicative Brownian noise. The simultaneous interplay of stochastic perturbations and time delay yields fundamental challenges to asymptotic stochastic flocking analysis, as the communication weight may lose a uniform positive lower bound, while the velocity moment is no longer monotone. To overcome these difficulties, we present a sufficient framework and an analytical tool combining the method of time-varying effective region and Lyapunov functional approach with time-delay corrections. This approach avoids any reliance on uniformly positive communication weights or monotone velocity moments. The proposed approach recovers sufficiently strong effective velocity alignment despite stochastic fluctuations and delay effects. As a consequence, we establish the mean-square stochastic flocking with an explicit polynomial convergence rate. The admissible decay exponent is determined by the communication kernel exponent and the orders of the spatial and velocity history moments. These results establish a quantitative theory for long-time stochastic flocking under simultaneous delay and multiplicative noise, and we provide a positive answer to an open problem raised by~[R. Erban, J. Haskovec, Y. Sun, SIAM J. Appl. Math., 76, 1535--1557 (2016)]. We also develop robust analytical tools applicable to delayed stochastic collective dynamics with degenerate communications.

papers.title: Nonsense nonlinear correlations between independent random walks
papers.abstract: Sample distance correlation can remain large between independent random walks. For centred walks with independent, identically distributed increments of finite, positive variance, we prove convergence in distribution to the distance correlation of the joint occupation measure of two independent Brownian paths. This universal limit lies strictly between zero and one almost surely and has full support on the unit interval. We calculate the expected squared distance covariance of the limiting measure and show that ordinary permutation calibration rejects independence with probability tending to one at every fixed nominal level. Gaussian simulations illustrate the persistent dispersion of random-walk correlations and the failure of permutation calibration.

papers.title: Optimal control for an anisotropic Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system
papers.abstract: We study an optimal control problem aimed at enhancing mixing in anisotropic electrolytes described by an instationary Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system in three space dimensions, where the anisotropy is encoded by a given director field in the diffusion and permittivity matrices. The control is the external electric potential entering through the Robin boundary condition of the Poisson equation. The cost functional combines tracking-type terms for the charge concentrations and an $L^2$-regularization of the control with a negative vorticity term that favors rotational flow. Assuming that the diffusion and permittivity matrices coincide, we first prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions with nonnegative, essentially bounded concentrations, together with Lipschitz continuous dependence on the control. Since, through the negative vorticity term, the cost functional is no longer weakly lower semicontinuous, existence of an optimal control relies on strong convergence of the velocity gradients. Finally, we prove Fr\'echet differentiability of the control-to-state operator, introduce the adjoint system, and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions in the form of a variational inequality.

papers.title: Quantitative Accumulation of Invariant Circles Near a Non-splitting Separatrix
papers.abstract: For a smooth area-preserving cylinder map with a non-splitting separatrix and an exact symplectic linearization at its saddle, we prove accumulation by smooth essential invariant circles when the boundary transition is sufficiently $C^4$-close to a translation. As an application, we give an answer to Herman's open problem in 1983.

papers.title: Optimal One Health control of antimicrobial resistance: a household mean-field model with community feedback and parameters from Burkina Faso
papers.authors: Mifiamba Soma, Pingawind\'e Sawadogo, Yisso Fid\`ele Bacye, Evariste Bako, Mari\'etou Sissao, Maurice Sarigda, Adama Kiemde
papers.abstract: We study how to combine three One Health interventions against antimicrobial resistance: prescription-only dispensing of antibiotics to people, access to veterinary care for animals, and treatment of household sludge and manure. Each household is a Markov chain on the carriage states of its people, animals and soil, and households are linked through the community, whose prevalence feeds the acquisition rates. We prove that, as the number of households grows, the distribution of household states converges to the solution of a nonlinear mean-field equation. This system is monotone for the stochastic order, so that no intervention increases carriage anywhere, and for every constant intervention it has exactly one equilibrium, which attracts all solutions and is given by a scalar equation. For the optimal control problem we prove existence, necessary conditions, positivity of all controls under a quadratic cost, uniqueness for short horizons, and a turnpike property under an explicit dissipativity condition, which we verify for our parameters by a computer-assisted numerical certification. With parameters from Tenkodogo, Burkina Faso, the optimal combined strategy averts about 17% of human carriage over three years in the baseline scenario, and 11% to 28% over the plausible scenarios for the parameters that the survey cannot identify; these figures are projections conditional on the model. The strategy itself is robust: the value of perfect information on the unmeasured parameters is about 2% of the achievable benefit. A compartmental model with the same transmission rates but without households underestimates the benefit, and targeting the interventions by zone of the town increases it.

papers.title: A Weighted Second-Order Nonlocal Total Variation Regularizer for Image Restoration
papers.authors: Francesc Alcover, Joan Duran, Catalina Sbert
papers.abstract: Despite the remarkable progress of deep learning in image processing, variational methods remain a fundamental and actively developing framework, offering interpretability, mathematical rigor, and well-founded guarantees. In this work, we introduce a weighted second-order nonlocal total variation regularizer for image restoration, which is based on measuring gradient differences across the image domain and allows for weights that are neither smooth nor symmetric and may vanish outside a search window. We first provide a rigorous definition of the regularizer and prove that it enjoys several desirable properties under realistic assumptions on the underlying weight function. We then consider a nonlocal variant of the variational image restoration model of Chambolle and Lions, and prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the associated minimization problem. On the computational side, we develop a discrete formulation of the model and derive the corresponding Chambolle-Pock primal-dual algorithm. Finally, we conduct an extensive experimental evaluation, comparing the proposed regularizer with a range of local and nonlocal, first- and second-order regularizers across several image restoration tasks. The results demonstrate its strong noise-suppression and texture-preservation capabilities, as well as its robustness to nonlocal weights computed under non-ideal conditions.

papers.title: On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds
papers.abstract:
A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(\eta,\omega)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $\eta$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $\omega$ satisfying
  \[
  d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega.
  \]
  We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families.
  Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $\alpha$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by
  \[
  \eta=\pi_2^*\xi,\qquad
  \omega=d(\pi_1^*\alpha)+\pi_1^*\alpha\wedge\eta,
  \]
  where $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $\xi$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular,
  none of these compact
  homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic
  structure, even without any invariance assumption.
  As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.

papers.title: Bloch groups of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$
papers.abstract: We give a generic presentation of the pre-Bloch group of a local ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$. We apply this to the calculation of pre-Bloch groups and Bloch groups of some local rings.

papers.title: The Query Complexity of Unknown Sparse Gradient Residuals
papers.abstract:
We study optimization of an average of \(n\) functions when gradient predictions are exact except for at most \(k\) unknown components. An initial scan may miss these exceptions.
  For a class of smooth problems, we prove that the optimal worst-case expected number of component-gradient evaluations needed to find an approximate stationary point is \[ \Theta\!\left(\min\left\{nk+\mathcal R,\frac nk\mathcal R\right\}\right), \] where \(\mathcal R\) represents the optimal cost when the exceptional components are known. Prediction evaluations are free.
  This bound shows that discovering even a few exceptions can cost more than one full scan and can account for most of the gradient evaluations.

papers.title: Variational approximation by complex Gaussians for the nonlinear logarithmic equation
papers.authors: Marianne Curely (UA, LAREMA), Lysianne Hari (UMLP, LMB)
papers.abstract: We consider the semiclassical logarithmic Schr{\"o}dinger equation, with an at most quadratic potential and with Gaussian initial states. For a critical nonlinear term in the semiclassical regime, we analyze an approximation based on the variational evolution of Gaussian wave packets. We also prove a nonlinear superposition principle for solutions issued from the sum of two Gaussian wave packets initially localized at distinct points in phase space. For both a single Gaussian wave packet and a superposition of two Gaussian wave packets, we compare the variational approximation with the standard coherent-state approximation and highlight their respective features. The required assumptions are weakened in this setting without becoming technically involved.

papers.title: Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS
papers.abstract: The performance of Zak-OTFS modulation depends critically on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain pulse shaping filter, which must support both accurate channel estimation and reliable data detection. Filters reported in the Zak-OTFS literature fall short in bit error rate (BER) performance for higher-order modulation due to sensitivity to model-free channel estimation errors and pilot-data interference. Motivated by this, in this paper, we introduce a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS and propose a filter coefficient optimization framework that minimizes the aggregate sidelobe energy while preserving the compact structure of the MM prototype. By trading exact Nyquist nulls for high localization, the optimized MM filter exhibits no sidelobes with the narrowest $-40$ dB DD domain pulsewidth compared to sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses. This compactness of the optimized filter tightly confines the pilot energy within the pilot region of the embedded frame, ensuring that the full response is captured for model-free channel estimation while significantly reducing pilot-data interference. This yields both an improved estimation performance and a significantly improved BER performance for higher-order QAM. For the proposed filter, we derive closed-form expressions for the effective DD domain channel and the covariance of the receive-filtered noise, which drastically reduce simulation run times. Our simulation results demonstrate that the optimized MM filter achieves significantly better uncoded/coded BER performance for higher-order QAM compared to that of sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters. For example, for 64-QAM with M=32, N=48, rate-1/2 convolutional code, and TDL-A channel model with fractional DDs, the optimized MM filter achieves a coded BER of 3x10^{-4} at an E_b/N_0 of 40 dB, while the sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters exhibit error floors above 10^{-2}.

papers.title: On 2-Homogeneous Colourings of Cubic Bipartite Graphs
papers.authors: Rong-Xia Hao, Jianbing Liu, Federico Romaniello
papers.abstract: A proper vertex colouring is 2-homogeneous if every open neighbourhood contains exactly two colours. We show that every cubic bipartite graph admits a 2-homogeneous colouring with at most four colours, proving a conjecture of Janicov\'a, Madaras, Sot\'ak and Lu\v{z}ar. For 3-connected det-extremal cubic bipartite graphs, we establish the stronger bound $\chi_h^{(2)}(G) = 3$, showing that every such graph admits a fall 3-colouring.

papers.title: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
papers.authors: Sutirtha Datta, Sourav Ghosh, Aniruddha Maji, Antara Manik
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
papers.abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

papers.title: Exact Tur\'an densities of even zycles
papers.abstract: We determine the exact Tur\'an density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 4$ with $3\nmid\ell$, showing that $\pi(Z_\ell)=5/9$. More generally, we prove that $\pi(Z_\ell)\le 5/9$ for all even $\ell\ge 4$. In the range of equality, we also establish a stability theorem, showing that every almost extremal $Z_\ell$-free $3$-graph is close in edit distance to the classical Tur\'an construction.

papers.title: Complete enumeration of maximal T-curves in degrees eight and nine
papers.authors: Zoe Geiselmann, Michael Joswig, Lars Kastner, Marcel Wack
papers.abstract: We use a highly parallelized backtracking algorithm implemented in CUDA to enumerate every compatible collection of Harnack splits in degrees eight and nine. By a theorem of Haas (1997) this yields every maximal T-curve. In this way, we find that exactly 38 real schemes of real plane algebraic curves of degree eight with 22 real components and 225 of degree nine with 29 real components are realized by combinatorial patchworking.

papers.title: On the size of the defect set of an analytic matrix field
papers.abstract: In this note, we study the defect set of a symmetric analytic matrix field $M$ defined on an open set $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge2$. A defect point $x \in \Omega$ of $M$ is defined as a point for which no eigenframe can be chosen continuously in any neighborhood of $x$. We show that the defect set $S(M)$ is contained in a locally finite union of analytic submanifolds of codimension at least $2$. The proof follows fairly directly from results by Parusinski and Rond (Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 2020) and by Kurdyka and Paunescu (Duke Math. J., 2008). This result can be applied in the context of the Landau-de Gennes Theory to estimate the physical defects of a nematic liquid crystal.

papers.title: A Derivative-Free Bellman Equation for Dynamic Time-to-Collision: Two-Sided Certificates and Explicit ReLU Approximation
papers.abstract: Dynamic time-to-collision (TTC) is the first contact time of a prediction flow and defines a feedback map implicitly. We study its capped value function $\VV$ for Carath\'eodory dynamics with bounded, measurable forcing. A self-contained argument establishes local Lipschitz continuity on the transversal collision domain. A derivative-free stopped-step Bellman equation then characterizes $\VV$ uniquely: it advances the prediction for a fixed duration or until contact and adds the elapsed time. A two-sided error bound uses only the candidate's residual along complete stopped trajectories and its error at their endpoints. Exact continuum iteration recovers $\VV$ after finitely many sweeps, including one additional sweep for initializations that violate the boundary condition. We also characterize an optional-duration infimum operator: its fixed points are the dynamic-programming subsolutions, so its residual alone does not identify $\VV$. Finally, on compact subsets of the transversal domain, an optimization-free ReLU construction has explicit size, controlled local residual, and robustness to errors in its nodal TTC values. The optimal velocity model provides the running application.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verd\'u--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

papers.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
papers.abstract: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $\zeta$-function $\zeta_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $\zeta$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.

papers.title: Refined critical flux bounds for Leray's problem in a pipe with the Navier-slip boundary
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness for stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes flows in infinite pipes with the Navier-slip boundary. For a cylindrical pipe of unit radius and a positive friction ratio, uniqueness holds when $|\Phi|\leq 2\pi\sqrt{40/7}\approx 15$. This significantly improves upon the result of the first author, Liu and Zhou (J. Differential Equations 461:114108, 2026) where the uniqueness requires $|\Phi|\leq \pi/16\approx 0.2$. For small positive friction ratio $\alpha$, this flux condition can be improved to $|\Phi|\leq 4\sqrt{2}\,\pi^2/\alpha$. For an infinite pipe with a bounded, smooth, simply connected cross-section $\Sigma$, we prove uniqueness for every $0<\alpha<\infty$ provided that $|\Phi|\leq c_\Sigma(1+\alpha)/\alpha$, where $c_\Sigma>0$ depends only on $\Sigma$.

papers.title: Exact Fourier Coupling Relations for the Method of Auxiliary Sources on Elliptic Cylinders
papers.authors: Prisca Le Dily, Arnaud Coatanhay, Marie Kintzinger, Yves-Marie Scolan
papers.abstract: The Method of Auxiliary Sources has been extensively studied in the case of cylindrical geometries. In this article, the authors provide analysis elements for the elliptical geometry case. Based on a Mathieu functions expansion, the impedance matrix is projected into a reduced diagonal matrix. At the same time, the matrix is studied in the Fourier domain. A checkerboard structure is found and a relation between the different elements of the matrix is proven. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results. We additionally identify an exact finite-grid parity rule, an aliasing identity connecting the discrete and continuous Fourier representations, and controlled near-circular Fourier-band localization. These results are mostly independent of a small-$q$ truncation of radial Mathieu functions.

papers.title: Strict $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-triangulation of subanalytic sets in low dimensions
papers.authors: Jos{\'e} F. Fernando, Riccardo Ghiloni, Wies{\l}aw Paw{\l}ucki
papers.abstract:
Let $R$ be a real closed field expanded by an o-minimal structure, let $A$ be a definable, closed and bounded subset of $R^n$ and let $p$ be a positive integer. It was recently shown in \cite{pa2} that $A$ admits a strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation $({\mathcal T},h)$, i.e., there exist a finite simplicial complex ${\mathcal T}$ in $R^n$ and a homeomorphism $h:|{\mathcal T}|\to A$ that is definable and of class ${\mathcal C}^p$.
  The aim of this article is to analyze a generalization of the notion of strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation of subanalytic sets to the case $p=\infty$. Examples in dimension $n=3$ show that such a generalization is not always possible within subanalytic geometry, where the class ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ is equivalent to the class ${\mathcal C}^\omega$. We formulate the conjecture that strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulations of subanalytic sets always exist in the wider o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, generated by subanalytic sets and the exponential function. We check the conjecture for all subanalytic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n\leq 3$, and prepare tools to address the conjecture for arbitrary $n$.
  We also apply the obtained strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulation results to approximate subanalytic continuous mappings $f:X\to Y$ between subanalytic sets $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-mappings $g:X\to Y$ definable in the o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, with respect to the strong Whitney ${\mathcal C}^0$ topology. If the continuous mapping $f:X\to Y$ is not necessarily subanalytic, we can still approximate it by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ mappings $g:X\to Y$.

papers.title: The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees
papers.abstract: We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root. The Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of vertices, and the terminal Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of leaves. Dividing by the number of pairs of vertices and pairs of leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance between vertices and average distance between leaves. For two important classes of random trees, we show that the average distance of the root to a random leaf is almost the same as the average distance to a random vertex and that the average distance between vertices is almost the same as the average distance between leaves. For Bienaym\'e--Galton--Watson trees, each of these differences is bounded in probability. For three varieties of increasing trees (recursive trees, $d$-ary increasing trees, generalised plane-oriented recursive trees), on the other hand, the differences converge to constants in probability. This allows the transfer of convergence results for the path length to the external path length, and results for the Wiener index to be transferred to the terminal Wiener index.

papers.title: Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
papers.authors: Miaomiao Lv, Juan Zhang, Zhen Jin
papers.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences. First, based on the SEAIR free-transmission model, we derive transmission characteristics, including the generation interval, the serial interval, the basic reproduction number, and the effective reproduction number, and describe the incidence using a renewal equation. Second, by considering two detection routes, we further obtain the distribution and mean of the IDH under different detection settings and quantify the infection size at the time of outbreak detection. Third, intervention measures are incorporated to derive a post-detection transmission model with generally distributed stage durations, followed by the derivation of the corresponding model under exponentially distributed stage durations and the determination of the final infection size. Finally, under the exponential-distribution assumption, the model is applied to the COVID-19 outbreak in Xi'an. The unified framework developed in this study provides a theoretical basis for evaluating early surveillance capacity for emerging infectious diseases, optimizing testing strategies, and determining the intensity of prevention and control measures after outbreak detection.

papers.title: Time-changed Compound Poisson Process
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a time-changed compound Poisson process (TCCPP) obtained by subordinating the classical compound Poisson process (CPP) with a subordinator and an inverse subordinator, which are defined via distinct Bernstein functions. We study the governing equations and distributional properties of a TCCPP including its moments, dependence structure and limiting behaviour. We derive distributions of the integrated CPP and a linear combination of TCCPPs. We also obtain the law of iterated logarithm, the central limit theorem and weighted sum representation for a TCCPP. Finally, we provide some characterizations of a TCCPP in terms of martingales, a univariate multinomial process, a triangular array process and waiting time distribution. The proposed framework generalizes several existing fractional stochastic processes and offers greater flexibility for modelling complex count data.

papers.title: Immaculate complexes and Strong Generation by Injectives
papers.abstract: We study the category of bounded complexes of finite sums of indecomposable injectives over a locally Noetherian scheme, which we call the immaculate complexes. We show that regularity and finiteness of dimension can be detected from this category using strong generation. Our methods involve studying when the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category is strongly generated by injectives. As applications we prove a conjecture of Hartshorne and recover a result of Keller and Krause. To any specialisation closed subset we associate a semi-orthogonal decomposition of the immaculates and use this to compute additive finitary invariants in terms of the completions of the local rings. The immaculates are equivalent to the perfect derived category of a left coherent preadditive category i.e. a ring with many objects and we compute this category for one-dimensional integral or Gorenstein schemes.

papers.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
papers.authors: Linus Behn, Roberto Colombo, Xavier Fern\'andez-Real, Florian Grube, Harsh Prasad, Xavier Ros-Oton
papers.abstract: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies asks whether uniform ellipticity implies $H^s$-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels of order $2s$, with $0<s<1$. We show that the conjecture fails whenever $n>2s$ for every $s \in (0,1)$ and $n \geq 1$, even for smooth compactly supported test functions; for $n=1$ and $s>1/2$, we show that it holds. The construction also gives bounded discontinuous weak solutions in $H^s_{\rm loc}$ to nonlocal equations in divergence form with kernels in this class. Despite the failure, we show that the conjecture holds for several important classes of kernels. We establish a general local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, which applies in particular to kernels satisfying both divergence- and nondivergence-form symmetry. The criterion also allows us to treat kernels comparable to stable kernels with bounded measurable coefficients, as well as non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels under a geometric nonconcentration assumption. As an application, we obtain a short and self-contained proof of the Gressman--Strain anisotropic coercivity estimate. Furthermore, by combining our new criterion with existing regularity results, we obtain H\"older estimates under ellipticity and cancellation assumptions.

papers.title: Fluctuations of Local Patterns in Non-Periodic Uniquely Ergodic Systems
papers.abstract: We study various families of non-periodic configurations of symbols assigned to vertices of regular graphs. We restrict ourselves to such systems where considered configurations support a uniquely ergodic measure. Symbols can be interpreted as particles and we are concerned with configurations which minimize the interaction energy of particles, the so-called ground-state configurations. One of the main questions then is whether ground-state configurations are stable with respect to small perturbations of interactions. Such stability may be interpreted as a sort of rigidity of non-periodic structures such as tilings, substitution systems, Sturmian systems, and other uniquely ergodic non-periodic systems. We introduce a property of bounded fluctuations of finite patterns of non-periodic configurations, the so-called Strict Boundary Property. We discuss how relevant this property is for stability of non-periodic structures. Examples of Robinson's tilings, Thue-Morse, and Sturmian systems are presented. Some open problems are formulated.

papers.title: An Analytic Toroidal MHD Equilibrium with Trivial Euclidean Symmetry Group
papers.abstract: We provide a method to construct a real-analytic ideal MHD equilibrium $(B,p)$ in a solid toroidal domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$, with $B$ tangential to the boundary $\partial\Omega$. The regular pressure level sets foliate $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ by nested tori surrounding a magnetic axis $\Gamma$, with $\nabla p\neq0$ away from the axis. We construct an example where the magnetic field is nonvanishing on $\Omega$, and the rotational transform equals 2 on every regular pressure surface. The equilibrium has a trivial Euclidean symmetry group. It is non-isolated in the sense that it belongs to a real-analytic one-parameter family connecting it to an axisymmetric equilibrium. The toroidal domain, magnetic field and pressure vary smoothly along this family. Under the MHD--Euler correspondence, the construction also yields a real-analytic steady incompressible Euler flow with a nonconstant Bernoulli function. This constructively disproves one formulation of Grad's conjecture by exhibiting a smooth toroidal MHD equilibrium with nested pressure surfaces whose Euclidean symmetry group is trivial.

papers.title: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
papers.abstract: We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. As a consequence, the validity of dimension-free moment criteria for entanglement in quantum information is undecidable. Second, we present a homogeneous symmetric function of degree 8 which is positive definite in every dimension but admits no sum of squares multiplier that is uniform in the number of variables. Consequently, Artin's solution of Hilbert's 17th problem and the Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz have no any-dimensional analog and any-dimensional Positivstellens\"atze asked for by Levin and Chandrasekaran cannot hold in general.

papers.title: Free G\"odel algebras over G\"odel hoops
papers.abstract: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from G\"odel algebras to G\"odel hoops. If $H$ is a G\"odel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the G\"odel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a G\"odel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary G\"odel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of G\"odel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of G\"odel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between G\"odel algebras and G\"odel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.

papers.title: The q-Jack Lemma and Its Applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a Jackson $q$-difference analogue of Jack's lemma and its higher-order extension by Miller and Mocanu, which serve as cornerstone tools in geometric function theory and differential subordination. Applying this foundation, we establish $q$-counterparts of Nunokawa's boundary theorem and the Miller-Mocanu subordination lemma, and deduce applications to circular enclosure bounds. All obtained results naturally recover their classical counterparts in the limiting case as $q \to 1^-$.

papers.title: Normal Squeezing and Strict Pseudoconvexity
papers.abstract: We prove that a boundary point $p$ of a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, is strictly pseudoconvex if the boundary is locally $C^{2,\alpha}$ near $p$, $0<\alpha\le1$, and the squeezing function tends to one along the inward normal. Neither finite type nor convexity is assumed. Under local $C^2$ regularity alone, the same limit gives the normal logarithmic Bergman-kernel growth exponent $n+1$. The proof uses normalized Bergman-kernel profiles and holomorphic translation semigroups on the ball.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery and Rigorous Certification of Periodic Solutions in Infinite-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
papers.authors: Aaron Loh, J. D. Mireles James
papers.abstract:
In this work, we consider a standard regression technique for time series analysis which fits a low-dimensional proxy system to a higher (even infinite) dimensional target model. We then propose a novel diagnostic that exploits a-posteriori computer-assisted proofs, and try to certify the existence of a true periodic solution of the target, nearby. When successful, this certification procedure provides mathematically rigorous information about how well an invariant structure in the proxy approximates a corresponding invariant structure in the target model.
  To illustrate the utility of the procedure, we develop surrogates using time series data from the Mackey--Glass delay differential equation, and for the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) partial differential equation, using periodic boundary conditions for forecasting and Neumann boundary conditions for certification. In both test cases we extract invariant dynamics from low-dimensional proxies and use this to validate the existence of corresponding structures in the targets.

papers.title: Complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional: examples and rigidity
papers.authors: Giovanni Catino, Paolo Mastrolia, Dario Daniele Monticelli
papers.abstract: We study complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional \[ g\mapsto\int_M S_g^2\,\dv_g, \] with criticality understood under compactly supported variations, focusing on rigidity phenomena and nontrivial examples. In dimension three, we prove that every complete critical metric is scalar-flat, without any additional assumption. In dimension four, we construct complete non-Einstein critical metrics with bounded, nonconstant negative scalar curvature. In every dimension $n\geq5$, we show that either $S_g\equiv 0$ or $S_g<0$ everywhere, and a new argument proves scalar-flatness whenever $S_g \in L^p$ for some $0<p\leq P_n$, where $P_n>2$ is an explicit threshold. Moreover, we construct complete critical metrics with bounded, negative scalar curvature, decaying to zero at infinity. These examples establish the optimality of our rigidity threshold $P_n$ in dimension six and in every dimension $n\geq10$. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first complete critical metrics for this functional that are neither scalar-flat nor Einstein.

papers.title: Higher moments of twisted Kloosterman sums and the arithmetic of algebraic varieties
papers.abstract: For an odd prime $p,$ consider the affine varieties $X_k: \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(x_i+x_i^{-1})=0$ over the finite field $\F_p.$ In this paper, a key feature of our work is arithmetic interpretation between the higher power moments of Kloosterman sums, modular forms and arithmetic geometry of the varieties $X_5$ and $X_6$ through their rational point counts. Our main results provide two distinct explicit formulas for the point count $\#X_5(\F_p).$ In the first formula, we express $\#X_5(\F_p)$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms and a certain weighted average of fourth power twisted Kloosterman moments, where the average is taken over multiplicative characters. We further establish an identity expressing this weighted average of fourth power moment of twisted Kloosterman sums in terms of fifth power quadratic twisted Kloosterman moment, together with Fourier coefficients of modular forms. Moreover, we derive an independent expression for the same average with different weight directly in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms. In the second identity for $\#X_5(\F_p)$, we express this purely in terms of Fourier coefficients of two modular forms. Moreover, we express $\#X_6(\F_p),$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of three modular forms. For these two expressions of $\#X_5(\F_p)$ and $\#X_6(\F_p),$ our approach is based on an identity that relates the point counts of $X_k$ to the $k$-th power moments of Kloosterman sum and its quadratic twist.

papers.title: Continuous Grassmannian Brascamp--Lieb inequalities and their equality cases
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the forward and reverse geometric Brascamp--Lieb inequalities for isotropic measures on a Grassmann manifold, and characterize their equality conditions. The proofs use transportation and the Grassmannian Ball--Barthe inequality of Li, Xi, and Zhang. The functions form a jointly continuous family whose fiber integrals are positive and continuous. The equality conditions are described by an orthogonal decomposition determined by the supporting projections. On the common eigenspaces, the forward inequality permits arbitrary independent factors, whereas the reverse inequality requires log-concavity for factors shared by a nontrivial parameter distribution. On the orthogonal complement, the extremizers have Gaussian factors. Their centers are compatible projections in the forward inequality and may vary continuously between fibers in the reverse inequality. Gaussian convolution preserves extremizers, and the original factors are recovered at a fixed positive time using characteristic functions. As applications, we obtain Gaussian rigidity results and volume bounds for bodies defined by projection integrals and barycentric infima. These bounds recover the reverse isoperimetric inequalities of Li, Xi, and Zhang for bodies associated with Grassmannian cosine transforms, together with their equality conditions away from the endpoint cases. We also establish a forward extension under weaker mass assumptions and give a mass-escape example for the reverse inequality.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of self-similar blow-up for the two-dimensional Zakharov system
papers.authors: Tej-eddine Ghoul, Jie Liu, Nader Masmoudi
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic stability of the small-parameter Glangetas-Merle self-similar blow-up solutions of the two-dimensional Zakharov system under nonradial perturbations in the energy space. The proof establishes dissipation on the wave time scale by canceling the fast density coupling. We impose nonlinear orthogonality to the ground state of the density-dependent Schr\"odinger operator for modulation and use successive energy corrections after subtracting the instantaneous density response from the Schr\"odinger error. The resulting dissipation yields power-law decay of the rescaled errors in the Schr\"odinger gradient, weighted local mass, and wave energy norms.

papers.title: Exterior-Row Replacement for Grid-Based Multinode Shepard Collocation on Implicit Planar Domains
papers.authors: Anouar El Harrak, Amal Bergam, Hatim Tayeq
papers.abstract: Grid-based multinode Shepard collocation combines tensor-product Lagrange interpolants on overlapping Cartesian subgrids.
