On an implicitly defined domain, retained subgrids may cross the boundary and contain exterior source nodes. Removing or moving these nodes changes the local interpolants. We introduce exterior-row replacement (ERR) to preserve the source nodes and coefficients of every retained subgrid. We assemble PDE rows at strictly interior sources and supply the remaining equations through boundary evaluations. We consider two square completion methods based on projection and redistribution, an oversampled weighted least-squares one (ERR-OS), and a completion method that selects boundary rows through the interior PDE nullspace (ERR-QR). Full column rank is characterized by the boundary action on this nullspace. We also give completion conditions for prescribed fitted rows and an error estimate in terms of the residual. Global-full (GF) support uses all retained subgrids, whereas nearest-active (NA) support uses only those containing the active source nearest to the evaluation point. NA keeps off-source boundary rows sparse. The numerical study covers a disk, an annulus, a smooth star-shaped domain, a square hole with fitted and implicit boundary components, and a fitted L-shaped domain. With degree-$4$ local tensor polynomials, ERR-OS and ERR-QR recover the expected fifth-order accuracy in the reported refinement study. Further experiments examine the effects of boundary oversampling and trimming on algebraic admissibility and boundary observability.

papers.title: Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains
papers.abstract: For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $\Omega$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partial\Omega$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $\Omega = U$.

papers.title: Fluctuations of sample eigenvalues in a spiked covariance model with Haar-rotated spikes: a transition at $p^2 \asymp n$
papers.abstract: We study the outlying eigenvalues of a sample covariance matrix whose population covariance is itself random. The population covariance is $\Sigma_p=A_p+O_pB_pO_p^*+\sigma^2I_p$, where $A_p$ and $B_p$ are deterministic positive semidefinite matrices of fixed ranks $r$ and $s$, and where $O_p$ is Haar distributed on the orthogonal group in the real case, and on the unitary group in the complex case. Conditionally on $O_p$, we observe $n$ independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance $\Sigma_p$, and we build the sample covariance matrix $\widehat\Sigma_p$ from these vectors. The fluctuations of the spike eigenvalues of $\widehat\Sigma_p$ come from two different sources: the Haar matrix $O_p$, which displaces the population spikes at the scale $1/p$, and the sampling, which acts at the scale $n^{-1/2}$. Comparing these two scales amounts to comparing $p^2$ with $n$, so the ratio which governs the fluctuations is $p^2/n$, while in the classical spiked model it is the aspect ratio $p/n$. We give the limiting law of each spike in four regimes where $n,p\to \infty$. When $p/n\to c>0$, and when $p/n\to0$ with $p^2/n\to\infty$, the sampling term dominates, the limit does not depend on $O_p$ and is Gaussian, as in the classical spiked model. When $p^2/n\to0$, the Haar randomness dominates, and the limit is a weighted sum of independent $\chi^2_1$ variables in the real case, and of independent exponential variables in the complex case. When $p^2/n\to\tau\in(0,\infty)$, the two terms are of the same order, and the limit is the convolution of Gaussian and $\chi^2_1$ or Exponential variables. We then apply these results to a linear mixed model with a continuous batch effect, in which the Haar assumption is what makes the separation of the signal and of the batch possible, and we build a test for the value of a single spike.

papers.title: Strong Completeness of Provability Logic for Languages of size at most continuum
papers.abstract: We investigate the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ for an infinite set of propositional variables $\mathbb P$ over ordinal spaces equipped with the interval topology $\mathcal{I}_1$. For every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, we consider the set \[ \Gamma_\kappa= \{\Diamond p_\xi:\xi<\kappa\} \cup \{\Box(p_\xi\to\Diamond p_\eta):\xi<\eta<\kappa\}, \] and prove that $\Gamma_\kappa$ has a model on an ordinal space with $\mathcal{I}_1$ if and only if $\kappa\nrightarrow_{\mathrm{ipath}}(\omega)^2_{\omega,<\omega}$. We also prove that if $|\mathbb P|<\mathfrak p$, then $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ is strongly complete with respect to $(\omega^\omega+1,\mathcal I_1)$. Finally, we establish the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ with respect to the same space whenever $|\mathbb P|=\aleph_1$.

papers.title: Existence, Nonexistence, and Regularity Results for Supercritical Quasilinear Elliptic Problems with Hardy Potential
papers.authors: Boumediene Abdellaoui, Susana Merch\'an, Luigi Montoro
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we investigate the existence of solutions to the following supercritical elliptic problem involving the $p$-Laplace operator and the Hardy-Leray potential \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{rcll}
  -\Delta_p u +u^\beta|\nabla u|^p &= & {\vartheta} \dfrac{u^q }{|x|^p}+ f\;\; &\hbox{in } \Omega
  u &\geq & 0\;\; &\hbox{in } \Omega
  u &= & 0\;\;&\hbox{on } \partial\Omega, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where $0\in\Omega$. We analyze the effect of the perturbation term $u^\beta|\nabla u|^p$, with $\beta \geq 0$, and the role of the exponent $q$ on the existence of solutions. We also analyze nonexistence of solutions when $f$ is a singular measure. Finally, we focus on the regularity and asymptotic properties of these solutions.

papers.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
papers.abstract:
We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $
u^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $
u$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-r
u^{ rac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-
u t}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim 
u^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $
u$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$.

papers.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
papers.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the H\"older topology.

papers.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
papers.abstract: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation. For rational maps, a Grassmann-bundle model gives a Pl\"ucker degree formula and an interpretation by prescribed critical points. We relate these loci to factorization of the Bezoutian in the ring of symmetric polynomials, where factors correspond to monodromy orbits on unordered pairs. Fried's polynomial criterion then determines the invariant reducibility locus. For rational maps we determine its composition components when a marked pole fiber has exactly one ramified point and at least one unramified point. The qualitative equivalence between finite full orbits and a first integral is already known. We give a direct proof from forward stabilization, with an explicit test using bounded forward orbits and with quotient fibers identified at every point. We also determine when absolute and invariant irreducibility differ and give a growth formula for a class of translation correspondences.

papers.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
papers.abstract: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.

papers.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
papers.abstract: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.

papers.title: Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions
papers.abstract:
Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[
  b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[
  b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor}
  \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$. These bounds improve Lassak's bound $b(n)\le2^{n-1}+1$ of 1982 in every dimension $n\ge4$. In dimension four they also improve the recent bounds $b(4)\le8$ (Tolmachev and Voronov, May 2026) and $b(4)\le7$ (Arman, Bondarenko, Prymak and Radchenko, October 2026); the bound $b(4)\le6$ was announced independently by Chalmers in November 2026.
  The bounds for $n\ge7$ have analytic proofs: a quantitative form of Lassak's reduction to coverings of the sphere is combined with normal partitions of weighted vector configurations, for which the smallest inner product within a region is estimated explicitly. The bound for $n=6$ uses a covering of $S^4$ by thirty sets, checked in rational arithmetic. For $n=4,5$ three contact points of the circumscribed ball reduce the problem to a four-parameter family of bodies, which is split by finitely many power diagrams; that all parts have diameter less than one is verified by a computer program with rigorous error control.

papers.title: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
papers.authors: Yuji Ando, Edmund Chen, Go Kato, Toyohiro Tsurumaru, Derek Zhang, Donald Zvada
papers.abstract: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.

papers.title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fr\'echet differentiability
papers.abstract: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fr\'echet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Ti\v{s}er. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fr\'echet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.

papers.title: Data-Driven Robust Inventory Planning and Advertising under Product Return
papers.authors: Hongyan Zhang, Yugang Yu, Qinshen Tang, Ye Shi, Li Chen
papers.abstract: Online advertising is a central marketing lever for e-commerce retailers, yet it complicates operational planning by simultaneously stimulating product demand and increasing product returns. Motivated by the practice of a fashion retailer on Amazon, we study a retailer's joint inventory and advertising problem across multiple products over a single season, in which advertising has both direct and cross-product spillover effects on demand and returns. Using linear net-demand and return models that capture both effects, we formulate a contextual stochastic optimization model that jointly determines inventory levels and advertising decisions before the selling season. Because ad clicks are realized only after the advertising decision, the predictive covariates are partially observable and decision-dependent, and their joint distribution with the demand and return errors is unknown. We therefore develop an estimate-then-robustify (ETR) approach grounded in a data-driven robust satisficing framework. We establish a finite-sample guarantee on the out-of-sample profit of the ETR solution that holds for any parameter estimator, show that the solution is asymptotically optimal when the estimator is consistent and the profit target approaches the empirical optimal profit, and derive a mixed-integer conic approximation via affine recourse adaptation that is exact for a single product. On the retailer's data, ETR improves out-of-sample profit over conventional estimate-then-optimize by 6.39\% and earns the higher profit in 74.5% of instances, with the largest gains when training data are scarce; the gain falls to 1.02% when the decision model omits cross-product spillovers.

papers.title: Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
papers.abstract: This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.

papers.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

papers.title: Parameter estimation in models with explosive drift and Gaussian noise
papers.authors: Yuliya Mishura, Kostiantyn Ralchenko, Mykyta Yakovliev
papers.abstract: We study drift parameter estimation for a positive stochastic process with singular mean-reverting drift driven by Gaussian noise. For Riemann-Liouville fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$, an observable fractional transformation reduces the model to a semimartingale with drift linear in the unknown parameters. Using the quasi-likelihood approach, we derive explicit estimators of both drift coefficients. For a broader class of Gaussian driving processes, we construct a strongly consistent estimator of the ratio $a/b$, which has a natural mean-reversion interpretation, and verify the required assumptions for several Gaussian models. The theoretical results are complemented by a simulation study investigating the effects of the observation horizon and the discretization step on the finite-sample accuracy of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Finite Bodies on Norton's Dome: Escape-Time Divergence and a Center-of-Mass Barrier Theorem
papers.abstract: Norton's dome illustrates how a Newtonian initial-value problem can admit both rest and delayed departure from the same initial state. We examine how this nonuniqueness changes when the point particle is replaced by a rigid sphere of positive radius. For a generalized family of Norton's domes, we show that any fixed positive sphere radius prevents spontaneous departure from rest at the apex. We then extend the analysis to more general bodies and establish two sufficient conditions: a geometric constraint on the distance between the center of mass and the apex, and an interior tangent ball condition for rigid bodies whose center of mass is vertically aligned with the initial contact point. Both arguments combine geometric estimates with an energy inequality and Gr\"onwall's inequality. The first condition also applies to passive deformable bodies without releasable internal energy. These results identify explicit conditions under which finite-body geometry excludes the spontaneous motion allowed by Norton's point-particle model.

papers.title: Nevanlinna theory for generalized tropical meromorphic functions and applications to ultra-discrete equations
papers.authors: Tingbin Cao, Risto Korhonen, Yuting Wang
papers.abstract:
The main purpose of this paper is to establish the tropical Nevanlinna theory to piecewise linear real functions with arbitrary first-kind discontinuities (called generalized tropical meromorphic functions). The key point is that we introduce the directional jump counting functions $J^+(r,f)$ and $J^-(r,f)$ for the case of arbitrary first-kind discontinuities to refine the single function $J(r,f)$ in the previous theory. We first obtain the new tropical version of the Poisson-Jensen formula, the first main theorem. Under the assumption that $f$ is slope-admissible, we show that $T(r,f)$ is nondecreasing and establish a logarithmic derivative lemma. These results unify the classical continuous case due to Halburd and Southall and the one-sided continuous case due to Halonen, Korhonen and Filipuk.
  As applications, we study several first-order and second-order ultra-discrete equations, showing that certain equations admit infinitely many generalized tropical meromorphic solutions, and that under suitable conditions infinite-order solutions also exist. Finally, using the logarithmic derivative lemma obtained above, we establish a tropical Clunie lemma.

papers.title: Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.

papers.title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
papers.authors: Yen-Chang Huang (Department of Applied Mathematics, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan), Yan-Hong Chen (Department of Applied Mathematics, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan)
papers.abstract:
This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $\pi$.
  We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints.
  We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.

papers.title: Observability from Measurable Sets for Heat Equations with Bounded Space-Time Potentials
papers.abstract: We establish final-state observability for heat equations with real-valued bounded space--time potentials on bounded $C^2$ domains, from arbitrary measurable space--time sets of positive measure. On $\mathbb R^n$, we prove observability from time-dependent sets whose spatial slices are uniformly thick on a set of times of positive measure. A counterexample for the free heat equation on $\mathbb R$ shows that integral thickness alone is insufficient for observability.

papers.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schr\"odinger algebras
papers.abstract: We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schr\"odinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schr\"odinger algebras to have bracket width one.

papers.title: Morse index, nullity and Jacobi fields of homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics
papers.authors: Qing Chen, Shuping Huang, Shoulan Yi
papers.abstract: We determine the Morse index and normal nullity of all linearly full homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics. These invariants satisfy a common relation involving only the ambient dimension and the induced Gauss curvature. We also prove that every normal Jacobi field is integrable through minimal immersions.

papers.title: Automatic Threshold Selection Leaves Finite-Degree Bias in Network Power-Law Fits
papers.abstract: Minimum-distance fitting selects a degree threshold and a power-law exponent from the same network. We study the procedure that fits a continuous Pareto law with the Hill estimator and minimizes the Kolmogorov--Smirnov distance over retained ranks. For homogeneous linear preferential attachment and Norros--Reittu graphs with Pareto weights, we derive the joint limiting law of the selected rank, retained fraction of the threshold tie, and exponent error. The selector retains of order $n^{2/(\alpha+2)}$ of $n$ vertices, where $\alpha$ is the survival exponent. At this rank, integer spacing and finite-degree departures from a Pareto tail have the same order as sampling fluctuations. The exponent estimate is consistent and retains a shift on the scale used for confidence intervals. For integer degree laws whose tail sums have a first-order inverse-degree expansion, adding the retained tie fraction divided by the threshold to the Hill statistic removes the leading contribution of the tie. Under homogeneous preferential attachment with a fixed known number of edges per new vertex, removing the remaining model-specific term and calibrating for selection gives confidence intervals with asymptotically exact coverage. Observed networks show sensitivity of the fitted exponent and the classification of degree variance to threshold ties. Simulations assess interval coverage and show improved pooled connectivity predictions after correction under both specified graph laws. Changes to the Norros--Reittu weight distribution can reverse the prediction gain.

papers.title: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $\Gamma$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $\Gamma$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $\Gamma$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $\Gamma$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Ab\'ert et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.

papers.title: A new proof of nonamenability for free Burnside groups of odd exponent
papers.authors: Anna Cascioli, Sam Shepherd, Katrin Tent
papers.abstract: We prove that the free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is nonamenable for every $m\ge 2$ and every odd exponent $n\ge 557$. This improves Adian's bound $n\ge 665$ and matches the infiniteness bound of Atkarskaya, Rips and Tent. Our proof combines their canonical form construction with a counting argument to obtain an explicit isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs
papers.abstract:
When solving a number of additive problems with almost equal summands, along with estimating short trigonometric sums with primes of the form $$ S_k(\alpha;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}\Lambda(n)e(\alpha n^k), $$ on the minor arcs, estimates of these sums on the major arcs are also needed, except in a small neighborhood of their centers, as well as an asymptotic formula in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs.
  In this paper, using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line, for $S_k(\alpha;x,y)$ on the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}(\mathscr{L}^b)$, $\tau=y^5x^{-2}\mathscr{L}^{-b_1}$, $\mathscr{L} =\ln xq$, except in a small neighborhood of their centers $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|>\left(2\pi k^2x^{k-2}y^2\right)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{1}{2k-1+\eta_k}}\mathscr{L}^{c_k}$, $$ \eta_k=\frac{2}{4k-5+2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}}, \qquad c_k=
  \frac{2A+22+\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2k-3}}{\sqrt{2k-2}}-1\right)b_1}{2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}-(2k-3)}, $$ a nontrivial estimate of the form $$ S_k(\alpha;x,y)\ll y\mathscr{L}^{-A}, $$ is obtained, where $A$, $b_1$, $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive numbers, and an asymptotic formula is proved in a small neighborhood of the centers of the major arcs.

papers.title: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
Explicit Edit Codes via Multicoloring
papers.abstract: For any fixed integers $q\ge2$ and $t\ge1$, we construct explicit $q$-ary codes of length $n$ that correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions, with redundancy at most $2t\log_q n+O_{q,t}(\log\log n)$ $q$-ary symbols. This matches the leading redundancy term of Levenshtein's classical existential bound. Building on the standard graph-coloring approach, we use a prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph to assign multiple colors to each $q$-ary word of length $m<n$. Appending a short, edit-protected representation of an assigned color to the length-$m$ word yields a length-$n$ codeword. The choice among the assigned colors carries additional message information, thereby reducing the redundancy. The construction admits deterministic encoding and decoding in $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{6t+2})$ and $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{7t+2})$ time, respectively.

papers.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
papers.abstract: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.

papers.title: An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
papers.authors: A. Yu. Chirkov, S. I. Veselov, D. V. Gribanov, D. S. Malyshev, N. Yu. Zolotykh
papers.abstract: We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question. For an $n$-dimensional corner polyhedron associated with an integer lattice of determinant $\delta$, the number of edges is at most $$ O\left(n6^n \cdot \bigl(1+\log_2(2\delta)\bigr)^{2n-3}\right). $$ This improves the standard bound obtained by counting pairs of vertices, reducing the logarithmic exponent from $(2n-2)$ to $(2n-3)$.

papers.title: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
papers.abstract:
The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''.
  Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter.
  For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.

papers.title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
papers.authors: Ronghao Cui, Jan Martin Nordbotten, Ivar Stefansson, Inga Berre
papers.abstract: Numerical simulations of fracture propagation require accurate computation of stress intensity factors (SIFs) to determine whether a pre-existing fracture will propagate. Even though displacement solutions from well-established numerical methods generally converge with mesh refinement, the convergence behavior of SIF estimates remains less understood. In this work, we propose a scaling law to improve the performance of SIF extraction using two-point displacement correlation methods. This scaling law relates sampling distance from the fracture tip to mesh resolution. It is developed by balancing the asymptotic truncation error against the numerical discretization error. Three numerical discretization methods--standard quadratic finite elements, quadratic finite elements with quarter-point elements, and a multi-point stress approximation finite volume method--are employed to validate the proposed scaling law on fracture benchmark problems under pure-mode and mixed-mode loading. We find that the conventional nearest-tip sampling strategy fails to compute convergent SIF estimates. In contrast, the proposed scaling-based approach yields decreasing errors in the SIF estimates as the mesh is refined. Across all three discretization methods, the proposed scaling law captures the sampling locations required for convergent SIF extraction, suggesting a general numerical characteristic of near-tip SIF extraction.

papers.title: On the quasi-static growth of cavities in incompressible elastomers
papers.abstract: For a variational model of incompressible elastomers exhibiting cavitation, we establish the existence of irreversible quasi-static evolutions driven by time-dependent boundary conditions. Our result extends previous work by Mora-Corral (2014) to incompressible materials under weaker regularity assumptions on the boundary datum. The proof employs the multiplicative splitting introduced by Francfort and Mielke (2006) to reduce the problem to time-independent boundary conditions and then invokes abstract results on the existence of energetic solutions to rate-independent systems. Specifically, the construction of mutual recovery sequences requires particular attention to accommodate the incompressibility constraint: to this end we employ the method by Moser (1965) to exhibit incompressible diffeomorphisms interpolating between localized translations and the identity.

papers.title: Gamma-positivity of support enumerators of preorders
papers.abstract: The support enumerator of a finite preorder counts lattice points of its polytope by support size. We prove Athanasiadis and Chapoton's conjecture that this polynomial is $\gamma$-positive. On an $n$-element preorder, the $j$th $\gamma$-coefficient counts points of the preorder polytope with entries in $\{0,1,2\}$, coordinate sum $n$, and exactly $j$ entries equal to $2$. Oh's correspondence for transversal matroids and Hall's theorem give a formula that records the support itself. For arbors, a separate proof gives a refinement by coordinate sum.

papers.title: Incidence Geometry with Polarity and Tiled Surfaces
papers.authors: Peixuan Liu, Zhiyuan Liu, Yuanqi Jiang
papers.abstract: In 2023, Fomin and Pylyavskyy introduced the master theorem to find and prove linear incidence theorems using quadrilateral tilings of oriented surfaces. Each face of the surface corresponds to an incidence condition, which they call a coherence condition. We extend their master theorem by incorporating polarity into coherence and allowing nonorientable surfaces. Our new coherence condition can be interpreted as perpendicularity from the perspective of Cayley--Klein geometry. Moreover, a polarity incidence theorem on a nonorientable tiled surface gives rise to a self-polar linear incidence theorem on the orientation double cover. We also extend the master theorem to Hermitian polarities over division rings, with its validity depending on the topology of the surface. Finally, we determine which incidence presentations admit proofs using tilings. When such proofs exist, we express the minimum Euler genus of the corresponding tiling in terms of the fundamental group.

papers.title: Completely Regular Growth of Transcendental Entire Solutions to Linear Difference Equations with Polynomial Coefficients
papers.authors: Xuxu Xiang, Jianren Long, Mingjin Li

papers.title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
papers.authors: Jieqiang Wei, Fahad Ali, Jonny Reichwald, Silun Zhang
papers.abstract: LLM agents, i.e., language models run by a harness, can now write, run and debug software autonomously. This raises the question of whether they can also carry out control system design. In this paper, we consider control system design as a task for LLM agents and grade the designed controller as control engineers do: the controller is given in a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, evaluated on held-out seeds against an ordered set of requirements, under specified physical perturbations and structural certificates, without using neural networks. We formulate the task as a chance-constrained feasibility problem and instantiate it in ControlHarbor, a benchmark of 44 tasks over 13 plants, which includes network consensus, vehicle platooning, the MuJoCo hopper, walker and humanoid. The tasks are packaged in the Harbor format, so that any agent harness can be run against them, and the same environments also serve learning algorithms other than LLMs, such as reinforcement learning (RL), under the same evaluation. With ControlHarbor, we observe that the controllers designed by three frontier coding agents, Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5, reach the RL return on every parity task, but only in a minority of sessions. We also observe that the controllers certified for return alone usually fail under perturbations. When robustness is part of the specification, a structured design meets it at the RL return on the humanoid task, where domain-randomised RL does not; under large pushes, domain-randomised RL succeeds and no designed controller does. The benchmark, the controllers, and their grades are released.

papers.title: Cavity collapse and vorticity gradient blow-up in free-boundary Euler flow
papers.abstract: We construct smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations with surface tension whose vorticity remains bounded while its full spatial gradient blows up in finite time. The solutions are axisymmetric without swirl and occupy bounded domains in which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at time $T$, while the outer free surface converges smoothly. The vorticity $\omega$ can be chosen arbitrarily small in $L^\infty$, uniformly up to collapse, and satisfies $\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_{L^\infty}\asymp (T-t)^{-1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{1/4}$ as $t\uparrow T$. A nonconstant material trace of the relative vorticity on the shrinking surface determines direction-dependent limits of the terminal vorticity, which therefore has no continuous extension across the collapse circle. The kinetic energy measure converges to the sum of a uniform line measure on this circle and a nonzero bulk part carried by a bounded rotational field. The construction couples vorticity transport to the boundary dynamics through weighted estimates in the collapsing collar and a cancellation in the normal acceleration.

papers.title: An FBSDE Approach to the Two-Dimensional Abelian-Higgs Model
papers.abstract: We develop an iterated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) approach to the two-dimensional infinite-volume Abelian-Higgs model in Coulomb gauge. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. We represent the lattice measure as the joint terminal law of the FBSDEs and establish uniform moment bounds for the corresponding terminal shifts. For the Higgs field, we combine a low-high frequency decomposition with covariant energy estimates to obtain bounds with sufficiently mild dependence on the gauge shift. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.

papers.title: Optimal Polyomino Fences
papers.authors: Alexis Langlois-R\'emillard, Mia N. M\"u{\ss}ig, Helmut Podhaisky, Erika Roldan, G\"unter Rote, Maximilian Br\"omme, Matthes Norden, Maximilian Prietzel, Daniel Yu, Mykhailo Lyader
papers.abstract: The $n$-omino fence problem asks how many cells can be surrounded by placing every $n$-omino exactly once in the grid. We present a new dynamic programming approach for this problem, allowing us to prove optimality for the pentomino and hexomino fence and to classify all possible pentomino orders by optimal area. For the first time we also provide strong heuristic solutions and upper bounds for all fences up to $n = 15$, after which we even approximate the $500$-omino fence with computational experiments. Finally, we generalize the problem to 3D, where we prove optimality for pentacubes and derive heuristic solutions for hexacubes and heptacubes.

papers.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
papers.authors: Emily M. Palmer, Anil V. Rao
papers.abstract: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: Covering the Square Lattice and the Honeycomb with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
papers.authors: Teeradej Kittipassorn, Nattawut Phetmak, Kirati Sriamorn
papers.abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the square lattice and $\mathcal{H}_d$ the honeycomb point set with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ these sets can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors; the periodic constructions of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol cover them only from $d=1/2$ and $d=2/\sqrt{37}$ on, with gaps. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points in a closed unit disk and $\rho$ for the number of points per unit area, we show that neither set can be covered when $\mathcal{N}(d)<2\sqrt3\,\rho$, and we determine these spacings exactly, thirteen intervals for $\mathcal{S}_d$ and twelve for $\mathcal{H}_d$. At their right endpoints the bound is attained; there $\mathcal{S}_d$ is never coverable, and $\mathcal{H}_d$ is not coverable at nine of the twelve endpoints. We also give new periodic coverings, of $\mathcal{S}_d$ at $d=2/\sqrt{34}$ and of $\mathcal{H}_d$ for $2/9\le d\le1/\sqrt{19}$. Consequently, the smallest coverable spacing lies in $(0.2581,\,2/\sqrt{34}]$ for the square lattice and in $(0.1781,\,2/9]$ for the honeycomb point set, and coverability is not monotone in $d$ for either set.

papers.title: A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
papers.authors: Su Mengwei, Sun Qiang, Xiong Ge
papers.abstract: For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subseteq\R^n$, we prove that there exists a volume-preserving linear transformation $T\in\SL_n(\R)$, such that for every $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ there is an origin-symmetric convex body $L$ with $(1-\varepsilon)TK\subseteq L \subseteq TK$ and the isoperimetric quotient $\iq(L)\le 40\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt n$. This resolves the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture.

papers.title: Counterexamples to flagged LLT and nonsymmetric Macdonald atom positivity
papers.abstract: We give a key polynomial of degree fourteen whose expansion in Demazure $t$-atoms has a coefficient with a negative term. This computation disproves the conjectured Demazure atom positivity of flagged LLT polynomials and the corresponding stable atom positivity assertion for modified nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.

papers.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
papers.authors: Tyler Franke, Ingo Runkel, Volker Schomerus
papers.abstract: We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions. We construct a number of new examples coming from quantum groups, as well as the associated quantum moment maps.

papers.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
papers.authors: Michael R. Douglas, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Fabian Lehmann, Daniel Platt, Yidi Qi
papers.abstract: We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.

papers.title: Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms
papers.abstract: We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial \omega_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(\Omega^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).

papers.title: Weak stability of Ricci flow with almost WPIC1 curvature
papers.authors: Pak-Yeung Chan, Lucas Lavoyer, Man-Chun Lee
papers.abstract: We prove weak $L^\infty$ stability for complete, non-collapsed Ricci flows with almost WPIC1 curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds. Small $L^\infty$ perturbations of the initial metric admit Ricci-DeTurck flows which remain uniformly close to the background flow and depend Lipschitz continuously on the initial data. This extends an earlier stability theorem of the first and third authors with Lai.

papers.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
papers.abstract: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.

papers.title: On the minimum energy required to trigger a spike
papers.abstract: We formulate and numerically study the problem of finding the minimum energy required to trigger a spike in a three-dimensional conductance-based excitable model. The variational formulation seeks a state trajectory that reaches the boundary of the spiking region with the least \textit{peak} cumulative work supplied through the membrane port. We approximate voltage histories by sums of real exponentials, reducing the problem to a finite-dimensional optimization. The best-found voltage waveform consists of a hyperpolarization phase followed by a depolarization phase, which seems to match the experimentally determined optimal stimulus in squid giant axons.

papers.title: CF-UAMG: A Coarse/Fine Splitting-Based Parallel Unsmoothed Aggregation Algebraic Multigrid Method
papers.authors: Zhibo Fan, Shaoliang Hu, Silu Huang, Xiaowen Xu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a coarse/fine splitting-based parallel unsmoothed aggregation algebraic multigrid (AMG) method, referred to as CF-UAMG. The proposed method utilizes the strong-connection structure identified by classical AMG (C-AMG) coarse/fine splitting to guide the selection of aggregate roots and the formation of aggregates, aiming to improve the quality of the aggregation-based coarse space and thus the convergence of unsmoothed aggregation AMG (UA-AMG). We also prove uniform two-grid convergence of CF-UAMG with a convergence bound independent of the matrix size for symmetric positive definite M-matrices with nonnegative row sums. Numerical experiments on three classes of three-dimensional problems, including Poisson-type equations, radiation diffusion equations, and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, demonstrate the robustness both in convergence and parallelism of CF-UAMG. Compared with UA-AMG methods employing four commonly used aggregation algorithms, CF-UAMG achieves average speedups of 1.29x, 2.04x, and 1.94x for the three classes of problems, respectively.

papers.title: Finite multiple harmonic sums and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values
papers.abstract: We introduce lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values and construct their harmonic regularizations. We show that they are independent of the branch of the $p$-adic logarithm and satisfy harmonic product relations. We express finite multiple harmonic sums as alternating convolutions of harmonic-regularized $p$-adic multiple zeta values and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values. This gives a $p$-adic analogue of the classical truncation identity, which reduces to the inversion relation between ordinary and star harmonic-regularized values when the truncation point is $1$. For truncation point $p$, it relates finite multiple zeta values to $p$-adic multiple zeta values.

papers.title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

papers.title: Optimal strong convergence rates of explicit stabilized method for the Galerkin finite element discretization SPDEs driven by multiplicative noise
papers.authors: Junwei Huang, Aiguo Xiao, Xiao Tang
papers.abstract: Explicit stabilized methods provide an efficient approach to stiff systems arising from deterministic parabolic equations, yet rigorous convergence theory for their application to stochastic partial differential equations remains scarce. To the best of our knowledge, the only prior fully discrete strong convergence analysis of explicit stabilized integrators for SPDEs is due to [A. Abdulle et al. IMA J. Numer. Anal. 43(1)(2023), pp. 258--292] and it is restricted to additive noise. The present work addresses the extension to multiplicative noise, by coupling Galerkin finite element spatial discretization with explicit stabilized time integrators. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and appropriate spatial regularity conditions, we derive the strong error bound $\mathcal{O}(h^{1+r}+\tau^{1/2})$ with $r\in[0,1)$, which achieves the optimal temporal strong convergence rate $1/2$ for the considered family of methods. One- and two-dimensional numerical tests with multiplicative noise validate the predicted convergence rates and compare the computational performance of explicit stabilized methods against the linearly implicit Euler method.

papers.title: Rohrbach's Conjecture for Finite Groups
papers.abstract: Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_h$ with $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{\alpha_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{\alpha_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]

papers.title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
papers.abstract: We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $\beta>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $\theta_1,\theta_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.

papers.title: Permutation polynomials of given index up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\ell$ be a divisor of $q-1$. We classify the permutation polynomials of $\mathbb F_q$ of polynomial index exactly $\ell$ up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence $G(X)\equiv uF(vX^d)\pmod{X^q-X}$, where $u,v\in\mathbb F_q^*$ and $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$, and we count the classes. For polynomials vanishing at $0$, the classes are the orbits of an explicit finite group on vectors of values at the $\ell$-th roots of unity. Through the permutation it induces on the roots of unity, each orbit lies over a double coset of the symmetric group $S_\ell$ with respect to its translation subgroup and an explicit affine group, and the stabilizers are explicit. For polynomials with nonzero constant term the action is free. Burnside's lemma, M\"obius inversion over the coefficient support and congruences along the cycles of affine permutations give an exact formula for the number of classes. For fixed $\ell\geqslant2$ these numbers are quasi-polynomials in $s=(q-1)/\ell$ of degree at most $\ell-1$, with period dividing $\ell$ for odd $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for even $\ell$; for polynomials vanishing at $0$ the degree is exactly $\ell-1$, and we determine the leading coefficient. For odd prime $\ell$ and for $\ell=4$ the counts are given in closed form. For index four we also count the binomials and trinomials at each admissible coefficient support. The sums of two binomial counts that occur are expressed through quartic Jacobi sums and Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and of a curve of genus two; one of the elliptic curves is the reduction of the curve $Y^2=X^3+8X^2+32X$, which has no complex multiplication over $\mathbb Q$. The trinomial counts are expressed through quartic cyclotomic numbers and these sums. All these terms cancel when the counts with a fixed residue of the vanishing order modulo $s$ are added.

papers.title: On the packing-dimension analogue of Bourgain's constant
papers.abstract: For every $n\geq 2$, we construct a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose harmonic measure has packing dimension $n$. That is, the packing analogue of Bourgain's constant is zero, in contrast with Bourgain's constant, which is positive. Moreover, the elliptic measure of the same domain also has packing dimension $n$ for every uniformly elliptic matrix.

papers.title: Gradient stability for the Sobolev inequality with optimal dimensional dependence
papers.abstract: Figalli and Zhang [29] established gradient stability for the sharp Sobolev inequality with the optimal exponent $r_p=\max\{2,p\}$. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$, the corresponding optimal stability constant $\mathsf C_{n,p}$ admits effective upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-1}$ for all integers $n>p$. In particular, the dimensional dependence $n^{-1}$ is optimal. Our result extends the optimal dimensional dependence established for $p=2$ by Dolbeault, Esteban, Figalli, Frank, and Loss [18] to every $p>1$.

papers.title: Stability Conditions on Twisted Derived Categories I: Existence and Full Numerical Support
papers.abstract: We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $\alpha$, the twisted derived category $D^b(X,\alpha)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. Based on Chunyi Li's construction and its extension to arbitrary fields, we establish uniform phase control under tensoring by an Azumaya algebra and calibrate the resulting slicing to the induced central charge. We further show that the constructed stability condition is geometric and satisfies a mass--Hom bound, which persists throughout its connected component.

papers.title: On real-analytic non-degeneracy of left-symmetric algebras in dimension 3
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that any three-dimensional differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra over $\mathbb R$ is non-degenerate both in the formal and real-analytic categories via the correspondence with Nijenhuis operators.

papers.title: Ramsey numbers of loose triangles versus cliques
papers.authors: Ayush Basu, Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku
papers.abstract:
An $r$-uniform loose triangle $C_3$ consists of three edges that intersect pairwise in exactly one vertex and have no vertex common to all three. For graphs, this is the usual triangle, and the Ramsey number $R(C_3,K_t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$ by celebrated results of Ajtai, Koml\'os, and Szemer\'edi and of Kim.
  Kostochka, Mubayi, and Verstra\"ete proved that $R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})=O_r(t^{3/2})$ for every fixed $r\ge3$ and showed that this bound is sharp up to a logarithmic factor. Motivated by the logarithmic saving in the graph case, they conjectured in 2013 that the upper bound could be improved to $o(t^{3/2})$.This conjecture has since received significant attention and has been reiterated in several papers. We prove the conjecture by showing that, for every fixed $r\ge3$, \[
  R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})
  =O_r\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\log\log t}}\right). \]

papers.title: An algorithm for solving the Burgers equation based on rational approximations and the collocation method
papers.authors: I. A. Bugoets, B. V. Semisalov
papers.abstract: We propose a numerical method for solving initial-boundary value problems for the Burgers equation that takes into account the presence of singularities of the analytic continuation of the solution into the complex plane. The algorithm uses rational approximations, a collocation method and a new scheme for time discretization combined with the relaxation method. An adaptive strategy is developed to account for the location of the singular point of the solution. Solutions to the well-known benchmark problem with a sine-shaped initial condition are obtained for the values of the viscosity as low as nu = 10^-8. Verification of the numerical results in such an extreme parameter regime makes it necessary to modify a classical formula for the exact solution so as to avoid floating-point overflow during its computation. The developed method is compared with an algorithm employing the Runge-Kutta scheme, and the conditions under which each approach yields superior results are outlined. An important feature of the proposed method is its capability to track the singular point of the solution. To verify this, we consider a problem whose solution has a simple analytical form and demonstrate that the exact and approximate coordinates of the singular point of the solution agree with high accuracy, even when the singularity comes extremely close to the domain of the problem. Taking the location of the singular point into account yields significant gains in both accuracy and run time relative to other methods.

papers.title: Non-existence of closed embedded magnetic geodesics
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to S. Novikov's 1982 conjecture that every Riemannian $2$-sphere contains a closed embedded curve of curvature $c$ for every $c>0$.

papers.title: A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$
papers.abstract: We exhibit a congruence subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_\Gamma$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
papers.abstract: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.

papers.title: Characterizations of Pettis Integrable Multifunctions in Locally Convex Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present characterizations of Pettis integrability in $bcc(X)$ and $cwk(X)$ of a multifunction $\Gamma : \Omega \to cc(X)$, where $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ is a complete finite measure space and $cc(X)$ $(bcc(X), cwk(X))$ is the family of all nonempty convex closed (bounded convex closed, convex weakly compact) subsets of a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$. Incidentally, a convergence theorem for scalarly integrable multifunctions is proved. As an application, we are going to prove full characterizations of Pettis integrability for fuzzy maps defined on $\Omega$ and taking values in the generalized fuzzy number hyperspace $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$.

papers.title: Rainbow matchings in non-uniform hypergraph systems
papers.abstract: Let $s\geq 1$, $r_1, r_2,\dots, r_{s+1}$ be given positive integers and $r=\max\{r_1, r_2,\ldots, r_{s+1}\}$. We prove that if $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ is a family of hypergraphs on a ground set of $n$ vertices, $n\geq 4r^2(s+1)$, such that $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$ and $|\mathcal{F}_i|>\binom{n}{r_i}-\binom{n-s}{r_i}-\binom{n-s-r}{r_i-1}+1$, for all $i \in [s+1]$, then $\mathcal{F}$ admits a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ or there exists $W \in \binom{[n]}{s}$ such that $W$ is a vertex cover of $\mathcal{F}_i$, for all $i \in [s+1]$. This improves upon the previously known range $n>2r^3s$ to $n>4r^2(s+1)$. Moreover, for a given family $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ of hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$, we give a best possible Ore-degree condition for $\mathcal{F}_{i}$'s that guarantees the existence of a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ for $\mathcal{F}$.

papers.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
papers.authors: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang
papers.abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.

papers.title: A binomial-adjusted $\theta$-trapezoidal tau-leaping method for chemical kinetic systems
papers.authors: Maximilian Scott, Sam McCallum, James Foster
papers.abstract: In Hu, Li and Min (2011), the authors propose a weak second order accurate $\theta$-trapezoidal method as an improvement to the classical tau-leaping method. However, for complex chemical kinetic systems their model's underlying analytical assumptions can fail to hold in practice, leading to a significant reduction in its computational effectiveness. Here we introduce a modification to the method which allows it to regain desirable convergence characteristics, both given the original and a relaxed version of the underlying assumptions. We confirm this improvement through a local error analysis and present numerical examples showing it consistently performs either better or comparable to the $\theta$-trapezoidal method.

papers.title: Non self-similar solutions to the Ricci flow coming out of metric cones
papers.authors: Alix Deruelle, Tristan Ozuch, Felix Schulze
papers.abstract: Given an asymptotically conical unstable expanding gradient Ricci soliton, we provide the existence of a family of Ricci flows starting at the same metric cone up to isometry. Moreover, the family of solutions we construct is shown to be parametrized by positive modes of the weighted Lichnerowicz operator associated to the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Each solution of this family is shown not to be induced by an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. If the background expander has no non-trivial infinitesimal deformations, we show furthermore that the solutions we provide are not self-similar. We finally prove that solutions are distinct up to isometries preserving the potential function of the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton.

papers.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.

papers.title: Certified Hierarchical Planning and Tracking: A Learning-Based Approach
papers.authors: Weijian Li, Vince Kurtz, Panos J. Antsaklis, Hai Lin
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a hierarchical control framework for nonlinear dynamical systems with safety constraints. Specifically, a low-fidelity model is introduced for trajectory planning, while a tracking controller is designed for the high-fidelity system. We first characterize the tracking error bound (TEB) using a storage function. Then, we formulate the synthesis of the tracking controller, the storage function, and the TEB as an optimization problem. Following that, we develop an offline learning approach to approximately solve the optimization problem, by incorporating behavior cloning and satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solver. We further integrate the learned controller and the TEB into online tracking of the high-fidelity system. This framework enables the control of high-dimensional nonlinear systems with safety guarantees, while maintaining computational efficiency for real-time implementation. Finally, experiments are provided for illustration.

papers.title: Direct Search meets Frank-Wolfe: Inexact Derivative-Free Bilevel Optimization over Polytopes
papers.authors: Matteo Pernini, Francesco Rinaldi, Gabriele Sanguin, Marco Viola
papers.abstract: In this work we propose BLDS-SIMPLEX, a derivative-free direct search method for the solution of bilevel optimization with polytope constraints at the upper level. The proposed method reformulates the feasible set using barycentric coordinates and explores it using Frank-Wolfe-type directions, relying on a fixed-accuracy black-box oracle for the upper-level objective function. We analyze its convergence properties and complexity in the case of smooth reduced objective; additionally, we analyze a variant for the case of nonsmooth objectives and show its convergence to a specific kind of stationary point that we introduce as a natural generalization to the classic stationarity notions in this setting. Numerical tests on modified instances from BOLIB support the viability of our new approach.

papers.title: A lift of Baxter's cyclic summation identity with applications to quantum topology
papers.abstract: While studying the chiral Potts model Baxter discovered a cyclic analogue of Ramanujan's ${}_1\psi_{1}$ summation identity. This identity was subsequently interpreted by Faddeev and Kashaev as a pentagon relation for the quantum dilogarithm function, a key ingredient in cyclic quantizations of Teichm\"uller theory. Existing forms of the identity involve multivalued functions so one must either accept overall phase ambiguities or keep track of branches on a complicated covering space. In this paper we show how to remove the phase ambiguities with a much simpler choice of covering space. As an application we compute the Fourier transform of the holonomy $R$-matrices of the author and Reshetikhin. A corollary is a simpler proof that Kashaev's $R$-matrix is a specialization of the colored Jones $R$-matrix, which was first shown by Murakami and Murakami.

papers.title: How to arrange four points in the plane
papers.abstract:
Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[
  D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[
  \begin{cases}
  \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1,
  \text{a rhombus with angle }\theta\in(\pi/3,\pi/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1.
  \end{cases} \]

papers.title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
papers.authors: Christa Cuchiero, Francesca Primavera, Sara Svaluto-Ferro
papers.abstract:
