We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem.
  We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.

papers.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
papers.authors: Bonan Chen, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo
papers.abstract:
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture.
  The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity.
  We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar.
  In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

papers.title: Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
papers.abstract: We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.

papers.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
papers.abstract: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.

papers.title: Real log canonical tresholds and real log canonical tresholds with signs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

papers.title: Poincar\'e polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
papers.authors: Marco Aldi, Samuel Bevins, Eleftherios Chatzitheodoridis, Sergio Da Silva, Quincy Frias, Tom\'as Mej\'ia G\'omez
papers.abstract: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.

papers.title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
papers.authors: Louison Bocquet-Nouaille, J\'er\^ome Morio, Benjamin Bobbia, Philippe Naveau
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

papers.title: Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web
papers.abstract:
The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $\Lambda_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(\Lambda_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $\Omega_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $\Omega_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $\Omega_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$.
  In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $\Omega_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $\Omega_N^\infty$.

papers.title: Large diameter for $(\Delta+2)$-colouring reconfiguration
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2\mu$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + \mu$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $\mu$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}\mu-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $\Delta$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} \mu$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.

papers.title: Spin-Boson Hamiltonians as Generators of Spin-Dressed Bogoliubov Dynamics
papers.abstract: Following Bach, Lieb and Solovej, quadratic Hamiltonians can be defined as generators of unitary groups implementing one-parameter groups of Bogoliubov transformations. We develop an analogous dynamical definition of generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians. For a single spin level, we review results of Guichardet and Derezi\'nski: the van Hove Hamiltonians, including the renormalized ones, are exactly the generators of affine Bogoliubov dynamics that do not mix creation and annihilation operators. For several spin levels, there is no analogue of this group, and we introduce spin-dressed implementations, that is to say the free flow of the fields is implemented up to bounded operator-valued displacements, which vanish at a rate measured by a so-called regularity scale and have a spin observable, the coupling map, as derivative at time zero. The one-particle Hamiltonian $\Upsilon$ and the coupling map are determined by the Hamiltonian, and the field obeys a quantum Langevin equation. Spin-dressed implementations in Fock space, at the finest scale and for form factors in $D(\Upsilon^{-1/2})$, are exactly the generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians, unique up to the spin Hamiltonian. At the roughest scale, the renormalized spin--boson Hamiltonian of a two-level system with ultraviolet-singular form factor and arbitrary tunnelling is a spin-dressed implementation, and the definition alone yields asymptotic Weyl operators on the test functions along which the coupling map is integrable, a dense set under standard assumptions.

papers.title: Accelerated Transformed Primal Dual Methods for Smooth Convex Optimization Problems with Affine Equality Constraints
papers.abstract: Accelerated transformed primal--dual (ATPD) methods are proposed for smooth convex optimization problems with affine equality constraints. The methods combine primal--dual dynamics with a transformation designed to accelerate convergence. In the strongly convex case, ATPD achieves an accelerated linear convergence rate and matches the known lower bounds on first-order oracle complexity in terms of gradient evaluations and matrix--vector products. The analysis distinguishes these two types of computational work when assessing the complexity of the method. For general convex objectives, a homotopy perturbation strategy is introduced, and an accelerated sublinear rate for the modified Lyapunov energy is proved under a uniform boundedness condition on the primal iterates at all homotopy stages. The acceleration mechanism is based on an exponentially stable ATPD flow and a modified discrete Lyapunov function. This continuous-time perspective guides the construction and analysis of the discrete methods. Numerical experiments on policy evaluation and constrained signal reconstruction problems support the theory and illustrate the efficiency of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density
papers.abstract: We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.

papers.title: Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
papers.authors: Jennifer Biermann, Kuei-Nuan Lin, Augustine O'Keefe
papers.abstract: We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph. We establish positive results for several families of graphs under suitable orientation and coprimality conditions, including weighted oriented paths and cycles, and show that any weighted oriented tree with a unique sink has the IDP.

papers.title: First Order Convergence of Representative Volume Element with Mixed Boundary Condition
papers.abstract: We study the cell problem with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann boundary condition to reconstruct the effective matrix for two-dimensional scalar divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, and possibly nonsymmetric coefficients. We prove uniform invertibility of the mean-gradient matrix. Moreover, we derive the first-order error estimate when the medium is periodic.

papers.title: Semiclassical Scaling Laws of Magnus Quantum Algorithms under Harmonic Confinement
papers.abstract: The simulation of semiclassical Schr\"odinger dynamics is often hindered by rapid oscillations, where classical numerical methods and quantum simulation algorithms can suffer severe precision loss as the semiclassical parameter $\varepsilon \to 0$. In this work, we uncover a surprising robustness of high-order Magnus quantum algorithms in the semiclassical regime. We establish two important results. First, we extend the theory of Magnus superconvergence from free-particle reference dynamics to a general class of Schr\"odinger operators whose reference Hamiltonian includes harmonic confinement. Second, and more importantly, we reveal a nontrivial semiclassical scaling law: while the expansion remainder term bound suggests an error prefactor of $O(\varepsilon^{-(p+1)})$ for a $p$th-order method, we prove that the loss is in fact order-independent and collapses to $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ for all $p$. The key analytical mechanism is the exact Egorov transport associated with quadratic flows in semiclassical Weyl quantization, which enables a symbol-level analysis of the interaction-picture Hamiltonian and its Magnus commutators. Our results show that high-order Magnus quantum algorithms remain far more robust in the semiclassical regime than naive series remainder term counting would suggest.

papers.title: On a PDE-ODE-ODE model for meniscus tissue regeneration with space-dependent, possibly degenerate diffusion tensor
papers.authors: Nishith Mohan, Ahmad Hussein, Bernd Simeon, Christina Surulescu
papers.abstract: We investigate a tissue regeneration model that describes the coupled dynamics of human mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), chondrocytes, and newly formed extracellular matrix (ECM). The system features motility terms only for the mesenchymal stem cells, more precisely myopic diffusion and haptotaxis towards increasing ECM; all of those terms involve a space-dependent, possibly degenerating tensor. The chondrocytes are obtained from MSCs by differentiation and provide positive feedback to MSCs via dedifferentiation. The considered macroscopic model was obtained by upscaling from a formulation within the kinetic theory of active particles. Under appropriate assumptions we prove global existence of classical solutions in 2D and 3D in the case of a nondegenerating tensor and global existence of weak solutions in 2D when the diffusion tensor is allowed to degenerate. Numerical simulations are performed in 2D in order to illustrate the solution behavior.

papers.title: Spectrum of non-Hermitian self-normalized random matrices with heavy tails
papers.abstract: We study non-Hermitian matrices $Y_n$ obtained by normalizing each row of an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. entries to Euclidean norm one. We consider regularly varying radial tails of index $\alpha\in[0,2]$, with $\alpha=0$ denoting slowly varying tails, and the broader normal domain of attraction. For $0<\alpha<2$, assuming angular tail convergence, we prove convergence in probability of the empirical singular value measures of every shift $Y_n-zI$ to deterministic laws characterized by the root resolvent of a column-normalized directed Poisson weighted infinite tree, extending the framework of Bordenave, Caputo and Chafai (arXiv:1006.1713). Under a bounded density assumption, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges in probability to a deterministic law $\mu_\alpha^{\mathrm{SN}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$. This law is rotationally invariant, is supported in the closed unit disk with outer radius one, and has neither point atoms nor mass on the unit circle. The laws interpolate between $\delta_0$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$ and the circular law as $\alpha\uparrow2$. These also describe the limiting eigenvalue distributions of $Y_n$ for real entries with slowly varying tails and for centered entries with bounded density in the normal domain of attraction, respectively. For real symmetric entries with bounded density, the spectral radius converges to one in probability for $0<\alpha\le2$, using the upper bound of Francois, Heiny and Hu (arXiv:2608.28169). We also give a general criterion identifying the outer support radius of rotationally invariant laws from fractional moments of fresh cavity weights, under explicit trace and radial-recovery assumptions.

papers.title: Asymptotic transportation cost of the optimal matching subject to different boundary conditions
papers.abstract:
We establish equality between several asymptotic limits of the transportation cost between stationary random measures, with respect to the Euclidean distance cost raised to the $p$-th power, with different boundary conditions.
  Our approach relies on a comparison with the optimizer of the mean transportation cost between the two random measures, which is defined on the whole space. In particular we do not use any PDE techniques related to the regularity theory for optimal transport maps.

papers.title: Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
papers.abstract: The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.

papers.title: Discrete unique continuation for Schr\"odinger equations
papers.authors: Torunn S. Jensen, Didier Pilod, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos
papers.abstract:
We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^{\alpha}$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^{\beta}$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schr\"odinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $\sigma\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,\sigma\}\big(\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\beta/(1-\beta)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, provided that $\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\beta/(1-\beta)<1$.
  Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $\alpha+\beta<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $\Gamma=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.

papers.title: The structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups of the real projective plane
papers.abstract:
In this paper we study the structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups
  $B_n(RP^2)$ of the real projective plane $RP^2$. It is known that the isomorphism classes of these subgroups are comprised of cyclic, dicyclic and binary polyhedral groups. Using specific elements of $B_n(RP^2)$, we construct embeddings of the cyclic and dicyclic subgroups, we show that there is a single conjugacy class of the maximal dicyclic groups, and for small values of n, we also construct embeddings of the bin- ary tetrahedral and octahedral groups. One interesting phenomenon that occurs is the existence of isomorphism classes of finite subgroups that admit embeddings in $B_n(RP^2)$ as both maximal finite and non-maximal subgroups. Up to conjugacy, we describe completely the lattice of the finite subgroups of $B_n(RP^2)$ for n = 3, 4, 5. Some of our results regarding the number of conjugacy classes of finite subgroups are obtained using the relation between $B_n(RP^2)$ and the mapping class group of $RP^2$ relative to n points. We also provide a new presentation of $B_n(RP^2)$ which has some interesting properties with respect to the classical presentation of Van Buskirk.

papers.title: Adaptive Constraint Sampling for Stochastic Gradient Methods in Constrained Optimization
papers.authors: Erik M\"uller, Naum Dimitrieski, Mohamed-Ali Belabbas, Christian Ebenbauer
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive constraint-sampling technique for stochastic gradient-based methods to efficiently solve constrained optimization problems with a large number of inequality constraints. The proposed constraint-sampling technique maintains a set of recently violated constraints and draws the constraint used in each iteration uniformly either from this set or from the set of all constraints. This keeps its per-iteration arithmetic overhead independent of the number of constraints. In simulations on synthetic convex optimization problems and in the synthesis of a control barrier function for the Dubins Car, the constraint-sampling technique is shown to significantly outperform uniform constraint sampling.

papers.title: Isotonic least squares is robust to heteroscedasticity, unimodal least squares is not
papers.abstract: We compare the least squares estimator (LSE) with the $\ell_{1}$-estimator recently introduced by Baraud and Maillard~\citeyearpar{BM-2026} for estimating a regression function under a fixed design, when the errors are independent but possibly heteroscedastic and heavy-tailed. We show that the two estimators coincide on the class of nondecreasing (or nonincreasing) functions on an interval. As a consequence, the isotonic LSE inherits the non-asymptotic $\ell_{1}$-risk bounds of the $\ell_{1}$-estimator, which only require a moment of order $p\in[1,2]$ on the errors and depend on the average of their $p$-th absolute moments rather than on their maximum. This coincidence no longer holds on the nonconvex class of unimodal functions: we exhibit a heteroscedastic Gaussian example in which the LSE is inconsistent while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator converges at the parametric rate. Finally, we show on a one-dimensional linear model that neither estimator dominates the other: depending on the way the noise is distributed among the design points, the LSE may converge at rate $1/n$ while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator is inconsistent.

papers.title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the perpendicular direction. This anisotropy leads to thin, steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods struggle to resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement. In this paper, we introduce the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a data-driven local model reduction approach, for anisotropic diffusion. The method utilizes a bottom-up construction to enable a complete offline-online splitting. We parametrize the local magnetic field and boundary conditions to generate a snapshot space that captures the essential physics of plasma confinement. Dominant modes are extracted via a local spectral problem to identify representative features. These modes are then mapped to the global domain using a partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space. This ensures that the basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing the online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations.

papers.title: A posteriori error estimates for fully coupled McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs with jumps
papers.abstract: We prove a two-sided a posteriori error estimate for numerical approximations of fully coupled McKean-Vlasov forward-backward SDEs with jumps under full-tuple law dependence. The coefficients may depend on the joint law of $(X,Y,Z,U)$, and we allow infinite jump activity. We construct a computable estimator ${\mathcal{E}_\pi}$ for the squared full-tuple error ${\mathcal{D}_\pi}$ relative to the exact Euler solution. The estimator uses the boundary and cumulative residuals of any admissible grid approximation. Under monotonicity and on sufficiently fine grids, $c\,{\mathcal{E}_\pi} \le {\mathcal{D}_\pi} \le C\,{\mathcal{E}_\pi}$. The efficiency bound holds without monotonicity or a mesh restriction. Analogous two-sided bounds hold for the continuous-time error up to a discretisation remainder that vanishes under coefficient time regularity. Closed-form and state-nonlinear benchmarks cover full-tuple law dependence, mark-dependent jump integrands, nonzero orthogonal martingales and infinite jump activity. In our experiments, the estimator tracks the discrete error during neural training and across Picard iterations. In a mean-field inventory model, we use the estimator and a computable discretisation term to bound the excess cost of the computed control over the discrete optimum.

papers.title: Mixed Inner Variation and Global Hessian Integrability for Degenerate Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
papers.abstract: We study the global Hessian integrability for nonzero convex solutions of the degenerate Monge-Amp\`ere equations $\det D^2u=M(-u)^p$ with zero boundary values on arbitrary bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in the global Lipschitz regime $p>n-2$. We establish global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for every $0<\varepsilon<\min\{(p-n+2)/n,1\}$ and determine the optimal range of $\varepsilon$ in dimension two. The flat faces of rectangular boxes and their intersections impose upper bounds on the admissible exponents of global Hessian integrability. A new input in the proof for general dimensions is a Caccioppoli-type estimate for the boundary Hessian mass using vector fields arising from a mixed second inner variation. For the sharp higher integrability result in the plane, we use the combined hodograph-Legendre transform to control the curvature of level sets.

papers.title: Quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces via Sierpi\'nski spaces
papers.abstract: We study quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces using Sierpi\'nski spaces. We introduce K3 surfaces of Sierpi\'nski type and prove that their limit sets are round Sierpi\'nski spaces. For such K3 surfaces, the quasi-isometry class of the automorphism group is equivalent to the rational isometry class of the N\'eron--Severi lattice together with its integral roots. As an application of this rigidity, we construct infinitely many quasi-isometry classes of hyperbolic automorphism groups in Picard rank 4. This reveals a new phenomenon in Picard rank 4, sharply contrasting with the finiteness of quasi-isometry classes in Picard ranks at most 3 and at least 6.

papers.title: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlev\'e VI
papers.authors: Ian Marquette, Anthony J. L. Parr
papers.abstract: We study quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular component is expressed through a generic Painlev\'e VI transcendent. We construct generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable. For the Painlev\'e VI angular Hamiltonian these operators satisfy $[N,J_\pm]=\pm2kJ_\pm$, where $N=\sqrt M$, and close through an eighth-degree norm polynomial. Combining the angular shifts with the radial shift operators of the oscillator, Coulomb and free Bessel systems yields higher-order integrals and deformed Racah-type polynomial algebras for the two-dimensional superintegrable models. This construction provides new families of Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz (TTW)- and Post-Winternitz (PW)-like Hamiltonians with integrals of arbitrarily high order and Painlev\'e VI in the potential. This framework also recovers models from the classification of third- and fourth-order integrals as particular cases. For a representative oscillator extension we compute the Casimir explicitly and recover the finite-dimensional energy spectrum from a deformed-oscillator realization. We then analyze the special-solution sector using the explicit families collected by Gromak, Laine and Shimomura. The resulting potentials are organized into a small number of spectral classes, and the distinction between formal zeros of the ladder norm and physical self-adjoint representations is made explicit. The regular nonclassical rational examples are rational Darboux deformations of the trigonometric P\"oschl--Teller system and lead to strictly isospectral exceptional-Jacobi sectors or to state-adding representations with an isolated angular level. A singular branch produces an interior inverse-square barrier and a split-domain problem. For one regular exceptional sector and two state-adding sectors we display the polynomial algebras.

papers.title: Universal sampling rules for the signed friendship paradox
papers.abstract: The friendship paradox describes a bias in mean degree induced by neighbour sampling. We study signed weighted networks, with transitions proportional to edge magnitudes and signed strength as the vertex score. We characterize all positive initial weights, depending on total strength and score, that guarantee a nonnegative one-step mean change on every connected graph. Without regularity assumptions, the same condition yields stochastic dominance at every fixed time. Continuous admissible rules are precisely total strength multiplied by a positive continuous nonincreasing function of the score. It is enough to test connected graphs with at most five vertices and two vertex types. The bound of five is optimal even for continuous rules; the proof uses a sharp four-vertex energy inequality. The complete score vector alone cannot determine a universally valid initial law with full support. Under marked local convergence and suitable integrability assumptions, we also obtain joint limits for local conditional mean score increments and compute an explicit limiting law and mean for independently signed random regular graphs. Under joint cut-norm convergence of the magnitude and signed kernels and uniformly bounded normalized strengths, we also obtain Wasserstein convergence of the sampling-weighted distributions of normalized local biases and convergence of their means.

papers.title: Mass gap for the fractional $\Phi^4_2$ model
papers.abstract: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $\Phi^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Bou\'e-Dupuis variational formula.

papers.title: Equidistribution of curves in hypersurfaces of low degree
papers.abstract: We prove that over $\mathbb{C}$, for any smooth projective curve $\mathscr{C}$ and any smooth hypersurface $V \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ such that $n \geq 2^d(d-1)$, Faisant's equidistribution principle holds for $(\mathscr{C},V)$. In other words, for any reasonable set of jet conditions $W$, the moduli space $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ of degree $e$ maps $\mathscr{C} \to V$ satisfying conditions $W$ converges in the Grothendieck ring of complex varieties, after renormalisation, as $e \to \infty$. This provides the dimension and decomposition into irreducible components of $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ for $e$ large enough. The strategy follows Bilu and Browning's motivic version of the circle method, and Hase-Liu's framework for genus $\geq 1$.

papers.title: Why should $\mathbb{Z}$ be Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
papers.authors: Alexander Kozachinskiy, Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux
papers.abstract: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers.

papers.title: Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition for Multitemperature Gas Mixtures on Unstructured Meshes
papers.authors: Domenico Caparello, Lorenzo Pareschi, Thomas Rey
papers.abstract: We present a dynamic domain decomposition method for gas mixtures described by a multi-species BGK model in the regime where collisions between particles of the same species are dominant. In this regime the hydrodynamic limit is a system of Euler equations in which every species keeps its own velocity and temperature, the species being coupled through momentum and energy exchange terms. To decide locally whether this multi-velocity, multi-temperature Euler description is accurate, we extend the moment realizability criterion of Levermore, Morokoff and Nadiga: for each species, a realizability matrix is derived from the Chapman--Enskog expansion of the kinetic model, and its zeroth- and first-order approximations are compared. The indicator involves only macroscopic quantities and is evaluated species by species, so that in the same cell one species may be described by the Euler equations and another one by the kinetic equation. The kinetic solver is therefore used only where, and for the species for which, the indicator detects non-equilibrium effects, such as across shocks or near obstacles in rarefied flows. Both solvers are discretized on unstructured triangular meshes with second-order accuracy in space and time. The kinetic equation is integrated by an asymptotic-preserving IMEX Runge--Kutta scheme, whose limit for vanishing Knudsen number is a consistent discretization of the multi-velocity, multi-temperature Euler system. In the numerical tests the hybrid solution stays close to the kinetic one, while the computational time is reduced by a factor between about three and almost five.

papers.title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{slip-spli}$
papers.abstract: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.

papers.title: $Z_\infty$-algebras: Zinbielification of $B_\infty$ and quasi-shuffle algebras
papers.abstract: Commutative $B_\infty$-algebras provide a natural generalisation of the shuffle and quasi-shuffle algebras, giving deformations of the shuffle algebra. We introduce a Zinbiel analogue in $Z_\infty$-algebras, giving deformations of the half-shuffle Zinbiel algebra. All commutative $B_\infty$-algebras have been shown to be isomorphic to the shuffle algebra, though this isomorphism is not canonical. We show that all $Z_\infty$-algebras are canonically isomorphic to the half-shuffle algebra, which gives a canonical isomorphism to the shuffle algebra for $B_\infty$-algebras arising from $Z_\infty$-algebras. Finally, we explore which $B_\infty$-algebras can be ``Zinbielified'' to a $Z_\infty$-algebra, working through a number of explicit examples in the case of quasi-shuffle algebras and uncovering a very explicit classification of simple Zinbielifications via semigroup cocycles.

papers.title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem
papers.abstract: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.

papers.title: Augmented Dynamical Sampling under unmodeled Forcing
papers.abstract: We study recovery of an initial state from dynamical samples of a trajectory driven by unknown additive forcing. Measurements against both the original sensors and their images under the adjoint nominal evolution yield one-step residuals that cancel the initial state exactly. These residuals separate forcing estimation from initial-state reconstruction. For a centered Gaussian forcing model with fixed covariance parameters, we combine Gaussian conditioning with canonical dual-frame reconstruction and derive an exact unconditional second-moment identity, including the correlation between the forcing-estimation error and the measurement noise. We also obtain high-probability bounds and identify the irreducible forcing uncertainty through a conditional covariance in the geometry induced by the prior. A hierarchy of augmented sensor systems separates the role of sampling depth in forcing visibility from that of the observation horizon in nominal observability. An image-transport experiment and finite-dimensional and periodic-convolution experiments illustrate the residual correction and the separate roles of sampling depth and observation horizon.

papers.title: Quantum loop symmetric pairs and meromorphic abelian K-matrices
papers.authors: Andrea Appel, Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki, Bart Vlaar
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra, let $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not be a root of unity, and let $\mathbf{U}=U_q(L\mathfrak{g})$ be the corresponding quantum loop algebra, equipped with Hernandez' deformed Drinfeld coproduct. For every diagram involution $\tau$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, we introduce a coideal subalgebra $\mathbf{B}$ in a topological completion of $\mathbf{U}$, obtained by adapting the Letzter-Kolb construction of quantum symmetric pairs to the Drinfeld generators of $\mathbf{U}$. We derive necessary constraints on the parameters defining $\mathbf{B}$ from a minimality condition on its intersection with the quantum loop Cartan subalgebra $\mathbf{U}^0\subset\mathbf{U}$. We show that $\mathbf{B}$ yields a topological realization of the quasi-split $\imath$quantum loop group $\mathbf{U}^\imath$ associated with $\tau$, in the presentation recently obtained by Lu-Pan, building on work of Chen-Lu-Pan-Ruan-Wang on $\imath$Hopf algebras. By pullback, this gives rise to a rational restriction functor on category O representations. For modules with rational weights and generic values of the spectral parameter, every $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-submodule of a restricted module is stable under the derived quantum loop algebra $\mathbf{U}'$. In particular, irreducibility is generically preserved under restriction for such modules.
  For $|q|\neq1$ and under explicit assumptions on the quantum Cartan matrix, we construct meromorphic abelian K-matrices whose tensor counterparts yield boundary $q$-characters for both $\mathbf{U}$-modules and $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-modules.
  Finally, we extend the coideal construction and Drinfeld coaction to shifted $\imath$quantum loop algebras with arbitrary coweight shifts, providing a new approach to $\imath$GKLO representations by restriction from ordinary shifted quantum loop algebras.

papers.title: Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
papers.authors: Sourav Pal, Guicong Su, Nitin Tomar
papers.abstract:
The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by
  \[
  \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}:
  \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}}
  \left|
  \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}}
  {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2}
  \right|<1
  \right\},
  \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0
  \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $\mu_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,\mu_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $\Psi_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[
  \Psi_{\mathbb H}(\xi_1, \xi_2,\lambda_1,\lambda_2)
  =
  \left(\frac{\lambda_1(\xi_1-1)}{2},
  \frac{\xi_2(\xi_1+1)}{2}, \
  \frac{\lambda_1\lambda_2(\xi_1+1)}{2}, \
  \xi_1 \xi_2\lambda_1\lambda_2
  \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $\Psi_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.

papers.title: K3 tails in the KSBA moduli of Kunev surfaces
papers.authors: Yongnam Lee, Elisa Scattone, Luca Schaffler
papers.abstract: In the context of compact moduli spaces of Koll\'ar, Shepherd-Barron, and Alexeev stable surfaces, a degeneration can acquire an exceptional K3 component in the limit, or more simply a K3 tail. We study this phenomenon for Kunev surfaces: minimal surfaces of general type with $K^2=p_g=1$ that arise as $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$-covers of the projective plane branched along two general cubics and a line. We classify the K3 tails that occur when the branch curve degenerates to a singular curve with a non-log canonical isolated semi-quasihomogeneous singularity, and describe the corresponding boundary strata. This builds on the Kerr-Laza classification of K3 tails arising from isolated semi-quasihomogeneous hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: Convergence rates for smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with nonlinear pressure
papers.authors: Piotr Gwiazda, Jakub Skrzeczkowski, Jakub Wo\'znicki
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative convergence results for the smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method approximating the compressible Euler equations with nonlinear pressure laws $\rho^\gamma$, $\gamma\geq 2$. Our approach is based on a nonlocal approximation of the pressure force that preserves the energy structure of the original system, including an exact energy balance. Using the relative entropy method, we prove convergence towards smooth solutions of the compressible Euler equations as the nonlocality parameter $\varepsilon\to0$, with algebraic convergence rates and an explicit algebraic relationship between $\varepsilon$ and the number of particles $N$. In particular, we obtain quantitative convergence rates for the density in the Wasserstein distance and negative Sobolev norms, and for the momentum in the flat metric. A key feature of our analysis is that it applies to measure-valued densities in the nonlocal system, providing a unified framework for both continuum and particle solutions. Our results extend the existing rigorous convergence theory for SPH beyond quadratic pressure ($\gamma=2$) to general nonlinear pressure laws with $\gamma\geq 2$ on the periodic domain.

papers.title: Higher integrability for parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with gradient-dependent sources
papers.abstract: This paper aims to establish higher gradient integrability away from the initial time for solutions to parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with general gradient-dependent lower-order terms throughout the singular and degenerate regimes. For this purpose, we develop an elliptic reconstruction argument based on an $L^2$-valued temporal H\"{o}lder estimate, thereby transferring the problem to elliptic estimates and quantitative control of the reconstruction error. In particular, our approach yields an explicit higher-integrability exponent. We further construct counterexamples illustrating that bounded continuous initial data alone are insufficient to ensure higher gradient integrability up to the initial time. Finally, we provide counterexamples demonstrating that gradient-dependent lower-order terms can prevent temporal Lipschitz regularity.

papers.title: Algebraic and geometric aspects of Demazure weaves
papers.abstract: These are notes to supplement my talks at the Current Developments in Mathematics Conference in 2026. They are an expository account of recent work in the study of braid varieties and their relation to low-dimensional contact and symplectic topology. A driving theme is the development and use of Demazure weaves to construct cluster algebra structures on the coordinate rings of such braid varieties.

papers.title: Covering numbers and pcf theory
papers.abstract: We develop a general technique for deriving covering theorems from pcf-theoretic information by refining sequences of partitions. The method gives a direct proof of Shelah's cov vs. pp theorem and analogous results for diagonal coverings associated with normal ideals and covering modulo arbitrary $\sigma$-complete ideals, where $\sigma$ is regular and uncountable. In each setting, we characterize the covering invariant through pseudopowers, true cofinalities of reduced products of progressive sets, and appropriate notions of cofinality in (possible non-progressive) intervals of regular cardinals.

papers.title: From Metric to Strong Metric Regularity: A Second Subderivative Criterion for Definable Prox-regular Subdifferentials
papers.abstract: We investigate when metric regularity of a subdifferential mapping rules out multiple local inverse branches and therefore upgrades to strong metric regularity. Let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]$ be proper, lower semicontinuous, definable, prox-regular, and subdifferentially continuous at $(\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}(\partial h)$. We characterize this ``upgrade'' through the second subderivative $q = \mathrm{d}^2h(\bar x|\bar v)$ of $h$. If $\partial h$ is metrically regular, then it is strongly metrically regular if and only if the set of negative curvature directions of $q$ on the unit sphere of $\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{dom}(q))$ has Euler characteristic $0$ or $2$. We also prove a simpler and directly verifiable sufficient condition: nonnegativity of $q$ on the lineality space $\operatorname{dom}(q)\cap(-\operatorname{dom}(q))$ forces a quadratic lower bound for $q$ on its entire domain and hence yields strong metric regularity. In particular, if $\bar x$ is a local minimizer and $\bar v=0$, the second subderivative is nonnegative on its domain $\operatorname{dom}(q)$, which proves a conjecture of Drusvyatskiy, Mordukhovich, and Nghia in the definable setting. The derived principle strengthens this conjecture by replacing local minimality with a weaker second-order condition on the lineality space.

papers.title: Solovay's Construction via Proof Search
papers.abstract: Solovay's celebrated result establishes the arithmetical completeness of GL by embedding Kripke models into arithmetic. We provide an alternative proof of the arithmetical completeness of GL, in which we instead embed failed proof searches into arithmetic. Our methodology requires only a well-behaved sequent calculus and does not rely on completeness with respect to Kripke semantics or any of its variants. This approach is particularly interesting for logics that do not behave well semantically, such as ER, for which we also provide a new proof of arithmetical completeness.

papers.title: Discrete Helicity on Graphs: Pfaffian Energies and Clique Bounds
papers.abstract: We introduce a helicity functional of each order on graphs for real-valued edge forms, and give it a unified local Pfaffian realization. Motivated by the continuous energy inequality, we further construct a discrete version of helicity energy, and prove sharp Maclaurin inequalities for these energies. In particular, a special case of these Maclaurin inequalities yields a lower bound on the clique number, depending on the choice of edge form. As an application, we use this certificate to prove that every nonempty $d$-regular graph with smallest adjacency eigenvalue at least $-3$ satisfies $\omega(G)\ge d\,g(\eta)-C$, where $C$ is an absolute constant and $g(\eta)$ is a rank-dependent coefficient taking values between $1/4$ and $1/3$. Building on the structural results of Koolen, Yang and Yang, this improves the known clique-number bound to the optimal leading constant $1/4$, whose asymptotic sharpness follows from Yang and Koolen's construction.

papers.title: Existence of a fluid phase for the two-dimensional one-component plasma
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional one-component plasma is a system of point charges that repel each other logarithmically, in a uniform neutralizing background. When the inverse temperature $\beta$ is at most $2$, we prove that its correlations decay exponentially, and that its Gibbs state is unique among point processes whose fluctuations are controlled. This constitutes part of the fluid phase predicted by physicists. As a consequence, we obtain the existence of an infinite-volume limit, extending the Ginibre point process, which we call $\mathrm{Gin}_\beta$. We show that its truncated two-point function, at the scale of the Debye length, is given to first order in $\beta$ by the Debye-H\"uckel approximation.

papers.title: Signature representations of certain BSDEs
papers.authors: Peter Bank, Christian Bayer, Marco Rauscher, Marco Rodrigues, Nikolas Tapia
papers.abstract: We link the solvability of backward stochastic differential equations with time-augmented Brownian signature data to the solvability of a differential equation on the tensor algebra of signature coefficients. We show that in certain cases the solutions are of closed form and remain within the class of linear functionals of the signature. Lastly, we derive a closed-form solution to a pricing and hedging problem in terms of the time-augmented Brownian signature.

papers.title: On transformations in the Second Painlev\'e family
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of algebraic relations among solutions of equations in the second Painlev\'e family $P_{II}(\alpha): y''=2y^3+ty+\alpha$, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}$. More precisely, we prove that if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generic solutions of $P_{II}(\alpha_1),\ldots,P_{II}(\alpha_n)$, respectively, and $tr.deg_{\mathbb{C}(t)}\mathbb{C}(t)(y_1,y_1',\ldots,y_n,y_n')<2n$, then for some $i<j$, we have that $\alpha_i\pm\alpha_j\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $y_i=T(y_j)$ for a classical B\"acklund transformation $T$. In particular, the classical B\"acklund transformations are the only B\"acklund transformations in the second Painlev\'e family.

papers.title: Time inconsistent linear quadratic optimal control for mean field games in Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: This paper studies time-inconsistent linear-quadratic mean-field games governed by stochastic evolution equations in Hilbert spaces. The time inconsistency arises through the dependence of the cost functional on the initial time, while the mean-field interaction enters through the mean of the state distribution. By employing a multiperson differential game approach, we show that the closed-loop equilibrium strategy admits an affine feedback representation characterized by an operator-valued Riccati equation and a novel coupled forward-backward equilibrium system. We establish the existence and uniqueness of mild solutions to the equilibrium system and hence the existence of a closed-loop equilibrium strategy.

papers.title: New bounds on the boxicity of Kneser graphs
papers.authors: L. Sunil Chandran, Suraj Kumar Sahoo
papers.abstract:
For a graph $G=(V,E)$, the boxicity $\operatorname{box}(G)$ is the least integer $d$ such that $G$ is the intersection graph of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ is the graph whose vertex set corresponds to the family of $k$ sized subsets of an $n$ sized ground set, and a pair of vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding sets are disjoint.
  In this short paper, we provide new bounds for the boxicity of $K(n,k)$. We first show that for $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 2k+1$, $\operatorname{box}(K(n,k))\ge n-2k$, thereby improving the lower bounds of Caoduro and Lichev [Discrete Mathematics 346(5):113333 (2023)] when $n\geq 3k+1$ and $k\ge 3$. The proof of this result uses the topological method and follows a strategy similar to Greene's proof of the Kneser's conjecture on the chromatic number of $K(n,k)$.
  We also show that for $k\ge 2$, $t\ge 1$ and $n=2k+t$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+t,k)) \leq O( t^3\log(2k+t) ).$ In particular, for every $t=t(k)\ge1$ with $t^3\log k=o(k)$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+t,k))=o(k)$. This is the first upper bound on the boxicity of $K(n,k)$ that is sublinear in $n$. We also show that for large enough $k$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+1,k))\le \frac{3\ln (2k+1)}{\ln\ln (2k+1)}$.

papers.title: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
papers.abstract: For $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $Q\ge 1$, set $F_Q(x,y)=Q\min_{1\le q\le Q}\lVert qx\rVert\lVert qy\rVert$, where $q$ ranges over positive integers and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes distance to the nearest integer. The set on which the uniform Littlewood constant $L=\limsup_{Q\to\infty}F_Q$ is positive has full Hausdorff dimension. We prove that for every fixed $c>0$ the superlevel set $\{L\ge c\}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two. More precisely, the Lebesgue measure of $\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2:F_Q(x,y)\ge c\}$ is $O_c(Q^{-\kappa(c)})$ for some $\kappa(c)>0$ and all $Q\ge 2$. The proof combines large deviations for one diagonal action on the space of unimodular lattices with effective equidistribution of expanding horospheres for another.

papers.title: Radius decay and boundary polymers: cluster expansion for long-range many-body tilts
papers.abstract: We consider a nearest-neighbor Gibbs measure on a region in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (e.g., the Ising model) tilted by $\sum_{x,r} g_{x,r}$, where $g_{x,r}$ is an arbitrary function of the spins in the ball of radius $r$ about $x$, with $\|g_{x,r}\|_\infty\leq \exp(-C r)$: an exponential decay in the radius of the ball rather than in its volume. Standard cluster expansions fail for such many-body tilts, as a ball of radius $r$ carries $\exp(c r^2)$ configurations. We show that the partition function can be resummed into a polymer model whose polymers are outer boundaries of connected unions of balls, decorated by the spins along them, with weights decaying exponentially in the boundary length. The proof uses only the domain Markov property of the base measure; it develops a version of this resummation argument that appeared in a recent work of the authors in the context of RG analysis of Grassmann variables. As applications, we show convergent cluster expansions for many-body tilts of Ising models at high and low temperatures; existence of infinite-volume limits; and exponential decay of correlations.

papers.title: Spinorial geometry of Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein manifolds
papers.authors: Beatrice Brienza, Matteo Kevin Crisafio, Anna Fino, Dario Martelli
papers.abstract: We present a pair of spinorial equations, generalizing the internal Killing spinor equations of Type I supergravity, and show that they characterize several classes of Bismut-Hermitian-Einstein structures on six-dimensional Riemannian spin manifolds. We show that in this framework the local reduction to a four-dimensional transverse Hermitian geometry is provided by two canonical, commuting, Bismut-parallel Killing vector fields arising as bilinears in the Killing spinors, without assuming compactness. In one class, the transverse geometry is conformally Kahler and both compact and non-compact solutions exist. We also discuss variants that do not admit compact solutions, one of which has hyper-Hermitian transverse geometry. We discuss the relation of these structures to the Hull-Strominger system with closed three-form and to five-dimensional Gauntlett-Kim geometries and provide explicit embeddings in Type I, Type IIB and massive Type IIA supergravity, as well as in generalized supergravity. We illustrate our results with a number of examples, both compact and non-compact.

papers.title: Matching statistics in regular hypergraphs and applications
papers.abstract:
For fixed $k\ge3$, we determine the first sublinear correction to the logarithm of the matching partition function for a class of $n$-vertex $d$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs, uniformly for activities in each fixed compact interval of $(0,\infty)$.Our hypotheses include every regular linear hypergraph of polynomial degree and a class of nonlinear hypergraphs described by higher codegrees and intersection patterns, which we introduce here. The weighted counting estimate implies an averaged version of Kahn's conjecture: under the uniform measure, the expected number of uncovered vertices is $(1+o(1))nd^{-1/k}$, with concentration and large deviations on this scale. The proof combines a novel variant of random greedy counting, based on short stages and regular completions, with a new entropy method that uses intersection patterns to control reconstruction after deleting matching edges.
  We highlight the following applications. (i) Partial transversals in Latin squares. Every Latin square of order $n$ has $(n/e^2)^n\exp((3+o(1))n^{2/3})$ partial transversals. Also, almost all partial transversals have $(1+o(1))n^{2/3}$ missing cells.
  (ii) Linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs. There are $(n/e^2)^{n^2/6}\exp((1/2+o(1))n^{5/3})$ linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs on $[n]$, and almost all have $n^2/6-(1/6+o(1))n^{5/3}$ edges.
  (iii) Matroids of fixed rank. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the number $m(n,r)$ of rank-$r$ matroids on $[n]$ satisfies $\log m(n,r)=\frac{n^{r-1}}{r!}(\log n-r+1)+\left(\frac1{(r-1)!}+o(1)\right)n^{r-1-1/r}$, refining the estimates of van der Hofstad, Pendavingh and van der Pol.

papers.title: Patterns, Distances, and Structure in Sparse Sets
papers.abstract:
A central theme in modern harmonic analysis, with strong connections to Ramsey theory, is the tension between randomness and structure: to what extent can a "large" set avoid prescribed configurations, and when must such patterns inevitably appear? The answer depends delicately on how size is measured, with notions such as Hausdorff dimension, Fourier dimension, and density leading to strikingly different phenomena.
  In this mini-course, we explore this theme through two complementary perspectives. On one hand, we study translation-invariant linear patterns, a natural class of Euclidean Ramsey-type configurations. On the other hand, we investigate distance sets of sparse subsets of Euclidean space, which encode metric configurations of pairs of points.
  Together, these results illustrate a unifying principle: while sparse sets may avoid individual configurations, sufficiently strong analytic or geometric conditions enforce the emergence of Ramsey-type structure. The course will emphasize key ideas, methods, and examples, aiming to provide an accessible entry point to current developments at the interface of harmonic analysis, geometric measure theory, and Euclidean Ramsey theory. Lectures are by Malabika Pramanik.

papers.title: Particle systems and the supercooled Stefan problem: Long time behaviour and fluctuations
papers.authors: Thomas Blore, D. G. M. Flynn, Ben Hambly
papers.abstract: We consider an infinite system of particles on the positive real line, initiated from a Poisson point process, which move according to Brownian motion up until the hitting time of a barrier. The barrier increases when it is hit, allowing for the possibility of sequences of successive jumps to occur instantaneously. The scaling limit gives a representation for the supercooled Stefan problem and its free boundary, from which we can determine the asymptotic limit for the barrier movement. We establish also a functional central limit theorem describing the fluctuations about this limit, from which we can determine the rate of convergence for particle system approximations to the supercooled Stefan problem under ``weak feedback" assumptions introduced in arXiv:1811.12356. We finally show that these fluctuations are identical to the fluctuations of a continuous analogue to 1D-MDLA.

papers.title: Qualitative properties of solutions to anisotropic parabolic equations: Part III- H\"{o}lder continuity
papers.authors: Simone Ciani, Eurica Henriques, Maria O. Savchenko, Igor I. Skrypnik
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the local H\"older continuity of non-negative solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear anisotropic partial differential equations, with prototype \[ u_t-\sum_{i=1}^N D_i\Big(|D_i u^{m_i}|^{p_i-2}D_i u^{m_i}\Big)=0, \quad m_i>0,\quad p_i>1,\quad i=1,\ldots,N. \] The main result shows that, when the exponents describing the diffusion in different spatial directions are sufficiently close to one another, the solutions enjoy local H\"older continuity. A key feature of the analysis is the distinction between two diffusion regimes: the degenerate and the singular cases; the local regularity results are established in both regimes, under suitable conditions on the exponents.

papers.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erd\H{o}s-Graham irregularity problem
papers.abstract: For $c>0$ let $f_c(n)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of distinct elements of $A$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham asked whether $f_c(n)$ depends on $n$ in an irregular way (Erd\H{o}s Problem \#361). We prove that $f_c(n)=\lfloor cn\rfloor-\lceil n/2\rceil$ for $c\ge 1$, while for $0<c<1$ the ratio $f_c(n)/n$ has $\limsup$ equal to $c/2$, attained along odd $n$, and, along the integers $n$ whose least non-divisor equals a prime power $q$, tends to \[ \max\Bigl\{\frac cq,\; c-\frac12+\frac{1-c}{q}\Bigr\} \qquad\text{whenever } 2^{q-2}\min\{c,1-c\}\le 1 . \] Consequently $f_c(n)/n$ converges if and only if $c\ge1$; for $0<c<1$ it has at least two limit points, and arbitrarily many as $c\to0^+$ or $c\to1^-$. For $c=1/2$ the set of limit points is exactly $\{1/6,1/4\}$. The upper bounds follow from an inverse theorem of independent interest: if $s\ge1$, $q$ is the least positive integer not dividing $s$, and $\varepsilon>0$, then every $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,E\}$ with $|A|\ge E/q+\varepsilon T$ has a subset summing to $sT$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $T$ and all $E\le sT/2^{q-2}$. For $s=2$, this extends Alon's theorem on subsets of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ with no subset sum equal to $2N$. The results for $c\ge1$ and the $\limsup$, as well as the limits and the inverse theorem for $q\in\{2,3\}$, have been formalized and machine-checked in the Lean~4 proof assistant.

papers.title: Irregular weight-one Eisenstein series and Euler systems
papers.abstract: Let $f=E_1(\chi_1,\chi_2)$ be an irregular Eisenstein series of weight one, that is, with $\chi_1(p)=\chi_2(p)$, and consider the generically cuspidal ordinary family passing through it. When $\chi_1$, $\chi_2$ and $\chi_1\chi_2^{-1}$ are primitive of the same conductor, we show that the specialization at $f$ of the modular-symbol $p$-adic $L$-function of this family, with periods taken in the cohomology of the compactified modular curves, factors as a product of two Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$. Since there are no complex critical values in weight one, the factorization is obtained directly from the cohomological construction: we compute the tame-twisted modular measure by means of the localized Sharifi map and explicit reciprocity, and show that tame twisting identifies the compact period modules at weight one. This gives a weight-one analogue of the factorization of Bella\"iche--Dasgupta for critical-slope Eisenstein series. As applications, and under explicit specialization hypotheses, we compare Kato classes with circular units, Heegner classes with elliptic units, and diagonal cycles with Kato classes through two successive Eisenstein degenerations. We also discuss the passage from compact to open periods, and include an exposition of the congruence and degeneration methods underlying these comparisons.

papers.title: Equilibrium points of logarithmic potentials
papers.abstract: We construct logarithmic potentials with positive masses at a sequence of points tending to infinity and with no critical points. These potentials can have any prescribed order $\rho \in [1/2, 1)$; for $\rho = 1/2$ we obtain examples of both normal and maximal type. For $1/2 < \rho < 1$, the masses at conjugate poles are prescribed by a power law. We determine the pole asymptotics and the angular growth of these potentials. For sums of simple fractions with absolutely summable complex residues and nonzero sum of residues, we prove the existence of infinitely many zeros and compare their counting function with that of the poles.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Dynamics on Arbitrary Time Scales
papers.authors: Billur Kaymak\c{c}alan (University of Turkish Aeronautical Association), Behiye \.{I}layda Sel\c{c}uk (Bilkent University)
papers.abstract: The leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron combines a passive membrane law with threshold-triggered firing and reset. We formulate this hybrid neuron model, under constant input, on an arbitrary Hilger time scale $\mathbb{T}$. Our central result is that, after the first spike, the firing times satisfy $t_{n+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}^{+}(t_n+T_c)$, where $T_c$ is the classical reset-to-threshold travel time. This recursion requires no periodicity, homogeneity, or translation invariance of $\mathbb{T}$; it holds for every time scale that is unbounded above. To preserve the passive membrane physics, we use the inverse cylinder transformation to construct a positively regressive coefficient $p_m$. The resulting delta-dynamic equation is exactly the restriction to $\mathbb{T}$ of the classical continuous-time LIF trajectory. By contrast, the direct transcription $V^\Delta=-(V-V_\infty)/\tau_m$ exhibits graininess-dependent sign reversal and amplification at coarse right-scattered points. The first firing time is the forward projection of the classical continuous threshold-crossing time onto $\mathbb{T}$, and, when the graininess is bounded by $\mu^\ast$, the per-event forward-projection delay -- from each reset to the next realized firing time, relative to the continuous crossing time computed from that same reset -- is bounded above by $\mu^\ast$. On $\mathbb{T}=h\mathbb{Z}$ we obtain the explicit lattice-quantized law $T_{\mathrm{ISI}}^{(h)}=h\lceil T_c/h\rceil$, which converges to the classical continuous-time inter-spike interval as $h\to0^+$. The framework therefore separates preserved membrane physics from the temporal opportunity structure imposed by the time domain. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic Hilger-calculus treatment of a threshold-and-reset LIF spiking neuron on an arbitrary time scale.

papers.title: FanCyqlone: A Parallelized Solver for Multi-Horizon Optimal Control
papers.authors: Matisse Teuwen, Pieter Pas, Mathijs Schuurmans, Panagiotis Patrinos
papers.abstract: Multi-horizon optimal control aims to select optimal control sequences simultaneously for several possible future scenarios, ensuring consistency at the first stage. While this enables advanced model predictive control schemes that explicitly handle prediction uncertainty, solving these problems tends to be costly. We introduce FanCyqlone, a linear solver that exploits parallelism across both time steps and scenario branches. The method builds on Cyqlone to compute the contribution of each branch and combines these results through a shared root problem. We integrate FanCyqlone into QPALM to develop FanCyQPALM, a solver for multi-horizon optimal control problems with general linear stage-wise constraints. We compare its performance with state-of-the-art solvers on spring-mass and quadruped control benchmarks.

papers.title: Laguerre tessellations in spaces of constant curvature and their sectional distributions
papers.abstract: We determine the sectional distributions of Poisson--Laguerre tessellations in spaces of non-zero constant curvature, proving closure under totally geodesic sections and deriving explicit weight intensity measures. This includes sections of Poisson--Voronoi tessellations. We construct the generalised polar region, a new geometric object which extends existing polar constructions for both positive and negative curvature and provides an alternative representation of Laguerre tessellations. We also give deterministic conditions for tessellation existence and establish sharp integrability criteria for Poisson--Laguerre tessellations.

papers.title: Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract:
We revisit the problem of estimating $k$ linear regressors with self-selection bias in $n$ dimensions up to error $\varepsilon$ with the maximum self-selection criterion, as introduced by Cherapanamjeri, Daskalakis, Ilyas, and Zampetakis [CDIZ23, STOC]. Our main result is a $\mathrm{poly}(n,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time algorithm for the unknown-index variant of this problem, thereby improving upon the running times of the best known algorithms due to Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] and Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Zhou [KMZ26, COLT] with exponential dependence on $k$. Our algorithm succeeds in the presence of correlated noise between regressors, which captures the related setting of max-affine regression. Consequently, we also give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem, improving on the prior works of Ghosh, Pananjady, Guntuboyina, and Ramchandran [GPGR22, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory] and Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] with exponential dependence on $k$.
  Prior works exhaustively search over a $k$-dimensional subspace spanned by the regressors, using conditional moments of the response to test candidates. In contrast, our algorithm is driven by an improved understanding of the moments of the covariates. We show that, restricting to observations with large response values, the degree-$(\log n)$ Hermite moment of the covariates approximately decomposes as a sum of tensor powers of the regressors. The first step of our algorithm can be viewed as a tensor decomposition algorithm for these implicitly represented high-order tensors, which outputs unit vectors parallel to the regressors. A secondary step based on a simple variant of ordinary least squares extracts estimates for the regressors given these unit vectors. We believe our analytic insight and algorithmic components may have applications to designing efficient algorithms for other latent-variable problems.

papers.title: Luenberger observers for two-gene regulatory networks with sigmoidal regulation: explicit observability conditioning, polytopic convergence certificates, and a logistic--Hill comparison
papers.abstract: Only a few species of a gene regulatory network can be measured, so the others must be reconstructed by a state observer, and how well this works depends on the function chosen to describe regulation. We examine this for the two-gene negative feedback loop with one measured protein, for monotone regulation functions including the logistic function and the Hill function with its leaky and shifted variants. Using standard tools, we show that the answer is set by the smallest and the largest slope of the regulation function on the concentrations visited. For every function considered, the unmeasured concentration can be recovered from the measured signal and its rate of change, with an error sensitivity set by the smallest slope. A Luenberger observer with explicit gains converges exponentially from any initial guess and tolerates bounded measurement noise whenever a checkable matrix condition involving only the largest slope holds, as it does for every model examined with bounded slopes. The guaranteed rate cannot exceed the degradation rate of the unmeasured protein unless the smallest slope is positive, and faster rates then hold only for small initial errors. All reported rates are certified from above and below. At matched threshold and steepness, no family is uniformly better: the logistic function is better conditioned when the threshold lies mid-range, leaky or shifted Hill functions when it lies low. Hill functions with exponent below one have an unbounded slope at zero concentration and lose the global guarantee, which logistic and shifted Hill functions keep.

papers.title: Mean-field Fluctuations for First-Passage Percolation with Symmetric Kernels
papers.abstract: We study first-passage percolation on finite weighted graphs whose normalized Weibull edge hazards form a symmetric Markov kernel on $N$ vertices. We prove that a uniform absolute spectral gap and an $O(N^{-1})$ bound on a fixed even-step return probability imply the stochastic mean-field passage-time limit and an independent Gaussian hopcount limit. Jointly with these quantities, the entire geodesic from an arbitrary source to an independent uniform target is approximated in total variation by an independent Markov chain stopped at the hopcount. This comparison yields laws of large numbers for fixed-length path segments and joint central limit theorems for bounded additive observables. The results extend to edge laws with a uniform relative hazard error $o(1/\log N)$, including common noise distributions with a power-law hazard and a positive-power error near zero. Applications include integrable singular torus kernels, macroscopic spread-out graphs, non-transitive regular graphs, finite groups, and discretizations of symmetric continuum kernels.

papers.title: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
papers.abstract:
We consider stationary log-correlated random fields of the form
  \[
  X_n(t):= \sum_{j\le n} f(e^{\tau_j} t+ v_{j})\,,\quad t\in \mathbb{R}
  \]
  for a centered 1-periodic analytic function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, where $(\tau_j)_{j\ge1}$ are the arrival times of a rate-1 Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ are iid uniform random variables in $[0,1)$.
  We show that with high probability,
  \[
  \max_{t\in[-1,1]}X_n(t) = c_1 n + c_2 \tau_n- (c_3+o(1))\log n
  \]
  where $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are positive constants depending on $f$.
  In particular, the random frequency $\tau_n$ produces a central limit fluctuation of order $\sqrt{n}$, together with a logarithmic correction different from the ubiquitous Bramson correction for models with strong comparisons to Gaussian fields, such as homogeneous branching random walks and log-characteristic polynomials of C$\beta$E matrices.
  Our proof makes a connection with branching random walks in random time-environment, where coarse-scale fluctuations of the arrival times $\tau_j$ play the role of a quenched random environment, and fine-scale fluctuations are leveraged to establish a branching decorrelation structure.
  We conjecture analogous asymptotics for the characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices, and expect the same mechanism to arise in other Poissonian fields such as characteristic polynomials of sparse random matrices.

papers.title: Permutation patterns and higher connectivity in inversion graphs
papers.abstract:
We prove that any permutation $\pi \in S_n$ whose inversion graph is $k$-connected has at least $\frac{k+1}{2}n - C$ inversions, where $C$ depends only on $k$.
