papers.authors: Julian Eisfeld, Hermann Kampermann, Nikolai Wyderka
papers.abstract:
The question of local encodability asks: can a given, multipartite pure quantum state be completed to an orthonormal basis using only local unitary rotations? If any such state in a given system has this property, it is called universally locally encodable (ULE), a feature, which has applications in quantum information theory, engineering and math. Despite its easy formulation, the answer to this question depends nontrivially on the local dimensions of the system: While universal local encodability is known for $2\times 2$, $4\times 4$ and $8\times 8$-dimensional systems, it was so-far only conjectured to hold in $3\times 3$, and non-ULE was recently proved for systems of four and more qubits by Pauwels and G\"uhne.
  We resolve the open conjecture by proving universality for two qutrits. Furthermore, we construct (among others) universal local encodings in dimensions $d\times2$ for $d\ge2$, in dimensions $d\times3$ for $d=3,4$ and $d\ge6$, and in every bipartite system with one or two infinite-dimensional subsystems. For finite-dimensional multipartite systems, we turn a heuristic parameter count into a necessary condition for universality, which excludes universal local encodability in infinitely many cases. Finally, we give universal local encodability an operational interpretation by showing that non-ULE is equivalent to whether general measurements yield an advantage over projectively simulable ones in discrimination tasks where unknown, random local unitary rotations have to be detected.

papers.title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
papers.abstract: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group $D_4$ and the quaternion group $Q_8$. We provide two complementary constructions of statistical processes. The first extends the Smith normal form algorithm in [Phys. Rev. X $\textbf{16}$, 011010 (2026), arXiv:2412.01886] to higher groups, generating processes from lattice geometry and prescribed local moves. For a finite higher group $\mathbb G$, we prove that statistical processes on a $d$-sphere are classified by $H_{d+2}(B\mathbb G,\mathbb Z)$. The second constructs processes directly from homology classes without examining exponentially many defect configurations, enabling us to study statistics for complex higher-group structures where the previous method is computationally prohibitive. These processes detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases. For example, we distinguish 2-group anomalies in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions. Higher-group statistics provide new invariants for characterizing coupled defects in quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: Infinite spin superparticles
papers.abstract: We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincar\'e algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.

papers.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
papers.authors: Erwin Luesink, Archishman Saha, Tanya Schmah, Cristina Stoica
papers.abstract: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations for symmetric programming and reasoning
papers.abstract:
We develop a mathematical abstraction for uniformly exploiting symmetries in programming and reasoning based on the mathematical proof principle `without-loss-of-generality' (w.l.o.g.). Given: group actions that describe symmetries of the input and the output; and a canoniser, which captures how arbitrary inputs get sent to canonical ones, our construction extends any function from the canonical inputs to the whole domain.
  We characterise the conditions on the canonisers which guarantee that the construction gives the unique equivariant (i.e. symmetry-preserving) extension. Furthermore, we adapt the construction to a dependently-typed setting, where it captures traditional symmetric w.l.o.g. arguments via the Curry-Howard correspondence. Finally, we extend the construction to algebraic data types, where the symmetries of the constructors both uniquely determine the symmetries of the data type and pave the way for efficient execution.

papers.title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs
papers.authors: Arnab Sanyal, Gourav Datta, Sandeep P. Chinchali
papers.abstract: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a $4$ GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an $8$ GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, $\texttt{llama.cpp}$'s K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At $1\%$ and $3.5\%$ perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are $5.7-31.4\%$ smaller than the best $\texttt{llama.cpp}$ format. A bit-exact $0.21$ mm$^2$ ASIC decoder unit ($1$ GHz, $7$ nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to $36\%$ and $38\%$ ($54\%$ and $44\%$ with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ needs $58-64\%$ less time and $53-57\%$ less energy per token than CPU $\texttt{llama.cpp}$, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6$\times$ faster at $3.89$ bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).

papers.title: Exact characterization of three-terminal fermion counting under one-body scattering
papers.authors: Zhanning Wang, Yongtao Li, Rub\'en Seoane Souto, Jos\'e C. Abadillo-Uriel
papers.abstract: Quantum scattering is a fundamental probe of the scattering region and the quantum dynamics of outgoing particles. In two terminals, the statistics of non-interacting fermions is described by a generalized binomial distribution, that arises from the Pauli exclusion principle, while deviations are a signature of interactions. In this work, we extend this result to a scattering region coupled to three outgoing terminals (or channels), obtaining exact bounds for the statistics of the outgoing fermions. In particular, for two fermions and three terminals, four inequalities involving six measured probabilities determine whether a non-interacting scatterer can explain the observed statistics. Applying these inequalities to recent scattering experiments in cold atoms, we are able to identify a regime where interactions have a significant contribution on the outgoing particles. Therefore, our work opens up the possibility of identifying fermion interactions at the nanoscale in systems that range from mesoscopic conductors to optical traps in cold atoms.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's. On AirfRANS its errors are second only to those of a boundary-integral model (GLOBE) and at least 1.6 times lower than those of Transolver and GeoTransolver.

papers.title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression
papers.authors: Carina Moreira Costa, Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Martin Schmidt
papers.abstract: We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. Using convex conjugacy of the softplus function, we replace the sigmoid relations by a single convex optimality-gap inequality and express the attacker's objective as a concave function. A change of variables makes the stationarity condition affine, leaving bounded bilinear equalities as the only nonconvex constraints. We derive finite bounds on all variables involved in these equalities, including a global bound on the coefficient norm and tighter bounds obtained by preprocessing based on convex optimization. Experiments on eight binary classification datasets evaluate attack effectiveness and compare the two reformulations when solved with \textsf{SCIP}. Attacks obtained by local optimization degrade predictive performance on most datasets, while the convex-analytic formulation produces substantially stronger reported dual bounds within a fixed time limit.

papers.title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
papers.authors: Anif N. Shikder, Ramit Dey, Jan Minac, Lyle E. Muller
papers.abstract: State space models (SSMs) are an emerging alternative to Transformers. SSMs offer linear-time inference and parallel training, but most implementations make the parallel scan efficient by making the recurrence diagonal: each channel of the hidden state is multiplied by an input-dependent real or complex number. These numbers commute, so the state records which inputs occurred but not their order. We formalize this with representation theory, which explains and fixes the state-tracking failures previously reported for SSMs. The state update defines a linear representation of the monoid of input sequences, and we show that an SSM tracks a group at every sequence length exactly when that group is a quotient of the group generated by its transition matrices. Two consequences follow. Diagonal real- and complex-valued SSMs can track only commutative groups, while the transition matrices of any SSM that can track a group must split into independent blocks over the real, complex, and quaternion numbers. We then introduce HyperSSM, which adds quaternion channels while keeping linear-time inference and parallel training. Trained only on final answers, HyperSSM solves the group tasks of recent state-tracking benchmarks exactly with at most five state numbers. This includes $S_5$ with 32 generators, where previous SSMs are at chance, and HyperSSM generalizes to sequences 25 times longer than those seen in training. Because the theory says what the transitions must encode, the learned weights of the linear recurrence can be interpreted directly. We demonstrate this by recovering the calibration of a real gyroscope, the rotations of imperfect qubit gates and the geometry of protein backbones.

papers.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
papers.abstract: We provide an efficient implementation of combinatorial Bernoulli factories. Such a factory turns coins of unknown biases $x$ into a random vertex of a polytope $P$ whose mean is exactly $x$. For every affine slice of the cube (the class of polytopes that admit a factory), we give a single algorithm whose expected number of coin flips and running time at every interior $x$ are polynomial in the dimension and in $1/{\delta_*}$, where ${\delta_*}=\min_i\{x_i,1-x_i\}$ is never supplied to the algorithm. For perfect matchings this gives $O(n^{8}{\delta_*}^{-2}\log(n/{\delta_*}))$ flips, while the factory of Niazadeh, Paes Leme, and Schneider [STOC 2021] spends at least $n^{2n-1}$ flips in expectation at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix. For other polytopes, our method rounds exactly given a point deep inside $P$ and the promise that $x$ is far from the boundary of $P$.

papers.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
papers.authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Shuoqing Deng, Daxin Huang, Dominykas Norgilas
papers.abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

papers.title: Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete
papers.abstract:
Kalah is a classic two-player game in the mancala family of sowing games. Computers have solved several standard-size starting positions, but the complexity of the game on boards of growing size has remained open. We study the natural generalization in which the number of pits per side is part of the input and an arbitrary position is given, with the stone counts given in unary. We show that deciding whether a designated player can force a win from such a position is PSPACE-complete. The hard positions have Alice to move first and both stores initially empty. The same positions are hard under either common convention for capture opposite an empty pit, and with or without the bonus rule, which gives a player another turn when the last stone is sown into their own store.
  We introduce Line Kalah as an intermediate problem, a game on a line in which stones that leave the line effectively disappear and Alice must save each of her target pits before Bob captures it, and we reduce quantified Boolean formulas to it. The reduction uses a set of sequential timer piles whose last stones approach a group of targets, forcing Alice to choose between two captures in order to set the truth value of a variable, and a final capture gadget to test a clause chosen by Bob (only one is needed adversarially).
  Since either player may move any pile at any time, the stages are placed so that premature timer firings protect earlier potential targets. For a true formula, Alice's strategy against arbitrary opposing play either gains enough time to save the remaining targets (after Bob deviates from the intended play) or reaches the final test with a correctly encoded, protected input. Finally, the line positions are embedded in Kalah with both stores empty. A separate Bob pit holds the score adjustment, so the winner takes a strict majority of the stones.

papers.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.

papers.title: Unequal-probability distributional balance and the Horvitz-Thompson estimator
papers.authors: Blair Robertson, Chris Price, Marco Reale, Philip Davies
papers.abstract: Auxiliary information can improve estimation precision under probability sampling, but the relationship between the study and auxiliary variables may not be known well enough to specify suitable balancing variables. Distributionally balanced designs address this by targeting agreement between sample and population auxiliary distributions. We extend energy-based distributional balance to prescribed unequal inclusion probabilities by comparing the empirical sample distribution with an inclusion-probability-weighted population distribution. Under a regularity condition relating the study values divided by their inclusion probabilities to the auxiliaries, we establish an upper bound on the design variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator in terms of the expected energy distance. This bound motivates an algorithm that exchanges units between randomly paired candidate samples without increasing their average energy distance. Combined with random initialization and uniform selection of a final candidate, the procedure preserves the prescribed first-order inclusion probabilities. We evaluate its auxiliary-space properties and estimation performance using generated populations and the Meuse data.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
papers.authors: Bowen Xiao, Zhiyao Yang, Huangjun Zhu
papers.abstract: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.

papers.title: Fictitious Play When Agents Are Not Expected-Utility Maximizers: A Geometric Analysis in $2$-Action Games
papers.authors: Hao Liang, Solaleh Mohammadi, Kaiqing Zhang
papers.abstract: Fictitious play (FP) is one of the earliest and most fundamental learning procedures in games, where each agent independently chooses a best response to the empirical distribution of opponents' past actions by maximizing the expected payoff with respect to it. However, learning agents may not always be expected-utility maximizers: they may use nonlinear evaluation functionals to account for the uncertainty induced by the opponents, e.g., via risk measures. In this work, we study nonlinear fictitious play (NL-FP), in which each pure action is evaluated by a general, possibly nonlinear functional of the payoff distribution induced by the opponent's empirical belief. To analyze NL-FP, we first identify a single-crossing property (SCP) of evaluation functionals that preserves the classical geometry of FP in $2\times2$ games. Furthermore, we conduct a novel geometric analysis of the convergence behavior of NL-FP in $2\times2$ games, even when the SCP fails. Beyond $2\times2$ games, we show that the convergence of NL-FP in $2\times n$ ($n\ge3$) games may fail even for continuous-time NL-FP, when the two-action player uses conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in a $2\times3$ game. In addition, we identify a finite-crossing condition that ensures convergence of the selected continuous-time dynamics and the discrete-time iterates in general $2\times n$ games, which also provides new insights into the global landscape of continuous-time classical FP in such games.

papers.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
papers.authors: Omar Bachain, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara
papers.abstract: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $\Lambda$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cram\'er--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.

papers.title: The q-WZ Method for Infinite Series
papers.authors: William Y. C. Chen, Ernest X. W. Xia
papers.abstract: Motivated by the telescoping proofs of two identities of Andrews and Warnaar, we find that infinite q-shifted factorials can be incorporated into the implementation of the q-Zeilberger algorithm in the approach of Chen, Hou and Mu to prove nonterminating basic hypergeometric series identities. This observation enables us to extend the q-WZ method to identities on infinite series. As examples, we will give the q-WZ pairs for some classical identities such as the q-Gauss sum, the $_6\phi_5$ sum, Ramanujan's $_1\psi_1$ sum and Bailey's $_6\psi_6$ sum.

papers.title: Arnold's problem on paper folding
papers.abstract: This is a story about the question of whether folding a square flat can increase its perimeter. It is written primarily for school students.

papers.title: Floer field theory for tangles
papers.abstract: We use quilted Floer theory to construct functor-valued invariants of tangles arising from moduli spaces of flat bundles on punctured surfaces. As an application, we show the non-triviality of certain elements in the symplectic mapping class groups of moduli spaces of flat bundles on punctured spheres.

papers.title: Reductive group actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study rationality properties of reductive group actions over fields k of characteristic zero. In doing so, we unify Luna's theory of spherical systems with the Borel-Tits theory of reductive groups. Specifically, for any reductive group action, we define a generalized Tits index; its main constituents are a root system and a generalization of the anisotropic kernel. For k-spherical varieties (i.e., those for which a minimal parabolic subgroup has an open orbit), we obtain explicit smooth completions of the set of rational points. Over local fields, this yields genuine compactifications that generalize the maximal Satake compactification of symmetric spaces. Our main tool is a k-version of the Local Structure Theorem.

papers.title: Iterative Refinement of A Modified Lavrentiev Regularization Method for De-convolution of the Discrete Helmholtz Type Differential Filter
papers.abstract: We analyze an iterated, modified Lavrentiev regularization method (Mitlar) for deconvolving the Helmholtz-type differential filter $G=(I-\delta^2\Delta)^{-1}$ used in large eddy simulation. The method replaces the Lavrentiev operator $G+\alpha I$ by the convex combination $(1-\alpha)G+\alpha I$; each step costs one Helmholtz solve, exactly as in iterated Lavrentiev regularization. We show that this one-line change has a precise structural meaning: the regularized operator is again a Helmholtz filter, now with the smaller radius $\sqrt{\alpha}\,\delta$, and $J$ refinement steps coincide with van Cittert approximate deconvolution of order $J$ applied to that filter. Consequently the regularization error is governed by the product $\alpha\delta^2$ rather than by $\alpha$ alone. We prove sharp error bounds of order $(\alpha\delta^2)^{s}$ on a Hilbert scale, $0\le s\le J+1$, with saturation exactly at $s=J+1$; show that for noise-free data the Mitlar error never exceeds the iterated Lavrentiev error, for every datum, every $\alpha$ and every $J$; give a priori parameter choices for noisy data with explicit $\delta$-dependence; and prove finite element error bounds whose constants grow only linearly in $J$. Finally we show that the iterates decrease a natural energy functional for every $\alpha>0$, and derive a computable stopping rule that guarantees monotone decrease of a weighted error and always terminates. Numerical examples illustrate the theory and compare Mitlar with a family of Tikhonov--Lavrentiev methods.

papers.title: On the fractional Dehn twist coefficients of branched coverings
papers.abstract: We discuss how the fractional Dehn twist coefficient behaves under a fully ramified branched covering of an open book, and give applications to both topological and contact 3-manifolds. Among them, we show that non-right-veering closed braids represent virtually loose transverse links.

papers.title: A Generalization of the Passivity Theorem and the Small Gain Theorem Based on $\rho $-Stability, with Application to a Parameter Adaptation Algorithm for Recursive Identification
papers.abstract: The usual passivity theorem considers a closed-loop, the direct chain of which consists of a strictly passive stable operator $H_{1}$, and the feedback chain of which consists of a passive operator $H_{2}$. Then the closed-loop is stable. Let $\rho >1$. We show here that the closed-loop is still stable when the direct chain consists of a strictly $\rho ^{-1}$-passive $% \rho ^{-1}$-stable operator (a weaker condition than above) and the feedback chain consists of a $\rho $-passive operator (a stronger condition than above). Variations on the theme of the small gain theorem (incremental or not) can be made similarly. This approach explains the results obtained in a paper on identification which was recently published.

papers.title: Derived invariance of the numbers $h^{0,p}(X)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be derived equivalent smooth projective varieties over the field of complex numbers. We prove that the numbers $h^{0,p}(X_1)$ and $h^{0,p}(X_2)$ are equal for any $p$.

papers.title: Some homological properties of category $\mathcal{O}$, V
papers.authors: Hankyung Ko, Volodymyr Mazorchuk, Rafael Mr{\dj}en
papers.abstract: We compute projective dimension of translated simple modules in the regular block of the BGG category $\mathcal{O}$ in terms of Kazhdan-Lusztig combinatorics. This allows us to determine which projectives can appear at the last step of a minimal projective resolution for a translated simple module, confirming a conjecture by Johan K{\aa}hrstr\"om. We also derive some inequalities, in terms of Lusztig's $\mathbf{a}$-function, for possible degrees in which the top (or socle) of a translated simple module can live. Finally, we relate Kostant's problem with decomposability and isomorphism of translated simple modules, addressing yet another conjecture by Johan K{\aa}hrstr\"om.

papers.title: Classification of the d-representation-finite symmetric k-algebras of finite representation type
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric Nakayama algebras and of all $d$-representation-finite trivial extensions of path algebras of quivers, over an arbitrary field. As a consequence we get a classification, up to Morita equivalence, of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric algebras of finite representation type over an algebraically closed field.

papers.title: Eigenvalue estimates of the drifted Cheng-Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
papers.authors: J\'ulio C. M. da Fonseca, Jos\'e N. V. Gomes
papers.abstract: We establish universal eigenvalue inequalities for a drifted Cheng--Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Our approach combines a universal quadratic eigenvalue inequality for operators in divergence form with a Rauch-type comparison theorem and a Bochner-type formula. We evaluate the geometric terms in this quadratic inequality under suitable assumptions on the radial behavior of the coefficient tensor and the drifting function, together with curvature pinching conditions. In the general setting, we establish a Rauch-type comparison theorem for the Cheng--Yau operator and derive two auxiliary estimates from its Bochner-type formula. We then prove integral estimates of independent interest and apply them to obtain the desired eigenvalue inequalities for both the Cheng--Yau operator and the drifted Laplacian, recovering known inequalities for the Laplacian. We also establish a rigidity result for the Cheng--Yau operator on a class of bounded annular domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds. In Euclidean space, this result can be applied, for instance, with the potential function of the Gaussian shrinking soliton. The hyperbolic space is treated separately in two settings, one exploiting the conformal relation between its metric and the Euclidean metric, and the other via its warped product structure, reducing the problem to one dimension. We extend the hyperbolic construction of the fundamental gap for the Laplacian to a class of operators in divergence form. Examples are provided to illustrate the scope and applicability of our results.

papers.title: The Multipartite Ramsey numbers $m_j(C_3, C_m, n_1K_2,n_2K_2,\ldots, n_iK_2)$
papers.abstract: Assume that $K_{j\times n}$ be a complete, multipartite graph consisting of $j$ partite sets and $n$ vertices in each partite set. For given graphs $G_1, G_2,\ldots, G_n$, the multipartite Ramsey number (M-R-number) $m_j(G_1, G_2, \ldots,G_n)$ is the smallest integer $t$ such that for any $n$-edge-coloring $(G^1,G^2,\ldots, G^n)$ of the edges of $K_{j\times t}$, $G^i$ contains a monochromatic copy of $G_i$ for at least on $i$. C. J. Jayawardene, E. T. Baskoro et al. $(2016)$ gave the size of M-R-numbe $m_j(nK_2, C_7)$ for $j \geq 2 $ and $n\leq 6$. Y. Rowshan et al. $(2021)$ gave the size of M-R-number $m_j(nK_2, C_7)$ for $j = 2,3, 4$ and $n\geq 2$. Y. Rowshan $(2021)$ gave the size of M-R-number $m_j(nK_2,C_7)$, for each $j\geq 5$ and $n\geq 2$. In this article we compute the size of M-R-number $m_j(C_3,C_3, nK_2)$ for each $j\geq 7$, $n\geq 1$, $m_j(C_3,C_3, n_1K_2,n_2K_,\ldots,n_iK_2)$ for each $2\leq j\leq 6$, $i\geq 2, n_i\geq 1$, and M-R-number $m_j(C_3,C_4, nK_2)$, for each $n\geq 1$, and small $j$.

papers.title: On the Hausdorff measure of sets of non-Lyapunov behaviour, and a Jarnik-type theorem for random Schroedinger operators
papers.abstract: We consider the growth of the norms of transfer matrices of ergodic discrete Schr\"odinger operators in one dimension. It is known that the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is slower than prescribed by the Lyapunov exponent is residual in the part of the spectrum at which the Lyapunov exponent is positive. On the other hand, this exceptional set is of vanishing Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is integrable at zero. Here we show that this condition on $\rho(t)$ can not in general be improved: for operators with independent, identically distributed potentials of sufficiently regular distribution, the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is arbitrarily slow has infinite Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is non-increasing and not integrable at zero. The main technical ingredient, possibly of independent interest, is a Jarn\'ik-type theorem describing the Hausdorff measure of the set of real numbers well approximated by the eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator. The proof of this result relies on the theory of Anderson localisation and on the mass transference principle of Beresnevich--Velani.

papers.title: Testing the number of common factors by bootstrapped sample covariance matrix in high-dimensional factor models and errata
papers.authors: Long Yu, Peng Zhao, Wang Zhou
papers.abstract: This paper studies the impact of bootstrap procedure on the eigenvalue distributions of the sample covariance matrix under a high-dimensional factor structure. We provide asymptotic distributions for the top eigenvalues of bootstrapped sample covariance matrix under mild conditions. After bootstrap, the spiked eigenvalues which are driven by common factors will converge weakly to Gaussian limits after proper scaling and centralization. However, the largest non-spiked eigenvalue is mainly determined by the order statistics of the bootstrap resampling weights, and follows extreme value distribution. Based on the disparate behavior of the spiked and non-spiked eigenvalues, we propose innovative methods to test the number of common factors. Indicated by extensive numerical and empirical studies, the proposed methods perform reliably and convincingly under the existence of both weak factors and cross-sectionally correlated errors. Our technical details contribute to random matrix theory on spiked covariance model with convexly decaying density and unbounded support, or with general elliptical distributions.

papers.title: On properties of the generalized Davenport Expansion
papers.abstract: We study the continuity properties of a generalized Davenport Fourier expansion we recently discovered, by imposing conditions on the coefficients. We also put our expansion into perspective from the position of Appell sequences.

papers.title: Variation of Hodge structures for non-K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss unpolarized, complex variation of Hodge structures for non-K\"ahler manifolds. In particular, consider a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds with central fiber $X$. Suppose that the inclusion of complexes $(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\hookrightarrow (A^\bullet(X),d)$ induces injective maps \[ H^j(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\longrightarrow H^j(A^\bullet(X),d),\qquad j=k,\ k+1. \] Under this condition, we show that the period map is holomorphic and transversal. An essential ingredient for the proof is a deformation theory of filtered $(p,q)$-forms. We prove a jumping formula for filtered de Rham cohomology and obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for its dimension to be invariant under deformation of complex structures.

papers.title: Homology with the theme of Matlis
papers.abstract: Matlis proved a lot of homological properties of the fraction field of an integral domain. In this paper, we simplify and extend some of them from 1-dimensional (resp. rank one) cases to the higher dimensional (resp. finite rank) cases. For example, we study the weakly cotorsion property of $\Ext(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadratic $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$

papers.title: Rational limit cycles of Abel differential equations
papers.authors: Jos\'e Luis Bravo, Luis \'Angel Calder\'on, Ignacio Ojeda
papers.abstract: We study the number of rational limit cycles of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$, where $A(t)$ and $B(t)$ are real trigonometric polynomials. We show that this number is at most the degree of $A(t)$ plus one.

papers.title: Stability of singular limit cycles for Abel equations revisited
papers.authors: J. L. Bravo, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda
papers.abstract: A criterion is obtained for the semi-stability of the isolated singular positive closed solutions, i.e., singular positive limit cycles, of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$, where $A,B$ are smooth functions with two zeros in the interval $[0,T]$ and where these singular positive limit cycles satisfy certain conditions, which allows an upper bound on the number of limit cycles of the Abel equation to be obtained. The criterion is illustrated by obtaining an upper bound of two positive limit cycles for the family $A(t)=t(t-t_A)$, $B(t)=(t-t_B)(t-1)$, $t\in[0,1]$. In the linear trigonometric case, i.e., when $A(t)=a_0+a_1\sin t +a_2\cos t$, $B(t)=b_0+b_1\sin t+b_2\cos t$, an upper bound of two limit cycles is also obtained for $a_0,b_0$ sufficiently small and in the region where two positive limit cycles bifurcate from the origin.

papers.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
papers.authors: Pawe{\l} Duch, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Paolo Rinaldi
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $\Phi^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.

papers.title: Local duality theorems for commutative algebraic groups
papers.abstract: Let k be a non-archimedean local field and let G be a commutative algebraic k-group that contains no nontrivial unipotent subgroups if car k=0. Given any presentation of G as an extension of commutative algebraic k-groups E: 0 --> L --> G --> A --> 0, where L is affine and A is an abelian variety, we establish Pontryagin duality theorems that relate the fppf cohomology groups of G (equipped with the extension structure E) to the hypercohomology groups of the dual of G in the truncated derived category D^{[-1,0]}(k_{fppf}). These results have applications (to be discussed elsewhere) to certain generalizations of Lichtenbaum-van Hamel duality to a class of non-smooth proper k-varieties.

papers.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.

papers.title: Crystal Structure of Upper Cluster Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct upper seminormal crystals on the $\mu$-supported tropical points of skew-symmetric cluster algebras from their exchange matrices. A generic potential provides an additive categorification in which boundary representations determine the Cartan matrices and generic ranks describe the crystal operators. Under frozen-Jacobi-finiteness and reachability, the raising operators lift to locally nilpotent derivations of the upper cluster algebra. For $\tau$-exact boundary pairs, these derivations give integrable actions of derived Kac--Moody algebras in characteristic zero. In particular, the associated Cartan matrices are positive semidefinite. When the generic characters form a basis, this basis is BK-biperfect and the $\tau$-exact crystals are normal. We also construct algebraic Tits actions and describe compatibly pointed biperfect bases through a coefficient graph. The theory is illustrated by classical and new examples.

papers.title: General elementary methods meeting elementary properties of correlations
papers.abstract:
This is a kind of survey on properties of correlations of two very general arithmetic functions, from the point of view of {\it Ramanujan expansions}. In fact, our previous papers on these links had, as a focus, the "{\it Ramanujan coefficients}" of these correlations and the resulting "{\it R.e.e.f.}", i.e., {\it Ramanujan exact explicit formula}. This holds under a variety of sufficient conditions, mainly under two conditions of convergence involving correlation's {\it \lq \lq Eratosthenes Transform\rq \rq}, namely what we call {\it Delange Hypothesis} (DH) and {\it Wintner Assumption} (WA) (the former implying the latter). We proved, on Hardy-Ramanujan Journal, the {\it Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture} on {\it $2k-$twin primes}, in particular, from (DH) (implying convergence of the Ramanujan expansion, whence {\it R.e.e.f.}); then, we gave a more general proof, from (WA), again {\it entailing the R.e.e.f.}, but from another method of summation for {\it Ramanujan expansions},
  that we detailed in arXiv, "On Ramanujan smooth expansions for a general arithmetic function". There we also started to introduce local Ramanujan coefficients. Which we deepen here, entailing a new conditional proof of quoted H-L Conjecture.

papers.title: A sharper bound of the Hotelling-Solomons inequality
papers.abstract: The original Hotelling-Solomons inequality states that an upper bound of the absolute difference between the mean and median, standardized by the standard deviation, is 1. However, in this paper, we introduce a new bound that depends on the sample size, which is strictly smaller than 1.

papers.title: Electromagnetic scattering by Minkowski-type bianisotropic media
papers.abstract: We consider the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves by a bounded stationary inclusion whose effective constitutive law is of Minkowski type. The constant vector $V$ is regarded as a constitutive moving parameter. Such a law arises as an effective description of synthetic moving media and of suitable traveling-wave space--time modulations. Starting from the implicit Minkowski relations, we derive a Maxwell transmission system and its Lippmann--Schwinger volume-integral formulation. The dimensionless parameter $\beta=|V|/c_\Omega$ governs the pointwise constitutive inversion, namely the matrix is invertible precisely for $\beta\neq1$, while on the subcritical branch $0\leq\beta<1$ its inverse admits an explicit convergent expansion. Using the algebraic structure of the cross-product operator, we obtain a spectral characterization of solvability and a quantitative sufficient condition separating the static material contrast from the $V$-dependent contribution which allows to justify the convergence of the corresponding Born series. As an application, we prove that full-aperture electric far-field data at a fixed frequency uniquely determine the support of the inclusion within this perturbative regime without assuming that $V$ is known.

papers.title: Zero-divisor algebras of graph functions: quantum caging, entangling routing and stochastic first-passage exclusion
papers.abstract:
We show how algebraic constraints on weighted graphs yield exact localization and controlled transport in quantum and stochastic systems. Antisymmetrizing a noncommutative, nonassociative product of vertex functions defines a Lie bracket. For a specified Lie cobracket over commutative rings without nonzero $2$-torsion, compatibility holds if and only if products of distinct incident edge weights vanish. When the coefficient ring is a finite product of integral domains, the edges with nonzero weights in each component of the ring form a matching. These matchings are determined by the edge weights and need not coincide across the components.
  These matchings yield exact two-vertex caging in fixed quantum channels; separately specified channel-selective controls enable coherent routing and path--internal-state entanglement. For matching-supported stochastic jump rates, they enforce first-passage exclusion, while prescribed internal-state switching opens inaccessible paths and yields a singular weak-switching escape limit. The bracket--cobracket factorization identifies a common edge operator underlying quantum kinetic Hamiltonians and Markov generators, subject to distinct sign and positivity conditions. The algebra fixes the channel structure; controlled motion requires additional dynamical operations.

papers.title: A Unified Algorithmic Framework for Dynamic Assortment Optimization under MNL Choice
papers.authors: Shuo Sun, Rajan Udwani, Zuo-Jun Max Shen
papers.abstract: We consider assortment and inventory planning problems with dynamic stockout-based substitution effects, and without replenishment, in two different settings: (1) Customers can see all available products when they arrive, a typical scenario in physical stores. (2) The seller can choose to offer a subset of available products to each customer, which is more common on online platforms. Both settings are known to be computationally challenging, and the current approximation algorithms for the two settings are quite different. We develop a unified algorithm framework under the MNL choice model for both settings. Our algorithms improve on the state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of approximation guarantee and runtime, and the ability to manage uncertainty in the total number of customers and handle more complex constraints. In the process, we establish various novel properties of dynamic assortment planning (for the MNL choice model) that may be useful more broadly.

papers.title: Families of two dimensional modular $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules
papers.abstract: Let $F/{\mathbb Q}_p$ be a finite unramified extension, let $k$ be a finite extension of the residue field of $F$. We provide explicit constructions of integral structures for all rank two \'{e}tale Lubin-Tate $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules over $k$. We construct algebraic families of such integral structures and show that these comprehensively reflect the degeneration behaviour of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules. These results reveal new combinatorial structures of the moduli stack of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules, and allow us, in particular, to rederive the fact that the Serre weights assigned to a two dimensional ${\rm Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$-representation over $k$ can be read off from the geometry of the stack.

papers.title: Nonlinear Eigen-approach ADMM for Sparse Optimization on Stiefel Manifold
papers.authors: Jiawei Wang, Li Wang, Richard Yi Da Xu, Ren-Cang Li
papers.abstract: With growing interest in machine learning and data science, creating efficient algorithms to optimize various dimension reduction objectives has become particularly important. This paper is concerned with optimization problems on the Stiefel manifold whose objective functions take the form as the sum of a smooth function and a nonsmooth one. A common practice is to split such a problem into a smooth optimization subproblem on the Stiefel manifold and a nonsmooth one and solve them by some version of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Usually the smooth subproblem is solved by standard optimization techniques skillfully adapting to the manifold. However, often the smooth subproblem has strong linear algebra characteristics which, if carefully exploited, can lead to much more efficient solvers than the standard optimization techniques that ignore the characteristics. In this paper, it is proposed to tackle the smooth subproblem through a nonlinear eigen-approach which can fully utilize rich linear algebra structures that dominantly present in objective functions from today's data science applications. We conduct convergence analysis and analyze computational complexity for obtaining an $\epsilon$-stationary point. Numerical experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed algorithm compared to the state-of-the-art approaches.

papers.title: Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embeddings: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the necessary and sufficient conditions on domain for Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embedding of the space $W^{1,\Phi(\cdot,\cdot)}(\Omega)$ where $\Phi(x,t):=t^{p(x)}{(\log(e+t))}^{q(x)}.$

papers.title: On the Stieltjes Approximation Error to the Logarithmic Integral
papers.abstract: We study the approximation errors $\varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{li}_{*}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)$ and $\varepsilon_{S}(x)=\operatorname{li}_{S}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)$ arising from the classical Stieltjes--van Boven and pure Stieltjes asymptotic expansions of the logarithmic integral, respectively. Our analysis establishes a top-down reduction based on the discrete error sequence $\varepsilon_n=\varepsilon(e^n)$ and its localized partial variations, for which we derive new, unconditional analytic bounds. By developing precise integral representations for these error increments and establishing sharp, fully explicit upper and lower estima-tes for the underlying kernel integrals, we obtain uniform bounds valid for every integer $n\geq 1$. These discrete results are subsequently lifted to the real domain to provide comprehensive estimates for all real $x\geq e$. In particular, we prove that $\varepsilon(x) = \frac{1}{3} \sqrt{2\pi/\log x} + O(1/\log x)$ as $x \to \infty$. Furthermore, we deploy these continuous bounds to uncover the fine structural behavior of the pure Stieltjes expansion, demonstrating that $|\varepsilon_{S}(x)| = \sqrt{2\pi}\,|1/3-\alpha|/\sqrt{\log x} + O(1/\log x)$ as $x\to\infty$, where $n=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ and $\alpha=\log x-n$. This establishes a novel and explicit asymptotic description of the absolute pure Stieltjes error, fully capturing its non-trivial oscillatory dependence on the fractional part of the logarithm.

papers.title: The Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for Z/4xZ/4
papers.authors: Noe Barcenas, Luis Eduardo Garcia-Hernandez, Raphael Reinauer
papers.abstract: We prove the Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for the group Z/4xZ/4 by computing the connective real k-homology of the classifying space with the Adams spectral sequence and two types of detection theorems for the kernel of the alpha invariant: one based on eta-invariants, closely following work of Botvinnik-Gilkey-Stolz, and a second one based on homological methods. Along the way, we determine differentials of the Adams spectral sequence for classifying spaces involved in the computation, and we study the cap structure of the Adams spectral sequence for sub-hopf algebras of the Steenrod algebra relevant to the computation of connective real and complex k-homology.

papers.title: A hybrid FEM-PINN method for time-dependent partial differential equations
papers.authors: Xiaodong Feng, Haojiong Shangguan, Tao Tang, Xiaoliang Wan
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a hybrid numerical method for solving evolution partial differential equations (PDEs) by merging the time finite element method with deep neural networks. In contrast to the conventional deep learning-based formulation where the neural network is defined on a spatiotemporal domain, our methodology utilizes finite element basis functions in the time direction where the space-dependent coefficients are defined as the output of a neural network. We then apply the Galerkin or collocation projection in the time direction to obtain a system of PDEs for the space-dependent coefficients which is approximated in the framework of PINN. The advantages of such a hybrid formulation are twofold: statistical errors are avoided for the integral in the time direction, and the neural network's output can be regarded as a set of reduced spatial basis functions. To further alleviate the difficulties from high dimensionality and low regularity, we have developed an adaptive sampling strategy that refines the training set. More specifically, we use an explicit density model to approximate the distribution induced by the PDE residual and then augment the training set with new time-dependent random samples given by the learned density model. The effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method have been demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments.

papers.title: Inequalities characterizing distinguished unipotent orbits
papers.authors: Alexander Bertoloni Meli, Teruhisa Koshikawa, Jonathan Leake
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a new characterization of the distinguished unipotent orbits of a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. For classical groups we prove the characterization by a combinatorial computation, and for exceptional groups we check it with a computer. This characterization is needed in the theory of cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters in the article ``Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters'' of the first two authors.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Invariants of Non-Convex Complete Intersections in Weighted Projective Stacks
papers.authors: Felix Janda, Nawaz Sultani, Yang Zhou
papers.abstract:
In this paper we compute genus-zero orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau threefold complete intersections in weighted projective stacks, regardless of convexity conditions. The traditional quantum Lefschetz principle may fail even for invariants with ambient insertions. Using quasimap wall-crossing, we are able to compute invariants with insertions from a specific subring of the Chen-Ruan cohomology, which contains all the ambient cohomology classes.
  Quasimap wall-crossing gives a mirror theorem expressing the I-function in terms of the J-function via a mirror map. The key of this paper is to find a suitable GIT presentation of the target space, such that the mirror map becomes invertible. An explicit formula for the I-function is given for all those target spaces and many examples with explicit computations of invariants are provided.

papers.title: Hankel Determinants for Weighted Lattice Paths with Two Horizontal Steps
papers.abstract: We evaluate all Hankel determinants of the formal power series \(G=a/(1+b_1x+b_2x^2+cx^kG)\), where \(k\ge4\). The defining equation arises from a weighted lattice-path model with horizontal steps of lengths one and two. For \(k=4\), the determinants are expressed through Fibonacci polynomials. For \(k\ge5\), explicit formulas describe each residue class of the determinant size modulo \(k\). The proofs combine quadratic transformations with a second-order recurrence for an auxiliary family. As an application, we recover known Hankel evaluations for the square of the weighted Motzkin generating function.

papers.title: On the lower central series of a large family of non-periodic GGS-groups
papers.authors: Gustavo A. Fern\'andez-Alcober, Mikel E. Garciarena, Marialaura Noce
papers.abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we fully determine the lower central series of a large family of non-periodic GGS-groups, which has a density of roughly $(\frac{p-1}{p})^2$ within all GGS-groups. We also describe the structure of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-Lie algebra associated to the lower central series of these groups. These results represent a major step forward in the knowledge of the lower central series of distinguished classes of branch groups, which to date was basically restricted to the Grigorchuk group. As part of our results, we obtain the exact values of the indices between consecutive terms of the lower central series, and we show that these groups, as well as their profinite completions, have lower central width equal to $2$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Bartholdi, Eick, and Hartung about the generalised Fabrykowski-Gupta groups.

papers.title: Geometric Leaves of Symplectic Groupoids
papers.authors: Erik Brodsky, Leonid Chekhov, Pranjal Dangwal, Skyler Hamlin, Xu Lian, Michael Shapiro, Samuel Sottile, Jenny Zhan
papers.abstract: A symplectic groupoid of triangular bilinear forms consists of pairs of matrices $(B,A)$ with $A\in \mathcal A$ - the set of real unipotent upper-triangular matrices - and $B\in {\rm SL}_n({\mathbb R})$ such that $\widetilde{A}=BAB^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal A$. The symplectic groupoid possesses a nondegenerate symplectic structure which induces a reflection-equation Poisson algebra on $\mathcal A$. Fock and Chekhov defined a Poisson map from the Teichm\"uller space ${\mathcal T}_{g,s}$ of genus $g$ surfaces with $s$ (one or two) holes to the space of unipotent upper-triangular $n\times n$ matrices; the image of this map forms a geometric locus. A matrix $A$ in the geometric locus satisfies the rank condition: $\operatorname{rank}\bigl(A+A^{\mathsf T}\bigr)\le 4$ and an additional positivity condition. We describe the coisotropic reduction of the Poisson cluster variety of $\mathcal A$ by the rank condition for $n=5$ and $6$ and show that these coisotropic reductions yield the corresponding geometric loci. Moreover, we analyze in both cases the cluster structures obtained by coisotropic reductions and recover the celebrated cluster structure of ${\mathcal T}_{2,1}$ for $n=5$ and ${\mathcal T}_{2,2}$ for $n=6$. We also discuss the positivity of the geometric cluster variables for $n=3,4,5,6$.

papers.title: Flows on uniform Roe algebras
papers.authors: Bruno de Mendon\c{c}a Braga, Alcides Buss, Ruy Exel
papers.abstract:
For a uniformly locally finite metric space $(X, d)$, we investigate \emph{coarse} flows on its uniform Roe algebra $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, defined as one-parameter groups of automorphisms whose differentiable elements include all partial isometries arising from partial translations on $X$. We first show that any flow $\sigma$ on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ corresponds to a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ such that $\sigma_t(a) = e^{ith} a e^{-ith}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, allowing us to focus on operators $h$ that generate flows on $ \mathrm{C}^*_u (X)$.
  Assuming Yu's property A, we prove that a self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ induces a coarse flow on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ if and only if $h$ can be expressed as $h = a + d$, where $a \in \mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ and $d$ is a diagonal operator with entries forming a coarse function on $X$. We further study cocycle equivalence and cocycle perturbations of coarse flows, showing that, under property A, any coarse flow is a cocycle perturbation of a diagonal flow. Finally, for self-adjoint operators $h$ and $k$ that induce coarse flows on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, we characterize conditions under which the associated flows are either cocycle perturbations of each other or cocycle conjugate. In particular, if $h - k$ is bounded, then the flow induced by $h$ is a cocycle perturbation of the flow induced by $k$.

papers.title: Combinatorics of generalized orthogonal polynomials of type $R_{II}$
papers.abstract: In 1995, Ismail and Masson introduced orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \), which are defined by specific three-term recurrence relations with additional conditions. Recently, Kim and Stanton found a combinatorial interpretation for the moments of orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_I \) in the spirit of the combinatorial theory of orthogonal polynomials due to Flajolet and Viennot. In this paper, we push this combinatorial model further to orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \). Moreover, we generalize orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \) by relaxing some of their conditions. We then prove a master theorem, which generalizes combinatorial models for moments of various types of orthogonal polynomials: classical orthogonal polynomials, Laurent biorthogonal polynomials, and orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \).

papers.title: Existence result for a 2 x 2 system of conservation laws with discontinuous flux and applications
papers.authors: Felisia Angela Chiarello, Simone Fagioli, Massimiliano Daniele Rosini
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for a one-dimensional 2x2 non-symmetric Keyfitz-Kranzer system of conservation laws with a flux f= f(x,U) that is discontinuous with respect to the spatial variable x. No monotonicity assumption is imposed on the mapping x \to f(x,U). We introduce a Kruzhkov-type entropy condition and establish global existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for initial data with arbitrarily large total variation. The proof relies on a wave-front tracking approximation. The main technical novelty consists in the introduction of adapted Riemann invariant coordinates, specifically designed to account for the discontinuities of the flux, which yield a uniform-in-time bound on the total variation of the approximate solutions U^n(t). As an application, we discuss the second-order ARZ model for vehicular traffic on inhomogeneous roads with abrupt collective changes in the speed law or road capacity.

papers.title: Nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian: Existence, non-existence and uniqueness results
papers.authors: Rakesh Arora, Jacques Giacomoni, Arshi Vaishnavi
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the existence, non-existence, and uniqueness results for nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian, and subcritical, critical, and supercritical logarithmic nonlinearities. The Poho\u zaev's identity and D\'iaz-Saa type inequality are proved, which are of independent interest and can be applied to a larger class of problems. Depending upon the growth of nonlinearities and regularity of the weight function, we study the small-order asymptotic of nonlocal weighted elliptic equations involving the fractional Laplacian of order $2s.$ We show that the least energy solutions of a weighted nonlocal problem with superlinear or sublinear growth converge to a nontrivial nonnegative least-energy solution of Br\'ezis-Nirenberg type and logistic-type limiting problem respectively involving the logarithmic Laplacian.

papers.title: Interface Energy and Phase Transformations: A Comparative Analysis of Cahn-Hilliard and CALPHAD-based Models in Ternary Substitutional Alloys
papers.authors: Wolfgang Flachberger, Thomas Antretter, Swaroop Gaddikere-Nagaraja, Silvia Leitner, Manuel Petersmann, Jiri Svoboda
papers.abstract: Diffusional phase transformations in alloys are modeled either by phase-field methods of Cahn-Hilliard type, in which a double-well free energy and a gradient term impose an interface energy, or by reactive diffusion models, in which the driving forces follow from the CALPHAD methodology, the convex hull of the molar free energy, and the interface carries no energy. Their numerical schemes are tied to their free energies: phase-field schemes break down when the interface energy is set to zero, and reactive diffusion codes rely on finite differences. We derive, from the thermodynamic extremal principle, a single finite element scheme that covers both limits: the stationarity of the Rayleighian functional (free energy rate plus one half of the dissipation, with mass conservation imposed by multipliers) with respect to the rates, fluxes and multipliers at a frozen state. Fluxes and chemical affinities are primary unknowns, so no derivative of the affinity is required. The time-discrete scheme is the corresponding incremental minimization; it conserves mass exactly and satisfies a discrete energy-dissipation inequality for every convex molar free energy, including the convex hull without regularization. We make explicit that this last case is a degenerate parabolic problem of Stefan type, whose degeneracy can be removed, without altering the free energy, only by a moving mesh; since our aim is the coupling to continuum mechanics and damage on a fixed mesh, we operate at the boundary of degeneracy and show that mass conservation, the energy balance and the second law remain intact there. Thermodynamic consistency is proved for multi-component systems, a scheme relating Onsager and diffusion coefficients is proposed, and the role of interface energy is studied in binary and ternary examples, the latter with vacancies as a non-conserved component.

papers.title: Cylinder decompositions on geometric armadillo tails
papers.abstract: We study a class of finite-area, infinite-type translation surfaces and construct an explicit cylinder decomposition on these surfaces. The cylinder decomposition contains a special curve which distinguishes it from cylinder decompositions in other periodic directions.

papers.title: Low-degree colorings without non-essential arguments
papers.abstract:
For the Hamming graph $H(n,q)$, where $q$ is a constant prime power and $n$ grows, we construct perfect colorings without non-essential arguments such that $n$ depends exponentially on the off-diagonal part of the quotient matrix. In particular, we construct unbalanced functions (in the case $q=2$, Boolean functions) such that the number of essential arguments depends exponentially on the degree of the function.
  Another framing of the main construction is that it gives a sequence of very regular functions (perfect colorings) whose number of essential arguments grows exponentially with respect to sensitivity. A classical result that connects sensitivity with the number of essential arguments in the binary ($q=2$) case is the Simon--Wegener theorem. We prove an analog of this theorem for an arbitrary $q$.
  Keywords: boolean functions, perfect colorings, equitable partitions, degree, sensitivity, essential arguments

papers.title: Boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $L$ be a 0-elliptic operator on X which is semi-Fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples include Hodge Laplacians and Dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. We construct left and right parametrices for L when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. The construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $X$ and $\partial X$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". This new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of Mazzeo--Melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. In the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $X^2$. By contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.

papers.title: Boolean combinations of graphs
papers.authors: Sarosh Adenwalla, Samuel Braunfeld, John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev
papers.abstract: Boolean combinations allow combining given combinatorial objects to obtain new, potentially more complicated, objects. In this paper, we initiate a systematic study of this idea applied to graphs. In order to understand expressive power and limitations of boolean combinations in this context, we investigate how they affect different combinatorial and structural properties of graphs, in particular $\chi$-boundedness, as well as characterize the structure of boolean combinations of graphs from various classes.

papers.title: The Rectifiable Rectangular Peg Problem
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of an inscribed rectangle with any prescribed aspect ratio for a large class of continuous Jordan curves that includes all rectifiable curves and Stromquist's locally monotone curves. Our proof is based on microlocal sheaf theory and is inspired by the recent work of Greene and Lobb.

papers.title: Categorical Diffusion of Weighted Lattices
papers.authors: Robert Ghrist, Miguel Lopez, Paige Randall North, Hans Riess
papers.abstract: Quantale-enriched categories unify ordered, metric, relational, and tropical structures that arise across networked systems. To study consensus and relaxation over such structures, we develop a theory of diffusion for cellular sheaves of quantale-enriched categories over graphs, governed by an order-theoretic Laplace operator that we call the Lawvere Laplacian. Over an arbitrary unital quantale, we define the weighted global sections of a cellular sheaf as the quantale-enriched category of natural transformations from a weight diagram into the sheaf, which over a commutative base is a weighted limit, and characterize them as the vertex data that agree up to edge tolerances across every edge. For an adjoint bisheaf, we prove that the weighted global sections coincide with the suffix points of the Lawvere Laplacian, which are the equilibria of its harmonic flow. Under a chain-continuity hypothesis, the harmonic flow converges to the greatest weighted global section below the initial cochain. Instances of the theory include shortest-path iteration over the Lawvere quantale, reconciliation of local cost estimates, quantale and clock synchronization, and coupled max-plus discrete event systems.

papers.title: Drift Parameter Estimation for an Ergodic Extension of the Double Heston Model
papers.authors: Mohamed Ben Alaya, Houssem Dahbi, Hamdi Fathallah
papers.abstract: The double Heston model is a widely used stochastic volatility model in financial mathematics, particularly for option pricing, risk management, and volatility surface calibration. This paper investigates the joint estimation of the drift parameters for an ergodic extension of the double Heston model. We first establish stochastic properties of the underlying process, including the existence of a stationary distribution and ergodicity. We then study maximum likelihood and conditional least squares estimators based on continuous-time observations. For both estimation procedures, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality under suitable ergodicity conditions.

papers.title: Numerical approximation of nonlinear fourth-order SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
papers.authors: Dirk Bl\"omker, Chengcheng Ling, Johannes Rimmele
papers.abstract: We consider the strong numerical approximation for a fourth-order stochastic nonlinear SPDE driven by space-time white noise on {{$d=1,2,3$}}-dimensional torus. We consider its full discretisation with a spectral Galerkin scheme in space and Euler scheme in time. We show the convergence with almost spatial rate $2-\frac{d}{2}$ and $\frac{6-d}{4} \wedge 1$-temporal rate obtained mainly via \it{Stochastic Sewing} technique.

papers.title: Leafwise positive scalar curvature and the Rosenberg index
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed spin manifold, in this paper, we show that if there is a foliation $(M,F)$ and a Riemannian metric on $M$ that has leafwise positive scalar curvature then the Rosenberg index of $M$ is zero.

papers.title: Applications of reduced and coreduced modules III: Derived torsion and completion over polynomial extensions
papers.abstract: We study when degree-zero identities for reduced and coreduced modules extend to ambient derived torsion and completion. For a non-idempotent ideal $I$ in an explicit polynomial ring, we construct a module $M$ that is simultaneously $I$-reduced and $I$-coreduced and satisfies $\Gamma_I(M)=\Lambda_I(M)=0$ but $H_I^2(M)\ne0$. The module is a union of finite reduced and coreduced submodules whose positive derived torsion vanishes. The supporting ideal has unrestricted torsion dimension two, whereas the dimension on each bounded-nilpotence quotient category is one. The calculations use compatible cone resolutions for $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$, where $J^2=J$. These give paired Ext--Tor formulas for coefficients annihilated by a fixed power of $t$. For arbitrary coefficients, an explicit mapping-fiber model realizes the standard derived-composition comparison sequence and identifies the obstruction to extending the bounded formula. Coordinate calculations for countably idempotent-generated ideals supply the computational foundation, and a valuation-domain example gives nonzero first derived completion on a cyclic reduced and coreduced coefficient.

papers.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: I. Order-Disorder Interface convergence
papers.authors: Moritz Dober, Alexander Glazman, S\'ebastien Ott
papers.abstract:
We study a $q$-state Potts model on the square grid when $q>4$ at the point $T_c(q)$ of its (discontinous) transition. This model exhibits exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures: $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). The current work deals with the Dobrushin order--disorder boundary conditions on a finite $N\times N$ box. Our main result is that this interface is a well-defined object, has $\sqrt{N}$ fluctuations, and converges to a Brownian bridge under diffusive scaling. The same holds also for the corresponding FK-percolation model for all $q>4$.
  Our proofs rely on a coupling between FK-percolation, the six-vertex model, and the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and on a detailed study of the latter. The coupling relates the interface in FK-percolation to a long subcritical cluster in the ATRC model. For this cluster we develop a ``renewal picture'' \`a la Ornstein-Zernike. This is based on fine mixing properties of the ATRC model that we establish using the link to the six-vertex model and its height function. Along the way, we derive various properties of the Ashkin-Teller model, such as Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics for its two-point function.
  In a companion work, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-order Dobrushin conditions. We show emergence of a free layer of width $\sqrt{N}$ between the two ordered phases (wetting) and establish convergence of its boundaries to two Brownian bridges conditioned not to intersect.

papers.title: Unavoidable subgraphs in Ramsey graphs
papers.authors: Christian Reiher, Vojt\v{e}ch R\"odl, Mathias Schacht
papers.abstract: We study subgraphs that appear in large Ramsey graphs for a given graph $F$. The recent girth Ramsey theorem of the first two authors asserts that there are Ramsey graphs such that all small subgraphs lie in `forests of copies of $F$' amalgamated on vertices and edges. We derive a few further consequences from this structural result and investigate to what extent such forests of copies must be present in Ramsey graphs. As an application, we improve a recent result on generalised Sidon sets with Ramsey-type properties.

papers.title: Time-optimal problem in the space of probability measures
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the value function in the time-optimal problem for a continuity equation in the space of probability measures. We derive the dynamic programming principle for this problem. Using this principle, we prove that the Kruzhkov transform of the value function is a unique discontinuous viscosity solution to the corresponding Dirichlet problem for the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of the value function in a perturbed problem to the value function in the unperturbed problem.
