papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of penalty dynamics for constrained variational inequalities
papers.authors: Siqi Qu, Mathias Staudigl, Juan Peypouquet
papers.abstract: We propose a comprehensive framework for solving constrained variational inequalities via various classes of evolution equations displaying multi-scale aspects. In an infinite-dimensional Hilbertian framework, the class of dynamical systems we propose combine Tikhonov regularization and exterior penalization terms in order to induce strong convergence of trajectories to least norm solutions in the constrained domain. Our construction thus unifies the literature on regularization methods and penalty-based dynamical systems. An extension to a full splitting formulation of the constrained domain is also provided, with associated weak convergence results involving the Attouch-Czarnecki condition.

papers.title: The threshold for loose Hamilton cycles in random hypergraph
papers.abstract: We show that w.h.p.\ the random $r$-uniform hypergraph $H_{n,m}$ contains a loose Hamilton cycle, provided $r\geq 3$ and $m\geq \frac{(1+\epsilon)n\log n}{r}$, where $\epsilon$ is an arbitrary positive constant. This is asymptotically best possible, as if $m\leq \frac{(1-\epsilon)n\log n}{r}$ then w.h.p.\ $H_{n,m}$ contains isolated vertices.

papers.title: Optimal linear filtering of partially observed polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to filtering, smoothing, and prediction of polynomial processes that are partially observed. These problems are known to allow for an explicit solution in the simpler case of linear Gaussian state space models. The key insight underlying the present piece of research is that in linear filtering applications polynomial processes and their discrete-time counterpart are indistinguishable from Gaussian processes sharing their first two moments. We describe the construction of these Gaussian equivalents of polynomial processes and explicitly compute optimal linear filters, predictors and smoothers for polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time. The consideration of Gaussian equivalents also opens the door to parameter estimation and linear-quadratic optimal control in the context of polynomial processes.

papers.title: Local Linear Convergence of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Semidefinite Programming under Strict Complementarity
papers.authors: Shucheng Kang, Xin Jiang, Heng Yang
papers.abstract: We investigate the local linear convergence properties of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) when applied to Semidefinite Programming (SDP). A longstanding belief suggests that ADMM is only capable of solving SDPs to moderate accuracy, primarily due to its sublinear worst-case complexity and empirical observations of slow convergence. We challenge this notion by introducing a new sufficient condition for local linear convergence: as long as the converged primal-dual optimal solutions satisfy strict complementarity, ADMM attains local linear convergence, independent of nondegeneracy conditions. Our proof is based on a direct local linearization of the ADMM operator and a refined error bound for the projection onto the positive semidefinite cone, improving previous bounds and revealing the anisotropic nature of projection residuals. Extensive numerical experiments confirm the significance of our theoretical results, demonstrating that ADMM achieves local linear convergence and computes high-accuracy solutions in a variety of SDP instances, including those cases where nondegeneracy fails. Furthermore, we identify where ADMM struggles, linking these difficulties with near violations of strict complementarity-a phenomenon that parallels recent findings in linear programming.

papers.title: A convex integration scheme for the continuity equation past the Sobolev embedding threshold
papers.authors: Maria Colombo, Roberto Colombo, Anuj Kumar
papers.abstract: We introduce a convex integration scheme for the continuity equation in the context of the Di Perna-Lions theory that allows to build incompressible vector fields in $C_{t}W^{1,p}_x$ and nonunique solutions in $C_{t} L^{q}_x$ for any $p,q$ with $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} > 1 + \frac{1}{d}- \delta$ for some $\delta>0$. This improves the previous bound, corresponding to $\delta=0$, or equivalently $q' > p^*$, obtained with convex integration so far, and critical for those schemes in view of the Sobolev embedding that guarantees that solutions are distributional in the opposite range.

papers.title: Homogenization theory of random walks in degenerate random environment
papers.abstract: Recent progress on the understanding of the Random Conductance Model is reviewed. A particular emphasis is on homogenization results such as functional central limit theorems, local limit theorems and heat kernel estimates for almost every realization of the environment, established for random walks among stationary ergodic conductances that are possibly unbounded but satisfy certain moment conditions.

papers.title: Shannon observables: A scalable approach to information decomposition
papers.authors: Aaron J. Gutknecht, Fernando E. Rosas, David A. Ehrlich, Abdullah Makkeh, Pedro A. M. Mediano, Michael Wibral
papers.abstract: Distributed systems, such as biological and artificial neural networks, process information via complex interactions engaging multiple subsystems, resulting in high-order structure of the information within the system with distinct properties across scales. Investigating how these systems process information remains challenging due to difficulties in defining appropriate multivariate metrics and ensuring their scalability to large systems. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel framework based on what we call "Shannon observables": quantities that capture essential properties of high-order information processing, yet can be computed directly from Shannon entropies and scale efficiently to large systems. Our theoretical results demonstrate how Shannon observables can be used to resolve long-standing ambiguities regarding the interpretation of widely used multivariate information-theoretic measures. On the practical side, we demonstrate the framework's versatility across several domains. An analytical study of error-correcting codes shows how Shannon observables trace out distinct encoding regimes as channel noise varies; analyses of deep classifiers and convolutional autoencoders reveal characteristic information-processing signatures across layers and over training; and applied to magnetoencephalography recordings from the human brain, the framework yields a cortical atlas exposing pronounced regional structure in directed information transfer. Overall, our framework resolves fundamental limitations in analysing high-order information phenomena and offers broad opportunities for theoretical developments and empirical analyses.

papers.title: Projective Variety Recovery from Unknown Linear Projections
papers.abstract: We study how a smooth irreducible variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$, $m\geq n+2$, can be recovered from the equations of its images under two generic projections from unknown centers. This extends earlier results on curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ to any dimension. Since $X$ is the normalization of each image, one image determines $X$ modulo the projective group when $X$ is linearly normal; what two images add is the configuration, that is the pair of projections. For complete intersections we prove unconditionally that the set of configurations compatible with the two images and their Hilbert polynomial is finite, of size at most $|\mathrm{Lin}(X)|$, the projective automorphism group of $X$. The argument is effective and the bound is attained. We then introduce an equation generalizing Kruppa's equation, relating the duals of the images to a fundamental matrix, encoding the pair of projections modulo the projective group. We give a necessary condition for its solution variety to be finite, a bound on its isolated points, and a sufficient condition under which the true fundamental matrix is rigid: no quadric may contain a generic line $L$ together with the locus of points of $X$ whose tangent space meets $L$. Rigidity is unconditional for curves; in higher dimension it holds under a first-order liftability hypothesis, which we certify for a del Pezzo quartic surface in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Global finiteness of that solution variety remains open, necessarily so, as it contains solutions realized by no variety; for $\dim X<\mathrm{codim}\,X-1$ the obstruction amounts to knowing the fundamental matrix itself. Once the projections are known, $X$ is recovered from the two cones over the images: in codimension two their intersection is $X$ plus a component of degree $d(d-1)$; in higher codimension $X$ is its unique component of maximal dimension.

papers.title: Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.

papers.title: $L^2$ extension of holomorphic functions in the general non-analytic setting
papers.abstract: In an influential $L^2$ extension theorem due to Demailly, the subvariety to extend from is defined by the multiplier ideal of a quasi-plurisubharmonic defining function with analytic singularities. In his theorem, the finiteness of an $L^2$ norm called the Ohsawa norm plays the crucial role of determining whether a given holomorphic function or section can be extended. In 2016, Demailly asked if the Ohsawa norm behaves equally well when the defining function is further generalized to admit non-analytic singularities. We answer this question negatively by showing that for a wide class of log canonical defining functions with a unique log canonical place, only the zero holomorphic function on the subvariety has finite Ohsawa norm. It follows that for such a defining function, the $L^2$ extension theorem is vacuous. This reveals a fundamental obstruction in the theory of $L^2$ extension in the general non-analytic setting.

papers.title: Perfect weight divisibility of (fork, co-fork$\cup K_1$)-free graphs
papers.authors: Ran Chen, Baogang Xu, Miaoxia Zhuang
papers.abstract: A {\em fork} is a graph obtained from $K_{1,3}$ (usually called {\em claw}) by subdividing an edge once, an {\em co-fork} is the complement graph of a fork, and a {\em co-cricket} is a union of $K_1$ and $K_4-e$. A graph is perfectly divisible if for each of its induced subgraphs $H$, $V (H)$ can be partitioned into $A$ and $B$ such that $H[A]$ is perfect and $\omega(H[B]) < \omega(H)$. A graph is perfectly weight divisible if the same condition holds for any positive integer weights on its vertices, using the maximum weight of a clique instead of the clique number. Sivaraman proposed the conjecture that every fork-free graph is perfectly divisible in a paper by Karthick {\em et al.} [Electron. J. Comb. 29 (2022), P3.19.]. In the same paper, they proved that every ((\text{fork},\text{co-cricket}))-free graph is either claw-free or perfectly divisible. In this paper, we show that every (fork, co-fork$\cup K_1$)-free graph is perfectly weight divisible, and hence perfectly divisible. This improves some results of Karthick {\em et al.}.

papers.title: Computing Projective Implicit Representations from Poset Towers
papers.abstract: A family of simplicial complexes connected by simplicial maps and indexed by a finite poset $P$ is called a poset tower. Poset towers subsume multi-parameter filtrations, zigzag filtrations, and one-parameter simplicial towers, while allowing arbitrary finite posets and simplicial maps. The homology of a poset tower is a $P$-persistence module. To compute it globally over $P$, we consider the chain complex segment of $P$-persistence modules $C_{\ell-1}\xleftarrow{\partial_{\ell}}C_\ell \xleftarrow{\partial_{\ell+1}}C_{\ell+1}$ induced by the simplices of the tower. Unlike in one-critical multi-filtrations, the chain modules $C_\ell$ need not be projective and may have a complicated structure. We address the problem of replacing this segment by projective modules and $P$-graded matrices while preserving homology. The resulting projective implicit representation (PiRep) plays the role of the graded boundary-matrix representation in the classical persistence algorithm: it converts simplicial data into algebraic input on which persistent homology can be computed globally over $P$. In particular, a PiRep can be used as input to algorithms for computing minimal presentations of persistent homology. We give an efficient algorithm to compute a PiRep from a poset tower. It constructs degreewise minimal presentations and asymptotically minimal second terms of projective resolutions of the chain modules $C_\ell$, lifts the boundary maps $\partial_\ell$ to these resolutions, and assembles the resulting data into a PiRep using an additional correction term. The method is tailored to chain complexes induced by poset towers and computes the required algebraic data combinatorially, exploiting their special structure and avoiding general-purpose algebraic reduction. In the context of poset towers, it is fully general and can serve as a foundation for efficient algorithms on specific posets.

papers.title: Fedder-type criterion for quasi-$F^e$-splitting and quasi-$F$-regularity
papers.abstract: We study quasi-$F^e$-split and quasi-$F$-regular singularities, which generalize Yobuko's quasi-$F$-splitting. We establish Fedder type criteria that characterize these properties for hypersurfaces. These criteria offer explicit tools for computation and verification. As an application, we construct a counterexample to the inversion of adjunction for quasi-$F$-regularity and compute the quasi-$F$-split threshold of the cone over the ordinary cusp.

papers.title: Analysis of non-linear fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets
papers.authors: Aaryan Dharmesh Shah, Sangita Jha, Anarul Islam Mondal
papers.abstract:
This article addresses three problems: (1) the construction of a general nonlinear fractal interpolation function on post-critically finite (PCF) self-similar sets; (2) the study of the energy and normal derivatives of uniform nonlinear fractal functions; and (3) the estimation of the box-counting dimensions of the proposed fractal functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket and the von Koch curve.
  We present a general framework for constructing attractors and fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets using Edelstein contractions. Further, we derive upper and lower bounds for the box-counting dimensions of the graphs of nonlinear interpolants. Finally, we provide several graphical and numerical examples to illustrate the construction and estimate the dimensions for different data sets.

papers.title: Classification of Certain Rational Isoparametric Functions on Damek-Ricci Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify isoparametric functions on Damek-Ricci spaces which can be written in terms of the standard coordinates $(v,z,t)$ on the half-space model as a polynomial function divided by $t$. Regular level sets of the functions in our classification encompass almost all previously known examples of isoparametric hypersufaces in Damek-Ricci space and also yield new ones. For the new examples, the focal varieties are determined and the mean curvatures of the regular level sets are expressed as a function of the distance from the focal variety. We also study the exceptional case of tubes about $\mathbb R\mathbf H^k$ in $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$, which are isoparametric, but cannot be obtained as the level sets of any function in our classification. We show that these tubes are level sets of a polynomial function divided by $t^2$, and that analogous functions on Damek-Ricci spaces can be isoparametric only in the case of $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$.

papers.title: A Brezis-Nirenberg Type Problem for a Mixed Local-Nonlocal Operator on the Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: This paper studies nonlinear elliptic equations involving the operator $-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N} + (-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s-\lambda$ on the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{B}^N$, where $0 < s < 1$ and $\lambda<\frac{(N-1)^2}{4}$. We prove that the best Sobolev constant of this mixed local-nonlocal operator equals the Euclidean Sobolev constant $S$ and is never attained, whereas the corresponding purely local constant may lie strictly below $S$. As a consequence, the purely critical problem has no ground state and no nontrivial solution of small $L^{2^*}$ norm. For the subcritical problem, and for the critical problem with a subcritical perturbation $\mu|u|^{p-1}u$, we obtain nonnegative radial solutions by variational methods, depending on $p$ and $\mu$. Along the way, we prove the continuous embedding $H^1(\mathbb{B}^N)\hookrightarrow H^s(\mathbb{B}^N)$ and the equivalence of the spectral and the pointwise definitions of $(-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s$.

papers.title: The mean curvature flow of subgroups on Lie groups of dimension three
papers.authors: Romina M. Arroyo, Gabriela P. Ovando, Mariel S\'aez
papers.abstract: In this work we study the existence of solutions to the Mean Curvature Flow for which the initial condition has the structure of a two-dimensional Lie subgroup within a Lie group of dimension three. We consider Lie groups with a fixed left-invariant metric and first observe that if the Lie group is unimodular, then every Lie subgroup is a minimal surface (hence a trivial solution). For this reason we focus on non-unimodular Lie groups, finding the evolution of every Lie subgroup of dimension 2 (within a 3 dimensional Lie group). These evolutions are self-similar for abelian subgroups (i.e. evolve by isometries), but not self-similar in the other cases.

papers.title: The Huang-Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
papers.authors: Emanuela L. Giacomelli, Christian Hainzl, Phan Th\`anh Nam, Robert Seiringer
papers.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin $1/2$ fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.

papers.title: On a class of generalized Roth-Lempel codes
papers.authors: Zhonghao Liang, Yongkang Wan, Qunying Liao
papers.abstract: Maximum distance separable (MDS), almost MDS (AMDS), and self-dual codes have applications in communications, data storage, and quantum coding. The construction and structural study of MDS codes that are not equivalent to generalized Reed-Solomon (GRS) codes are important problems in coding theory and finite geometry. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Roth-Lempel (GRL) codes \(GRL_k(\alpha, v, A_{3\times 3})\) introduced by Li et al. [28] in the case of a \(3\times 3\) appended matrix. Using the Cauchy matrix method of Roth and Lempel, we derive a sufficient condition under which these codes are not equivalent to GRS codes. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for their duals to be AMDS and for the codes to be self-dual. The self-duality criterion extends the corresponding result in [28], and we provide examples illustrating our results. Under suitable parameter assumptions and an explicit rank condition, we show that the Schur square of an \([n, k]_q\) GRL code \(GRL_k(\alpha, v, A_{3\times 3})\) has dimension \(2k + 2\). Using this invariant, we show that, under certain conditions, these GRL codes are not equivalent to codes from several known non-GRS families.

papers.title: Unregularized limit of stochastic gradient method for Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization
papers.abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization offers a framework for model fitting in machine learning under potential shifts in the data distribution. We study a regularized variant of this problem in which entropic smoothing produces a sampled approximation of the original objective. We establish convergence of the approximate gradients to subgradients of the unregularized objective as the regularization parameter vanishes, enabling convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods. We obtain qualitative convergence results under general assumptions, then we provide convergence rates under additional regularity. In particular, we prove rates for the convergence of the unregularized objective values, up to sampling errors, when the regularization level is decreased across iterations. Our analysis yields byproducts of independent interest, including approximation results for smoothing of maximum functions subdifferentials and empirical lower bounds for dual solutions of Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization.

papers.title: Existence of minimizing $n$-harmonic maps in homotopy classes by critical exponents
papers.authors: Antoine Detaille, Adam Grzela, Katarzyna Mazowiecka
papers.abstract:
We investigate the existence of energy minimizing $n$-harmonic maps from an $n$-dimensional sphere to a compact manifold inside a prescribed homotopy class. Our results are of two kinds.
  First, inspired by the work by T. Rivi\`ere (1998) on minimizing 3-harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ with given Hopf degree and by the work of R. Hardt and T. Rivi\`ere (2008) on critical and optimal Sobolev exponents for rational homotopy classes, we exhibit a general principle that guarantees the existence of infinitely many homotopy classes with a minimizing map inside. We apply this principle, each time proving the optimality of the relevant Sobolev exponents, to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{4n-1}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2n}$, where the relevant homotopical quantity is the Hopf invariant, and to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ to $\mathbb{CP}^{n}$, where homotopy classes are generated by the circle bundle on the projective space. These results hold for first-order as well as for fractional Sobolev mappings.
  Second, elaborating on the recent preprint of Wang G. and Zhang M. (2026), we derive sharp lower energy bounds for mappings with given Hopf invariant. We apply these bounds to deduce a sufficient energetic condition for the existence of minimizing maps in a given homotopy class. Finally, we exploit this condition, by explicit construction of mappings satisfying it, to prove the existence of energy minimizers from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ of Hopf degree $d \in \{\pm2,\pm3,\dotsc,\pm6\}$ and from $\mathbb{S}^{7}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{4}$ of Hopf degree $\pm1$.

papers.title: Dissipative solutions for 2D Onsager's conjecture
papers.authors: Lili Du, Xinliang Li, Weikui Ye
papers.abstract: In 1949, L. Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations in $C_{t,x}^{\gamma}$ are energy conservative when $\gamma>\frac{1}{3}$, whereas nonconservative solutions exist when $\gamma<\frac{1}{3}$. Constantin, E and Titi [13] proved the conservation part, while Isett [26] constructed nontrivial $C^\gamma_{t,x}$ weak solutions with compact support in time in three dimensions for each $0<\gamma<\frac{1}{3}$. Building on this breakthrough work, Buckmaster, De Lellis, Sz\'ekelyhidi Jr. and Vicol [7] obtained strictly dissipative solutions below the Onsager threshold. In two dimensions, Giri and Radu [23] first constructed a nontrivial weak solution in $C^{\frac{1}{3}-}(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ and left an open problem whether it would be possible to construct dissipative solutions (controllable energy) below $\frac{1}{3}$ threshold. In this paper, we reslove this question and thereby obtain infinitely many strictly dissipative weak solutions in $C^\gamma(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ for every $0<\gamma<\frac{1}{3}$. Moreover, we prove that the associated wild initial data are dense in the divergence-free subspace of $C^{\gamma'}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for any $0<\gamma' <\frac{1}{3}$. The key new ingredient is a family of staircase traveling waves, which we combine with a Picard iteration coupled to the Newton--Nash scheme to control both the Reynolds stress and the kinetic energy. The construction also applies in every dimension $d\geq2$.

papers.title: Minimal W-algebras of $\mathfrak{so}_N$ at level minus one
papers.authors: Thomas Creutzig, Justine Fasquel, Vladimir Kovalchuk, Andrew R. Linshaw, Shigenori Nakatsuka
papers.abstract: For $N \in\mathbb Z_{\geq 7}$ we show that the simple minimal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra of $\mathfrak{so}_N$ at level minus one is isomorphic to the even subalgebra of the tensor product of the simple affine vertex superalgebra of $\mathfrak{osp}_{1|2}$ at level $\frac{N-6}{2}$ with $N-4$ free fermions. In particular when $N$ is even this minimal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra is strongly rational as conjectured by Arakawa-Moreau.

papers.title: On the Convergence Rates of Iterative Regularization Algorithms for Composite Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper investigates iterative methods for solving bilevel optimization problems where both inner and outer functions have a composite structure. We establish novel theoretical results, including the first analysis that provides simultaneous convergence rates for the Iteratively REgularized Proximal Gradient (IRE-PG) method, a variant of Solodov's algorithm. These rates for the inner and outer functions highlight the inherent trade-offs between their respective convergence behaviors. We further extend this analysis to an accelerated version of IRE-PG, proving faster convergence rates under specific settings. Additionally, we propose a new scheme for handling cases where these methods cannot be directly applied to the bilevel problem due to the difficulty of computing the associated proximal operator. This scheme offers surrogate functions to approximate the original problem and a framework to translate convergence rates between the surrogate and original functions. Our results show that the accelerated method's advantage diminishes under this translation.

papers.title: A PINNs approach for the computation of eigenvalues in elliptic problems
papers.authors: Julian Fernandez Bonder, Ariel M. Salort
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for computing eigenvalues of elliptic problems using Deep Learning techniques. A key feature of our approach is that it is independent of the space dimension and can compute arbitrary eigenvalues without requiring the prior computation of lower ones. Moreover, the method can be easily adapted to handle nonlinear eigenvalue problems.

papers.title: Exponentially Fading Memory Signature
papers.abstract: We introduce the exponentially fading memory (EFM) signature, a time-invariant transformation of an infinite (possibly rough) path that serves as a mean-reverting analogue of the classical path signature. We construct the EFM-signature via rough path theory, carefully adapted to accommodate improper integration from minus infinity. The EFM-signature retains many of the key algebraic and analytical properties of classical signatures, including a suitably modified Chen identity, the linearization property, path-determinacy, and the universal approximation property. From the probabilistic perspective, the EFM-signature provides a "stationarized" representation, making it particularly well-suited for time-series analysis and signal processing overcoming the shortcomings of the standard signature. In particular, the EFM-signature of time-augmented Brownian motion evolves as a group-valued Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We establish its stationarity, Markov property, and exponential ergodicity in the Wasserstein distance, and we derive an explicit formula \`a la Fawcett for its expected value in terms of Magnus expansions. We also study linear combinations of EFM-signature elements and the computation of associated characteristic functions in terms of a mean-reverting infinite dimensional Riccati equation.

papers.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
papers.abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.

papers.title: Diophantine equations in matrix rings and semirings
papers.abstract: For every fixed positive integer $n$, we prove that it is undecidable whether a single noncommutative polynomial equation with scalar integer coefficients has a solution in $M_n(\mathbb N)$ or in $M_n(\mathbb Z)$. An integral range calculation for central polynomials yields a common reduction from integer Diophantine equations; the single-equation and finite-system problems are computably enumerable complete. The same polynomials have exact range $\mathbb Q I_n$ on rational, even nonnegative rational, arguments. Consequently, the single-equation and finite-system problems over $M_n(\mathbb Q)$ are computably many-one equivalent to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$, unconditionally. The rational undecidability claims reported in 2026 by OpenAI and Zhi-Wei Sun imply rational-matrix undecidability, with at most $86$, $87$, and $88$ matrix variables in dimensions $1$, $2$, and at least $3$, respectively. An explicit Diophantine definition of $\mathbb Z$ in $\mathbb Q$ reported by the project coordinated by Elliot Glazer further gives completeness among computably enumerable problems. These consequences of recent arithmetic claims are stated conditionally.

papers.title: Quivers with Polynomial Identities
papers.authors: Giovanni Cerulli Irelli, Javier De Loera Ch\'avez, Elena Pascucci
papers.abstract: We provide a topological characterization of quivers whose path algebra satisfies a polynomial identity. This class includes the oriented cycle and acyclic quivers and, in the latter case, we describe the associated T-ideal. We introduce a generalization of Arnold's A-graded algebras, which we call locally A-graded algebras, and prove that they are also PI. We give an example of a quiver algebra satisfying a polynomial identity, even if the path algebra of the quiver does not.

papers.title: Time asymptotics, time regularity and separation rates for Navier-Stokes flows in supercritical solution classes
papers.abstract: This paper extends the weak solution theory for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations of Barker, Seregin and Sverak from a critical setting to a supercritical setting making sure to include a useful a priori energy bound as well as a statement about stability under weak-star convergence. Two applications of the a priori bound are then explored. The first provides a spatially local, short-time asymptotic expansion in the time variable starting at $t=0$ which, as a corollary, provides an upper bound on how fast hypothetical non-unique solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations can separate locally. The second establishes higher-order time regularity at a singular time and at spatial points positioned away from the singularity. This quantifies the degree to which the non-local nature of the pressure allows a far flung singularity to disrupt the time regularity at a regular point.

papers.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
papers.abstract: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

papers.title: The limiting spectral distribution for sparse elliptic random matrices
papers.abstract: This paper studies sparse elliptic random matrix models which generalize both the classical elliptic ensembles and sparse i.i.d. matrix models by incorporating correlated entries and a tunable sparsity parameter $p_n$. Each $n\times n$ matrix $X_n$ is formed by entry-wise multiplication of an elliptic random matrix by an elliptic matrix of Bernoulli($p_n$) variables, where $np_n$ tends to infinity at a sufficient rate, allowing for interpolation between dense and sparse regimes. The main result establishes that after appropriate normalization, the empirical spectral measures of these matrices converge weakly in probability to the uniform measure on a rotated ellipsoid in the complex plane as the dimension $n$ tends to infinity. Interestingly, the shape of the limiting ellipsoid depends not only on the mirrored entry-wise correlation structure, but also non-trivially on the sparsity limit $p=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}p_n$.

papers.title: Bounds for spectral projectors on the three-dimensional torus
papers.authors: Pierre Germain, Simon L. Rydin Myerson, Daniel Pezzi
papers.abstract:
We study $L^2$ to $L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with $L^p$ norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain. For the three-dimensional torus we prove new cases of a previous conjecture of the first two authors concerning the size of these norms; we also refine certain prior results to remove $\epsilon$-losses in all dimensions. We use methods from number theory: the geometry of numbers, the circle method and exponential sum bounds due to Guo. We complement these techniques with height splitting and a bilinear argument to prove sharp results.
  We exposit on the various techniques used and their limitations.

papers.title: Augmentation categories in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: For an exact symplectic manifold $M$ and a Legendrian submanifold $\Lambda$ of the contactification $M\times \mathbb{R}$, we construct the augmentation category (over a field of characteristic 2), a unital $A_\infty$-category whose objects are augmentations of the Chekanov-Eliashberg differential graded algebra. This extends the construction of the augmentation category by Ng-Rutherford-Shende-Sivek-Zaslow to contact manifolds of dimension greater than 3.

papers.title: Generalized Bicycle Codes with Low Connectivity: Minimum Distance Bounds and Competitive Circuit-Level Performance
papers.authors: Reza Dastbasteh, Olatz Sanz Larrarte, Arun John Moncy, Paul Schnabl, Pedro M. Crespo, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Ruben M. Otxoa
papers.abstract: We present new upper and lower bounds on the minimum distance of certain generalized bicycle (GB) codes that go beyond the capabilities of techniques based on classical codes. These bounds are shown to capture the true minimum distance for specific subclasses within the GB family. In particular, we demonstrate the existence of two highly degenerate GB code families with parameters $[\![d^2+1,2,d]\!]_2$ for odd $d \geq 3$ and $[\![d^2,2,d]\!]_2$ for even $d \geq 4$, both having qubit connectivity of four, similar to that of surface codes. For the odd-distance family, we analyze the structure of low-weight logical Pauli operators and establish the existence of a fault-tolerant logical CNOT gate between the two logical qubits, achievable via a simple relabeling of data qubits. Next, using nearly self-inverse polynomials, we extend our results to construct an infinite class of connectivity-six GB codes with an improved rate. For GB codes based on these polynomials, we further present a technique to realize transversal logical CNOT gates via data-qubit permutations. We further construct syndrome extraction schemes for our connectivity four GB families that avoid reductions in minimum distance due to circuit-level faults propagating from check qubits to data qubits. Finally, we numerically evaluate the logical error rate performance of the mentioned connectivity four families of GB codes under circuit-level noise, obtaining thresholds comparable to those of rotated surface codes.

papers.title: An interpolation of Bradley's sum formula
papers.abstract: The sum formula for $q$-multiple zeta values is a well-known relation. In this paper, we present its generalization for the $q$-multiple zeta function.

papers.title: Webification of symmetry classes of plane partitions
papers.abstract: Webs are graphical objects that give a tangible, combinatorial way to compute and classify tensor invariants. Recently, Gaetz, Pechenik, Pfannerer, Striker, and Swanson found a rotation-invariant web basis for $\mathrm{SL}_4$, as well as its quantum deformation $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$, and a bijection between move equivalence classes of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$-webs and fluctuating tableaux such that web rotation corresponds to tableau promotion. They also found a bijection between the set of plane partitions in an $a\times b\times c$ box and a benzene move equivalence class of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$-webs by determining the corresponding oscillating tableau. In this paper, we similarly find the oscillating tableaux corresponding to plane partitions in certain symmetry classes. We furthermore give a combinatorial map, defined on the span of the invariants of webs arising from certain symmetry classes, from $U_q(\sl_4)$ invariants to $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_r)$ invariants for $r=2,3$.

papers.title: Algebraic magnetism, formally verified and extended: a survey
papers.abstract: We formalize in the Lean proof assistant the three papers on algebraic magnetism published in Semigroup Forum: "Algebraic magnetism", "Algebraic magnetism invariants of self-actions of diagonalizable monoid schemes" and "Algebraic magnetism: $X$-products of attractors via $\mathbb{F}_1$-geometry". We also prove further results and comment on the relation with other work in the literature. The description of this formalization and of these results forms in itself a survey of the theory, from the perspective opened by the formalization. The first main mathematical contribution consists of a Bialynicki-Birula decomposition for faces and of proofs of the existence of strongly fixed-point-reflecting atlases, of the finiteness of pure magnets and of the vanishing of the higher monoid cohomology of $\mathrm{A}(M)$ with quasi-coherent coefficients, three conjectures of "Algebraic magnetism". The case of algebraic stacks, where the analogue of the existence of fixed-point-reflecting atlases fails, is treated in joint work with Sylvain Brochard, in which the finiteness of pure magnets was first proved privately, by a comparable method. The second main contribution, for split reductive groups, is a description of the pure magnets and of the join-irreducible ones: besides the classical roots, they are the join-irreducible pure magnets equal to $(1-w)M$ for some $w$ in the Weyl group, which encode the components of attractors; a prime $p$ is a torsion prime of the group, in the sense of Steinberg, if and only if some join-irreducible Weyl magnet $(1-w)M$ has $w$ of $p$-power order.

papers.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo integration over $\mathbb{R}^s$ with boundary-damping importance sampling
papers.authors: Zexin Pan, Du Ouyang, Zhijian He
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new importance sampling (IS) method tailored to quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) integration over $\mathbb{R}^s$. IS introduces a multiplicative weight that compensates for sampling from a proposal distribution rather than the target distribution. An unsuitable proposal, however, can yield an integrand that exhibits severe boundary growth and suffers from the curse of dimensionality, thus degrading QMC performance. Our approach is to design a weight function with the desired regularity and then construct a transport map realizing it as an IS proposal, thereby obtaining a transformed integrand amenable to QMC integration. We provide a rigorous analysis based on Fourier coefficients and apply it to lattice rule integration. Under suitable conditions, the proposed estimator achieves a fast convergence rate independent of the dimension $s$, making it suitable for high-dimensional problems.

papers.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
papers.abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $\lambda_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $\lambda_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.

papers.title: Berger-Joyal duality and traces I
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that the opposite of Joyal's disk category $\mathcal{D}_n$ is Berger's wreath product category $\Theta_n = \Delta\wr\cdots\wr\Delta$. Our techniques continue to apply when the simplex category $\Delta$ is replaced by Connes' cyclic category $\Lambda$ and some other crossed simplicial groups.

papers.title: Brauer groups of certain affine cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Brauer groups of affine surfaces that are complements of singular hyperplane sections of smooth cubic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$. We determine the Brauer group over the algebraic closure as a Galois module for all the possible singular hyperplane sections. For the case when the hyperplane section is geometrically the union of three lines, we give explicit examples where transcendental elements of order $2$ and $3$ exist over $\mathbb{Q}$. We end with an explicit example of an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle given by an element of order~$3$ on an affine cubic surface with singular boundary.

papers.title: When is the canonical conductor minimal?
papers.abstract: For a one dimensional analytically unramified Cohen-Macaulay local ring $R$, the blowup algebra of the canonical ideal is a module finite birational extension. The conductor of this extension always contains the conductor of $R$. We study the case when there is equality. This is the case where $R$ is far from being almost Gorenstein. We characterise such rings among Arf domains and numerical semigroup rings. As an application, we compute the cohomology annihilator ideal of an explicit family of rings and show it to be equal to the conductor ideal.

papers.title: On a fractional Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman-type monotonicity formula
papers.authors: Fausto Ferrari, Davide Giovagnoli, Enzo Maria Merlino
papers.abstract: In this paper, by exploiting mean value properties of $s$-harmonic functions, we introduce some monotonicity formulas in the nonlocal setting. Our approach is purely nonlocal and does not rely on the extension technique. As a byproduct we also establish interior nonlocal gradient estimates and a nonlocal analogue of the Bochner identity.

papers.title: Non-fibered strongly quasipositive links and tightness
papers.abstract: It is well known that for fibered links in $\mathbb{S}^3$ being strongly quasipositive and supporting a tight contact structure are equivalent notions (arXiv:math/0509499). In this note we analyze the relation between these two properties for non fibered links. A non fibered link (together with an incompressible Seifert surface) induces a natural partial open book (arXiv:2509.09615). We prove that strongly quasipositive links induce tight contact structures. We also show that, in contrast to the fibered case, the converse is not true, giving examples of links that are not strongly quasipositive but support tight contact structures.

papers.title: Generalized Fermat's principle and Snell's law for cone structures and applications
papers.authors: Miguel \'Angel Javaloyes, Steen Markvorsen, Enrique Pend\'as-Recondo, Miguel S\'anchez
papers.abstract: Fermat's principle is fully generalized to the case where a smooth interface separates two cone structures -- Lorentz-Finsler lightcones -- representing wave propagation in a potentially inhomogeneous, anisotropic, time-dependent and discontinuous medium. The interface, wave source and receiver are assumed to be a hypersurface, a submanifold and a curve in the spacetime, respectively, of any causal character. For a trajectory to fulfill Fermat's principle -- i.e., to be a critical point of the arrival time functional -- its direction must change at the interface, obeying a precise condition that generalizes Snell's law of refraction when the wave crosses the interface, or the law of reflection when it remains in a single medium. Both laws are analyzed in detail to establish the conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of refracted and reflected trajectories, and to determine whether they actually minimize the arrival time. Applications to Zermelo's navigation problem and the determination of geodesics in discretized spacetimes are also emphasized.

papers.title: Continuous cochains on Furstenberg boundaries and injectivity of the comparison map
papers.abstract: Monod proved that any continuous cohomology class of a semisimple Lie group $G$ can be represented by a measurable cocycle on the associated Furstenberg boundary, which we upgraded to an alternating cocycle. In the current paper we improve that result by showing that we can actually take a representing cocycle which is continuous on an explicit subset of generic tuples. We give an analogous result in the case of bounded cohomology. Finally, we exploit this characterization to prove the injectivity of the comparison map in degree $3$ for $\mathrm{Isom}^\circ(\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{C}}^n)$, when $n \geq 2$, and in degree $4$ for $\mathrm{Isom}^\circ(\mathbb{H}^n_{\mathbb{R}})$, when $n \geq 2$.

papers.title: Integrated Localization, Mapping, and Communication through VCSEL-Based Light-emitting RIS (LeRIS)
papers.authors: Rashid Iqbal, Dimitrios Bozanis, Dimitrios Tyrovolas, Sotiris Ioannidis, Christos K. Liaskos, Muhammad Ali Imran, George K. Karagiannidis, Hanaa Abumarshoud
papers.abstract: Light-emitting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (LeRISs) have recently emerged as a promising solution for providing the spatial awareness required for reliable millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication in programmable wireless environments (PWEs). However, existing LeRIS designs rely on the diffuse emission of light-emitting diodes, while LiDAR-assisted solutions require dedicated sensing modules that hinder their direct integration into RIS panels. In this paper, a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL)-based LeRIS framework is developed to jointly support user localization, obstacle-aware mapping, and mmWave communication. Specifically, the narrow Gaussian beams and multimode operation of VCSELs are exploited to derive closed-form schemes for the joint recovery of the user position and orientation from received signal strength measurements. According to the provided simulation results, is shown that five VCSELs are sufficient for unique recovery, while this requirement is reduced to three dual-mode VCSELs under specific geometric conditions. Furthermore, the position error bound (PEB) is derived to characterize the achievable localization accuracy, while reflected-signal time-of-arrival measurements are employed to identify obstructed links and enable blockage-resilient LeRIS routing. As a result, the proposed framework achieves cm-level localization accuracy, reliable obstacle detection, and substantial spectral-efficiency and minimum-user-rate gains, thereby establishing VCSEL-based LeRISs as a solution for spatially aware and resilient PWEs.

papers.title: Solving the BGK Model and Boltzmann equation by Fourier Neural Operator with conservative constraints
papers.abstract: The numerical approximation of the Boltzmann collision operator presents significant challenges because of its high dimensionality, quadratic nonlinearity, and nonlocal integral structure. In this work, we develop a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO)-based framework for learning finite time evolution operators associated with the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation and its simplified BGK model in different velocity space dimensions. The framework learns mappings between distribution functions in either sequence-to-sequence or point-to-point form and, once trained, enables rapid evaluation without repeated classical time evolution. To improve physical consistency, we introduce a conservative FNO (C-FNO) by augmenting the training loss with soft penalties for deviations in mass, momentum, and energy from the conservation law. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate that the learned operators accurately reproduce the principal collision dynamics, while C-FNO generally reduces macroscopic drift relative to the standard FNO, highlighting its potential as a promising framework for physics-constrained operator learning in kinetic theory and other nonlinear integro-differential equations.

papers.title: Solid realization of motives with modulus
papers.abstract: We construct a covariant realization functor $\mathrm{Solid}^m(-)$ from the category of motives with modulus to the derived category of solid modules in the sense of Clausen-Scholze. For a smooth modulus pair $(X,D)$, the dual of $\mathrm{Solid}^m(X,D)$ recovers the Kelly-Miyazaki Hodge realization of $(X,D)$. Let $X$ be a smooth proper variety over a field, let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor whose support has simple normal crossings, and let $U\subset X$ be an open subscheme. We compute $\mathrm{Solid}^m(\mathrm{Cone}(\underline{M}(U,D|_U)\to\underline{M}(X,D)))$ explicitly in terms of the formal completion along $X\setminus U$ of a model of $X$ of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Differential equations for intertwining operators among untwisted and twisted modules
papers.abstract: Given any vertex operator algebra $ V $ with an automorphism $ g $, we derive a Jacobi identity for an intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is an untwisted $ V $-module, and $ W_2 $ and $ W_3 $ are $ g $-twisted $ V $-modules. We say such an intertwining operator is of $\left(\!\begin{smallmatrix} g\\ 1 \ g \end{smallmatrix}\!\right)$-type. Using the Jacobi identity, we obtain homogeneous linear differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ when $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ are of $\left(\!\begin{smallmatrix} g\\ 1 \ g \end{smallmatrix}\!\right)$-type and the modules are $ C_1 $-cofinite and discretely graded. In the special case that $ V $ is an affine vertex operator algebra, we derive the ``twisted KZ equations" and show that its solutions have regular singularities at certain prescribed points when $ g $ has finite order. When $ V $ is general and $ g $ has finite order, we use the theory of regular singular points to prove that the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ converges absolutely to a multivalued analytic function when $ |z_1| > \cdots > |z_N| > 0 $ and analytically extends to the region $ z_i, z_i - z_j \neq 0 $. Furthermore, when $ N = 2 $, we show that these multivalued functions have regular singularities at certain prescribed points.

papers.title: A Dynamical N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich Criterion via Orbital Arboreal Representations
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field and $\varphi : \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$ a rational endomorphism of degree $d \geq 2$ over $K$. In the tame case ($p \nmid d$), we show that strict good reduction is equivalent to the existence of a nonempty Zariski open subset $U_k \subset \mathbb{P}^1_k \setminus \mathrm{PC}(\widetilde{\varphi})$ over which the canonical residual morphism is finite \'etale of degree $d$. The criterion separates two complementary local invariants of a normalized integral lift: $\mathrm{Res}(F,G)$ controls residual degree drop, while the fiber discriminants $\mathrm{Disc}(F_{n,x})$ control \'etaleness of the residual fibers once full residual degree is ensured. Consequently, for every finite $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$ with $\bar{x} \in U_k$, the extensions $K(X_n(x))/K$ are unramified for all $n \geq 1$. We introduce the orbital preimage tree $T_{O^+(x)} = \varinjlim_n X_\infty(\varphi^n(x))$, the colimit in $G_K$-sets along the forward orbit, and the orbital arboreal Galois image $\mathcal{G}_{O^+(x)} = \mathrm{Im}(G_K \to \mathrm{Aut}(T_{O^+(x)}))$. On the forward-invariant safe locus $U_k^{\mathrm{safe}} = \bigcap_{m \geq 0} \widetilde{\varphi}^{-m}(U_k)$, strict good reduction is captured by the bijectivity of the orbital reduction map $X_n(x_m) \to \widetilde{X}_n(\bar{x}_m)$. This canonical orbit-invariant framework connects with arboreal Galois representations (Boston-Jones, Jones, and others) and yields pointwise and orbit-level reformulations. Explicit examples over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ illustrate the criterion.

papers.title: Maximal non-compactness of embeddings between sequence spaces
papers.abstract: We will focus on studying the ball measure of non-compactness $\alpha(T)$ for various particular instances of embedding operators in sequence spaces. Our first main goal is to find necessary and sufficient conditions for an identity operator to be maximally non-compact. Next, we will focus on studying Lorentz sequence spaces $\ell^{p,q}$ and their basic properties. We will characterize the inclusions between Lorentz sequence spaces depending on the values of $p$ and $q$. Then we will try to determine exact values of the norms of the identity operators between these embedded spaces. Lastly, we will determine whether these identity operators are maximally non-compact by using our general theorems.

papers.title: Effective existence of primitive k-normal elements via affine spaces
papers.authors: Josimar J. R. Aguirre, Sarah F. M. Mazzini, Victor G. L. Neumann
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ be the finite field with $q^n$ elements. An element $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ is $k$-normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$ if $\alpha$ and its conjugates span an $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of dimension $n-k$. It is known that, for $q$ larger than a constant $c(n)$, a primitive $k$-normal element exists if and only if there exists a $k$-normal element free of binomials, but $c(n)$ is not explicit. We count the $k$-normal elements in affine subspaces of the form $\beta+\ker L_h$ and show that, when $h$ is an irreducible factor of the $\mathbb{F}_q$-order of $\beta$, all but at most one of them are $k$-normal. We also show that, when $\beta$ is free of binomials, these affine subspaces have degree $n$, so that character sum estimates over affine spaces apply to them. Combining these facts with a sieve, we make the equivalence above effective, with explicit lower bounds on $q$. As an application, we compute these bounds for $5\le n\le 8$ and give a complete characterization of the existence of primitive $k$-normal elements in $\mathbb{F}_{q^6}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

papers.title: Higher representation infinite algebras and toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two
papers.abstract:
We prove the existence of and classify basic $d$-tilting bundles consisting of line bundles on d-dimensional smooth toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two. A $d$-tilting bundle is a tilting bundle whose endomorphism algebra has global dimension at most $d$.
  The classification is motivated by dimer models, where internal perfect matchings give rise to $2$-representation infinite algebras. The algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$ introduced by Herschend, Iyama and Oppermann are higher-dimensional analogues in the simplex case. The same principle leads to a new class of algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$.
  Upper sets provide a common framework for tilting bundles, toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs), and cuts of higher-dimensional dimer-type quivers. In the Picard-number-one case, the bundles are in bijection with non-trivial upper sets in the Picard group, and their endomorphism algebras are precisely $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$. In the Picard-number-two case, a first upper set determines the ambient toric NCCR, and a second selects an internal cut of its quiver. This gives a complete classification of such $d$-tilting bundles and realizes their endomorphism algebras precisely as $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$.
  The resulting geometric models give a combinatorial description of $d$-APR tilting modules and show that both classes of algebras are closed under $d$-APR tilts.

papers.title: A Class of Self-Orthogonal, NMDS, or LCD MDS $(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{P})$-Twisted Generalized Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.authors: Zhonghao Liang, Chenlu Jia, Dongmei Huang, Qunying Liao, Chunming Tang
papers.abstract: Maximum distance separable (in short, MDS), near MDS (in short, NMDS), linear complementary dual codes (in short, LCD) and self-orthogonal codes play a pivotal role in algebraic coding theory, particularly in applications such as quantum communications and secret sharing schemes. Recently, the construction of non-generalized Reed-Solomon (in short, non-GRS) codes has emerged as a significant research frontier. This paper focuses on a class of $(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{P})$-twisted generalized Reed-Solomon (TGRS) codes $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{\eta}\right)$ characterized by $\ell+1$ twists. By considering a special class of parity-check matrices derived from existing results, we derive the corresponding necessary and sufficient conditions or sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{\eta}\right)$ to be self-orthogonal, and then generalize the corresponding results given by Liu et al. (2021), Sui et al. (2021), and Zhang et al. (2025). As applications, leveraging these self-orthogonal structures, we can obtain several families of LCD MDS codes. Secondly, we provide a characterization of the NMDS property for the codes $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{\eta}\right)$, offering a partial solution to the open problem concerning general $(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{P})$-TGRS codes posed by Hu et al. (2025). Finally, we rigorously prove that the codes $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{\eta}\right)$ are of non-GRS type when $2k > n>k+\ell+2$.

papers.title: Logarithmic double phase embeddings with variable exponents: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the necessary and sufficient conditions in the domain for Sobolev-type embedding of the space $W^{1,\Phi(\cdot,\cdot)}(\Omega)$ where $\Phi(x,t):=t^{p(x)}+ a(x) t^{q(x)}\log^{r(x)}(e+t)$ with $1\leq p(x)\leq q(x).$ We have established subcritical embedding in bounded John domains under some regularity assumptions on exponents $p,$ $q,$ $r$, and $a$. Conversely, we have proved that if the embedding holds in any domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^n,$ then $\Omega$ must satisfy the log-measure density condition.

papers.title: Polychromatic Localized Waves with Complex Frequencies in Nonlinear Maxwell Equations with Material Dispersion
papers.authors: Tomas Dohnal, Maximilian Hanisch, Runan He
papers.abstract: We study the existence of polychromatic solutions of cubically nonlinear Maxwell equations in the whole space and with dispersive media, i.e., with a time delayed polarization. Due to the complex nature of the dielectric function, the frequencies are complex, resulting in a decay in time. The geometry is that of a waveguide in $x$ with the propagation direction being $y$ and the solutions are localized in $x$ and have a transverse magnetic polarization. These are often referred to as breathers. They are given as a Fourier series in $y$ and $t$ with the leading frequency $\omega$ being an eigenvalue of a corresponding operator pencil on $\mathbb{R}$ (in the $x$ variable). Each term in the series corresponds to a different temporal decay rate or a different frequency. The series is constructed iteratively via a sequence of linear ordinary differential equations. Our general result provides the existence under some assumptions on the spectrum and on estimates of the resolvent of the corresponding linear operator. We also produce an example of a waveguide given by the interface of two spatially homogeneous physically relevant media for which these assumptions are satisfied. For such an interface setting the constructed solutions correspond to nonlinear polychromatic surface plasmons.

papers.title: On $\pi_1$-injectivity of self-maps in low dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that all self-maps of non-zero degree of $3$-manifolds not covered by $S^3$ and of Thurston geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums not diffeomorphic to $N\#(\#_{p\geq0}S^2\times S^2)\#(\#_{q\geq0}\mathbb C P^2)$, where $N$ is an $S^2\times\mathbb X^2$ or $S^3\times\mathbb R$ manifold, are $\pi_1$-injective. We thus determine when these maps induce $\pi_1$-isomorphisms. The results in dimension three were previously established by Shicheng Wang. We give a uniform group theoretic proof in all cases based only on the residual finiteness of the fundamental groups for the $\pi_1$-injectivity and then only on numerical invariants for the $\pi_1$-isomorphisms.

papers.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville properties for the drifted Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the validity of Liouville-type theorems involving the drifted Laplacian on complete, non-compact Riemannian manifolds endowed with a smooth vector field $X$. In particular, we prove new Liouville properties both for positive $X$-harmonic functions and for non-negative $X$-subharmonic functions which are in an $L^{p}$-space, $p\in(1,+\infty)$, with respect to any invariant measure for the operator. The main tool for the analysis is a local gradient estimate for positive solutions to the semilinear equation $\Delta_{X}u=F(u)$, which is valid if $F$ satisfies certain structural conditions and the Bakry-\'Emery-Ricci curvature associated to $X$ is bounded below. On the one hand, this estimate is used in a novel way to deduce the Liouville property for positive solutions and, on the other hand, it is used to construct cut-off functions for the $X$-Laplacian that yields the $L^{p}$-Liouville results.

papers.title: Parabolic equations with large long-range random potentials of arbitrary Hermite rank: convergence to Hermite-driven Feynman-Kac limits
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional heat equation with a large, rapidly oscillating random potential, obtained by applying a polynomial of arbitrary Hermite rank to a stationary Gaussian process with long-range dependence. When the correlations decay slowly enough, the solution does not homogenise to a deterministic limit. We prove that it converges in law, as a random field, to a Feynman-Kac functional driven by a Hermite process, which is fractional Brownian motion for Hermite rank one and the Rosenblatt process for Hermite rank two. The proof rests on an identity which expresses the exponent of the Feynman-Kac formula as a continuous functional of the integrated potential, so that neither local times of fractional processes nor exponential moments with respect to the potential are needed. We also show that the limit has moments of every order for Hermite rank one, and for Hermite rank two with a negative second Hermite coefficient, whereas for a positive coefficient its mean is infinite, although it is finite almost surely. A numerical experiment illustrates the convergence of the integrated potential to the Rosenblatt law.

papers.title: Banach-Valued Carr\'e du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a projective-tensor-valued carr\'e du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fr\'echet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carr\'e du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: Asymptotic behaviour of stochastic inertial dynamics incorporating a Tikhonov regularization term
papers.abstract: In a separable Hilbert space, we study the minimization problem of a convex smooth function with Lipschitz continuous gradient whose evaluations are corrupted by random noise. To this end, we associate a stochastic inertial system that incorporates Tikhonov regularization with the optimization problem. We establish existence and uniqueness of a solution trajectory for this system. Then, we derive an upper bound on the expected value of an appropriate associated energy function given square-integrability of the diffusion $\sigma_X$ before focusing on the particular case where the parameter function multiplied by the Tikhonov term is given by $\frac{1}{t^r}$ for $0<r<2$. For this setting, we show a.s. convergence rates as well as convergence rates in expectation for the function values along the trajectory to an infimal value, the trajectory process to an optimal solution and its time derivative to zero under a stronger integrability condition on $\sigma_X$.

papers.title: Integrated Control and Communication in LQG Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Integrated Communication and Control (ICAC) problem. Specifically, we investigate how messages can be transmitted from the controller/encoder to the observer/decoder through the control signal in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) vector-state Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) systems under control constraints. We provide a computable capacity expression using semidefinite programming. We further show that it is possible to transmit data at a nonzero rate over an LQG system while maintaining the same optimal control cost as in the case where no information message are transmitted. Finally, we discuss how this framework generalizes communication over MIMO Gaussian channels with feedback, both with and without InterSymbol Interference (ISI).

papers.title: On Composite Foster Functions for a Class of Singularly Perturbed Stochastic Hybrid Inclusions: Theory and Applications
papers.abstract: We study sufficient conditions for stability and recurrence in a class of singularly perturbed stochastic hybrid dynamical systems. The systems considered combine multi-time-scale deterministic continuous-time dynamics, modeled by constrained differential inclusions, with discrete-time dynamics described by constrained difference inclusions subject to random disturbances. Under suitable regularity assumptions on the dynamics and causality of the associated solutions, we develop a family of composite nonsmooth Lagrange-Foster and Lyapunov-Foster functions that certify stability and recurrence properties by leveraging simpler functions related to the slow and fast subsystems. Stability is characterized with respect to compact sets, while recurrence is established for bounded open sets. The proposed framework is illustrated through several examples and applications, including the stability analysis of singularly perturbed switching systems with stochastic spontaneous mode transitions, feedback optimization problems with stochastically switching plants, and momentum-based feedback optimization algorithms with stochastic restarting.

papers.title: On $R$-equivalence of Automorphism Groups of Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional associative $k$-algebra with identity. The primary aim of this paper is to study the rationality properties of the group of all $k$-algebra automorphisms of $A$, as an affine algebraic group over an arbitrary field $k$. We investigate mainly the $R$-equivalence property of the identity component of $\mathrm{Aut}_{k}(A)$ over a perfect field $k$.

papers.title: Heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
papers.authors: Soobin Cho, Panki Kim, Renming Song, Zoran Vondra\v{c}ek
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes on closed subsets $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a Borel subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. We assume that $F\setminus \Sigma$ is a $\kappa$-fat set and is dense in $F$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $F$, that the Assouad dimension of $F$ is strictly less than $d$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. The jump kernels under consideration take the form $J(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-\alpha}{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, where $\alpha\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal B}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. A fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $F\setminus \Sigma$. Examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $\alpha$-stable processes in some unbounded $C^{1,\rm Dini}$ sets, processes in Lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal Neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.

papers.title: On the well-posedness of two-dimensional Hele-Shaw flow with an elastic interface
papers.abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional Hele-Shaw free-boundary problem with a nonlinear elastic interface, for both one-phase and two-phase scenarios. Using the paradifferential formulation, we demonstrate that the problem is locally well-posed in $H^s$ for $s\geq 2$ for arbitrary initial data. Furthermore, for the one-phase case and the stable two-phase case $(\rho^+ \leq \rho^-)$, we establish global well-posedness for small initial data in $H^s$ when $s> \frac{3}{2}$.

papers.title: Universal concentration for sums under arbitrary dependence
papers.abstract: We present a universal concentration bound for sums of random variables under arbitrary dependence, and we prove that it is asymptotically optimal for broad families of marginals admitting a uniform integrable tail-quantile envelope. The bound follows directly from the subadditivity of expected shortfall, a property well known in the risk-measure literature. Our sharpness result relies on an explicit construction of asymptotically extremal couplings. We furthermore provide practical sufficient conditions -- based on convex transformation order comparisons with exponential and power-law envelopes -- under which the bound admits simple, explicit tail profiles.

papers.title: On identity Seidel switches
papers.abstract: An identity Seidel switch of a graph is a vertex subset whose Seidel switch produces an isomorphic graph. We distinguish the elementary abelian group of switching operations from the family of identity switches of a fixed graph, which need not be a group. We obtain an edge-count condition for identity switches and deduce that every vertex-identity switch has degree half the number of remaining vertices. In particular, no graph of order at least two has every vertex as an identity switch. For a two-vertex switching set inducing an edge, we characterize the switches admitting an isomorphism that preserves the endpoint pair, in terms of automorphisms of the remaining induced subgraph. We establish modification results under this additional hypothesis and give explicit constructions of identity switches. Counterexamples show why edge-count conditions and unrestricted modification assertions do not suffice.

papers.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
papers.authors: Topias Terho, Fabricio Oliveira, Ahti Salo, Pedro Munari
papers.abstract:
Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces.
  The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.

papers.title: Bi-Lipschitz invariance of Newton polygons along gradient canyons
papers.authors: Piotr Migus, Lauren\c{t}iu P\u{a}unescu, Mihai Tib\u{a}r
papers.abstract: We study bi-Lipschitz right-equivalence of holomorphic function germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ via polar arcs and gradient canyons. For a polar arc $\gamma$ we consider the Newton polygon of $f_x(X+\gamma(Y),Y)$ and define its augmentation by adjoining the point $(0,\operatorname{ord} f(\gamma(y),y)-1)$. We prove that the resulting augmented Newton polygon is constant along each gradient canyon of degree $>1$ and is invariant under bi-Lipschitz right-equivalence. Moreover, its compact edges decompose into a topological part and a Lipschitz part: the latter encodes, through simple intercept relations, the second-level Henry-Parusi\'nski type invariants. As applications, we obtain two numerical bi-Lipschitz invariants attached to a canyon: its polar multiplicity and, via the Koike-Kuo-P\u{a}unescu curvature formula, the total asymptotic Gaussian curvature concentrated in it.

papers.title: A construction of smooth varieties admitting small contractions
papers.abstract: Given a smooth variety together with two smooth subvarieties, we construct, via two successive blowups, smooth varieties admitting small contractions. This generalizes Kawamata's example of small contraction in dimension 4. We also construct the flip of the contraction explicitly. As an application, from products of two del Pezzo surfaces we obtain smooth weak Fano fourfolds that admit small contractions with Picard number up to 10.

papers.title: The Leibniz adjunction in homotopy type theory, with an application to simplicial type theory
papers.authors: Tom de Jong, Nicolai Kraus, Axel Ljungstr\"om
papers.abstract: Simplicial type theory extends homotopy type theory and equips types with a notion of directed morphisms. A Segal type is defined to be a type in which these directed morphisms can be composed. We show that all higher coherences can be stated and derived if simplicial type theory is taken to be homotopy type theory with a postulated interval type. In technical terms, this means that if a type has unique fillers for $(2,1)$-horns, it has unique fillers for all inner $(n,k)$-horns. This generalizes a result of Riehl and Shulman for the case $n = 3, k \in \{1, 2\}$. Our main technical tool is the Leibniz adjunction: the pushout-product is left adjoint to the pullback-hom in the wild category of types. While this adjunction is well known for ordinary categories, it is much more involved for higher categories, and the fact that it can be proved for the wild category of types (a higher category without stated higher coherences) is non-trivial. We make profitable use of the equivalence between the wild category of maps and that of families. We have formalized the results in Cubical Agda.

papers.title: Low-order CR--RT equilibrated-flux certification for semilinear problems on anisotropic meshes
papers.abstract: We study a posteriori certification of semilinear diffusion--reaction problems on anisotropic simplicial meshes. Given a conforming finite element approximation, we bound its dual-norm residual by solving an auxiliary Crouzeix--Raviart problem and reconstructing an equilibrated Raviart--Thomas flux. Together with a coercivity estimate and a local derivative-Lipschitz bound, this gives a Newton--Kantorovich test for existence and local uniqueness in a computable energy-norm ball. We then use the verified radius to bound volume-type quantities of interest. The adjoint estimate accounts for the primal and adjoint residuals and retains explicit Taylor remainders for the nonlinear equation and, where relevant, the output functional. We also prove a conditional flux-mismatch consistency result on anisotropic mesh families.
