papers.title: Swapping and Switching for Markov Processes: Symmetrisation and Fast-Exchange Limits
papers.abstract: In parallel tempering, exchanging the positions of the replicas (swapping) and exchanging the assignment of dynamics to the replicas (switching) are often used interchangeably. We study the two descriptions as stochastic processes, for Markov species (the dynamics that are exchanged) and bounded measurable exchange rates. To guarantee the Markovianity of each process under the exchanges, switching records both the positions and the label that tracks which species each replica carries; swapping records only the positions. Driving both with one exchange clock places them on a common probability space and lets us write swapping as switching with the label forgotten. This relation holds pathwise at every time and, once decomposed over the label, yields an exact identity between their transition kernels. This characterisation lets us relate, in a precise way, where the two processes agree and where they differ. We describe mainly the relation between their decay rates at finite exchange rate, and between their distributions and observables at finite and infinite exchange rate. The relation between the Markovianity of the two is particularly interesting. At finite rate, switching needs the label to be Markov, while swapping is Markov on its own. In the infinite-rate limit this reverses: swapping becomes non-tight, while switching becomes Markov on the physical coordinates alone. We illustrate all these relations on a solvable benchmark of two Brownian motions with drift under a constant exchange rate. The rich behaviour already visible in this simple case, and developed throughout the paper, suggests that the swapping mechanism is of interest in its own right, beyond the balance conditions needed in parallel tempering.

papers.title: Bifurcation of periodic and antiperiodic solutions in non-autonomous potential-type delay systems
papers.abstract: As a continuation of our previous work, where bifurcations of periodic and antiperiodic orbits near an equilibrium were studied for autonomous differential delay systems with one or two delays, this paper investigates bifurcations of periodic and antiperiodic solutions for five classes of non-autonomous potential delay differential systems with multiple delays. By reformulating these systems as generalized Hamiltonian systems on Euclidean spaces, we apply the Hamiltonian bifurcation theory recently developed by the author to establish alternative bifurcation results of both Fadell-Rabinowitz and Rabinowitz type.

papers.title: Characteristic classes on a noncommutative background: a new approach
papers.authors: Dimitry Gurevich, Vladimir Roubtsov, Pavel Saponov
papers.abstract:
We introduce analogues of partial derivatives with respect to the generators of the enveloping algebras $U(gl(N))$ and their $q$-deformations, the so-called modified reflection equation algebras. Using these quantum partial derivatives, we introduce the corresponding differential algebras, define the quantum de Rham operator, and exhibit the Leibniz rule for its action. Our Leibniz rule differs from its classical analogue and stems from the construction of a quantum double. In the case of the algebra $U(gl(N))$, we present another form of the Leibniz rule that is more convenient for prolonging the differential calculus to certain extensions of this algebra.
  We then use analogues of the Cayley--Hamilton identity for the generating matrices of $U(gl(N))$ and of reflection equation algebras to construct projective modules over these algebras. For these projective modules, we introduce Grassmannian connections and define the corresponding Chern classes.

papers.title: Duality in Biperiodic Fibonacci Words: Substitution, Frequencies and Combinatorial Invariants
papers.abstract: The biperiodic Fibonacci word $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$ is the standard Sturmian word with directive sequence $(a,b,a,b,\dots)$. The words $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$ and $\mathfrak{F}^{(b,a)}$ are related by the morphism $\sigma_a\colon 0\mapsto 0^a1,\ 1\mapsto 0$ through the exact identity $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}=\sigma_a\bigl(\mathfrak{F}^{(b,a)}\bigr)$. This identity gives the letter frequencies, the return words of both letters, the derived sequence with respect to the letter $0$, and the transport of palindromic prefixes from $\mathfrak{F}^{(b,a)}$ to $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$. The slope of $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$ has the continued fraction expansion $[0;a+1,\overline{b,a}]$, and the critical exponent equals $2+\alpha/\min(a,b)$, where $\alpha$ is the positive root of $t^2-ab\,t-ab=0$. The frequency of the letter $1$ and the return words of $1$ depend on the order of $a$ and $b$, whereas the critical exponent, the balance, the abelian complexity and the palindromic complexity do not.

papers.title: Repeated differentiation of deterministic polynomials with asymptotically radial root distributions
papers.abstract:
Recent works of Galligo, Najnudel, and Vu (2025) and Najnudel and Vu (2026) study repeated differentiation for polynomials of the form $P(z)=p(z^m)$, where $p$ is a deterministic polynomial of degree $n$ with real, non-negative roots, in the regime where $m$ and $n$ are large. If $m\gg \log(n)$ and the root distribution of $P$ converges to a compactly supported, radial probability measure $\mu_0$, these works show that for $0\le t<1$, the root distribution of the $\lfloor nmt\rfloor$-th derivative of $P$ converges to a compactly supported probability measure $\mu_t$ given by an explicit formula for its radial quantile function.
  We give a substantially simplified proof of this result and also extend the result from repeated differentiation to repeated applications of the differential operator $z^a(d/dz)^b$. Our proof is based on new, sharp estimates on the roots of polynomial with real, non-negative roots in terms of the coefficients of the polynomial.
  We also compute the limiting root distribution in the case when $m$ is fixed and $n$ tends to infinity. Then letting $m$ tend to infinity we obtain the same limit as before. Along the way, we prove a generalization of the free multiplicative law of large numbers that is of independent interest.

papers.title: Recurrence Coefficients of Oscillatory Gegenbauer-type Orthogonal Polynomials
papers.abstract: We study two classes of oscillatory Gegenbauer-type weight functions. One is $w_1(x)=(1-x^2)^{\lambda-1/2}\exp(i\zeta x),x\in[-1,1]$, where $\lambda>-1/2$ is rational and $\zeta\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ is a zero of the Bessel function $J_{\lambda-1}$. The other is $w_2(x)=x(1-x^{2})^{\gamma-1/2} \exp(\mathit{i}\eta x), x\in[-1,1]$, where $\gamma$ and $\eta$ are chosen such that the corresponding orthogonal polynomials exist. By using the ladder operators established in recent work for monic orthogonal polynomials associated with Jacobi-type weight functions and three compatibility conditions, we derive two coupled difference equations for the three-term recurrence coefficients corresponding to $w_1$ and $w_2$, respectively. For $w_1$, and for $w_2$ where $\gamma=0$ and $\eta$ is a positive zero of $J_0$, or $\gamma=1/2$ and $\eta=m\pi$ with $m$ denoting a nonzero integer, we determine the initial values for the recurrence coefficients and compute the first few terms via the difference equations. Then we conjecture general-$n$ symbolic forms for the recurrence coefficients and for $\textbf{p}(n)$, the coefficient of $x^{n-1}$ in the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$. The case $\lambda=0$ in $w_1$ is treated separately, since the conjectured general-$\lambda$ forms degenerate here, yielding substantially different results. For $w_1$, we also derive a third-order difference equation satisfied by $\textbf{p}(n)$.

papers.title: Essential-Surface Complexes of Knot Exteriors: Image, Kernel, and Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Ivanov's theorem recovers the mapping class group of a surface from its curve complex. We study the analogous question for the essential-surface complex $\mathcal{ES}(E)$ of a knot exterior $E=E(K)$, equivalently Schultens's initial surface complex, organized around three questions: which combinatorial symmetries are geometric (the image), which homeomorphisms are invisible (the kernel), and how much of $E$ can be read off from the complex (reconstruction). Call a knot slope-separated if its exterior contains no closed and no meridional essential surface and at most one essential surface for each boundary slope. For such a knot every orientation-preserving mapping class acts trivially on $\mathcal{ES}(E)$, and the image of the action is $\mathbb{Z}/2$ exactly when the knot is amphichiral and has a nonzero boundary slope. Torus knots are determined among all knots by the complex decorated with surface types and boundary slopes, and for a connected sum of nonfibered prime knots the decomposing-annulus twist translates Banks's winding coordinate, so an infinite cyclic subgroup is visible. For two-bridge knots the problem is solved in a companion paper, whose results are surveyed here without proofs. The article is written as an entry point: the objects are first drawn in classical examples, the elementary structure theory (flag property, layering by boundary slope, finite but unbounded dimension, Kakimizu's complexes as full subcomplexes) is collected with proofs, and the article closes with a three-task formulation of the rigidity problem, a list of problems with their current status, and a worked two-bridge recipe.

papers.title: Incompressible surfaces, hierarchies and unknot recognition
papers.abstract: We present a new algorithm to determine whether a compact orientable surface properly embedded in a compact orientable 3-manifold is incompressible. As a special case, this provides a new algorithm to detect the unknot. The central technique is the use of hierarchies. Unlike previous algorithms, no challenging invariants need to be computed and no lengthy search procedures are required. This algorithm leads to a new proof that determining whether a compact orientable 3-manifold has incompressible boundary is in NP.

papers.title: A CIR-Type Diffusion Driven by Hermite Processes: Well-Posedness, Positivity and Malliavin Analysis
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic differential equation \[ dX_t=a\bigl(b(t)-X_t\bigr)\,dt+\bigl(\sigma_0+\sigma_1\sqrt{\phi_\eps(X_t)}\bigr)\,dZ_t^{(q,H)}, \qquad X_0=x_0, \] where $Z^{(q,H)}$ is a Hermite process of order $q\geq1$ and Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$, $b$ is a periodic target, $\sigma_0>0$, and $\phi_\eps$ is a smooth positive function equal to $x+\eps$ on $[0,\infty)$. The equation is understood pathwise, in the sense of Young. We prove that it has a unique solution. We give lower bounds on the probability that the solution stays positive on $[0,T]$, for every $\sigma_1\geq0$: after a Lamperti-type change of variables, which makes the noise additive, a last-passage argument shows that the probability of reaching $0$ before $T$ is at most of order $\exp(-c\,\Lambda(m_0)^{2/q}/T^{2H/q})$, where $m_0$ is the smaller of the initial level and the minimum of the target and $\Lambda$ is the natural scale of the diffusion coefficient. For $q\le2$ and $\sigma_1=0$ we show that the solution reaches negative values with positive probability, so that no almost-sure positivity holds in that case. Finally, the solution at each time belongs to $\D^{1,\infty}$, with an explicit representation of its Malliavin derivative, and its law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. The proofs of these two results are self-contained and rely on the additive form of the equation. Numerical experiments based on a wavelet-type simulation of Hermite processes illustrate the results.

papers.title: The D'Alembert-Lagrange Principle and Lagrange Equations
papers.abstract: In this expository-research article we present a rigorous geometric framework for analytical mechanics in the extended phase space, accommodating general constraints that may be non-linear in velocities. We prove that the space of virtual displacements and ideal constraint reactions depend strictly on the intrinsic geometry of the constraint manifold and are entirely invariant under the choice of analytical constraint equations. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equations of the second kind are derived through the covector covariance of the variational derivative operator under the embedding mapping of the configuration manifold.

papers.title: d-Spectral Bitopological Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce the category of d-spectral spaces, a bitopological analogue of the spectral spaces of Stone and Hochster. A d-spectral space is a bitopological space satisfying three conditions: the join of its two topologies is compact, it is d-sober in the sense of Jung and Moshier, and each of its two topologies is a coherent frame. We establish a dual equivalence between this category and the category of d-lattices satisfying the finitary cut rules. The constructions implementing the duality are the d-lattice of compact open sets of a d-spectral space and the d-spectrum construction for d-lattices. We further show that spectral spaces embed as a full subcategory of d-spectral spaces that is both reflective and coreflective. Finally, the patch space of a d-spectral space is d-Boolean, and its de Groot dual is again d-spectral, mirroring the classical spectral case.

papers.title: Invariant forms compute the Dolbeault cohomology of complex nilmanifolds
papers.authors: Keizo Hasegawa, Lorenzo Sillari, Adriano Tomassini
papers.abstract: We prove that the inclusion of left-invariant forms into the Dolbeault complex of a compact nilmanifold $M$ endowed with a left-invariant complex structure $J$ induces an isomorphism in cohomology in every bidegree, settling a long-standing conjecture originating from a question of Console-Fino and Cordero-Fern\'andez-Gray-Ugarte. As consequences, we show that small deformations of $J$ are still invariant, as conjectured by Hasegawa, and that Bott-Chern, Aeppli, and Fr\"olicher invariants are computed by invariant forms and are independent of the lattice, settling a conjecture of Angella on Bott-Chern cohomology.

papers.title: Remarks on some quasi-linear fourth order parabolic equations arising in mathematical physics
papers.authors: Francesco Fanelli, Rafael Granero-Belinch\'on, Martina Magliocca, Matthieu Pageard
papers.abstract: This note proves existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to a broad class of fourth-order quasi-linear parabolic equations in the class of Wiener spaces. It improves upon previous results in the literature, devoted to some special cases falling within the general framework developed here, in which uniqueness held true in a smaller class than the space where existence was proven. Gain of analyticity, as well as generalisations to higher-order equations and to propagation of higher regularities, are also discussed.

papers.title: Small-data $L^2$ theory for the intermediate NLS and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations (NLS) in a unified way. This class includes two important examples: the intermediate NLS (INLS) and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS (CM-DNLS). Our main results are twofold. First, we prove small-data global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ for a broad class of equations. This includes both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for arbitrary choices of its parameters. Second, we prove small-data scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ under an additional assumption. This result covers both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for specific choices of its parameters. Both the formulation of the problem, including the notion of solution, and the proofs rely crucially on a linear theory for Schr\"odinger equations with rough time-dependent potentials. This theory is also of independent interest, since we allow potentials so rough that the standard Duhamel formulation may not make sense. Our approach is perturbative and is built on the bilinear Strichartz estimate proved by Ozawa and Tsutsumi in 1998. In particular, our argument does not rely on integrability.

papers.title: Convergence and Stability Analysis of a Generalized Proximal Point Algorithm and Its Inexact Version
papers.authors: Ba Khiet Le, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Michel A. Thera
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of adaptive strong monotonicity and establish a linear convergence of the recently proposed Generalized Proximal Point Algorithm (GPPA) for computing approximate solutions to nonmonotone inclusion problems in Hilbert spaces. We also investigate the Inexact Generalized Proximal Point Algorithm (IGPPA) in the presence of nondiminishing errors.

papers.title: Two-Sided Dimension Bounds for the Peterson Hit Problem via Projections and Matrix Minors
papers.authors: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal P_k=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_k]$, with $\deg x_i=1$, be the polynomial algebra equipped with the standard unstable action of the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra $\mathcal A$. The Peterson hit problem asks for a minimal homogeneous set of $\mathcal A$-generators for $\mathcal P_k$, or equivalently for a homogeneous basis of the cohit space $Q\mathcal P_k=\mathcal P_k/\mathcal A^+\mathcal P_k = \mathbb F_2\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal P_k$, where $\mathcal A^+ $ denotes the augmentation ideal of $\mathcal A$. The dimension of $(Q\mathcal P_k)_d$ therefore gives the number of generators required in positive degree $d$. Although solved in every degree $d$ for $k\leq 4,$ the problem remains open in general. As the number of variables $k$ and degrees $d$ increase, exact calculations involve increasingly large systems of Steenrod relations. Motivated by this difficulty, in this work, we establish explicit upper and lower bounds for $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(Q\mathcal P_k)_d$ for arbitrary positive integers $k$ and $d$. Our method combines binary combinatorics and linear algebra with graph-theoretic and simplicial structures in the matrix of the generating Steenrod squares.

papers.title: Permutation Decoding of AG Codes from Curves Defined by Separated Polynomials
papers.authors: Alonso S. Castellanos, Guilherme Tizziotti, Wilson Olaya-Le\'on
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate permutation decoding for algebraic geometry (AG) codes arising from algebraic curves defined by separated polynomials. Using automorphisms of the underlying curves, we construct permutation automorphisms of the associated algebraic geometry codes and exploit the resulting orbit structure to determine information and check positions. We introduce a class of curves, called SAP curves (Separated Additive Polynomial curves), and investigate one-point AG codes defined on them. For these codes, we obtain permutation decoding sets that correct burst errors supported on coordinates associated with rational points sharing a common coordinate. We further identify a subclass of special SAP curves, including Hermitian curves, generalized Hermitian curves, and certain maximal curves, for which additional automorphisms yield more powerful decoding sets.

papers.title: Sliding Methods for H\"older-Smooth Convex--Concave Minimax Optimization with Bilinear Coupling
papers.abstract: We study convex-concave minimax optimization problems with bilinear coupling of the form $\min_{x\in \mathcal X}\max_{y\in \mathcal Y} \; f(x)+\langle y,\mathbf{B}x\rangle-g(y),$ where the functions $f$ and $g$ have H\"older continuous (sub)gradients. This setting covers a broad range of regimes, from nonsmooth problems with bounded subgradient variation to smooth problems with Lipschitz continuous gradients; for a smooth component used in the coupling-induced regularizer, its Lipschitz-gradient constant is assumed to hold in the ambient space. We propose a sliding method that exploits the composite structure of the problem by querying the oracles associated with $f$, $g$, and the bilinear coupling operator at prescribed frequencies determined by their individual properties. The method is based on a recursive sliding scheme for monotone variational inequalities. We establish convergence guarantees under H\"older continuity and show how the resulting complexity bounds depend explicitly on the H\"older exponents, H\"older constants, strong convexity parameters, and spectral properties of the coupling matrix. Our analysis covers nonstrongly convex and partially strongly convex regimes. For stochastic function oracles, we prove componentwise H\"older guarantees with separate variance costs: a uniform expected-gap bound on bounded domains and, when both functions are strongly convex on their feasible sets, a restarted Lyapunov guarantee without an anchor noise floor. Numerical experiments reproduce the predicted H\"older exponents and confirm that the number of gradient evaluations required for each function separates according to its own smoothness level rather than the worse of the two. A tomographic benchmark shows runtime gains when gradient evaluations are more expensive than the additional matrix-vector products.

papers.title: Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature and Edge-Connectivity of Hypergraphs
papers.abstract:
We give a local geometric criterion ensuring that the edge-connectivity of a hypergraph equals its minimum incidence degree: every locally finite connected simple $r$-uniform linear hypergraph with $r\ge3$ and nonnegative Lin--Lu--Yau curvature has this property. Among the various extensions of Ollivier--Ricci curvature to hypergraphs, we work with the equal-edges random walk on hypergraphs \cite{CoupetteEtAl2023}. Moreover, we show that both uniformity and linearity are essential: if either assumption is removed, there exist positively curved hypergraphs for which the gap between minimum incidence degree and edge-connectivity is arbitrarily large.
  For adjacent vertices in any locally finite simple hypergraph, the Ollivier--Ricci idleness function is concave and piecewise affine with at most three affine pieces, and is affine on $[1/2,1]$. In particular, $\kappa_{\LLY}=2\kappa_{1/2}$, which we use to verify positive curvature in the two families of examples.

papers.title: Density of list- and correspondence-critical graphs
papers.abstract:
A graph $G$ is list $k$-critical if $G$ is not $(k-1)$-list-colorable, but every proper subgraph of $G$ is $(k-1)$-list-colorable. In this paper, we study the function $f_{\ell}(n,k)$ denoting the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex list $k$-critical graph, as well as the function $g_{\ell}(k) = \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac 2n f_{\ell}(n,k) - k + 1$. We show that for all $k \geq 4$, every list $k$-critical graph on $n \geq k+2$ vertices has more than $(k-1+\frac 1{28})\frac n2$ edges, which implies that $g_{\ell}(k) \geq \frac{1}{28}$ for all $k \geq 4$. This is the first result showing that $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty} g_{\ell}(k) > 0$. We also show that $g_{\ell}(k) \geq \frac{1}{24}$ for all $k\geq 352$. As a corollary to our result, we obtain the following improvement to Brooks' theorem: For all $d \geq 3$, if $G$ has no $K_{d+1}$ subgraph and has maximum average degree at most $d+\frac 1{28}$, then $G$ is $d$-list-colorable.
  All of our results hold in the setting of correspondence coloring (DP-coloring) as well. As a corollary of our correspondence coloring result, we also show that for each $d \geq 3$, a minimal unsatisfiable anti-functional binary constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) with variable domains of size $d$ has a primal graph whose unique nontrivial component either contains $K_{d+1}$ or has average degree at least $d+\frac 1{28}$.

papers.title: The sharp volume gap for K\"ahler manifolds with positive Ricci curvature
papers.authors: Chi Li, Minghao Miao, Kewei Zhang
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp volume gap estimate: if an $n$-dimensional compact K\"ahler manifold $(X, \omega)$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)\ge (n+1)\omega$ and $X\not\cong \mathbb{P}^n$, then $\mathrm{vol}(X, \omega)\le \frac{2n^n}{(n+1)^n}\mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{P}^n,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})=\frac{2^{n+1} \, \pi^n \, n^n}{(n+1)^n}$. Moreover $\mathrm{vol}(X, \omega)= \frac{2^{n+1} \, \pi^n \, n^n}{(n+1)^n}$ occurs if and only if $(X, \omega)$ is biholomorphically isometric to the K\"ahler-Einstein metric on the quadric hypersurface $Q^n$ or on the product $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We also obtain sharp volume gap estimates for K-semistable toric log Fano pairs.

papers.title: Remarks on refined scissors congruence group and the third homology of $\mathrm{SL}_2$
papers.abstract:
This work revisits the key sufficient conditions on a ring $A$ that guarantee the existence of the exact sequence \[ H_3(\mathrm{SM}_2(A), \mathbb{Z})\to H_3(\mathrm{SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}) \to \mathcal{RB}(A) \to 0 \]
  and of the isomorphism
  \[ H_3(\mathrm{SL}_2(A), \mathrm{SM}_2(A); \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathcal{RP}_1(A). \]
  We show that there are rings which satisfy the relations above but do not satisfy the condition that -1 is an square, for example some rings $\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{m}]$ and finite local rings. In addition, we study the special case of non-dyadic local fields with characteristic not 2, obtaining a refined Bloch-Wigner exact sequence when -1 is not an square.

papers.title: The motivic Selmer scheme of the thrice-punctured line
papers.abstract: Let $X = \mathbb{P}^1 \smallsetminus \{0,1,\infty\}$ be the thrice-punctured line over a ring of $S$-integers $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ in a number field $K$. For any quotient $\pi_1^{\mathrm{mot}}(X,0) \twoheadrightarrow \Pi$ of Deligne--Goncharov's motivic fundamental group there is an associated Selmer scheme which parametrises $\Pi$-torsors with a mixed Tate motive structure. We give several descriptions of the motivic Selmer scheme which make it amenable to computations, using $\mathbb{G}_m$-equivariant cocycles of algebraic groups, Lie algebras, and complete Hopf algebras. We prove that the Selmer scheme is isomorphic to an affine space $\mathbb{A}^N_{\mathbb{Q}}$, and we construct coordinates realising this isomorphism. This is a key ingredient for making the motivic Chabauty--Kim method explicit in a general setting, without restrictions on the base field or the choice of fundamental group quotient.

papers.title: Support $\tau$-tilting posets and Hochschild reconstruction for matrix centralizer algebras
papers.authors: Jiangsheng Hu, Yu-Zhe Liu, Tiwei Zhao
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a field and $A$ the endomorphism algebra of a finite direct sum of cyclic modules over a finite-dimensional commutative local principal ideal $R$-algebra. An explicit central quotient identifies the support $\tau$-tilting poset of $A$ with the weak order on a symmetric group. The center of $A$, together with degree-zero Hochschild homology as a module over the center, recovers the truncated local algebra and the multiset of successive length gaps. Applied to centralizer matrix algebras, these results show that the support $\tau$-tilting poset determines exactly the multiset of distinct-exponent counts of the primary blocks, whereas the center--Hochschild pair recovers their local algebras and gap multisets. Combined with the known classification, this characterizes derived equivalence by isomorphism of these algebra--module pairs. We also establish Morita reconstruction results in the string and gentle classes.

papers.title: Disconnected graphs and extremal bounds for realizable distance orders
papers.authors: Gerardo L. Maldonado, Leonardo Mart\'inez-Sandoval, Miguel Raggi, Edgardo Rold\'an-Pensado
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph together with a total order $\prec$ on its edges. We say that $\prec$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^d$ if there is a placement of the vertices of $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the Euclidean lengths of the edges induce exactly the order $\prec$. Almendra-Hern\'andez and Mart\'inez-Sandoval proved that every total order on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$. We show that the same is not true for the disjoint union of two complete graphs: for every $n\geq 3$ there is a total order on the edges of $K_n\sqcup K_n$ that is not realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$, but is in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. Thus, the realizability of an order on a disconnected graph is not determined by its restrictions to the connected components. We also study the extremal problem of maximizing the number of edges of an $n$-vertex graph all of whose edge-orders are realizable in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and show that for every fixed $d$ this maximum is $dn+o(n)$, with explicit bounds on the error term. On the real line we sharpen these bounds and show that a disjoint union of two cycles is realizable in $\mathbb{R}$ unless both cycles are triangles.

papers.title: Internal Reasoning and Consistency in Reflective Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract:
Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic allowing direct expression of any general-recursive computation. Every RGA term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation, with a proof certificate at each universal quantifier. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, that such a system is powerful enough to carry out its own metamathematics. A fuel-indexed decider of RGA's grounded semantics and checkers for RGA's proofs are compiled primitive-recursive RGA terms. RGA proves internally that its decider never affirms 0 = 1, and that every well-formed term it affirms has an RGA proof accepted by a transparent test. RGA proves that, for each valid RGA proof, its conclusion is true. RGA proves that each grounded-true well-formed term is provable. RGA proves that no proof in either of two decided classes of RGA proofs derives 0 = 1.
  RGA's truth predicate also serves as a medium for proof by reflection, of the kind that adds nothing to the system. RGA derives disquotation for quantifier-free formulas as rules in every context, at a free variable, and proves, as one sentence, that whenever its normalizer for polynomials in one variable gives two terms the same normal form, the equation between them is true at every value of the variable. Each such polynomial identity then follows from that sentence by closed evaluation and disquotation, with no reflection rule. A companion paper proves G\"odel's incompleteness theorems for RGA and its extensions.

papers.title: If the moduli space of metrics is Borel, then it is completely metrizable
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metrizable space. We prove that the space of compatible metrics on $X$ is Borel in the space of continuous pseudometrics, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence, if and only if $X$ is $\sigma$-compact. These conditions are equivalent to complete metrizability of the space of compatible metrics; the same characterization holds for each component. For ultrametrizable $X$ and $R\subseteq[0,\infty)$ containing $0$ and arbitrarily small positive elements, we prove analogous results for compatible $R$-valued ultrametrics and their $R$-components, {with neighborhoods defined by agreement at every point pair where either ultrametric exceeds a positive $\epsilon\in R$}. For the nonempty subspaces of complete compatible metrics and complete compatible $R$-valued ultrametrics, Borelness and complete metrizability are equivalent to compactness of $X$. The proofs use continuous families of metrics parametrized by trees or subsets of compact completions.

papers.title: Isometric embeddings of trees: why 32 leaves can require six dimensions, and bounds for every tree
papers.abstract: We identify the first failure of the $\lceil\log_2 t\rceil$ leaf-count bound for isometric embeddings of $t$-leaf trees under the maximum norm. Every tree with at most $31$ leaves attains the bound, but a $32$-leaf tree requires six dimensions. This answers a question of Fitzpatrick and Nowakowski and disproves a conjecture of Aksoy, K{\i}l{\i}\c{c} and Ko\c{c}ak. We explain this failure by showing how requirements within and between branches force an additional coordinate. For a family of three-branch trees, we prove that the leaf bound is attained exactly when the two larger branches have equal leaf counts; otherwise, one additional coordinate is necessary. We also prove that every tree embeds in $\lceil 1.162832\log_2 t\rceil$ dimensions, improving the coefficient of approximately $1.44042$ established in 2005. These results hold for arbitrary positive edge lengths and the entire metric realization. We also construct infinite families in which the excess persists under repeated leaf expansion. Both main theorems are formalised in Lean using only standard axioms.

papers.title: Squarefree polynomials with missing digits
papers.abstract: We establish an asymptotic formula for squarefree polynomials over a finite field whose coefficients are in $\{0,1\}$. This resolves a function-field analogue of a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s, Mauduit and S\'ark\"ozy. More generally, we estimate the probability of a polynomial $\sum \varepsilon_it^i$ being squarefree, where $\varepsilon_i$ are random variables sampled according to measures on $\mathbb{F}_q$.

papers.title: Non-equivalence of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants
papers.abstract: Suppose $p > 7$ is a prime number, and $F$ is a nonarchimedean local field of residual characteristic $p$ satisfying $F \neq \mathbb{Q}_p$. Generalizing results of Ghate--Le--Sheth, Le--Singh, and Huang, we show that any split, connected, reductive group $G$ over $F$ which is not a torus admits a smooth, irreducible, non-admissible mod $p$ representation. We use this to show that the functor of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants does not induce an equivalence between the category of smooth mod $p$ $G$-representations generated by their pro-$p$-Iwahori invariant vectors and modules over the pro-$p$-Iwahori--Hecke algebra, contrary to what happens for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

papers.title: Orbit equivalence and total weak mixing of free group actions
papers.abstract:
We prove that the orbit equivalence class of every free ergodic probability-measure-preserving (pmp) action of a free group contains a totally weak mixing action. Equivalently, every ergodic treeable pmp equivalence relation of cost $n\in\mathbf{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ is generated by a free totally weak mixing action of $\mathbf{F}_n$. This answers a question of Miller and Tserunyan.
  The proof goes by considering a Polish space of edge slidings along a fixed mixing transformation and proving that for every $w\not=e\in\mathbf{F}_n$ the set of edge slidings that produce an action with $w$ weakly mixing forms a comeager set.

papers.title: Systole Increasing Deformations to Maximal Translation Surfaces
papers.abstract: A unit-area translation surface is called \emph{maximal} if it maximizes the length of its shortest saddle connection among all surfaces in the same stratum. We investigate whether a non-maximal translation surface can be continuously deformed into a maximal one while the systole increases strictly monotonically. Although such deformations do not exist in general due to the presence of local, non-global maxima of the systole function, we explicitly construct them for the family of so-called $2k$-gonal translation surfaces for any fixed $k \ge 2$. Furthermore, we generalize this construction to translation surfaces composed of mixed polygons. Specifically, we prove that any translation surface formed by gluing a combination of coherently aligned regular $2k$-gons with potentially varying values of $k$, provided every polygon side length equals the surface's systole, also admits a continuous, strictly systole-increasing deformation terminating at a maximal surface.

papers.title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
papers.authors: Ehsan Mirafzali, Frank Proske, Razvan Marinescu
papers.abstract: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of R\"ockner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $\Phi_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $\gamma_t = \int_0^t \Phi_r \Phi_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $\Phi_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $\Phi$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}\Phi$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same H\"older triangle of moment exponents.

papers.title: Tilting realizations of derived-equivalent matrix centralizer algebras
papers.authors: Jiangsheng Hu, Xin Ma, Jinbi Zhang, Tiwei Zhao
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a centralizer matrix algebra over an arbitrary field. We prove that a centralizer matrix algebra $B$ is derived equivalent to $A$ if and only if $B\simeq{\rm End}_A(T)^{\rm op}$ for some tilting $A$-module $T$ of projective dimension at most one. We classify the basic tilting $A$-modules and identify their poset with a product of right weak orders on symmetric groups. For a fixed primary block, mutations exchange adjacent entries of the gap word. The isomorphism classes of the resulting opposite endomorphism algebras are parametrized by left cosets of the stabilizer of this word. The quotient of its labeled mutation graph by the stabilizer action is a Schreier multigraph. We also characterize when the right weak-order orientation descends to the nonloop edges of this quotient.

papers.title: Cluster Geometry of Universal Schubert Polynomials I: Geometric Bases and Cluster Monomials
papers.abstract: We study Fulton's universal Schubert polynomials through the cluster structure on the upper unitriangular group and representations of type $A$. The convex hull of the initial tropical vectors of standard-elementary monomials is unimodularly equivalent to a product of simplices, and right-regular multisegments index three integral geometric bases of the standard-elementary module. A recursive prefix-record condition characterizes those universal Schubert polynomials that are homogeneous under diagonal conjugation, coincide with the corresponding generic and dual canonical basis elements, and are extended cluster monomials. On this locus, cover forests give squarefree factorizations into cluster variables. Outside it, the initial Laurent expansion has a coefficient $-1$.

papers.title: The average number of rational preperiodic points of polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: Let $M_d(X)$ denote the average number of rational preperiodic points among degree-$d$ polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$ with vanishing $z^{d-1}$ coefficient, constant term $1$, and height at most $X$. We prove that, for every integer $d\ge2$, $M_d(X) \sim \gamma_d X^{-1}$ for an explicit constant $\gamma_d>0$. For $d\ge4$, the error term is $O_{d,\varepsilon}(X^{-2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; for $d=3$ the error term is $O(X^{-3/2})$; and for $d=2$ the error term is $O(X^{-3/2}\log X)$.

papers.title: Analysis of the Virtual Element Approximation for the Smagorinsky Model
papers.authors: Karol L. Cascavita, Francesca Marcon, Maria Strazzullo
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Smagorinsky model for the Navier-Stokes equations within a virtual element framework. Under the standard assumption of small data, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a solution. Assuming more regularity to the solutions, we derive the known \del{suboptimal} convergence rates $h$, using $k>1$, for the a priori error estimates of the Smagorinsky model in two dimensional domains. We additionally prove that divergence-free virtual discretizations provide improved convergence orders, with weaker regularity assumptions than in the finite element literature. We conclude the paper with numerical results that corroborate the theory.

papers.title: Turing universality, computability, and incompleteness in hypergraph Tur\'an theory
papers.abstract:
The hypergraph Tur\'an problem asks for the maximum asymptotic edge density of hypergraphs avoiding a forbidden family and the structure of near-extremizers. We prove that both encode arbitrary computation. Fix a universal Turing machine $\mathsf{U}$. For each fixed $r\ge3$, there is a rational $\tau_r\in(0,1)$ and an effective map from binary words $\beta$ to finite families $\mathcal{F}_{r,\beta}$ of $r$-graphs such that $\pi(\mathcal{F}_{r,\beta})=\tau_r$ if $\mathsf{U}$ does not halt on $\beta$, and $\pi(\mathcal{F}_{r,\beta})>\tau_r$ otherwise. For $r=3$, a single forbidden $3$-graph $P_\beta$ suffices.
  For all sufficiently large fixed $r$, we construct finite families exhibiting a parallel structural dichotomy. Nonhalting gives a unique extremal limit and edit-distance stability around a fixed finite profile. Halting yields 2 nonempty compact phases with opposite signs of a continuous statistic depending only on $r$; each phase is homeomorphic to the full extremal limit space of $P_\beta$. Hence uniqueness, connectedness, and finite-profile stability are undecidable.
  Our ZFC-verifiable reductions also yield independence results for every consistent computably axiomatized extension of ZFC, even for single forbidden $3$-graphs. We further classify the complexity of exact density comparison, characterize densities attainable by effectively enumerated families, and establish Busy-Beaver growth of minimal witnesses and the absence of computable positive lower bounds on density gaps.

papers.title: Filtrations on D-modules and multiplicities of roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we relate multiplicities of Bernstein--Sato-type polynomials with respect to a function f to several singularity invariants. First, we introduce certain ``mod'' b-functions and show that they characterize the weight filtration on the localization of a simple algebraic holonomic D-module along f, and we provide an algorithm to compute them. Second, we show that they can be approximated by the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions (i.e., the b-functions with respect to powers of f). Furthermore, we give a sharp upper bound for the Hodge level of elements given by a certain sum of such multiplicities. Next, we give an effective asymptotic solution to the Gelfand problem by determining an explicit threshold after which every integer shift of a root of b_f(s) is a pole of the Archimedean zeta function of f. We also show that the order of these poles is equal to the nilpotency index of the logarithmic monodromy operator, which we further express as the limit of the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions. We define several filtrations, relating them to the weight and Hodge filtrations, based upon which we leave some open questions that we address in the affirmative in the case when f has a homogeneous isolated singularity, or it is a hyperplane arrangement, or a semi-invariant on a spherical variety. We give several immediate applications to our results, including a solution to a question of Torrelli on whether 1/f lies in the intersection complex of the hypersurface of f if and only if -1 is a simple root of b_f(s).

papers.title: On the topological dynamical system of tilings
papers.abstract: Tilings can be studied from the perspective of dynamical systems and ergodic theory. Some fundamental features of tiling spaces as topological dynamical systems, such as the continuity of the action by translation, the compactness with the tiling metric, and the minimality of the system generated by a repetitive tiling, are among the most frequently mentioned basic facts in the dynamical theory of aperiodic order. Nonetheless, despite their classical status, complete proofs of these facts, together with the preliminary material they rely on, to the best of our knowledge, are not available in the literature. The purpose of this survey is to give a self-contained, rigorous, and pedagogical treatment of these foundations with detailed preliminary material. We hope that this exposition will provide a useful reference and contribute to a clearer and more accessible understanding of the fundamentals of the theory of tiling dynamical systems.

papers.title: Cotorsion pairs and model structures induced by resolution dimensions relative to Frobenius pairs
papers.abstract: We explore some methods to obtain cotorsion pairs and model category structures from a Frobenius pair. Specifically, we consider a type of Frobenius pair $(\mathcal{X},\omega)$ in an abelian category $\mathfrak{C}$ for which there exists a nonnegative integer $m$ such that every object in the right orthogonal complement $\mathcal{X}^{\perp_1}$ of $\mathcal{X}$ under $\text{Ext}^1_{\mathfrak{C}}(-,\sim)$ has a special $\omega^\wedge_m$-precover and a special $[\omega^\wedge_m]^{\perp_1}$-preenvelope, where $\omega^\wedge_m$ denotes the class of objects in $\mathfrak{C}$ with resolution dimension relative to $\omega$ at most $m$. The cotorsion pairs and model structures obtained from these Frobenius pairs will involve the classes $\mathcal{X}$, $\omega$, $\mathcal{X}^\wedge_m$, $\omega^\wedge_m$, and their orthogonal complements, in the description of its cofibrant, fibrant and trivial objects. As applications of our results, we obtain several cotorsion pairs and model structures related to relative and absolute Gorenstein homological dimensions.

papers.title: The linear scale in metric cotype for Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Eskenazis, Mendel, and Naor by proving that the optimal universal scaling parameter in metric cotype $2$ for complete Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature has order $n$. The upper bound follows from a dyadic application of the Lang--Schroeder inequality, and the lower bound follows from snowflake universality of $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on the Number of Small Cuts
papers.abstract: A $k$-cut of an undirected graph is a minimal edge set whose removal leaves at least $k$ connected components, and its cost is the sum of its edge costs. Write $\lambda_k$ for the minimum cost of a $k$-cut. For fixed $k\ge2$ and $\alpha\ge1$, we show that in any $n$-vertex graph with $n\ge k$ and nonnegative edge costs, the number of $k$-cuts of cost strictly below $\alpha\lambda_k$ is $O(n^{\lceil\alpha k\rceil-1})$. This implies an $O(n^{\lfloor\alpha k\rfloor})$ bound for $k$-cuts of cost at most $\alpha\lambda_k$, sharpening the $O(n^{\alpha k})$ bound of Gupta, Harris, Lee and Li. For $k=2$, our strict bound resolves a conjecture of Henzinger and Williamson and an open question of Karger. The exponent $\lceil\alpha k\rceil-1$ is optimal for $k$-cuts for every $k\ge2$ and $\alpha>1$.

papers.title: Compact totally separated types
papers.abstract: Perhaps surprisingly, there are infinite types that can be exhaustively searched mechanically in finite time. We use ideas from topology to build plenty of them, referring to searchable types as compact types, and we use ordinals to measure their logical complexity. We consider two systems of ordinal notations under which a single notation denotes both a discrete ordinal and a compact one, with an embedding of the former into the latter whose image has empty complement. A boolean valued function decides which points in the image of the embedding are isolated and which are topological limit points. The first system consists of the traditional Brouwer codes and the second is an inductive-recursive universe generalizing them. The discrete ordinals so obtained are trichotomous, and the compact ones have the least element property for complemented subsets, but these two desirable properties cannot be fulfilled simultaneously in a constructive setting. The compact ordinals obtained from Brouwer codes further enjoy a boolean Leibniz principle, which has the notion of total separatedness as its topological counterpart. This extends previous work from G\"odel's system T to intensional Martin-L\"of type theory with univalent universes, and is formalized in Agda in the TypeTopology repository.

papers.title: Fence Posets, Good Gradings and Frobenius Maximal Parabolics
papers.authors: Anthony Giaquinto, John Irving, Aaron Lauve, Mitja Mastnak
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak L$ be a Frobenius maximal parabolic subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. For any $F\in\mathfrak L^*$ for which the Kirillov form $B_F(x,y)=F([x,y])$ is non-degenerate, let $\widehat F$ denote the associated principal element. We prove that the multiplicities of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}_{\widehat F}$ on $\mathfrak L$ form a unimodal sequence symmetric about $\frac12$. We also prove that the multiplicities of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}_{\widehat F}$ on $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ form a unimodal sequence symmetric about $0$. The proof relates the ranked meander associated to $\mathfrak L$ to the order ideals of a related fence poset through Panyushev reduction. The known unimodality of the rank polynomial of the fence poset implies that of the meander, which in turn determines a good grading of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the sense of Elashvili and Kac. We prove that this grading coincides with that induced by the principal element and that the pyramid associated to this grading may be filled in such a way that its good element $e$ lies in $\mathfrak L$. The two unimodality results then follow from the injectivity properties of $\operatorname{ad}_e$ coming from the good grading and the duality induced by the bilinear form $B_F$.

papers.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem an extension of Green Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design (GSCND)[Olfat, L., e. a. (2022), Sreyneath, C. (2021)]. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem CFLP and is known to be NP-hard [Garey, M. R. and Johnson, D. S. (1979)]. This paper formally specifies the decision variables objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming ILP formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP (B) three Fully Polynomial Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing $1+\epsilon$ approximate solutions for $\epsilon := 0.15$ and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers the exact solver certifies the optimal sampled supported solutions across eight weight combinations while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

papers.title: Minimum central circles: an effective characterization of the global asymptotic constant
papers.abstract:
Let $R^\ast(n)$ be the minimum radius of a central circle externally tangent to nonoverlapping circles of radii $1,\ldots,n$. We prove that $R^\ast(n)=C_\ast n^2+o(n^2)$ and give finite linear programs that enclose $C_\ast$ with prescribed error.
  An exact angular comparison reduces the problem to marked points on a line with separation at least the geometric mean of each pair of marks. Concatenation with bounded joining cost and reassignment to the prescribed normalized radii prove existence of the limit. Balanced finite-word programs give a bracket of width $(1/k+1/r)/\pi$, before directed arithmetic error, using $k$ types and words of length $r$.
  We also obtain explicit geometric bounds. For the upper bound, we recover finite and countable reflected-block constructions by actual permutations, retaining all pair constraints. A coupled terminal-subset argument gives an explicit lower bound strictly above $1/8$. Together these give $C_{\rm term}+\eta_{\rm width}\le C_\ast\le U_4$. The lower endpoint comes from the terminal-subset argument, and the upper endpoint from the four-block construction; neither is asserted sharp.
  The finite-word scheme establishes computability; efficient high-precision evaluation and the structure of global optimizers remain open.

papers.title: Poisson problem with Hardy operator on lattice graph $ \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the application to semilinear equations
papers.authors: Huyuan Chen, Bobo Hua, Wendi Xu
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we investigate the analytic properties of the Hardy-type operator $-\Delta + \mu H_0$ on the $d$-dimensional integer lattice graph $\mathbb{Z}^d$, where $\mu \geq -1$ and $H_0$ is a critical Hardy potential at infinity--arising naturally from discrete Hardy inequalities. We derive sharp fixed-pole Green kernel estimates on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and obtain a necessary and sufficient weighted summability condition characterizing the solvability of the nonnegative Poisson problem associated with this operator.
  Building upon this classification, we provide a complete characterization of the nonexistence of positive solutions to the semilinear elliptic inequality
  $$
  -\Delta u + \mu H_0 u \geq W u^p \quad \text{in } \mathbb{Z}^d,
  $$
  where $p > 0$, $d \geq 3$, $\mu \geq -1$, and $H_0, W \in C(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ are strictly positive potentials satisfying the asymptotic behaviors $H_0(x) \sim |x|^{-2}$ and $W(x) \sim |x|^{\theta}$ as $|x| \to \infty$, with $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$.

papers.title: Orthonormal bases of spherical harmonics with maximal Lp norm growth
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for every p>2, there is an orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics on the n-dimensional unit sphere which achieves the maximal Lp norm growth. More precisely, one basis achieves this growth for p up to the critical exponent 2(n+1)/(n-1), and another for p from the critical exponent up to infinity. The first basis is built from rotations of the real part of a highest weight spherical harmonic. The second is built from zonal harmonics whose poles are selected from a spherical design. In both cases, the selection uses the restricted invertibility theorem of Bourgain and Tzafriri. This extends earlier results of Bourgain and of the author (arXiv:1404.5016) on the 2-dimensional sphere for 2<p<=6 to all dimensions and all p>2, and improves the positive density subsequence there to a whole basis.

papers.title: Subset-Sum Density Realization in Locally Finite Abelian Groups
papers.authors: Norbert Hegyv\'ari, Thang Pham, Boqing Xue
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a countable locally finite abelian group, and let \[ G_1\leq G_2\leq\cdots, \qquad \bigcup_{i\geq1}G_i=G, \] be any filtration of $G$ by finite subgroups. For $A\subseteq G$, let $\mathcal P(A)$ denote the set of all finite subset sums of elements of $A$, and let $2G:=\{2g:g\in G\}$. We prove that $|2G|=\infty$ if and only if for every filtration and every interval $[\alpha,\beta]\subseteq[0,1]$, there exists $A\subseteq G$ such that the set of limit points of \[ \left( \frac{|\mathcal P(A)\cap G_i|}{|G_i|} \right)_{i\geq1} \] is exactly $[\alpha,\beta]$. We also prove a positive-density result that does not require $|2G|=\infty$: if $G$ is infinite and $\mathcal P(A)$ has positive upper density along the given filtration, then there is an infinite set $B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$ such that $B+B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$. Combining this with the realization theorem, we show that, when $|2G|=\infty$, every interval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $0\leq\alpha\leq\beta\leq1$ and $\beta>0$ can be realized by a set $A$ with this additional property.

papers.title: The stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb{R}^{7}$
papers.authors: Han Hong, Haizhong Li, Gaoming Wang
papers.abstract: We give a Green-function proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb R^7$ for smooth, connected, complete, two-sided stable minimal hypersurfaces, thus resolving the last case of the stable Bernstein problem.

papers.title: The Strong Naor--Schechtman Convolution Inequality on the Product of Cyclic Groups
papers.authors: Yong Jiao, Sijie Luo, Dmitriy Zanin, Dejian Zhou
papers.abstract: In this paper, we resolve the convolution inequality problem posed by Naor and Schechtman in \cite[Question 6.1]{N-S2016} (see also \cite{Na2016}). More precisely, we establish the following strong convolution inequality on products of finite cyclic groups: For each $1\leq p<\infty$ there exists $c_{p}>0$ such that for every $n$, $m\in \mathbb{N}$ the following holds \[ \begin{split} &\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x+\varepsilon)-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x-\varepsilon)\right|^{p}\\ \leq& c^{p}_{p}\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|\varepsilon_{j}\left[E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x+e_{j})-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x-e_{j})\right]\right|^{p}, \end{split} \] $E_{A}f(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{\delta\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}f\left(x+\sum_{j\in A}\delta_{j}e_{j}\right)$ for every $A\subseteq \{1,\cdots,n\}$. The growth order we obtain here $c_{p}=O(p)$ as $p\to \infty$. For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.

papers.title: Multiscale and stability analysis of an Aw-Rascle-Zhang-type model with driver-dependent acceleration
papers.abstract: We introduce a new traffic flow model. The main idea is to describe acceleration effects in the Aw-Rascle-Zhang model through an additional driver-dependent equation, thereby allowing individual driver characteristics to evolve dynamically rather than being prescribed solely by the traffic density. The resulting system provides a hyperbolic description of traffic dynamics and admits an explicit analysis of its characteristic structure, Riemann problem, and entropy properties. To investigate the stability of the proposed model, we perform a Chapman-Enskog expansion up to second order and derive the corresponding diffusive and higher-order corrections. This analysis reveals how the stability properties depend on the underlying velocity and pressure functions. Several examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: On $t$-sumfree sequences
papers.abstract: In this paper we explore the world of $t$-sumfree sequences, primarily for $t=2$ and $t=3$. Starting with $t$ increasing positive integers, build an infinite sequence by choosing as the next entry the least positive integer that is not the sum of $t$ distinct previous values. The main open problem concerns the question of the conjectured ultimate periodicity of these sequences. We formulate a sufficient condition to prove that a conjectured preperiod and period are correct. We also prove periodicity for a considerable subclass of 2-sumfree and of 3-sumfree sequences. Finally, we present the results of extensive computations on 3-sumfree sequences.

papers.title: Sufficient conditions for multiplicity and uniqueness of positive solutions of the H\'enon equation
papers.abstract: We establish explicit sufficient conditions for multiplicity of positive solutions of the H\'enon equation in the unit ball and for uniqueness in one dimension. In the Sobolev-subcritical range, a spherical harmonic function argument shows that the radial solution has Morse index greater than one and therefore differs from a ground state. In even dimensions, a degree-four perturbation in a symmetry and monotonicity cone yields a sufficient condition for nonradiality in the supercritical range. The one-dimensional uniqueness criterion follows from a comparison of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues and a concavity estimate.

papers.title: Koszul Duality for Symmetric Algebras and Derived Loop Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove Koszul duality for symmetric algebras of connective complexes consisting of locally free sheaves of finite rank, which is not necessarily bounded below. As an application, we construct an equivalence between derived categories of derived loop spaces and the symmetric algebra of the tangent complex for arbitrary separated schemes of finite type over a field $k$ of characteristic zero. This can be regarded as a generalization of the classical duality between derived loop spaces and cotangent bundles by Kapranov in the smooth cases. We also give a geometrical interpretation of our equivalence in terms of derived formal stacks.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels--Part I: $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: We study the {\epsilon}-capacity regions of mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with general mixture and cost constraints by the information spectrum method. The starting point is a general formula for the {\epsilon}-capacity region of general MACs with cost constraint, together with the random-coding and converse lemmas from which it is derived. For the quasi-static fading Gaussian MAC, with random fading coefficients and noise variance, we show that the {\epsilon}-capacity region is the {\epsilon}-outage capacity region, which gives the latter a Shannon-theoretic operational meaning. The direct part follows from the general formula, and the converse part from the strong converse property of the Gaussian MAC, which is stronger than the {\epsilon}-strong converse, applied to each component. The {\epsilon}-capacity regions coincide in all four scenarios of availability of channel state information (CSI), and the results extend to K users. With CSI at both terminals, variable-rate coding enlarges the 0-capacity region to the polymatroid whose rank function is the average of those of the components. For mixed MACs with general components and a countable parameter space, CSI at the receiver alone never enlarges the {\epsilon}-capacity region, and the region with CSI at the transmitters is given by an information spectrum formula; unlike the Gaussian case, the regions with and without CSI at the transmitters may differ. For uncountable parameter spaces, only the formula for the region with CSI at both terminals survives in general. Parts II and III treat finite-alphabet mixed MACs and the strong converse for the K-user Gaussian MAC, respectively.

papers.title: Infinitesimmaly homogeneous manifolds with symplectic and almost contact structure groups
papers.authors: Carlos Alberto Mar\'in Arango, Alejandro Pinilla Barrera
papers.abstract: We study infinitesimally homogeneous affine manifolds with prescribed structure groups. First, for the real symplectic group $\operatorname{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, we prove that the corresponding infinitesimally homogeneous structures are precisely flat torsion-free symplectic affine structures. Second, for \(\operatorname{U}(n)\times\{1\}\), whose \(G\)-structures are equivalent to almost contact metric data, we classify the torsion-free characteristic tensors and obtain the general torsional case by invariant deformation. The admissible torsion and inner-torsion parameters are governed by a single algebraic relation, and the horizontal distribution is contact precisely when a certain combination of these parameters does not vanish. We also describe the compatible connections and relate the torsion-free branches to trans-Sasakian geometry.

papers.title: Backward log orthogonal functions and their approximation theory
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of backward logarithmic orthogonal functions and generalized backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, constructed by applying a terminal-endpoint logarithmic mapping to generalized Laguerre polynomials. These functions are designed for backward spectral approximations of problems whose solutions exhibit weak singularities at the terminal endpoint. The proposed basis functions generate non-polynomial weighted approximation spaces with nodes naturally clustered near the singular endpoint, and therefore provide an effective framework for resolving algebraic and logarithmic endpoint singularities. We develop the basic approximation theory for these backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, including recurrence relations, derivative formulas, orthogonality, Sturm--Liouville characterization, mapped Laguerre--Gauss quadrature rules, weighted projection estimates, backward Lagrange interpolation estimates, inverse inequalities, and stability properties in weighted Sobolev-type spaces defined through a terminal logarithmic pseudo-derivative. A generalized version of the basis is also introduced by incorporating an algebraic scaling parameter, which improves the flexibility of the approximation space and allows singular factors to be represented more effectively. The error analysis and numerical results show that the proposed backward logarithmic basis is particularly suitable for weakly regular functions with terminal-endpoint singularities and can recover exponential or high-order convergence rates that are typically lost when usual polynomial approximations are applied directly.

papers.title: On normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
papers.abstract: We study real-analytic planar maps, that admit a real-analytic first integral with a non-degenerate extremum, in a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We prove that, if the map preserves an analytic area form, it is real-analytically and symplectically conjugate to a twist map, both in the resonant and in the non-resonant case. Using an example, we show that without the area-preservation assumption the conclusion fails. We then prove that a second, continuous, first integral is either a function of the first one or forces the map to be periodic, in which case the map is analytically (and, when area-preserving, symplectically) conjugate to its linear part. We illustrate our results, we study the McMillan map, and a planar map obtained from the Adler--Yamilov Yang--Baxter map.

papers.title: Maximal singular curves over finite fields from elliptic and hyperelliptic curves
papers.authors: Cesar Hilario, Rodrigo Salom\~ao, Renato Vidal Martins
papers.abstract: We construct explicit families of maximal singular curves over finite fields. A maximal singular curve is a curve that attains the Aubry-Perret bound, which is the natural extension of the Hasse-Weil-Serre bound on the maximum number of rational points on a smooth curve over a finite field. Starting from a smooth elliptic or hyperelliptic curve $\tilde{C}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ ($q$ odd), we generate singular curves $C$ with non-split singularities or cusps. In our approach we use linear projections of geometric embeddings, and we apply St\"ohr's embedding of hyperelliptic Gorenstein curves and the Rosa-St\"ohr's theory of trigonal Gorenstein curves. Some of our models attain the Aubry-Perret bound, whenever their normalization is maximal, and the construction is applied to the Tafazolian and Tafazolian-Torres smooth maximal curves to produce the desired family. Finally, we determine the gonality over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of most of the curves we construct.

papers.title: Conformal Killing--Yano Ricci solitons: Basic structure and first examples
papers.authors: Mohammadjavad Habibivostakolaei, Abbas M. Sherif, Yen-Kheng Lim
papers.abstract: We introduce a conformal Killing-Yano Ricci soliton, coupling conformal Ricci soliton geometry to conformal Killing-Yano 2-forms via the divergence of the form. In four-dimensional Lorentzian signature, the principal conformal structure is not preserved under non-trivial conformal deformation, so the associated form on local Kerr-NUT-(A)dS backgrounds is not closed. For Einstein backgrounds in any dimension and signature, integrability forces the form to be Killing for the background and conformal Killing for the necessarily Einstein soliton metric, with the conformal factor satisfying eigenvalue and Obata-type Hessian equations; the coupling fixes the Einstein constant. Vanishing coupling reduces the data to Killing data on the fiber; otherwise the soliton metric is Ricci-flat. Locally the background is a warped product. In the compact Riemannian case, the manifold is the round sphere. Explicit static spherically symmetric and BTZ constructions are given, with applications to exact geometries in general relativity.

papers.title: Grothendieck rings of strictly weakly integral fusion categories of rank six
papers.authors: Kai Wang, Jingcheng Dong, Libin Li
papers.abstract: We classify, up to based-ring isomorphism, the Grothendieck rings of strictly weakly integral fusion categories of rank six over $\mathbb C$. The dimension grading and the classification of integral Grothendieck rings of rank at most five reduce the problem to twelve candidate fusion rings. We exclude four of them using the twist trace and the induction pairing in the Drinfeld center. The remaining eight admit known categorifications. In particular, every such category has commutative Grothendieck ring and Frobenius--Perron dimension in $\{8,10,16,20\}$.

papers.title: Noncommutative Maximal Ergodic Theorems for Modulated $(C,\alpha)$-Averages with Operator-Valued Weights
papers.authors: Arup Chattopadhyay, Debabrata De, Disha Shaw
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study modulated $(C,\alpha)$-ergodic averages with operator-valued weights and their subsequential versions in the setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras. Our framework combines $(C,\alpha)$-type modulation with operator-valued weights and extends both scalar-weighted and operator-valued weighted ergodic theories. We establish mean ergodic theorems and maximal inequalities for these averages on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We then study bilateral almost uniform and almost uniform convergence in noncommutative Orlicz spaces, including convergence along subsequences of density one when $\alpha\geq 1$. A key ingredient in our approach is the introduction of the $p$-convexity condition on the underlying Orlicz function. This condition allows us to transfer appropriate maximal estimates from noncommutative $L_p$-spaces to establish bilateral uniform equicontinuity in measure at zero on the corresponding noncommutative $p$-convex Orlicz spaces. Together with the noncommutative Banach principle, this yields the desired pointwise convergence results. As an additional consequence of our $p$-convexity argument, we extend Rota theorem to a larger class of noncommutative Orlicz spaces associated with the $p$-convex Orlicz functions considered in this article.

papers.title: Benign Geometry and Distributional Robustness of $\mathcal{H}_2$ Synthesis
papers.authors: Arman Sharifi Kolarijani, Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani, Tam\'{a}s Keviczky, Mohamad Amin Sharifi Kolarijani
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study standard and distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem of a stabilizing state-feedback controller for discrete-time linear time-invariant systems. Without requiring a nonsingular disturbance controllability Gramian or a positive-definite control penalty, we establish that stationarity of a stabilizing gain in standard $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis is equivalent to global optimality and derive an exact Pythagorean identity for the performance difference. We then generalize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem by considering i.i.d. disturbances with zero mean and uniformly bounded second moments, and extend the stationarity-optimality equivalence to the corresponding distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis. Moreover, we show that every standard $\mathcal{H}_2$-optimal gain is simultaneously optimal for every such distributionally robust problem. Finally, we specialize the framework to Frobenius, Kullback--Leibler, and Wasserstein-2 ambiguity sets and obtain explicit characterizations of their worst-case covariances, which, in turn, provide performance certificates for a common optimal controller.

papers.title: Numerical Realization of an Entropy-Based Selection Principle in the Example of Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend numerical schemes based on parameterized Young measures and linear programming to two space dimensions and apply them to the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability governed by the two-dimensional Euler equations of gas dynamics. We construct first-, second-, third-, fifth-, seventh-, and ninth-order Young-measure schemes and compare them with corresponding standard local Lax-Friedrichs (LLF) flux-splitting schemes and LLF schemes equipped with an entropy-based local characteristic decomposition (LLF-ELCD). We examine instantaneous and time-averaged density profiles, cumulative averages across spatial reconstruction orders, regional empirical density distributions, averaged density marginals, and several selection criteria for dissipative weak solutions. The numerical results reveal scheme-dependent flow patterns, particularly in the small-scale structures generated during the roll-up of the shear layers. At every reconstruction order considered, the Young-measure schemes yield the largest time-averaged physical entropy. By contrast, the LLF-ELCD schemes do not systematically yield larger entropy than the standard LLF schemes and therefore do not constitute a consistent maximum-entropy selection mechanism. The averaged density marginals of the Young measures are concentrated on several neighboring density states, and the later cumulative averages are closer for all Young-measure schemes. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the two-dimensional Young-measure formulation and show that the objective function in the linear-programming problem can act as an effective selection mechanism. The observed entropy preference is consistent with the local optimization of the expected physical entropy. It cannot be reproduced by merely incorporating entropy into a conventional numerical construction.

papers.title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequalities via Curvature
papers.authors: Zejia Chen, Zongchen Chen, Xinyuan Zhang
papers.abstract: Isoperimetric inequalities on the Boolean hypercube play a fundamental role in the analysis of Boolean functions. These inequalities have been established primarily for the uniform measure and for biased product measures, often through Fourier-analytic or inductive arguments. We develop a curvature-based semigroup framework to establish isoperimetric inequalities for measures with weakly dependent coordinates. In particular, we show that a Dobrushin-type condition, together with marginal boundedness of the distribution, implies the local Bobkov inequality, Talagrand's $L^1$--$L^2$ and variance--surface-area inequalities, the Kahn--Kalai--Linial inequality, and the Eldan--Gross inequality. Our results apply to zero-field Ising models with interaction matrix $J$ throughout the Dobrushin uniqueness regime $\|J\|_1<1$. The framework builds on discrete Bakry--\'Emery theory and gradient estimates and can also be extended to measures on Hamming slices or hypergrids.

papers.title: The existence and uniqueness of magic-faced hypercubes, and applications to Khajuraho most-perfect magic squares, cubes, and hypercubes
papers.abstract:
A $\textit{magic-lined hypercube}$ (or, simply, $\textit{magic hypercube}$) of order $k$ and dimension $n$ is an arrangement of the numbers $1,\dots,k^n$ in a $k\times\cdots\times k$ ($n$-fold) grid such that every line of $k$ numbers parallel to a coordinate axis has the same magic sum. While such hypercubes exist for every order $k\ge 3$ and every dimension $n$, no magic-lined hypercube of order $2$ exists in any dimension $n\ge 2$.
  For hypercubes of order $2$, we thus relax the magic condition from lines to two-dimensional faces or planes. We call an arrangement of the numbers $1,\dots,2^n$ in a $2\times\cdots\times2$ ($n$-fold) grid \emph{magic-faced} if every $2\times2$ face has the same magic sum. We prove that a magic-faced hypercube of order $2$ exists in every dimension $n\ge0$, and that it is unique up to a certain natural set of transformations of size $2^n(n+1)!$ when $n$ is even and $2^n n\cdot n!$ when $n$ is odd.
  As an application, we recover and generalize the classical $4\times4$ Khajuraho magic square, give a new, conceptual answer to a question of Coxeter on the group acting on the $384$ ``most-perfect" $4\times4$ magic squares, and extend the picture to higher dimensions. In particular, we prove that, in dimension $n$, these most-perfect hypercubes form a single orbit under a certain natural action of the Weyl group $W(B_{2n})$.

papers.title: Degenerations of chain complexes
papers.abstract: We study degenerations of orbits in varieties of chain complexes of projective modules. We show that degenerations are characterized in terms of certain admissible short exact sequences in the exact category of complexes of projectives, analogously to work from Riedtmann and Zwara. We then extend our study to the homotopy category. In this context, complexes of projectives with a given $g$-vector form an ind-variety, and we prove that degenerations of orbits are characterized by the existence of certain distinguished triangles in the category. This links to the algebraic definition of degeneration for triangulated categories introduced by Jensen, Su and Zimmermann.

papers.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of Speed Monotonicity for the Biased Random Walk on a Galton-Watson Tree Beyond the Known Range
papers.abstract: The speed $v(\lambda)$ of the $\lambda$-biased random walk on a supercritical Galton--Watson tree without leaves is conjectured to be nonincreasing on $[0,m)$, where $m$ is the mean offspring. For non-constant offspring, monotonicity is known only for small bias: $\lambda\le 1/1160$, $\lambda\le 1/2$, and, when every vertex has at least $m_1\ge 2$ children, $\lambda\le m_1/(1+\sqrt{1-1/m_1})$. For offspring uniform on $\{2,3\}$ ($m=2.5$) the last bound is $2/(1+\sqrt{1/2})\approx1.1716$. We prove, with computer assistance, that $v$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1.755]$ for this law. The proof has three parts. A\"id\'ekon's speed formula gives $v=(R-\lambda)/(R+\lambda)$ for an explicit functional $R$, so $v$ decreases exactly when $R/\lambda$ does; we compare $R/\lambda$ at two biases directly, which avoids differentiating the conductance.
