papers.abstract: Fast and accurate classical simulation of quantum systems is a central challenge in the design and control of quantum computers, but the highly oscillatory dynamics of these systems severely limit the efficiency of standard numerical methods. To address this, we adapt Filon quadrature for oscillatory integrals into two numerical methods, called Filon and Controlled Filon, for solving linear systems of ODEs with highly oscillatory solutions. We tailor both methods for efficient implementation in controlled quantum systems, and the Controlled Filon method additionally accounts for the oscillatory structure of the control pulses. We show by numerical experiments that these methods significantly reduce the computational cost of accurately simulating systems of superconducting transmon qubits by decreasing the number of timesteps needed to reach a given level of precision, with only a modest increase in the cost per timestep. For a realistic simulation of the dynamics of a CNOT gate, the Controlled Filon method is the most efficient method tested at every target accuracy, outperforming the best Hermite method by up to 6x and the Hermite method of the same order by up to 500x.

papers.title: Semantic-Aware Task Clustering for Constructive and Cooperative Multi-Tasking
papers.authors: Ahmad Halimi Razlighi, Maximilian H. V. Tillmann, Edgar Beck, Bho Matthiesen, Armin Dekorsy
papers.abstract: Cooperative multi-task semantic communication (CMT-SemCom) improves task execution performance by leveraging shared representations. However, as we demonstrated in [1], cooperative multi-tasking can be either constructive or destructive, depending on the semantic relationships among tasks. To ensure constructive cooperation, we propose a semantic-aware task clustering method for CMT-SemCom. We have formulated a sequential multi-stage optimization problem in which semantically aligned tasks are clustered once after a short initial training phase, and then end-to-end (E2E) joint training is conducted exclusively within the discovered groups. Specifically, the problem decomposes into two stages: (i) a semantic clustering problem leveraging hierarchical density-based spatial clustering, and (ii) an intra-cluster E2E CMT-SemCom learning problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates destructive cooperation and negative transfer, yielding accuracy gains compared to unclustered multi-tasking and individual training baselines.

papers.title: Joint Communication-Control Strategy Optimization with Partially Nested Information Structures: The Linear-Quadratic Case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formalize a joint communication-control strategy optimization (JCCO) problem in multi-agent linear systems with quadratic costs, under the common-information-based (CIB) framework from decentralized stochastic control. For computational tractability, we focus on such JCCO problems with partially nested (PN) information structures (ISs). In particular, with a baseline communication protocol that leads to a PN IS, we establish a series of conditions under which the partial nestedness is preserved under the (additional) communication strategies to be optimized, while violating them may cause nonlinearity or non-existence of the optimal control strategies, with open-loop communication strategies. Under these conditions, we then develop a dynamic-programming-based approach to compute the optimal control strategies of JCCO with open-loop communication strategies, which yields a set of closed-form Riccati Equations. As a byproduct of independent interest, such an approach also offers a new way to solve decentralized linear-quadratic control with PN ISs and output feedback, under the CIB framework and the aforementioned conditions. Finally, we extend such an approach to JCCOs with closed-loop communication strategies, yielding a more tractable dynamic program than an infinite-dimensional CIB-belief-based one.

papers.title: How much averaged null energy must an anisotropic bounce violate?
papers.abstract: We show that in Einstein gravity a null-complete, non-static Bianchi I universe (homogeneous, spatially flat and anisotropic) violates the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along every complete light ray outside at most four null directions, and along all of them if its total energy density, cosmological constant included, is ever positive. Along each complete ray the averaged null energy is at most $-J_p/(8\pi G)$, with equality whenever the integral converges, where $J_p$ is the squared expansion and shear accumulated by a thin bundle of light rays. With spatial sections $\mathbb{R}^3$ the achronal ANEC therefore leaves only Minkowski space, as for flat and open Friedmann models. Under the pointwise null energy condition, every null geodesic of a non-static Bianchi I universe is incomplete. The isotropic bounce of effective loop quantum cosmology has $J_p=1.478\,\omega_B H_{\max}$ (light frequency at the bounce times largest Hubble rate), and at the same critical density the cheapest ray of a strongly anisotropic bounce pays four to five times as much. A Casimir-supported turning point on a three-torus has a deficit of the same order, but at Hubble rates well below the Planck scale its light rays circumnavigate the torus and are not achronal, so the achronal ANEC does not apply to them.

papers.title: The microscope is the mask: privileged views and labels from a cryo-ET forward model
papers.authors: Bogdan Toader, Kiarash Jamali, Tanmay A. M. Bharat, Sjors H. W. Scheres
papers.abstract: We explore the use of simulated data for training a model for protein annotation in crowded cryo-electron tomography volumes reconstructed from images collected at limited tilt angles and severely corrupted by the measurement operator. Firstly, we leverage the corruptions imposed by the forward model to generate domain-specific augmented paired views of the exact same scene for an invariance objective integrated into the LeJEPA self-supervised training framework. Secondly, we use additional information from the simulation pipeline such as the positions and identity of proteins in the simulated volumes to inform the architecture of the model and the loss function, so that semantic information is localised at protein positions in the resulting dense feature volume. The resulting model, CARNIVAL, is evaluated without finetuning on classification and detection tasks in real tomograms, using a benchmark dataset containing multiple protein types and two tomogram processing types. We show that CARNIVAL outperforms a state-of-the-art model trained using a contrastive objective on simulated data but without forward model-based paired views or privileged information.

papers.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant. In four spacetime dimensions, the standard AdS-invariant boundary conditions set the rescaled magnetic field to zero for electromagnetism and the rescaled magnetic Weyl tensor to zero for Einstein gravity on the conformal boundary. We generalize these standard boundary conditions by setting arbitrary linear combinations of the electric and magnetic fields, or the corresponding Weyl tensors, to zero, and we conjecture that these exhaust the local, AdS-invariant, conservative boundary conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$. Boundary conditions with non-AdS-invariance and in different spacetime dimensions are also studied. The AdS-invariant conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$ extend to Yang-Mills theory and nonlinear gravity in a general Fefferman-Graham setting. We construct phase spaces for these general boundary conditions. The covariant phase spaces for general conditions are naturally associated with Lagrangians containing Pontryagin terms and, in gravity, a Gauss-Bonnet term. In gravity, except for the standard boundary condition, no nontrivial asymptotic symmetries exist and all conserved charges such as ADM mass vanish identically, as in a closed universe. Spacetimes with Killing fields including AdS then exhibit linearization instability in the sense of Fischer and Marsden and Moncrief. For nonstandard boundary conditions, the modified symplectic structure yields new expressions for the entropy formula of black holes.

papers.title: Learning to Solve Stochastic Controls with Unknown Drifts and Running Rewards: Theory, Algorithms and Convergence
papers.authors: Jin Ma, Gaozhan Wang, Jianfeng Zhang, Xunyu Zhou
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time and possibly high-dimensional stochastic control problems where drift coefficients and running reward functions are unknown. Due to these missing model primitives, we take the exploratory, reinforcement learning (RL) framework of Wang, Zariphopoulou, and Zhou(2020) with relaxed controls and entropy regularization. The objective is to develop theoretically grounded, efficient and scalable RL algorithms to learn both the optimal value functions (which also solve the exploratory HJB equation) and optimal exploratory feedback control policies. When the diffusion coefficients do not contain control, we employ probabilistic representations of both the optimal value function and its gradient based on an auxiliary state process depending only on the diffusion part of the original dynamics. With a delicate analysis on some properly defined mappings and their fixed points, this leads to the introduction of our policy iteration algorithms and their convergence. We demonstrate the performance of our algorithms through various numerical examples. Finally, we study a special control-dependent diffusion case where probability representation of the Hessian is called for.

papers.title: A complete classification of the existence of finite-dimensional quantum solutions to inconsistent linear constraint systems
papers.abstract:
Linear constraint systems (LCS) provide a compact algebraic language for nonlocal games and state-independent contextuality. In the binary case the Mermin--Peres square shows that inconsistent LCS can be solved by promoting variables to local Pauli operators, whereas a series of no-go results excludes analogous Pauli-, Clifford- and monomial unitary-based constructions at odd prime modulus. We first isolate the reason for this difference: for tensor-product quantum solutions, the obstruction to a classical solution of a LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ decomposes into obstruction classes carried by the individual factors. As a consequence, a genuinely global obstruction cannot arise solely by tensoring locally unobstructed systems. The argument is specific to odd modulus; at even modulus the reordering phase need not vanish, as in Pauli-based examples.
  Given this distinction, we instead associate LCS to finite arrangements of rank-one projectors and resolutions of the identity in finite-dimensional vector spaces. Quantum solvability for such LCS is automatic and the search for a quantum-classical gap rests entirely on proving classical unsatisfiability of the underlying modular incidence problem of the arrangement. By relating such LCS with group-valued frame functions, we identify a family of examples in the work of [Harding, Jager, and Smith, Int. J. Theor. Phys. 44, 539 (2005)]. To establish the (non)existence of classically unsatisfiable LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with quantum solutions in all dimensions $d$ and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we further construct explicit examples for the cases $d=n$ prime. Our main result thus positively resolves the existence problem of such LCS beyond the binary case: such systems exist if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $\gcd(n,d)>1$. Moreover, we establish the existence of LCS with a quantum-classical gap over finite fields if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $p\mid d$.

papers.title: An energy-stable and accuracy-preserving finite volume scheme for wall-distance computations
papers.abstract: The distance to the nearest wall provides a length scale in models of wall-bounded turbulence. Computing this distance accurately on highly stretched meshes is challenging because small near-wall cells restrict explicit pseudo-time steps and geometric singularities can induce spurious oscillations. To address these challenges, this paper presents a semi-implicit finite-volume scheme based on a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) for solving the pseudo-time Eikonal equation on unstructured meshes. An upwind weighted least-squares reconstruction supplies the gradients used to evaluate the cell-averaged Eikonal residuals. The artificial-viscosity term is discretized using a two-point face flux whose coefficient vanishes as the regularized residuals in both adjacent cells tend to zero. The SAV update advances the semi-discrete system in pseudo-time by evaluating the residuals and viscosity coefficients explicitly and coupling the wall-distance averages and auxiliary variables implicitly. The analysis establishes unconditional energy stability under homogeneous Dirichlet conditions, permitting a grid-independent global pseudo-time step. The system's M-matrix structure guarantees nonnegative cell averages of the physical wall distance under a separate step restriction, while residual regularization and artificial viscosity preserve the formal order of spatial accuracy. Numerical tests confirm second-order spatial convergence for the quarter-cylinder case and demonstrate robust wall-distance computation on highly stretched meshes typical of Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes simulations. The SAV formulation is independent of the reconstruction scheme, providing a basis for extensions to higher-order finite-volume methods and other nonconservative scalar equations.

papers.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
papers.authors: Alex Prygarin, Claudelle Capasia Madjuogang Sandeu, Karam Shekh Yusuf
papers.abstract: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.

papers.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
papers.abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.

papers.title: Precise Convergence Speed of Clipped SGD
papers.abstract: We present a tightened convergence analysis of clipped gradient descent on $(L_0, L_1)$-smooth functions, with quantitative constants. Building on the ideas of Koloskova et al (2023), we refactor several case disjunctions to reveal the central role of a control of the bias derived from fundamental properties of $\ell_2$-projection, simplifying proofs. We also extend the domain of validity from $\eta \leq 1 / (9 \beta)$ to $\eta < 1 /\beta$ where $\beta = L_0 + c L_1$ for clipping constant $c$, which matches the more traditional analysis of smooth functions. We strengthen the convergence criterion from $\left( \min_{t < T} \mathbb{E}[\lVert \nabla f(x_t) \rVert_2] \right)$ to $\left( \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t < T} \mathbb{E}[\lVert \nabla f(x_t) \rVert_2] \right)$ with matching speed, and lower the final achievable floor from $\mathcal{O}(\min(\sigma^2/c, \sigma))$ to the more precise $6 \min(\sigma^2 /c, 3 \sigma)$.

papers.title: Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation for General Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.authors: Eugenio Durazo Rocha, Olai \AA. Mostad, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes
papers.abstract:
Low-depth syndrome extraction for Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum low-density parity-check codes can be formulated as a proper ordered edge-coloring problem subject to quantum parity constraints. A proper edge-coloring of the CSS Tanner graph ensures that each data or ancilla qubit participates in at most one two-qubit gate per layer, but does not guarantee a valid interleaving of the X- and Z-check measurements as for every overlapping X/Z check pair, the number of shared data qubits on which the X interaction precedes the Z interaction must be even. The minimum number of colors in a proper ordered edge-coloring satisfying the quantum parity constraints equals the minimum two-qubit depth when each stabilizer check is measured with a single ancilla.
  We introduce local automorphism-aware syndrome compilation (LocalASC), which reduces the constraint system to edge-orbit variables under a subgroup of the Tanner graph automorphisms and lifts each feasible orbit assignment to the full graph. Although the $6$-layer degree lower bound is unattainable for the published weight-$6$ IBM bivariate bicycle codes, we show that this is not universal among two-block CSS codes. Among code instances for which the maximum check weight equals the maximum Tanner graph degree, LocalASC finds depth-optimal syndrome-extraction schedules for several two-block CSS codes with odd component weights, including instances with unequal odd weights. We also obtain lower-bound-saturating syndrome-extraction schedules for several quantum Tanner codes satisfying the same degree condition. To obtain the subgroups used by LocalASC without computing the full automorphism group of the Tanner graph, we construct translation subgroups for two-block group-algebra CSS codes over abelian groups. For quantum Tanner codes, we give conditions under which square-complex symmetries extend to Tanner graph automorphisms.

papers.title: Gluons and Knots
papers.abstract:
We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. The amplitude is constant in chambers of kinematic space, its resonances are located at walls and its factorization is determined by wall-crossing. Yangian invariance dictates the amplitude to be determined by a 2d null Wilson loop that can be lifted into a positive and transverse 3d link. By reinterpreting wall-crossing and the Weinberg soft theorem as skein relations and Reidemeister moves of the subknots, we construct a state-counting description consisting of adding the `corners' of their HOMFLY-PT polynomials. Beyond the classical limit, we argue that this provides a conjectured but precise connection to topological field and string theory.
  The new formula is rigorously derived via a Lean-formalized dependency graph (DAG) as detailed in a companion paper, laying out the precise assumptions including Reidemeister III invariance. It is further tested exhaustively, including novel `star' kinematics where the amplitude and state count are shown to become Catalan numbers, in agreement with knot theory literature.

papers.title: Small area learning
papers.authors: Katarzyna Reluga, Nicola Salvati, Setareh Ranjbar, Nikos Tzavidis, Mark van der Laan
papers.abstract: Small area estimation (SAE) traditionally borrows strength across domains through a prespecified working model. We introduce small area learning (SAL), a novel learner-agnostic framework that formulates SAE as a multi-target semi-supervised learning problem and treats outcome prediction as a nuisance task. Areas may differ through unrestricted covariate shift and structured conditional shift, with information shared through common and area-specific components. We develop estimators with and without cross-fitting, accommodating low-complexity and flexible learners and unifying synthetic, model-based, and semi-supervised estimators. For area means, we establish a unified asymptotic theory for these estimator families, characterizing conditions for consistency, asymptotic normality and providing variance estimators and confidence intervals without prescribing a particular learning algorithm. We extend the theory to settings with only aggregated population covariates and characterize the resulting aggregation bias. SAL reveals clearly a bias-variance trade-off: partial residual correction in classical estimators can reduce mean squared error, whereas full correction yields estimators robust to the misspecification of working models, potentially at higher variance. Simulations yield RMSE reductions of 34%-49% relative to direct estimation, with the best configuration varying across settings. The numerical studies also illustrate how shrinkage can produce overly optimistic confidence intervals at the expense of strong modeling assumptions.

papers.title: A perturbation theory for Feynman-Kac models and their particle interpretations
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbation analysis of Feynman--Kac models, describing how local errors introduced at each step of the Feynman--Kac recursion propagate over time. Under general conditions on the potential functions and the Markov transitions, which are shown to hold for a large class of state-space models, we prove that the global error for any time horizon $T\geq 1$ is bounded by $C\,\Delta_T\log(1+\Delta_T^{-1})$, where $\Delta_T$ is the largest local error; this bound holds both for the prediction and the updated models. These conditions require no Lyapunov function and no stability of the Markov transitions, and allow for non-compact state spaces: confinement is provided by the potential functions. Our perturbation bounds hold in total variation and in the Kolmogorov norm; for the latter, we extend the Hardy--Krause variation and the Koksma--Hlawka inequality to unbounded domains. Our perturbation theory is applied to derive time-uniform bounds for linearized Kalman filters, Euler schemes for partially observed diffusions and nudged state-space models, as well as high-probability error bounds, uniform over whole trajectories, for particle filters and, more generally, for mean field particle methods such as sequential Monte Carlo and diffusion Monte Carlo algorithms.

papers.title: The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.

papers.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Bounds
papers.abstract:
We give a conic upper bound on the asymptotic rank of every weighted graph tensor over every field. If $W$ is the logarithmic edge-weight matrix of its dimension matrix $Q$, then $$ \operatorname{MaxCut}(W)\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{WT}(Q))\le U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W). $$ Here $U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W)$ maximizes $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}W_{i,j}P_{i,j}$ over nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrices $P$ such that $J-2P$ is copositive and $P_{i,j}\le P_{i,k}+P_{k,j}$ for all distinct vertices. The matrix $J$ is all-one, and copositivity means nonnegativity of the quadratic form on nonnegative vectors.
  Our starting point extends OpenAI's polynomial multiplication method and its subsequent arbitrary-field developments from three tensor legs to arbitrary order. We prove $$ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n))\le\frac{n^2}{4}. $$ The edge exponent is at most $n/(2(n-1))$ and tends to the optimal value $1/2$, improving the previous Coppersmith--Winograd bounds and answering Question 1.3.1 of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. The bounds coincide for every even $n$.
  For every odd $m\ge3$, the theorem gives $\log_2\widetilde R_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{GT}_2(C_m))\le m-1+1/(m+1)$, improving the previous cycle bound with a gap of only $1/(m+1)$ above the maximum cut. On weighted triangles, the program recovers the rectangular matrix multiplication curve of Uzna'nski and Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam. The CP and semidefinite programs, with or without path constraints, all have value $9/4$ on the unweighted triangle, giving this upper bound a natural conic interpretation. Further applications give explicit bounds for complete multipartite graphs, split graphs, and wheels, including new cases of maximum-cut equality.

papers.title: Towards Exact Multidimensional Fluxes: A Structure-Preserving Data-Informed Framework for Riemann Solvers
papers.abstract:
Finite volume and discontinuous Galerkin methods evolve the discrete solution using space-time flux integrals over mesh faces, which typically depend on solutions to local Riemann problems. In the multidimensional Riemann problem setting, this integral is difficult to evaluate exactly because of complex wave interactions. In this work, we show that the exact space-time flux integral is a polynomial in the time step and face dimensions. This motivates a learning-based approach, as only the mapping from the initial states to the polynomial coefficients needs to be learned. We propose a structure-preserving, data-informed Riemann solver framework that uses a neural network trained on high-resolution simulation data to learn this mapping. Key structural properties, including consistency and mirror symmetry, are enforced by construction. Provided that the high-resolution simulations converge to the exact flux integrals and the network accurately predicts the coefficients, this framework yields near-exact flux integrals for use in numerical simulations.
  We demonstrate the framework using classical implosion and explosion problems for the two-dimensional Euler equations. In an unsplit MUSCL-Hancock scheme, the learned Riemann solver remains stable at a CFL number of 0.9, whereas the same scheme using the exact one-dimensional Riemann solver fails. Compared with the latter scheme at CFL=0.45, the learned scheme is slightly more accurate and requires approximately 30% less computational time.

papers.title: Spontaneous Spirals in Spatial Systems
papers.abstract: Several chemical and biological systems produce spontaneous spirals in their dynamical behavior, such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction in chemistry and the slime mold Dictyostelium in biology. In a previous study, such spiral wave formation was accurately replicated with a computational spatial system known as the Ideal Storage Cellular Automaton Model (ISCAM). Here, a more detailed investigation is presented of the ability of this model to generate spontaneous spirals depending on its parameter values. A dynamical systems analysis is performed, and bifurcation diagrams, phase space diagrams, and snapshots of the model's spatial dynamics are presented for a range of parameter values. This analysis reveals that spiral waves can only be sustained in the system when the parameter values of the model fall well within the regime of a so-called Neimark-Sacker bifurcation.

papers.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
papers.authors: Jiantao Liu, Cheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Qingcheng Zeng
papers.abstract: We study generalized discrete fractal dimensions of sequences of finite connected graphs whose diameters tend to infinity. Using normalized shortest-path metrics and a general scale function, we define regularized energy dimensions for vertex probability measures and their optimized versions. We then establish a variational principle that identifies the optimized energy dimension with the supremum of ball-mass concentration dimensions. We also establish monotonicity in the moment order, stability under uniformly comparable measures, and upper bounds in terms of R\'enyi entropy growth and the upper mass dimension. Cluster estimates and explicit graph constructions show that local vertex concentration can lower the uniform energy dimension without changing the mass dimension. Finally, for uniformly Ahlfors-regular graph families, we obtain an integral criterion for energy boundedness and explicit formulas for the critical dimensions. These results clarify how global growth, local distance distributions, and the choice of scale function jointly determine discrete fractal dimensions.

papers.title: The maximum packing fraction of disordered bidisperse discs: theory and predictions
papers.abstract: Predicting the highest packing fraction that disordered packing of bidisperse discs can achieve, $\phi_{max}$, is an important unresolved problem. Such a predictive theory is hindered by the density dependence on the packing protocol and by ensuring disorder. In bidisperse packings, this is more complicated because $\phi_{max}$ is not a number but a function of the disc species size ratio, $D$, and one of the disc species concentration, $p$. These difficulties have been overcome in monodisperse disc packings by using the cell order distribution (COD)~\cite{Bl21}. Focusing on size ratios that prohibit rattlers, a COD-based theory is constructed here. It introduces bidisperse statistical closure equations, which combine an explicit disorder criterion with consistent cell and edge statistics, and yields $\phi_{max}(p,D)$ and structural predictions. The a-priori disorder-guaranteeing criterion proposed here ensures fast exponential a decay of the occurrence probability of ordered clusters with size. Using a constrained maximum-entropy analysis to ensure maximum disorder, the occurrence probabilities of all the possible cell and edge configurations are derived in terms of $p$ and $D$ and they are found to be binomial. All the results are assembled to yield an exact prediction of $\phi_{max}(p,D)$.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
papers.abstract: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

papers.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach
papers.authors: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu
papers.abstract: Stochastic bilevel optimization provides a general framework for many machine learning applications, such as hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic reinforcement learning. However, most existing bilevel optimization methods treat matrix-valued gradients as flattened vectors and perform optimization in the resulting vectorized space, ignoring the matrix structures common in modern neural networks. Moreover, the lower-level (LL) problem curvature can induce significant spectral imbalance in the upper-level (UL) geometry. Such limitations of existing bilevel optimization methods motivate us to develop BiMuon, a geometry-aware stochastic bilevel optimization method that integrates implicit hypergradient estimation in bilevel optimization with Muon-style orthogonalized updates at the UL. To our knowledge, BiMuon is the first stochastic BLO method with Muon-style orthogonalized matrix updates and an $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ iteration-complexity guarantee, matching the best-known rates achieved by Muon-type methods based on matrix parameterizations. To improve computational and parallel efficiency for models with multiple matrix parameters, we further study BiMuon for blockwise diagonal matrix approximation and derive a relative stepsize allocation rule based on UL progress and blockwise LL sensitivity. We evaluate BiMuon on representation learning and blockwise bilevel optimization, providing empirical support for our methods.

papers.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
papers.authors: Haejoon Lee, Thomas Marshall Vielmetti, Xinyi Wang, Dimitra Panagou
papers.abstract: Decision making in multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. We establish a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer and show that this bound converges to one as the number of denoising steps increases. Extensive experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling demonstrate that Discrete MBD outperforms SBO baselines in nearly all settings while achieving solution quality competitive with that of mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning methods at a fraction of their computational cost.

papers.title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
papers.abstract:
Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised.
  We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation.
  Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to na\"ive KM risks.
  The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.
